2c3c3702-22d5-8095-89c1-c7a175fab5c4.title: Company Goals -2026
2c3c3702-22d5-8095-89c1-c7a175fab5c4.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2c3c370222d5809589c1c7a175fab5c4 as of 2026-03-19T14:58:02.799Z: {"title":"Company Goals -2026"} **BFL's single most important sentence about what winning looks like this year:

Go from the image model to the best visual intelligence platform: shipping SOTA across modalities on a repeatable cadence, backed by the team and systems to sustain it, and revenue that proves it.** # **In 2026, BFL has 3 lifts ** company goals ## **Painful trade-offs, what we are not doing this year (missing)** {toggle="true"} ## Research/Data {toggle="true"} Initiatal Research shop list
Goal 1 Goal 2 Goal 3
**Goal** Ship FLUX.3: SOTA multimodal model (image + video + audio) at time of release Build a repeatable model development playbook that FLUX.4 inherits Post-training: make FLUX.3 strong on the use cases that drive revenue
**Ladders to which lift** Lift 1 — SOTA Visual Intelligence Lift 2 — Repeatable Operating System of Model dev Lift 3 — Revenue Engine
**One metric** FLUX.3 ranks #1 on primary multimodal benchmark at time of release (yes/no) FLUX.4 enters training using the same compute + data playbook as FLUX.3 (yes/no by Dec) Top 3 enterprise use cases addressed in post-training data by launch date
**Winning initiatives** (2-3 bets) (1) Joint video + audio AE training complete and validated. (2) Realtime mode at 720p/12fps. (3) FullHD 10–20s top-quality output (1) Unified eval suite that persists across model generations. (2) Data procurement pipeline repeatable. (3) Research → Product → GTM handoff codified (1) Structured GTM → Research use case pipeline. (2) Image editing as first-class task. (3) In-house prompt upsampling replacing 3rd party LLMs
**Owner + timeline** Axel + Robin / Q3 2026 Axel + Robin / H2 2026 Axel + Robin / Q3 2026
**What we're NOT doing this year (painful trade offs) ** Not building a separate video-only model — FLUX.3 is the unified bet. No custom text model. Not rebuilding the eval infrastructure from scratch for each model. Not chasing every customer request — GTM filters to the top 3 use cases
**One highlight** Architecture validated; video AE training underway Compute planning process formalised; data procurement pipeline operational Customer feedback → research loop defined in BizOps goals
**One risk / blocker** Audio AE training schedule — slippage here moves the full joint training window Research team bandwidth across 3 simultaneous architecture workstreams No dedicated post-training lead yet; dependency on GTM to surface the right use case signal
Lead: Founding team - led by Axel, Robin ## GTM / Sales (complete) {toggle="true"} [GTM/Sales goals](/2a3c370222d580698f5df9b29ef9e646?pvs=25)
**Goal 1** **Goal 2** **Goal 3**
**Goal** (measurable outcome) Build a scalable revenue machine Diversify revenue: reduce concentration, scale the ecosystem Customer & sales excellence: retain and grow
**Ladders to which lift** 2 (Revenue) 2 (Revenue) + 3 (Predictability) 3 (Predictability)
**One metric** (yes/no by September) \$30M net-new revenue 20 customers above \$500K ARR Net Revenue Retention (NRR) from 84% to 95%
**Winning initiatives** (2-3 bets) 1. New OW license tiers: standardized packages, kill bespoke deal pricing (Amanda). 2. Automated volume-based discount framework (Anthony). 3. Define ICP and customer journey with clear stage gates (Seb) 1. Define and operationalize three selling motions: sell to (direct), sell with (co-sell), sell through (distribution), each with clear playbook, owners and metrics (Amanda+Matt). 2. Win and scale 2 anchor enterprise logos (Sam). 3. Launch new key distribution partnerships (AWS) and scale Microsoft effort (Matt) 1. Redefine account ownership and tiering: every customer has a named commercial and technical owner (Jakob). 2. Build structured account engagement framework: onboarding, quarterly reviews, expansion triggers, renewal process (Seb). 3. Full revenue dashboarding and forecasting: pipeline visibility, churn signals, renewal tracking (RevOps). 4. Customer advisory board: CxO level, top 5-10 logos (Sam)
**Owner + timeline** Anthony & team / Q2 Anthony & team / Q3 Anthony & team / Q2
**What we're NOT doing this year** **One highlight** **One risk / blocker (sorry, 2) **
Custom pricing below \$1M. Standard packages are the norm, not the exception. No SMB long-tail: they come through ecosystem or self-serve, not sales time. Align the commercial org to the API company we are becoming: standardized products, scalable motions, predictable revenue so we’re ready to launch FLUX.3 and grab most revenue 1. Not being SOTA. 2. Hitting target requires revenue streams that don't exist yet (FDE, etc.). If the company doesn't evolve its operating model to support these new motions, we cap out
Lead: Anthony ## Marketing & Growth (complete) {toggle="true"}
Goal 1 (H1 2026) Goal 2 (H1 2026) Goal 3 (H1 2026)
**Goal** (measurable outcome) Build **quality awareness** for BFL & FLUX Establish foundation of an **enterprise GTM** engine Drive **engagement & retention** of our models
**Ladders to which lift** 3 (Revenue) 3 (Revenue) 3 (Revenue)
**One metric** 37M cumulative impressions
Total Impressions

329c3702-22d5-8015-95d1-f6bb7d7d824d.title: Long Context (Perc + Arch)
329c3702-22d5-8015-95d1-f6bb7d7d824d.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/329c370222d5801595d1f6bb7d7d824d as of 2026-04-16T09:33:29.769Z: {"title":"Long Context (Perc + Arch)"} This Notion aims to document the Long Context Project of and (consolidating two of the three long context jobs) Newest at the top. --- ## Alignment April 15th Dominik and me sat together to discuss how we take this project further, there are a lot of directions that have been explored, many new questions and problems popping up on the way. **We want to push the frontier for long video generation. **
This is very vague, and can be interpreted in many ways, so we need to sharpen it a bit. The above statement includes pushing the frontier into a bunch of different aspects: 1. More **efficient architectures/attention patterns/context spaces** to be able to train on long sequences. This potentially includes the entire enc-dec line, but also more compact representations of the context, sparser attention patterns etc. 2. **Training the model to actually reference long context**. The dynamics of video are inherently local, see this plot of latent frame similarity in lemur. The question if we need to encourage this behavior is relevant seeing e.g. how the dual time step loss was able to encourage global 2D reference. Anecdotally Cheng saw in her LongLive experiments how this behavior needs to be kind of enforced when posttraining. 3. **Autoregressive frameworks**. If we want to generate long videos, we need to do this in some chunked manner. It is not clear what approach is optimal here. 4. The last point directly ties into **mitigating Drift**. Long generations are cursed by Drift, which needs to be mitigated for long video generation. Wondering off to SCD, Perceiver et al in toyish settings we were not able to get an understanding for ourselves if we are pushing our current SOTA further into any of these directions or if our insights are limited to the setting at hand.
We want to push our current internal SOTA method with the Flux 3 arch and approach as our baseline. Aiming to get insights into better recipes for longer video generation, understanding the shortcomings of our current approach and being able to directly measure against it to not second guess if this result will hold.
For this reason we want to look into comparing approaches on Full Sequence vs e.g. AR training evaluated through FVD on lemur first since this seems like a prerequisite for the other points to us and something that should yield signal on the dataset. In addition we saw a strong degradation porting torch code to schwarzwald which will be investigated by Dominik. (EDIT: seems like model.eval() is doing unexpected things)
We currently see the video game datasets as tools to dive into when we want to deeper understand a problem we see but given that we currently do not trust any “positive” insight made on these we want to use them more for a problem resolution method. The above is to be finalized and discussed but a current assessment. Open for feedback. ## Lemur Wonderings (April 13-17th) Planning out further ablations we were not sure if any conclusions would hold based on TECO 300. So we decided to port to schwarzwald to also be able to examine results against our current F3 ablation runs.
Getting things into place, Dominik retrained the TECO 300 data in. Schwarzwald and was observing worse behaviour, which is currently being evaluated through evaling the same checkpoints across codebases to pinpoint if it is an eval or training issue.
The lemur dataset as pointed out by Hila, is very complex while being very small making it hard for the model to learn anything or get any good qualitative signal from it. Zions loopnav and CSGo dataset might fill the gap of complex enough to be able to be more confident in the signal while not being too complex. We are currently evaluating that. On lemur we used the chance to use the F3 ablation setting to train the model with a causal instead of bidirectional mask (still full sequence diffusion) Which led to very incoherent samples, potentially due to a different AR inspired inference schedule needed, nevertheless an interesting observation. (TODO add video)
## **SCD Baseline Experiments (April 7th - 10th)** After the initial Perceiver explorations and some signal from ’s baseline experiment that a higher patching factor on the context does not yield worse performance we decided to examine the currently claimed SOTA baseline [SCD](https://github.com/xingjian-bai/sparse-causal-diffusion/tree/main). As it offers a nice testbed with many potential design decision ablations to explore the space of 1) long context attention patterns 2) encoder type models to take redundant computation out of the denoising process 3) the interplay of long and short context 4) Autoregressive training paradigms But first, let’s take a look at the TECO 300 performance which was quite good out of the box. **First realization: **The initial FVD protocol was wrong in a few ways, updated protocol does i3d features + 4 rollouts per sample (256 samples) averaging the fvd of the full 300 frames (including 36 context frames) over the 4 rollouts. 🫠

Reproducing the SCD setting we are unable to match the exactly reported numbers and get to a FVD of \~40 vs \~37 (SCD_M_Encoder, Global batch size 16, 1M steps)
Interestingly the source code suggest the authors did Diffusion Forcing while the paper suggests Teacher Forcing with added noise on the encoder latents. Comparing Teacher Forcing (clean_enc_output_noise) vs Diffusion Forcing we see the following:

A dual approach that has a short context window and a long context window, where the short context window shares the same latent patching factor and space and the long context window has a higher patching factor p=4.
This setup enables us to compress long context sequences by a factor of 16 which would already enable much longer sequence training without any additional tricks. - [Baseline run](https://wandb.ai/black-forest-labs/scd_torch_long/runs/b4f27kxq?nw=nwuserfreddybfl) - [Dual run](https://wandb.ai/black-forest-labs/scd_torch_long/runs/nt42hyes?nw=nwuserfreddybfl) (the speedup is not as pronounce here due to the small block sizes which prohibit fa4 from being more efficient) The two runs are very close in terms of val loss and qualitative sample with one being an order of magnitude more efficient. **Experiment 2: Long Context relevance** **Sparse causal attention — a different long-context ablation.** Same single-stream encoder (`SCD_M_encoder`, same token layout as the baseline), but the attention mask itself gates which past frames are visible. A query at frame *t* attends to a key at frame *k* iff `causal AND (in_window OR strided)`, where `in_window = (t - k) < attn_window` and `strided = (k % attn_stride) == 0`. - **window=8, stride=8** — dense last 8 frames + every 8th frame as a long-term anchor. \~37 anchors over 300 frames → \~45 keys per query. Fine-grained long-term memory. - **window=8, stride=128** — dense last 8 frames + only frames 0, 128, 256 as anchors. \~3 anchors → \~11 keys per query. Aggressive ablation asking how much long-range context is actually needed. ```plain text # Query at frame t = 200 on a 300-frame sequence # allowed = causal AND (in_window OR strided) A = anchor, D = dense recent window = 8, stride = 8 frame: 0 8 16 24 ... 184 192 | 193 ... 200 ... keep? A A A A A A | D D [dense last 8 frames] ~8 recent + ~25 anchors = ~33 keys per query window = 8, stride = 128 frame: 0 ... 128 ... 192 | 193 ... 200 ... keep? A A | D D [dense last 8 frames] ~8 recent + 2 anchors = ~10 keys per query ``` Trying to adress the question if long context information actually helps the model. We keep the short dense context window and then a sparse this time causal pattern of every S=8/128 frame. --- ## Latent bottleneck analysis (2026-03-23) **Hypothesis:** The ctx32 perceiver collapses because (a) the 128–1024 variable latent budget prevents token specialization, and (b) the bottleneck is too small for 32 frames. ### Diagnostic analysis: perceiver latent probing **Method:** We ran 4 diagnostic tests on trained ctx4, ctx32, and ctx256 checkpoints using 64 videos from the Minecraft test set. Each test encodes context frames through the perceiver and compares the resulting latent tokens: - **Shuffle test:** Feed context frames in random order vs sequential. If cosine similarity ≈ 1.0, the perceiver ignores temporal order. - **Repeat test:** Feed N copies of a single frame vs N different frames. If cosine ≈ 1.0, the perceiver ignores multi-frame content. - **Cross-window test:** Encode two non-overlapping windows from the same video, and windows from different videos. If same-video ≈ diff-video cosine, latents are generic and don't encode scene-specific information. - **Variance test:** Measure per-token variance across the batch. Low variance = latents collapse to a similar representation regardless of input. ### Results at 200K steps (ctx4 vs ctx32 vs ctx256)
Test Metric ctx4 ctx32 ctx256
Shuffle cosine sim 0.846 **0.848** 0.816
Repeat cosine sim 0.846 **0.848** 0.816
Cross-window same-video 0.845 0.847 0.830
Cross-window diff-video 0.841 **0.847** 0.830
Cross-window gap (same − diff) **0.004** **0.000** **0.000**
Variance token variance **97,666** 1,363 1,063
### Results at 1.5M steps (ctx4 vs ctx32)
Test Metric ctx4 ctx32
Shuffle cosine sim 0.866 0.802
Repeat cosine sim 0.867 0.800
Cross-window gap (same − diff) **0.004** 0.003
Variance token variance 2.7M 5.5M
### Interpretation **ctx32/ctx256 are completely collapsed at 200K.** Cross-window gap is 0.000 — the perceiver produces nearly identical latents for different videos. Token variance is 70–90× lower than ctx4. The bottleneck (256 tokens) squashes 32×1024 input patches (32:1 compression) into a generic "Minecraft" representation, vs ctx4's manageable 4:1 ratio. **ctx32 partially recovers by 1.5M** — token variance jumps to 5.5M (exceeding ctx4) and shuffle sensitivity improves (0.802 vs 0.866). But the cross-window gap is still only 0.003 — barely distinguishing between videos. The model spends most of training recovering from an early collapse rather than learning useful representations. **Root causes:** (a) The variable latent budget (128–1024) prevents token specialization since any token beyond the minimum may randomly disappear. (b) The 256-token bottleneck is too tight for 32+ frames of input.

**Interpretation:** - **Shuffle/repeat sensitivity is dramatically better.** Original ctx32 has cosine 0.902 (nearly ignoring input). Var512–2048 drops to 0.795 — more sensitive to input than ctx4 (0.868). The perceiver is now actually encoding what it sees. - **Spatial variance recovers.** Fixed1024 and var512–2048 both reach \~11,800 (close to ctx4’s 13,464), vs original’s 6,156. Tokens within each video are encoding different spatial information. - **Token variance still low across videos (228–338 vs 2,922).** The individual tokens aren’t yet diversifying across different videos. May improve with more training. - **Cross-window gap still \~0.** Neither fix resolves this at 100K steps — the perceiver can’t yet distinguish between videos. But the shuffle sensitivity improvement suggests the representations are much less collapsed. - **Both fixes help, var512–2048 more than fixed1024.** Higher capacity matters more than removing pruning alone. ### Findings **1. Causal encoder + cross-attn matches perceiver.** At 850K steps, nearly identical f9/f99/FVD. The causal self-attention encoder is as effective as the perceiver cross-attention — without a fixed bottleneck. This is important for long-context scaling: causal encoder output tokens scale with input length. **2. Cross-attn conditioning \>\> seq-concat.** Regardless of encoder, cross-attn decoder is 40-80% better on FVD and 30-50 points better on drift f99. Seq-concat is not competitive. **3. Watch: loss instability.** `causal_crossattn` and `perceiver_seqconcat` both have rising loss. Monitor whether `causal_crossattn` plateaus or diverges as it approaches 2M steps. **4. Next step:** If causal_crossattn stays on track to 2M, try **causal_crossattn with ctx32** — the causal encoder doesn't have a fixed bottleneck, so it might handle long context where the perceiver collapsed. --- ## Key questions these runs answer 1. **Does the perceiver help?** → Compare perceiver vs identity at same settings (964204 vs 964164, 964206 vs 964207, 964111 vs 964118) 2. **Does more context help?** → ctx4 vs ctx32 vs ctx256 (964204 vs 964231 vs 964232) 3. **Pixel vs latent space?** → 964204 vs 964111 4. **Frame skip matters?** → skip1 vs skip2 (964204 vs 964206) 5. **Batch size scaling?** → bs8 vs bs256 (964206 vs 964217) 6. **Does MAE masking improve latents?** → 964204 vs 964310 7. **Variable vs fixed context?** → 964205 vs 964232 ## FVD evaluation All runs use `teco_minecraft_36_136` protocol (100 gen frames, context 0→36). Reference stats: - 128×128: `/mnt/data/freddy/datasets/minecraft/fvd/teco_minecraft_36_136_videomae2.npz` FVD is computed every 25K–50K steps depending on run. Check wandb project `perceiverio_gen`. --- ## Analysis: Drift FID & FVD (2026-03-23) ### Final rankings (latest checkpoint, sorted by drift_fid_f99)
Run Step f9 f99 spread FVD
**perceiver_ctx4_skip2** 2M 91.0 **96.2** 5.2 **180**
**perceiver_ctx4_skip1** 2M **87.2** 98.3 11.1 **171**
perceiver_ctx4_mae 2M 94.0 108.7 14.7 651
identity_ctx4_skip2 2M 103.2 117.6 14.4 190
perceiver_ctx4_bs256 650K 83.5 125.5 42.0 193
perceiver_ctx32_skip1 1.5M 103.1 125.9 22.8 779
latent_perceiver_ctx4 300K 121.3 141.9 20.6 216
latent_identity_ctx4 300K 126.3 144.0 17.7 212
*drift_fid_f9 = FID of frame 9 in rollout; drift_fid_f99 = FID of frame 99; spread = f99 − f9 (lower = less drift)* ### Key findings **1. Perceiver clearly reduces drift.** Both perceiver ctx4 runs reach f99 \< 100 at 2M steps; identity stays at \~118. The perceiver compresses context more effectively, reducing error accumulation during autoregressive rollout. **2. Skip2 best on drift, skip1 best on FVD.** perceiver_ctx4_skip2 achieves the flattest drift profile (spread=5.2, nearly no degradation over 100 frames) with FVD 180. perceiver_ctx4_skip1 wins on FVD (171) but drifts slightly more (spread=11). Skip2 may produce more diverse temporal patterns that resist mode collapse. **3. MAE masking: good per-frame FID, terrible FVD.** The MAE run converges to decent drift_fid (108.7 at f99) but FVD is 651 at 2M steps — 3.6× worse than baseline. Masking regularization damages temporal coherence while preserving per-frame quality. FVD is still slowly declining (was 1400+ midway) but the gap is enormous. **Not recommended.** **4. ctx32 is worse than ctx4 across the board.** Despite 8× more context frames, drift FID is 126 (vs 98) and FVD is 779 (vs 171). The perceiver bottleneck cannot usefully compress 32 frames at this model size. FVD is slowly declining from 1600→779 over 1.5M steps but the trend is not promising. ctx256 has no drift_fid data yet. **5. bs256 has best early-frame FID but high drift.** At only 650K steps, f9=83.5 (best of all runs!) but f99 drifts to 125.5 (spread=42). Larger batch clearly helps per-frame quality. FVD is competitive (160-193). **Needs more training** — drift may close. **6. Latent space plateaus early.** Both latent runs converge by 150K steps to FVD \~210-215 and f99 \~140-144. No further improvement. At equal compute, pixel-space perceiver is significantly better. Latent space may need a larger model to benefit. ### What to do next - **Keep training bs256** — it has the best f9 and competitive FVD; drift may decrease with more steps - **ctx256** and **varctx** — still running, need drift_fid evaluation enabled - **Consider skip2 as default** — best drift control with minimal FVD penalty - **Drop MAE** — 3.6× FVD penalty not justified by modest drift improvement - **Drop ctx32 at Medium size** — maybe revisit with a larger model that can handle more context ### Plots #### 1. raw.title: Long Context (Perc + Arch)
raw.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/329c370222d5801595d1f6bb7d7d824d as of 2026-04-16T09:33:29.769Z: {"title":"Long Context (Perc + Arch)"} This Notion aims to document the Long Context Project of and (consolidating two of the three long context jobs) Newest at the top. --- ## Alignment April 15th Dominik and me sat together to discuss how we take this project further, there are a lot of directions that have been explored, many new questions and problems popping up on the way. **We want to push the frontier for long video generation. **
This is very vague, and can be interpreted in many ways, so we need to sharpen it a bit. The above statement includes pushing the frontier into a bunch of different aspects: 1. More **efficient architectures/attention patterns/context spaces** to be able to train on long sequences. This potentially includes the entire enc-dec line, but also more compact representations of the context, sparser attention patterns etc. 2. **Training the model to actually reference long context**. The dynamics of video are inherently local, see this plot of latent frame similarity in lemur. The question if we need to encourage this behavior is relevant seeing e.g. how the dual time step loss was able to encourage global 2D reference. Anecdotally Cheng saw in her LongLive experiments how this behavior needs to be kind of enforced when posttraining. 3. **Autoregressive frameworks**. If we want to generate long videos, we need to do this in some chunked manner. It is not clear what approach is optimal here. 4. The last point directly ties into **mitigating Drift**. Long generations are cursed by Drift, which needs to be mitigated for long video generation. Wondering off to SCD, Perceiver et al in toyish settings we were not able to get an understanding for ourselves if we are pushing our current SOTA further into any of these directions or if our insights are limited to the setting at hand.
We want to push our current internal SOTA method with the Flux 3 arch and approach as our baseline. Aiming to get insights into better recipes for longer video generation, understanding the shortcomings of our current approach and being able to directly measure against it to not second guess if this result will hold.
For this reason we want to look into comparing approaches on Full Sequence vs e.g. AR training evaluated through FVD on lemur first since this seems like a prerequisite for the other points to us and something that should yield signal on the dataset. In addition we saw a strong degradation porting torch code to schwarzwald which will be investigated by Dominik. (EDIT: seems like model.eval() is doing unexpected things)
We currently see the video game datasets as tools to dive into when we want to deeper understand a problem we see but given that we currently do not trust any “positive” insight made on these we want to use them more for a problem resolution method. The above is to be finalized and discussed but a current assessment. Open for feedback. ## Lemur Wonderings (April 13-17th) Planning out further ablations we were not sure if any conclusions would hold based on TECO 300. So we decided to port to schwarzwald to also be able to examine results against our current F3 ablation runs.
Getting things into place, Dominik retrained the TECO 300 data in. Schwarzwald and was observing worse behaviour, which is currently being evaluated through evaling the same checkpoints across codebases to pinpoint if it is an eval or training issue.
The lemur dataset as pointed out by Hila, is very complex while being very small making it hard for the model to learn anything or get any good qualitative signal from it. Zions loopnav and CSGo dataset might fill the gap of complex enough to be able to be more confident in the signal while not being too complex. We are currently evaluating that. On lemur we used the chance to use the F3 ablation setting to train the model with a causal instead of bidirectional mask (still full sequence diffusion) Which led to very incoherent samples, potentially due to a different AR inspired inference schedule needed, nevertheless an interesting observation. ## **SCD Baseline Experiments (April 7th - 10th)** After the initial Perceiver explorations and some signal from ’s baseline experiment that a higher patching factor on the context does not yield worse performance we decided to examine the currently claimed SOTA baseline [SCD](https://github.com/xingjian-bai/sparse-causal-diffusion/tree/main). As it offers a nice testbed with many potential design decision ablations to explore the space of 1) long context attention patterns 2) encoder type models to take redundant computation out of the denoising process 3) the interplay of long and short context 4) Autoregressive training paradigms But first, let’s take a look at the TECO 300 performance which was quite good out of the box. **First realization: **The initial FVD protocol was wrong in a few ways, updated protocol does i3d features + 4 rollouts per sample (256 samples) averaging the fvd of the full 300 frames (including 36 context frames) over the 4 rollouts. 🫠

Reproducing the SCD setting we are unable to match the exactly reported numbers and get to a FVD of \~40 vs \~37 (SCD_M_Encoder, Global batch size 16, 1M steps)
Interestingly the source code suggest the authors did Diffusion Forcing while the paper suggests Teacher Forcing with added noise on the encoder latents. Comparing Teacher Forcing (clean_enc_output_noise) vs Diffusion Forcing we see the following:

A dual approach that has a short context window and a long context window, where the short context window shares the same latent patching factor and space and the long context window has a higher patching factor p=4.
This setup enables us to compress long context sequences by a factor of 16 which would already enable much longer sequence training without any additional tricks. - [Baseline run](https://wandb.ai/black-forest-labs/scd_torch_long/runs/b4f27kxq?nw=nwuserfreddybfl) - [Dual run](https://wandb.ai/black-forest-labs/scd_torch_long/runs/nt42hyes?nw=nwuserfreddybfl) (the speedup is not as pronounce here due to the small block sizes which prohibit fa4 from being more efficient) The two runs are very close in terms of val loss and qualitative sample with one being an order of magnitude more efficient. **Experiment 2: Long Context relevance** **Sparse causal attention — a different long-context ablation.** Same single-stream encoder (`SCD_M_encoder`, same token layout as the baseline), but the attention mask itself gates which past frames are visible. A query at frame *t* attends to a key at frame *k* iff `causal AND (in_window OR strided)`, where `in_window = (t - k) < attn_window` and `strided = (k % attn_stride) == 0`. - **window=8, stride=8** — dense last 8 frames + every 8th frame as a long-term anchor. \~37 anchors over 300 frames → \~45 keys per query. Fine-grained long-term memory. - **window=8, stride=128** — dense last 8 frames + only frames 0, 128, 256 as anchors. \~3 anchors → \~11 keys per query. Aggressive ablation asking how much long-range context is actually needed. ```plain text # Query at frame t = 200 on a 300-frame sequence # allowed = causal AND (in_window OR strided) A = anchor, D = dense recent window = 8, stride = 8 frame: 0 8 16 24 ... 184 192 | 193 ... 200 ... keep? A A A A A A | D D [dense last 8 frames] ~8 recent + ~25 anchors = ~33 keys per query window = 8, stride = 128 frame: 0 ... 128 ... 192 | 193 ... 200 ... keep? A A | D D [dense last 8 frames] ~8 recent + 2 anchors = ~10 keys per query ``` Trying to adress the question if long context information actually helps the model. We keep the short dense context window and then a sparse this time causal pattern of every S=8/128 frame. --- ## Latent bottleneck analysis (2026-03-23) **Hypothesis:** The ctx32 perceiver collapses because (a) the 128–1024 variable latent budget prevents token specialization, and (b) the bottleneck is too small for 32 frames. ### Diagnostic analysis: perceiver latent probing **Method:** We ran 4 diagnostic tests on trained ctx4, ctx32, and ctx256 checkpoints using 64 videos from the Minecraft test set. Each test encodes context frames through the perceiver and compares the resulting latent tokens: - **Shuffle test:** Feed context frames in random order vs sequential. If cosine similarity ≈ 1.0, the perceiver ignores temporal order. - **Repeat test:** Feed N copies of a single frame vs N different frames. If cosine ≈ 1.0, the perceiver ignores multi-frame content. - **Cross-window test:** Encode two non-overlapping windows from the same video, and windows from different videos. If same-video ≈ diff-video cosine, latents are generic and don't encode scene-specific information. - **Variance test:** Measure per-token variance across the batch. Low variance = latents collapse to a similar representation regardless of input. ### Results at 200K steps (ctx4 vs ctx32 vs ctx256)

### Interpretation **ctx32/ctx256 are completely collapsed at 200K.** Cross-window gap is 0.000 — the perceiver produces nearly identical latents for different videos. Token variance is 70–90× lower than ctx4. The bottleneck (256 tokens) squashes 32×1024 input patches (32:1 compression) into a generic "Minecraft" representation, vs ctx4's manageable 4:1 ratio. **ctx32 partially recovers by 1.5M** — token variance jumps to 5.5M (exceeding ctx4) and shuffle sensitivity improves (0.802 vs 0.866). But the cross-window gap is still only 0.003 — barely distinguishing between videos. The model spends most of training recovering from an early collapse rather than learning useful representations. **Root causes:** (a) The variable latent budget (128–1024) prevents token specialization since any token beyond the minimum may randomly disappear. (b) The 256-token bottleneck is too tight for 32+ frames of input.

Perceiver clearly reduces drift.** Both perceiver ctx4 runs reach f99 \< 100 at 2M steps; identity stays at \~118. The perceiver compresses context more effectively, reducing error accumulation during autoregressive rollout. **2. Skip2 best on drift, skip1 best on FVD.** perceiver_ctx4_skip2 achieves the flattest drift profile (spread=5.2, nearly no degradation over 100 frames) with FVD 180. perceiver_ctx4_skip1 wins on FVD (171) but drifts slightly more (spread=11). Skip2 may produce more diverse temporal patterns that resist mode collapse. **3. MAE masking: good per-frame FID, terrible FVD.** The MAE run converges to decent drift_fid (108.7 at f99) but FVD is 651 at 2M steps — 3.6× worse than baseline. Masking regularization damages temporal coherence while preserving per-frame quality. FVD is still slowly declining (was 1400+ midway) but the gap is enormous. **Not recommended.** **4. ctx32 is worse than ctx4 across the board.** Despite 8× more context frames, drift FID is 126 (vs 98) and FVD is 779 (vs 171). The perceiver bottleneck cannot usefully compress 32 frames at this model size. FVD is slowly declining from 1600→779 over 1.5M steps but the trend is not promising. ctx256 has no drift_fid data yet. **5. bs256 has best early-frame FID but high drift.** At only 650K steps, f9=83.5 (best of all runs!) but f99 drifts to 125.5 (spread=42). Larger batch clearly helps per-frame quality. FVD is competitive (160-193). **Needs more training** — drift may close. **6. Latent space plateaus early.** Both latent runs converge by 150K steps to FVD \~210-215 and f99 \~140-144. No further improvement. At equal compute, pixel-space perceiver is significantly better. Latent space may need a larger model to benefit. ### What to do next - **Keep training bs256** — it has the best f9 and competitive FVD; drift may decrease with more steps - **ctx256** and **varctx** — still running, need drift_fid evaluation enabled - **Consider skip2 as default** — best drift control with minimal FVD penalty - **Drop MAE** — 3.6× FVD penalty not justified by modest drift improvement - **Drop ctx32 at Medium size** — maybe revisit with a larger model that can handle more context ### Plots #### 1. 30dc3702-22d5-80e9-a472-c283f18c4ccf.title: What does World Class Developer Experience mean?
30dc3702-22d5-80e9-a472-c283f18c4ccf.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/30dc370222d580e9a472c283f18c4ccf as of 2026-04-16T08:51:06.983Z: {"title":"What does World Class Developer Experience mean?"} As part of our goal in 2026, we want to become the platform with the best Developer Experience in the world - what does that mean? FLUX gets people in the door. The experience is what makes them stay and pay. Developers have many options, very high standards, and usually default to trying to build it themselves with Claude Code. If we want to win them, we need to feel so good that building on us is obviously better than building it yourself. To get there, we also need to invest in design. Right now we only have engineers - we can build great things but we're missing someone who understands how a platform should *feel*, for both humans and agents. That's a gap we need to close. ## Principles for a world Class DevExp - **Obvious by default.** If a developer has to read the docs to understand a parameter name or error message, that's our bug, not theirs. Smart defaults, self-explanatory design. - **Two minutes to magic.** Sign-up to first generated image via the API in under two minutes. That's the north star. Everything is measured against it. - **Progressive disclosure.** One line of code for basic generation. Full control when you need it. Never overwhelm the 80% to serve the 20%. - **Fail gracefully.** Every error message is a mini-doc: what happened, why, how to fix it. A developer should never feel stuck. - **Meet developers where they are.** HTTP calls, Python SDK, ComfyUI, agent framework - we show up in their workflow, not the other way around. - **Trust is earned in the boring parts.** Uptime, versioning, changelogs, deprecation warnings. This is what separates "fun to try" from "safe to build on." - **The API is the product.** The model is the engine, the API is the car. API design gets the same attention as model training. ## Developer Dashboard A world class Developer Experience means having a world class Developer Dashboard - this might not sounds like the sexiest thing ever but is extremely important. It also means that the Dashboard has a lot of features and they should all make sense! It means having: - Creating an API key easily in different locations - Time to first generation is \<1 min from registration - Observability - Requests responses (2xx, 4xx, 5xx) - Alerts - Spending per model - Cost calculators, clear per request pricing, spend alerts - P50, P99 for responses - Rate limits / Spends - Datasets that can be used for LoRA training - Having quick starts I would see those features being built in part by our product engineer - the dashboard even though being a tool should be world class and that takes a lot of work. ## API & SDK ### SDK We should aim to have the best SDK in the game, and I don’t mean a pale copy of our API - it should add way more than this, otherwise it doesn’t bring much value imo Vercel did this with their AI SDK - they positioned it as being THE sdk for AI developers using Typescript, we won’t go there as it would mean adding other model providers but the SDK should add new capabilities. [AI SDK by Vercel](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/introduction) We should design SDK-level abstractions that unlock new capabilities on top of the API - composable workflows, multi-step generation pipelines, and higher-order features that don't exist as single API calls but feel like they should ### API The API should have more features than a simple image generation / editing - it should bring real value to the developers and users. It should be an API so well-designed that the docs almost feel unnecessary. This includes: - Batch prediction - Finetuning so easy people don’t think about it - Grounding - The best DevExp there is, we should be opinionated and make sure everything makes sense - Error messages that are obvious and would tell agents how to fix it ### MCP & Skills & More On top of having the best SDK and the best API, we should also reflect it with our MCP server and Skills - we have very basic workflows at the moment for those, we should work on making them really amazing so that *they just work *with agents. To make that possible, I would like to add a DevExp specialized in SDK / API to the DevRel team - you can read more about it here ## Ecosystem and Integration FLUX should be the default visual AI capability everywhere developers build. Some of that we build ourselves, most of it we make easy for the ecosystem to build. Everywhere where FLUX is, it should be running it in an optimal way. We should build and maintain strategic first party integrations that matter most - that means we should own our ComfyUI nodes for example, we should make sure everything is optimal there and also on day 0, we need to create reference implementations, integration guides as well so that when people add FLUX into their system, they have the best results and the best experience. We also need to release an open-source project showing how to do LoRA on our models, we should be the ones offering the best experience and the simplest! It should be known that if you use our tool, you get the best result. This should also be added into our API, we should have the best LoRA tuning there is out there, making it obvious to come to our platform to do so. To make that possible, I would like to add a DevExp specialized in Ecosystems & Integrations to the DevRel team - you can read more about it here ## Documentation & Education World class developer experience means having the best documentation there is - in an ideal world there is no need for any documentation as our users should figure out what they can do before but this isn’t the case yet. We would have different sections as well for our documentation. - We have a proper docs explaining the different concepts, getting started, the API, features and what is possible. - [Overview \| xAI](https://docs.x.ai/overview) - [OpenAI for developers](https://developers.openai.com/) - [Replit Docs](https://docs.replit.com/getting-started/intro-replit) - [Online payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/online-payments#integrate-platform-plugin) - Guides - Showing how to do LoRA, complex workflows, cookbooks as well - [Videos](https://developers.openai.com/codex/videos) - [Codex Prompting Guide](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/gpt-5/codex_prompting_guide) - [Fine-tune an image model](https://replicate.com/docs/get-started/fine-tune-with-flux) - [Working with LoRAs](https://replicate.com/docs/guides/extend/working-with-loras) An API reference that is interactive and that is clearer that we can try out the API code - it should be obvious to everyone that joins - that would also lead to more API creations and hopefully more stickiness because it’s just so easy! A release note that is up to date with the changes we wanna communicate with the community, everything we update that adds values to our users should be communicated, we should also send monthly updates over emails if some people care. - [Replit Docs](https://docs.replit.com/updates/2026/02/13/changelog) - [Changelog - Vercel](https://vercel.com/changelog) On top of this, it also means being more present where Developers are - we can for example monitor HF discussions to see what people are talking about, if there things that are not clear - we should work on fixing it. Same for Discord, having an eye there is important so we can fix those. To make that possible, we are hiring 2 DevRels on top of me and a Creative Technologist. We already have myself and Can doing it a bit.

raw.title: What does World Class Developer Experience mean?
raw.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/30dc370222d580e9a472c283f18c4ccf as of 2026-04-16T08:51:06.983Z: {"title":"What does World Class Developer Experience mean?"} As part of our goal in 2026, we want to become the platform with the best Developer Experience in the world - what does that mean? FLUX gets people in the door. The experience is what makes them stay and pay. Developers have many options, very high standards, and usually default to trying to build it themselves with Claude Code. If we want to win them, we need to feel so good that building on us is obviously better than building it yourself. To get there, we also need to invest in design. Right now we only have engineers - we can build great things but we're missing someone who understands how a platform should *feel*, for both humans and agents. That's a gap we need to close. ## Principles for a world Class DevExp - **Obvious by default.** If a developer has to read the docs to understand a parameter name or error message, that's our bug, not theirs. Smart defaults, self-explanatory design. - **Two minutes to magic.** Sign-up to first generated image via the API in under two minutes. That's the north star. Everything is measured against it. - **Progressive disclosure.** One line of code for basic generation. Full control when you need it. Never overwhelm the 80% to serve the 20%. - **Fail gracefully.** Every error message is a mini-doc: what happened, why, how to fix it. A developer should never feel stuck. - **Meet developers where they are.** HTTP calls, Python SDK, ComfyUI, agent framework - we show up in their workflow, not the other way around. - **Trust is earned in the boring parts.** Uptime, versioning, changelogs, deprecation warnings. This is what separates "fun to try" from "safe to build on." - **The API is the product.** The model is the engine, the API is the car. API design gets the same attention as model training. ## Developer Dashboard A world class Developer Experience means having a world class Developer Dashboard - this might not sounds like the sexiest thing ever but is extremely important. It also means that the Dashboard has a lot of features and they should all make sense! It means having: - Creating an API key easily in different locations - Time to first generation is \<1 min from registration - Observability - Requests responses (2xx, 4xx, 5xx) - Alerts - Spending I would see those features being built in part by our product engineer - the dashboard even though being a tool should be world class and that takes a lot of work. ## API & SDK ### SDK We should aim to have the best SDK in the game, and I don’t mean a pale copy of our API - it should add way more than this, otherwise it doesn’t bring much value imo Vercel did this with their AI SDK - they positioned it as being THE sdk for AI developers using Typescript, we won’t go there as it would mean adding other model providers but the SDK should add new capabilities. [AI SDK by Vercel](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/introduction) We should design SDK-level abstractions that unlock new capabilities on top of the API - composable workflows, multi-step generation pipelines, and higher-order features that don't exist as single API calls but feel like they should ### API The API should have more features than a simple image generation / editing - it should bring real value to the developers and users. It should be an API so well-designed that the docs almost feel unnecessary. This includes: - Batch prediction - Finetuning so easy people don’t think about it - Grounding - The best DevExp there is, we should be opinionated and make sure everything makes sense - Error messages that are obvious and would tell agents how to fix it ### MCP & Skills & More On top of having the best SDK and the best API, we should also reflect it with our MCP server and Skills - we have very basic workflows at the moment for those, we should work on making them really amazing so that *they just work *with agents. To make that possible, I would like to add a DevExp specialized in SDK / API to the DevRel team - you can read more about it here ## Ecosystem and Integration FLUX should be the default visual AI capability everywhere developers build. Some of that we build ourselves, most of it we make easy for the ecosystem to build. Everywhere where FLUX is, it should be running it in an optimal way. We should build and maintain strategic first party integrations that matter most - that means we should own our ComfyUI nodes for example, we should make sure everything is optimal there and also on day 0, we need to create reference implementations, integration guides as well so that when people add FLUX into their system, they have the best results and the best experience. We also need to release an open-source project showing how to do LoRA on our models, we should be the ones offering the best experience and the simplest! It should be known that if you use our tool, you get the best result. This should also be added into our API, we should have the best LoRA tuning there is out there, making it obvious to come to our platform to do so. To make that possible, I would like to add a DevExp specialized in Ecosystems & Integrations to the DevRel team - you can read more about it here ## Documentation & Education World class developer experience means having the best documentation there is - in an ideal world there is no need for any documentation as our users should figure out what they can do before but this isn’t the case yet. We would have different sections as well for our documentation. - We have a proper docs explaining the different concepts, getting started, the API, features and what is possible. - [Overview \| xAI](https://docs.x.ai/overview) - [OpenAI for developers](https://developers.openai.com/) - [Replit Docs](https://docs.replit.com/getting-started/intro-replit) - [Online payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/online-payments#integrate-platform-plugin) - Guides - Showing how to do LoRA, complex workflows, cookbooks as well - [Videos](https://developers.openai.com/codex/videos) - [Codex Prompting Guide](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/gpt-5/codex_prompting_guide) - [Fine-tune an image model](https://replicate.com/docs/get-started/fine-tune-with-flux) - [Working with LoRAs](https://replicate.com/docs/guides/extend/working-with-loras) An API reference that is interactive and that is clearer that we can try out the API code - it should be obvious to everyone that joins - that would also lead to more API creations and hopefully more stickiness because it’s just so easy! A release note that is up to date with the changes we wanna communicate with the community, everything we update that adds values to our users should be communicated, we should also send monthly updates over emails if some people care. - [Replit Docs](https://docs.replit.com/updates/2026/02/13/changelog) - [Changelog - Vercel](https://vercel.com/changelog) On top of this, it also means being more present where Developers are - we can for example monitor HF discussions to see what people are talking about, if there things that are not clear - we should work on fixing it. Same for Discord, having an eye there is important so we can fix those. To make that possible, we are hiring 2 DevRels on top of me and a Creative Technologist. We already have myself and Can doing it a bit.

Each test case ran **10 times in parallel** per model. Latency reported as p50 (median) and p95.
Test image: `test_image.jpg` (2000x1333, woman reading at a cafe). ## Pricing
Model Input / 1M Output / 1M
gpt-5.1 \$1.25 \$10.00
gpt-5.4-mini \$0.75 \$4.50

30bc3702-22d5-8179-9fe2-cd8b15815783.title: Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Transition Plan (v2)
30bc3702-22d5-8179-9fe2-cd8b15815783.text: Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/30bc370222d581799fe2cd8b15815783 as of 2026-02-19T11:32:07.030Z: {"title":"Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Transition Plan (v2)"} BFL \| February 2026 \| Post first alignment with Matt & Amanda --- ## Executive Summary BFL is entering Q2 with two commercial functions operating without a clear separation of mandate. This doc defines what each function does, establishes rules for Q1 (no ownership changes, introduce routing and single-ownership principles), and sets a North Star for Q2+ where Sales owns all commercial execution and quota, and Partnerships becomes a focused function around ecosystem insights, strategic deal-making, and partner program management. The biggest open questions — who owns strategic accounts and carries quota on them, and how to handle resellers — are flagged explicitly and require a dedicated decision before Q2 launch. Anthony will align with Sanjana on next steps. ## Context This is the second version of the Sales × Partnerships framework, updated after discussion with Matt and Amanda on Feb 17. The first version established the classification principle and account map. This version incorporates their feedback and introduces a two-phase approach: a transition phase for Q1 (no changes to current ownership) and a North Star definition for Q2+ that more clearly separates the two functions. Key inputs from the discussion: - Amanda: Partnerships should be defined by its function (ecosystem insights, strategic deal-making, program management), not by which accounts it "owns." Partnerships teams in mature orgs are small, focused, and don't carry traditional revenue quota. - Matt: Adding multiple people to strategic accounts risks breaking the orchestration advantage we have today. Needs more time to see Amazon and Microsoft generate meaningful revenue before layering in expansion plays. - Shared: No account ownership changes in Q1. Strategic accounts need quota treatment — how quota is structured for these accounts needs to be defined. The sooner we define the target state, the better — hiring, comp, and process decisions compound. --- ## Phase 1: Q1 Transition (Now through end of Q1) No account ownership changes. Current structure stays as-is. The goal for this phase is alignment on definitions and rules, not reshuffling. ### What stays the same - All current deal owners keep their deals through close - Matt continues to lead Amazon, Microsoft, Apple; Amanda continues Adobe, Samsung, Krea, agencies - Sales team (Seb, Sam) continues on current accounts. Anthony is currently interim Head of GTM — his accounts will need to be distributed across the sales team as it grows, likely requiring an additional senior AE in EU - Inference providers / resellers stay with current ownership until the new Partnerships hire is in place ### What we introduce now - **Classification principle:** Account ownership follows the motion, not the size. Orchestration → Partnerships. Execution → Sales. - **One deal owner, always.** Every deal in the CRM has a single owner. - **Sales qualifies and routes all inbound.** Sales qualifies every new lead and routes to Partnerships if the motion fits. - **Weekly alignment in pipeline call** for any unclear account routing - **No mid-deal ownership changes.** Transitions happen after close or at natural breakpoints. - **Review trigger:** If an account's motion changes (partnerships account becomes transactional, or vice versa), flag it for reassignment. ### Account map (Q1 — current state) Partnerships accounts: Amazon (Matt), Microsoft (Matt), Apple (Matt), Adobe (Amanda), Samsung (Amanda), Krea (Amanda), inference providers (current ownership until new hire starts), Cloudflare/Runware (current ownership until new hire starts), agencies (Amanda) Founder-led: Meta (Robin/Andi + Anthony on execution), LMArena (TBD — discuss with Sam) Sales accounts: Freepik, Photoroom, Canva, Gamma, Picsart (Seb — to be distributed as team grows), Snap, Mercado Libre, Shopify, NBCU (Sam), Envato, Wix, Deutsche Telekom, Bending Spoons (Anthony — to be distributed as he focuses on Head of GTM), HeyGen (Sam post-close), Siemens/VSCO/Schwarz (TBD) --- ## Phase 2: North Star (Q2+ target state) This is where we want to get to. The shift is more fundamental: Partnerships becomes a distinct function with its own mandate. Sales owns all commercial execution and quota. ### Partnerships: What it becomes *This is Seb's interpretation of the discussion with Amanda and Matt. This section is up for the Partnerships team to define and refine — they know best what the function should look like.* Partnerships is a small, focused team that drives long-term strategic value. The team is organized around initiatives, not permanent account ownership. **Three pillars:** 1. **Ecosystem insights** — Owns the competitive and partner landscape. Brings market intelligence back to leadership. Understands where BFL sits in the ecosystem and where the opportunities are. 2. **Strategic deal-making** — Negotiates and structures complex, multi-dimensional partnerships. These are deals involving investment, co-development, deep product integration, or ecosystem positioning. Examples: Adobe Foundry, Samsung on-device, Amazon co-selling, Microsoft multi-product. *A tension point: how these deals are reflected in quota (Sales quota, shared credit, or separate treatment) needs to be resolved.* 3. **Program & partnership management** — Manages live partnerships post-launch. Ensures integrations ship, usage grows, and the relationship delivers value over time. As partnerships mature, this becomes program management at scale (developer platforms, reseller programs, etc.). **What Partnerships does NOT do in the North Star:** - Carry traditional quarterly revenue quota - Own deal execution, procurement, or forecasting - Manage transactional API/license customers **Partnerships KPIs (to be defined together with the Partnerships team):** Starting point for discussion — Partnerships should propose what they believe the right metrics are. Some initial ideas: - Pipeline sourced / influenced revenue (with clear definitions of "sourced" vs "influenced") - Integrations shipped and live - Revenue from partner-sourced channels (tracked, not quota'd — noting that for some channels like inference providers, the long-term goal may actually reduce this number) ### Sales: What it becomes Sales owns all commercial execution, pipeline generation, forecasting, and revenue accountability. Sales is organized around verticals or geos with clear account lists. **Sales owns:** - All deal execution, including deals within strategic accounts - Quota for all forecastable revenue (API licensing, dev licensing, enterprise contracts) - Inbound lead qualification and routing - Account management for all non-strategic accounts (see strategic accounts section below for the open question on where those sit) - Expansion within existing accounts (upsell, cross-sell, renewal) **How Sales works with Partnerships on strategic accounts:** Sales carries the quota on strategic accounts. This creates a tension point: having quota on an account you don't own doesn't make much sense. This reinforces the need to define account ownership for strategic accounts (see open question below). Regardless of where ownership lands, Partnerships provides the orchestration layer — relationship context, timing sensitivities, cross-BU strategy, and strategic priorities. On strategic accounts, the account owner checks with Partnerships before making major moves. If there's a conflict between short-term revenue and long-term strategic positioning, it escalates to Head of GTM. ### Strategic accounts: Ownership & structure (open question) *This is the biggest open question in the framework and needs dedicated discussion. Getting this right matters more than getting it fast.* The top strategic accounts (Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Apple, Adobe) are the most complex, highest-value relationships we have. They require both orchestration (Partnerships) and execution (Sales). The question is: who owns them? The logic of this framework points toward Sales ownership — if Sales carries the quota on these accounts, Sales should own them. Splitting ownership from quota accountability creates confusion and conflict. The person who's measured on the number should control the account. More importantly, strategic accounts make up a significant chunk of the company revenue goal. That goal translates into GTM quota, which means these accounts need to be quota'd. The question then becomes: where should these accounts sit organizationally? Options worth exploring: - Directly under Head of GTM, with dedicated account owners - As the org matures, a dedicated strategic accounts team with its own leadership - Within Sales, with Partnerships providing the orchestration layer For now, these accounts stay with their current owners (Q1, no changes). The structure question should be resolved as part of Q2 planning. **Regardless of ownership, strategic accounts should have:** - A single accountable owner - Partnerships support on orchestration, cross-BU strategy, and ecosystem context - Dedicated SE/FDE (allocation TBD with SE/FDE leadership) - **Cadence:** Customer check-ins (bi-weekly/monthly), monthly internal account reviews + founder updates, quarterly external QBRs, quarterly internal strategy deep-dives --- ## Transition plan: Q1 → Q2 **Now (rest of Q1):** - Align on Phase 1 rules (this doc) - No account changes, no quota changes - Start Q2 quota conversation immediately (target: decision by end of Feb) - Matt and Amanda comment on this doc, we iterate **March:** - Finalize Q2 quota structure for Sales and Partnerships — company revenue goal transfers into GTM quota; how quota is allocated across direct revenue vs. channel revenue (e.g., AWS/Azure distribution) within strategic accounts needs to be part of this discussion - Define KPIs for Partnerships (non-quota metrics) - Recommend including strategic accounts in quota — these accounts represent significant revenue and are part of the company target. That target translates into quota, which means strategic accounts need to be quota'd. - Scope new Sales AE hires against the North Star account split **Q2 launch:** - New quota structure live - Strategic account ownership and quota model goes live - Partnerships transitions to North Star definition (ecosystem insights, strategic deals, program management) - Sales owns all execution and forecastable revenue - Account team model goes live for top 5 strategic accounts - Review and adjust after 1 quarter --- ## Open questions for next discussion 1. **Strategic account ownership, quota & revenue structure:** Who owns strategic accounts (Sales, Head of GTM, dedicated team)? How is quota structured for direct revenue (e.g., Amazon API deal, PowerPoint integration) vs. channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Azure distribution) within these accounts? Both feed into the company revenue goal, which transfers into GTM quota — the allocation model needs to be defined. This is the most consequential decision in the framework. 2. **Q2 quota for Partnerships:** KPIs only, or transitional joint quota on strategic accounts? 3. **Inference providers:** These are channel partners by definition (Partnerships motion), but also our largest API revenue source. The ownership question is tied to a bigger strategic decision: do we want to grow the reseller channel, wind it down in favor of direct, or find a middle ground? This needs to be discussed as part of the overall company strategy before we can assign clear quota ownership. 4. **Founder-owned pipeline:** Andi's deals should be transitioned to team ownership. The question is timing and sequencing — which deals move first, and to whom. --- *Updated by Seb after alignment call with Matt & Amanda, Feb 17 2026. Next step: comments from Matt & Amanda, then finalize Q2 quota discussion.* --- Older version: Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Account Ownership Framework

This version incorporates their feedback and introduces a two-phase approach: a transition phase for Q1 (no changes to current ownership) and a North Star definition for Q2+ that more clearly separates the two functions. Key inputs from the discussion: - Amanda: Partnerships should be defined by its function (ecosystem insights, strategic deal-making, program management), not by which accounts it "owns." Partnerships teams in mature orgs are small, focused, and don't carry traditional revenue quota. - Matt: Adding multiple people to strategic accounts risks breaking the orchestration advantage we have today. Needs more time to see Amazon and Microsoft generate meaningful revenue before layering in expansion plays. - Shared: No account ownership changes in Q1. Strategic accounts need quota treatment — how quota is structured for these accounts needs to be defined. The sooner we define the target state, the better — hiring, comp, and process decisions compound. --- ## Phase 1: Q1 Transition (Now through end of Q1) No account ownership changes. Current structure stays as-is. The goal for this phase is alignment on definitions and rules, not reshuffling. ### What stays the same - All current deal owners keep their deals through close - Matt continues to lead Amazon, Microsoft, Apple; Amanda continues Adobe, Samsung, Krea, agencies - Sales team (Seb, Sam) continues on current accounts. Anthony is currently interim Head of GTM — his accounts will need to be distributed across the sales team as it grows, likely requiring an additional senior AE in EU - Inference providers / resellers stay with current ownership until the new Partnerships hire is in place ### What we introduce now - **Classification principle:** Account ownership follows the motion, not the size. Orchestration → Partnerships. Execution → Sales. - **One deal owner, always.** Every deal in the CRM has a single owner. - **Sales qualifies and routes all inbound.** Sales qualifies every new lead and routes to Partnerships if the motion fits. - **Weekly alignment in pipeline call** for any unclear account routing - **No mid-deal ownership changes.** Transitions happen after close or at natural breakpoints. - **Review trigger:** If an account's motion changes (partnerships account becomes transactional, or vice versa), flag it for reassignment. ### Account map (Q1 — current state) Partnerships accounts: Amazon (Matt), Microsoft (Matt), Apple (Matt), Adobe (Amanda), Samsung (Amanda), Krea (Amanda), inference providers (current ownership until new hire starts), Cloudflare/Runware (current ownership until new hire starts), agencies (Amanda) Founder-led: Meta (Robin/Andi + Anthony on execution), LMArena (TBD — discuss with Sam) Sales accounts: Freepik, Photoroom, Canva, Gamma, Picsart (Seb — to be distributed as team grows), Snap, Mercado Libre, Shopify, NBCU (Sam), Envato, Wix, Deutsche Telekom, Bending Spoons (Anthony — to be distributed as he focuses on Head of GTM), HeyGen (Sam post-close), Siemens/VSCO/Schwarz (TBD) --- ## Phase 2: North Star (Q2+ target state) This is where we want to get to. The shift is more fundamental: Partnerships becomes a distinct function with its own mandate. Sales owns all commercial execution and quota. ### Partnerships: What it becomes *This is Seb's interpretation of the discussion with Amanda and Matt. This section is up for the Partnerships team to define and refine — they know best what the function should look like.* Partnerships is a small, focused team that drives long-term strategic value. The team is organized around initiatives, not permanent account ownership. **Three pillars:** 1. **Ecosystem insights** — Owns the competitive and partner landscape. Brings market intelligence back to leadership. Understands where BFL sits in the ecosystem and where the opportunities are. 2. **Strategic deal-making** — Negotiates and structures complex, multi-dimensional partnerships. These are deals involving investment, co-development, deep product integration, or ecosystem positioning. Examples: Adobe Foundry, Samsung on-device, Amazon co-selling, Microsoft multi-product. *A tension point: how these deals are reflected in quota (Sales quota, shared credit, or separate treatment) needs to be resolved.* 3. **Program & partnership management** — Manages live partnerships post-launch. Ensures integrations ship, usage grows, and the relationship delivers value over time. As partnerships mature, this becomes program management at scale (developer platforms, reseller programs, etc.). **What Partnerships does NOT do in the North Star:** - Carry traditional quarterly revenue quota - Own deal execution, procurement, or forecasting - Manage transactional API/license customers **Partnerships KPIs (to be defined together with the Partnerships team):** Starting point for discussion — Partnerships should propose what they believe the right metrics are. Some initial ideas: - Pipeline sourced / influenced revenue (with clear definitions of "sourced" vs "influenced") - Integrations shipped and live - Revenue from partner-sourced channels (tracked, not quota'd — noting that for some channels like inference providers, the long-term goal may actually reduce this number) ### Sales: What it becomes Sales owns all commercial execution, pipeline generation, forecasting, and revenue accountability. Sales is organized around verticals or geos with clear account lists. **Sales owns:** - All deal execution, including deals within strategic accounts - Quota for all forecastable revenue (API licensing, dev licensing, enterprise contracts) - Inbound lead qualification and routing - Account management for all non-strategic accounts (see strategic accounts section below for the open question on where those sit) - Expansion within existing accounts (upsell, cross-sell, renewal) **How Sales works with Partnerships on strategic accounts:** Sales carries the quota on strategic accounts. This creates a tension point: having quota on an account you don't own doesn't make much sense. This reinforces the need to define account ownership for strategic accounts (see open question below). Regardless of where ownership lands, Partnerships provides the orchestration layer — relationship context, timing sensitivities, cross-BU strategy, and strategic priorities. On strategic accounts, the account owner checks with Partnerships before making major moves. If there's a conflict between short-term revenue and long-term strategic positioning, it escalates to Head of GTM. ### Strategic accounts: Ownership & structure (open question) *This is the biggest open question in the framework and needs dedicated discussion. Getting this right matters more than getting it fast.* The top strategic accounts (Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Apple, Adobe) are the most complex, highest-value relationships we have. They require both orchestration (Partnerships) and execution (Sales). The question is: who owns them? The logic of this framework points toward Sales ownership — if Sales carries the quota on these accounts, Sales should own them. Splitting ownership from quota accountability creates confusion and conflict. The person who's measured on the number should control the account. More importantly, strategic accounts make up a significant chunk of the company revenue goal. That goal translates into GTM quota, which means these accounts need to be quota'd. The question then becomes: where should these accounts sit organizationally? Options worth exploring: - Directly under Head of GTM, with dedicated account owners - As the org matures, a dedicated strategic accounts team with its own leadership - Within Sales, with Partnerships providing the orchestration layer For now, these accounts stay with their current owners (Q1, no changes). The structure question should be resolved as part of Q2 planning. **Regardless of ownership, strategic accounts should have:** - A single accountable owner - Partnerships support on orchestration, cross-BU strategy, and ecosystem context - Dedicated SE/FDE (allocation TBD with SE/FDE leadership) - **Cadence:** Customer check-ins (bi-weekly/monthly), monthly internal account reviews + founder updates, quarterly external QBRs, quarterly internal strategy deep-dives --- ## Transition plan: Q1 → Q2 **Now (rest of Q1):** - Align on Phase 1 rules (this doc) - No account changes, no quota changes - Start Q2 quota conversation immediately (target: decision by end of Feb) - Matt and Amanda comment on this doc, we iterate **March:** - Finalize Q2 quota structure for Sales and Partnerships — company revenue goal transfers into GTM quota; how quota is allocated across direct revenue vs. channel revenue (e.g., AWS/Azure distribution) within strategic accounts needs to be part of this discussion - Define KPIs for Partnerships (non-quota metrics) - Recommend including strategic accounts in quota — these accounts represent significant revenue and are part of the company target. That target translates into quota, which means strategic accounts need to be quota'd. - Scope new Sales AE hires against the North Star account split **Q2 launch:** - New quota structure live - Strategic account ownership and quota model goes live - Partnerships transitions to North Star definition (ecosystem insights, strategic deals, program management) - Sales owns all execution and forecastable revenue - Account team model goes live for top 5 strategic accounts - Review and adjust after 1 quarter --- ## Open questions for next discussion 1. **Strategic account ownership, quota & revenue structure:** Who owns strategic accounts (Sales, Head of GTM, dedicated team)? How is quota structured for direct revenue (e.g., Amazon API deal, PowerPoint integration) vs. channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Azure distribution) within these accounts? Both feed into the company revenue goal, which transfers into GTM quota — the allocation model needs to be defined. This is the most consequential decision in the framework. 2. **Q2 quota for Partnerships:** KPIs only, or transitional joint quota on strategic accounts? 3. **Inference providers:** These are channel partners by definition (Partnerships motion), but also our largest API revenue source. The ownership question is tied to a bigger strategic decision: do we want to grow the reseller channel, wind it down in favor of direct, or find a middle ground? This needs to be discussed as part of the overall company strategy before we can assign clear quota ownership. 4. **Founder-owned pipeline:** Andi's deals should be transitioned to team ownership. The question is timing and sequencing — which deals move first, and to whom. --- *Updated by Seb after alignment call with Matt & Amanda, Feb 17 2026. Next step: comments from Matt & Amanda, then finalize Q2 quota discussion.* --- Older version: Sales × Partnerships — Definition & Account Ownership Framework

340c3702-22d5-803d-b3d2-ef4ea677bbe0.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/340c370222d5803db3d2ef4ea677bbe0 as of 2026-04-17T14:04:58.675Z: {"title":"Showcases (Demo Hub)"} Showcases are our way to collect and share demos and workflows. These are typically revolving around individual endpoints, but can be also a combination of capabilities or a targeted for a specific vertical. One showcase can consist of multiple individual demos or capabilities. We group them pragmatically. ## Existing Showcases - **Fashion/VTO**: Primarily the BFL Shop to showcase near realtime virtual try on (VTO) - Owner: - Goal: On the way to rolling out for specific clients and eventually making it Public - [App](https://showcase-vto.preview.bfl.ai/) - [Code](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/feldberg/tree/lab/vto-app/apps/showcases/vto) - **FLUX Tools**: Showcasing new FLUX.2 finetunings like Inpainting, Outpainting, … - Owner: Shared, but initially - Goal: Focus on showing new capabilities to selected customers, probably **no **path to public - [App](https://showcase-flux-tools.preview.bfl.ai/) - [Code](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/feldberg/tree/showcases/flux-tools/apps/showcases/flux-tools) ## Tech Overview - **Feldberg** as Monorepo to leverage existing implementations around Auth etc. - Staging and Production DB in **Supabase** for simple Authentication and connection to existing client assets (Not used in any App yet) - **PostHog** for fine-grained control who can access the apps - Per default, we whitelist all BFL colleagues for showcases - We can then roll out the whitelisting to specific clients as we see fit - Separate **Vercel** Deployments for each Showcase ## Deployment 1. \[IDE\] Create Branch in feldberg, use VTO or Flux Tools as reference on how to implement 1. Getting the dev setup locally to work requires some further work, but should be part of the Feldberg Repo and not this Document 2. \[current workaround\] Ping for the required .env variables 2. \[IDE\] Vercel Link 3. \[VERCEL\] Link Github repo 4. \[POSTHOG\] Create PostHog Feature Flag 5. \[VERCEL\] Add Env Variables (Make sure to use Production ENV for supabase) 6. \[VERCEL\] Change (Vercel) Environment to track branch ### Deployment Detailed (still messy) {toggle="true"} - setting up local Feldberg - Where to get staging .env variables? `vercel pull` gets prod - Needs to be copy pasted into new showcase + auth - Setting up the local commands for each showcase like
`echo "$LOCAL new-showcase.bfl.ai" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts > /dev/null
export NEXT_PUBLIC_NEW_SHOWCASE_URL='`[`https://new-showcase.bfl.ai:300`](https://homepage.bfl.ai:3000/)`X'` - When developing two apps in parallel and running Auth + Showcase 1 + Showcase 2, there seems to be a cookie collision (not 100% sure) between the Showcases which yields to login / logout issues. Generally even when just using one app, it seems like hot reloads mess with the Auth service which logs me out quite often locally - Vercel - Using `vercel link` to create a new project in vercel - this still requires to - connect to feldberg repo (optional when deploying via vercel cli) - set production / preview environment to the branch - set the env variables (most secrets are not shared secrets in playground afaik) - set the [build-and-deployment](https://vercel.com/blackforestlabs/showcase-flux-tools/settings/build-and-deployment) settings

We group them pragmatically. ## Existing Showcases - **Fashion/VTO**: Primarily the BFL Shop to showcase near realtime virtual try on (VTO) - Owner: - Goal: On the way to rolling out for specific clients and eventually making it Public - [App](https://showcase-vto.preview.bfl.ai/) - [Code](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/feldberg/tree/lab/vto-app/apps/showcases/vto) - **FLUX Tools**: Showcasing new FLUX.2 finetunings like Inpainting, Outpainting, … - Owner: Shared, but initially - Goal: Focus on showing new capabilities to selected customers, probably **no **path to public - [App](https://showcase-flux-tools.preview.bfl.ai/) - [Code](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/feldberg/tree/showcases/flux-tools/apps/showcases/flux-tools) ## Tech Overview - **Feldberg** as Monorepo to leverage existing implementations around Auth etc. - Staging and Production DB in **Supabase** for simple Authentication and connection to existing client assets (Not used in any App yet) - **PostHog** for fine-grained control who can access the apps - Per default, we whitelist all BFL colleagues for showcases - We can then roll out the whitelisting to specific clients as we see fit - Separate **Vercel** Deployments for each Showcase ## Deployment 1. \[IDE\] Create Branch in feldberg, use VTO or Flux Tools as reference on how to implement 1. Getting the dev setup locally to work requires some further work, but should be part of the Feldberg Repo and not this Document 2. \[current workaround\] Ping for the required .env variables 2. \[IDE\] Vercel Link 3. \[VERCEL\] Link Github repo 4. \[POSTHOG\] Create PostHog Feature Flag 5. \[VERCEL\] Add Env Variables (Make sure to use Production ENV for supabase) 6. \[VERCEL\] Change (Vercel) Environment to track branch ### Deployment Detailed (still messy) {toggle="true"} - setting up local Feldberg - Where to get staging .env variables? `vercel pull` gets prod - Needs to be copy pasted into new showcase + auth - Setting up the local commands for each showcase like
`echo "$LOCAL new-showcase.bfl.ai" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts > /dev/null
export NEXT_PUBLIC_NEW_SHOWCASE_URL='`[`https://new-showcase.bfl.ai:300`](https://homepage.bfl.ai:3000/)`X'` - When developing two apps in parallel and running Auth + Showcase 1 + Showcase 2, there seems to be a cookie collision (not 100% sure) between the Showcases which yields to login / logout issues. Generally even when just using one app, it seems like hot reloads mess with the Auth service which logs me out quite often locally - Vercel - Using `vercel link` to create a new project in vercel - this still requires to - connect to feldberg repo (optional when deploying via vercel cli) - set production / preview environment to the branch - set the env variables (most secrets are not shared secrets in playground afaik) - set the [build-and-deployment](https://vercel.com/blackforestlabs/showcase-flux-tools/settings/build-and-deployment) settings
