343c3702-22d5-8107-b814-c0a1cb9d911b.title: Platform - DevExp
343c3702-22d5-8107-b814-c0a1cb9d911b.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/343c370222d58107b814c0a1cb9d911b as of 2026-04-16T08:00:07.116Z:
<page url="https://www.notion.so/343c370222d58107b814c0a1cb9d911b">
<ancestor-path></ancestor-path>
<properties>
{"title":"Platform - DevExp"}
</properties>
<content>
# The Starting Point
- FLUX gets people in the door. The experience is what makes them stay and pay.
- Developers have many options, very high standards, and now default to building it themselves with agents.
- If we want to win: building on us needs to feel obviously better than building it yourself.
---
# North Star: Two Minutes to Magic
- You can try the models without paying first
- Sign-up → first image via the API in under two minutes. Everything measured against this.
- **Dogfooding.** If we can't build on ourselves properly, we can't expect devs to build on us. We should be our own hardest customer.
- **Progressive disclosure**: one line of code for basic generation, full control when you need it.
- **Fail gracefully**: every error message is a mini-doc - what happened, why, how to fix it. Agents should be able to self-correct from our errors alone.
- **Trust is earned in the boring parts**: uptime, versioning, changelogs, deprecation warnings. This separates "fun to try" from "safe to build on."
---
# 1. Developer Dashboard
The front door to our platform - needs to be world-class (think Vercel / Stripe).
- **Observability**: request metrics (2xx/4xx/5xx), spending per model, P50/P99 latency, spend alerts, limits
- **Quick starts & templates**: get people generating in seconds, not minutes
- **Integrated playground/demos**: interactive, try-it-live experiences - not just docs
- **Model browsing**: capabilities, pricing, comparison at a glance
- Evaluation, comparison tools, and request logs (came up in yesterday’s workshop as well)
---
# 2. API & SDK
The model is the engine, the API is the car. API design should get the same attention as any other engineering tasks.
- **SDK should be more than a wrapper** - unlock capabilities that don't exist as single API calls: composable workflows, multi-step pipelines, session/iteration history
- **API priorities**: batch prediction, finetuning that is so easy it’s obvious, grounding (coming soon though :D )
---
# 3. Agent Readiness (MCP & Skills)
- Agents discover us through one MCP - if they don't find the right capabilities, they go elsewhere. This was raised today.
- Our MCP server and Skills are basic right now. They need to *just work*. (more coming soon)
- Error messages must tell agents how to fix issues, not just what went wrong.
- Context extraction + session tracking: agents need to maintain state across generations.
---
# 4. Ecosystem & Integrations
- FLUX should be the default visual AI capability everywhere developers build.
- **Own our strategic integrations**: ComfyUI nodes, reference implementations on day 0.
	- We should own this one to make sure it’s the best experience there is
- **Open-source LoRA**: we should offer the simplest, best fine-tuning experience — it should be known that our tooling gives the best results.
- Integration guides so FLUX runs optimally wherever it appears.
---
# 5. Docs & Education
- **Interactive API reference** you can try directly 
- **Guides & cookbooks**: LoRA, complex workflows, agent integration patterns
- **Changelog**: every update that adds user value gets communicated. Monthly email updates.
- **Community presence**: actively monitor HF, Discord, GitHub - fix confusion before it spreads.
---
# Let’s build!

Two monitors. On the left, you are generating images on the playground. On the right: Claude for prompt refinement, Figma for layout, a browser tab running an upscaler. Four tools. One brain. Zero flow state.
Then it happens! After fourteen attempts, finally - the first decent image. Exact mood, exact light. You push your luck and try one more seed. Version 15 is a miss. Version 16 is worse. You want to go back, but the playground doesnt keep history - every session starts blank, and anything you didnt manually save is simply gone in a endless long history.
Ten minutes of reconstructing prompts from memory later or ten minutes of scrolling down the playground until you find the image - your momentum is ***dead.***
This is where professional AI design actually lives right now. The models themselves are extraordinary with photorealistic output in seconds. But the (most) interfaces wrapping them.. They are chat windows. Support ticket boxes basically. We accepted the chatbox because the models were new and the outputs were miraculous enough that the interface didnt matter. That period is over since last year. The models are now amazing and the prompt box has become the bottleneck it always was. Designing complex layered visual work through a chat window is the wrong tool for the job - in the same way a telephone is the wrong tool for architecture. *You can communicate ideas through it. You cannot build in it.* Designing visually complex, multi-layered work through a single text prompt in a chatbox is the wrong tool for the job and the infinite canvas is the only one that makes sense (right now). ## **The Problem Space** The productivity wall isnt coming from the models. Flux and other Models have never been more capable. The wall is coming from the medium and the medium right now is fundamentally broken for visual work. ### **The Linear Trap of Chatbots and Historys** The most glaring flaw of traditional LLM interfaces and image generation tools (like Midjourney, our Playground or other Examples) is that they operate on a strictly chronological, linear timeline. You input a prompt at the bottom, the output appears, and the entire conversation shifts upward. But design doesnt work that way. Design is spatial. It branches. It is an iterative spatial and branching process. A real creative process looks nothing like a chat thread. You generate a baseline, then split into three color directions. You take the second direction and explore four different compositional approaches. Then you pull back and hold the result next to the original to feel the distance traveled. That back and forth that simultaneous comparison thats where the actual thinking happens. A chat thread and our playground do not support this. In a chat interface, previous iterations are buried under the weight of new ones. In the Playground, the history disappears after a page reload, and bugs in the history feature prevent you from finding it again. This creates a severe psychological friction known as **Scroll Fatigue**. I find myself constantly scrolling up and down, trying to mentally hold the context of "Version 4" while looking at "Version 47." The interface treats every generation as a disposable, isolated transaction rather than a piece of a larger, evolving puzzle. ### **Context Switching and the Fragmented Mind** Because the chatbox cannot serve as a workspace and professionals are forced into what we call the "Frankenstein Workflow." You use a textbased AI to brainstorm the brief. You use a linear Chatbot to generate the raw imagery. You use a web-based Upscale. You use a heavy desktop software to composite the image. you use Slack to share the Images. This forces the brain to endure the **Context Switch Penalty**. Every time a professional switches between different software environments, it takes an average of 23 minutes to regain deep focus. you are moving your brain between entirely different modes of interaction from creative prompting to spatial layout, to technical file management. Furthermore - all systems loses context at every step. When you drag an image out of Playground into Figma (or whatever space we use to save and share images), the image becomes "dumb." Figma doesnt know what prompt generated it. If you need to make a slight adjustment to the lighting or change something else, you have to jump back into Playground and hope the UI lets you scroll to the missing Prompt. The bridge between generation and execution is completely broken. ![A recent FLUX Project I worked on - impossible to do in the Playground](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/dcb297f8-3a9b-48e6-9823-1f2e77449001/Bildschirmfoto_2026-04-15_um_09.54.54.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4662CPTWCCK%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095703Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIDyi6ova11bl83yhDG%2BrqbbNy3Fs%2BuObthwckLx4p9PmAiBILFNw84%2B9gPdtwiecYz9KeNbjYxYtOkmBH5DMCm9YLir%2FAwgCEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMLG0TwBY%2FLgCYW0vjKtwDEKfbxgwCpqw3XQRTP9VlvVRmOkkmhWDU7HInHmnlD0zQf%2BX%2BvHfI1xiwBcimz5FJJVkrNtAq%2BYWvacHi8jMEg5InyrMTuiq4zj6%2B866Y8NgRBBYPWkL%2FwH80LNyXe0j2JWqdC4NTdd0DHWhtI5m1Lc9QMa4PSYfluxJ9MCskJ7Pi8mAGksASVqT0jWY77E%2FiLNDEMrPTyz5DEcGmSfvsvdt%2Fvglc8F3hPOeNZwFscWPDaY4%2FHbirrJ0QLhMhH%2BBeL1Kf4wOOIzWlj0U%2BtDiHm%2FP5TUbUXaKOE%2Bqh%2FtCyHz1YaZPusD3pAdHUYl0It1SiMW47c69GI3BQZHfPQCaRS4MYNS4CEGy%2BZqkP63y8ZFv8J3%2Bc2yD7U6SRZvWF5%2BzHMtTayln3QNMSe37W1cMIIiVYeN69FX8EXaOP1Te%2BcVEFtgtZa355ndwEz9YuIZIto5lq7g28N88NSl4GYuV3i%2Fi3T0UmHx%2BSHZjODhvLJ7HY2hZH4EaIks4qflbsdLRfAuOppOy3rxvkWaJs298nmdukw7ZWVLcdVr9GAtzH4aiiiYfT6XNENquP4qA4q2MeQXSxbEZo1s00gpo%2Ft7hM6a0UJMJ7y9zmKB1m%2FWfXBcAiFenNqJZw%2F5ijJZMw06%2BSzwY6pgF86GIPqqs4VfK%2FrmkdZYXVnxFD9rTmL%2FAMtDE8JaetWSxHBK6B1NEHzNxS77J7ztXEa5vlBh0S4IDzfmtSdtLXpB%2B8uJhOSqkc53aISpCK045%2Bn5QW%2BAPumg32C9L2q2kEe9qVGZ%2FB9u%2BHcu5tV1sUyg5kZkIZW3WKkDZN3MSlys9JzT7CMvJribwJR7M4nIMf%2Fl0qUipfx94re4w5%2Btps9e3kK3o9&X-Amz-Signature=e8f8c31cc6f05be1405c5951161526dabdc4b8f39efe0a98acac47ae17255e61&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) ## **Part 2: The First Principles of Visual Ideation ** If the chatbox is the wrong answer what does the right one look like? To get there we have to stop thinking about "talking to an agent" and start thinking about how creative thinking actually works. before software, before ai, before screens, before any of this. So if the chatbox fails - what replaces(d) it? The answer isnt found in better software or agents. Its found by stepping back further than that. Before the interface debate, before AI, before screens entirely and asking a simpler question: *how does creative thinking actually work?* ### **The Architecture of the Human Moodboard** Long before digital design tools existed creative professionals used physical space to think. They pinned images on the wall with polaroid photographs into massive corkboards. ![A oldschool in(finite) cana](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/d7437879-1a0c-4a1f-8430-c6b13a43aa72/1_ia4Z2bQWOTD_Ri14eXlrIg.webp?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4662CPTWCCK%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095703Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIDyi6ova11bl83yhDG%2BrqbbNy3Fs%2BuObthwckLx4p9PmAiBILFNw84%2B9gPdtwiecYz9KeNbjYxYtOkmBH5DMCm9YLir%2FAwgCEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMLG0TwBY%2FLgCYW0vjKtwDEKfbxgwCpqw3XQRTP9VlvVRmOkkmhWDU7HInHmnlD0zQf%2BX%2BvHfI1xiwBcimz5FJJVkrNtAq%2BYWvacHi8jMEg5InyrMTuiq4zj6%2B866Y8NgRBBYPWkL%2FwH80LNyXe0j2JWqdC4NTdd0DHWhtI5m1Lc9QMa4PSYfluxJ9MCskJ7Pi8mAGksASVqT0jWY77E%2FiLNDEMrPTyz5DEcGmSfvsvdt%2Fvglc8F3hPOeNZwFscWPDaY4%2FHbirrJ0QLhMhH%2BBeL1Kf4wOOIzWlj0U%2BtDiHm%2FP5TUbUXaKOE%2Bqh%2FtCyHz1YaZPusD3pAdHUYl0It1SiMW47c69GI3BQZHfPQCaRS4MYNS4CEGy%2BZqkP63y8ZFv8J3%2Bc2yD7U6SRZvWF5%2BzHMtTayln3QNMSe37W1cMIIiVYeN69FX8EXaOP1Te%2BcVEFtgtZa355ndwEz9YuIZIto5lq7g28N88NSl4GYuV3i%2Fi3T0UmHx%2BSHZjODhvLJ7HY2hZH4EaIks4qflbsdLRfAuOppOy3rxvkWaJs298nmdukw7ZWVLcdVr9GAtzH4aiiiYfT6XNENquP4qA4q2MeQXSxbEZo1s00gpo%2Ft7hM6a0UJMJ7y9zmKB1m%2FWfXBcAiFenNqJZw%2F5ijJZMw06%2BSzwY6pgF86GIPqqs4VfK%2FrmkdZYXVnxFD9rTmL%2FAMtDE8JaetWSxHBK6B1NEHzNxS77J7ztXEa5vlBh0S4IDzfmtSdtLXpB%2B8uJhOSqkc53aISpCK045%2Bn5QW%2BAPumg32C9L2q2kEe9qVGZ%2FB9u%2BHcu5tV1sUyg5kZkIZW3WKkDZN3MSlys9JzT7CMvJribwJR7M4nIMf%2Fl0qUipfx94re4w5%2Btps9e3kK3o9&X-Amz-Signature=35d55617c760fd44892f0d72828d5651abc26966e6489ea78cae8827bb879e1c&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) This is a cognitive necessity based on the theory of the **Extended Mind**. The human brain struggles to hold multiple complex visual images in its shortterm memory simultaneously. By placing items in physical space we offload that cognitive burden onto our environment. We use spatial juxtaposition and placing a harsh brutalist font directly next to a soft organic photo to instantly gauge harmony or tension. ### **Jobs to Be Done (JTBD) in Creative Collaboration** When we apply the "Jobs to Be Done" framework to enterprise design the inadequacy of the chat interface becomes even more clearer When a Marketing Director sits down to work, their JTBD is almost never "I want to generate a single, isolated 1024x1024 PNG of a dog riding a skateboard." Their JTBD is: "I need to orchestrate a marketing campaign with 40 different Flux Images. I need a primary hero image for the website, three vertical video variations for TikTok, a 3D product mockup for our investor deck, and a consistent color palette that ties them all together." A chatbox cannot deliver this. It delivers isolated assets and not a visual world. ### The “Flow” in Workflow As I already said: When I use the Playground or our API im stuck in a one-at-a-time mode: Input prompt, wait for result, and if I want to try something different, start a whole new process. Its typical of many AI design tools and it breaks my focus. Almost exactly one year ago something changed. Weavy and Flora were launched. Two Infinite Canvas UI - both have grown incredibly fast. Weavy has since been acquired by Figma. Flora recently closed its Series B round with \$45 million in new funding. With these infinite canvas I can run several ideas at once and see them develop side by side. This matches how I actually think when designing or protoyping - considering multiple options simultaneously rather than one after another. ![*A demo of Flora*](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/2eb9a63b-f8d6-4a17-98cd-58f751eb2b3c/optimized_Screenshot_2025-03-14_at_10.45.04_AM.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4662CPTWCCK%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095703Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIDyi6ova11bl83yhDG%2BrqbbNy3Fs%2BuObthwckLx4p9PmAiBILFNw84%2B9gPdtwiecYz9KeNbjYxYtOkmBH5DMCm9YLir%2FAwgCEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMLG0TwBY%2FLgCYW0vjKtwDEKfbxgwCpqw3XQRTP9VlvVRmOkkmhWDU7HInHmnlD0zQf%2BX%2BvHfI1xiwBcimz5FJJVkrNtAq%2BYWvacHi8jMEg5InyrMTuiq4zj6%2B866Y8NgRBBYPWkL%2FwH80LNyXe0j2JWqdC4NTdd0DHWhtI5m1Lc9QMa4PSYfluxJ9MCskJ7Pi8mAGksASVqT0jWY77E%2FiLNDEMrPTyz5DEcGmSfvsvdt%2Fvglc8F3hPOeNZwFscWPDaY4%2FHbirrJ0QLhMhH%2BBeL1Kf4wOOIzWlj0U%2BtDiHm%2FP5TUbUXaKOE%2Bqh%2FtCyHz1YaZPusD3pAdHUYl0It1SiMW47c69GI3BQZHfPQCaRS4MYNS4CEGy%2BZqkP63y8ZFv8J3%2Bc2yD7U6SRZvWF5%2BzHMtTayln3QNMSe37W1cMIIiVYeN69FX8EXaOP1Te%2BcVEFtgtZa355ndwEz9YuIZIto5lq7g28N88NSl4GYuV3i%2Fi3T0UmHx%2BSHZjODhvLJ7HY2hZH4EaIks4qflbsdLRfAuOppOy3rxvkWaJs298nmdukw7ZWVLcdVr9GAtzH4aiiiYfT6XNENquP4qA4q2MeQXSxbEZo1s00gpo%2Ft7hM6a0UJMJ7y9zmKB1m%2FWfXBcAiFenNqJZw%2F5ijJZMw06%2BSzwY6pgF86GIPqqs4VfK%2FrmkdZYXVnxFD9rTmL%2FAMtDE8JaetWSxHBK6B1NEHzNxS77J7ztXEa5vlBh0S4IDzfmtSdtLXpB%2B8uJhOSqkc53aISpCK045%2Bn5QW%2BAPumg32C9L2q2kEe9qVGZ%2FB9u%2BHcu5tV1sUyg5kZkIZW3WKkDZN3MSlys9JzT7CMvJribwJR7M4nIMf%2Fl0qUipfx94re4w5%2Btps9e3kK3o9&X-Amz-Signature=91cf9bd2038fb1a8be92fb559df0255251e652cb986de7e17241cacc537fbf46&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) The sauce is in how closely the Flora team worked with actual creative professionals to understand their workflow. They collaborated with New York Universitys Tisch School of the Arts, designfirm Pentagram, and other major creative institutions and agencies across the US. They are building it for real creative workflows because they are embedded in those communities. You can feel that closeness to the end user when you are using the product. It just makes sense. The lesson im taking away: In the world of AI powered tools, understanding your users deeply is (slowly) becoming more important than the underlaying models. Its not just about the Models anymore. Two monitors. On the left, you are generating images on the playground. On the right: Claude for prompt refinement, Figma for layout, a browser tab running an upscaler. Four tools. One brain. Zero flow state.
Then it happens! After fourteen attempts, finally - the first decent image. Exact mood, exact light. You push your luck and try one more seed. Version 15 is a miss. Version 16 is worse. You want to go back, but the playground doesnt keep history - every session starts blank, and anything you didnt manually save is simply gone in a endless long history.
Ten minutes of reconstructing prompts from memory later or ten minutes of scrolling down the playground until you find the image - your momentum is ***dead.***
This is where professional AI design actually lives right now. The models themselves are extraordinary with photorealistic output in seconds. But the (most) interfaces wrapping them.. They are chat windows. Support ticket boxes basically. We accepted the chatbox because the models were new and the outputs were miraculous enough that the interface didnt matter. That period is over since last year. The models are now amazing and the prompt box has become the bottleneck it always was. Designing complex layered visual work through a chat window is the wrong tool for the job - in the same way a telephone is the wrong tool for architecture. *You can communicate ideas through it. You cannot build in it.* Designing visually complex, multi-layered work through a single text prompt in a chatbox is the wrong tool for the job and the infinite canvas is the only one that makes sense (right now). ## **The Problem Space** The productivity wall isnt coming from the models. Flux and other Models have never been more capable. The wall is coming from the medium and the medium right now is fundamentally broken for visual work. ### **The Linear Trap of Chatbots and Historys** The most glaring flaw of traditional LLM interfaces and image generation tools (like Midjourney, our Playground or other Examples) is that they operate on a strictly chronological, linear timeline. You input a prompt at the bottom, the output appears, and the entire conversation shifts upward. But design doesnt work that way. Design is spatial. It branches. It is an iterative spatial and branching process. A real creative process looks nothing like a chat thread. You generate a baseline, then split into three color directions. You take the second direction and explore four different compositional approaches. Then you pull back and hold the result next to the original to feel the distance traveled. That back and forth that simultaneous comparison thats where the actual thinking happens. A chat thread and our playground do not support this. In a chat interface, previous iterations are buried under the weight of new ones. In the Playground, the history disappears after a page reload, and bugs in the history feature prevent you from finding it again. This creates a severe psychological friction known as **Scroll Fatigue**. I find myself constantly scrolling up and down, trying to mentally hold the context of "Version 4" while looking at "Version 47." The interface treats every generation as a disposable, isolated transaction rather than a piece of a larger, evolving puzzle. ### **Context Switching and the Fragmented Mind** Because the chatbox cannot serve as a workspace and professionals are forced into what we call the "Frankenstein Workflow." You use a textbased AI to brainstorm the brief. You use a linear Chatbot to generate the raw imagery. You use a web-based Upscale. You use a heavy desktop software to composite the image. you use Slack to share the Images. This forces the brain to endure the **Context Switch Penalty**. Every time a professional switches between different software environments, it takes an average of 23 minutes to regain deep focus. you are moving your brain between entirely different modes of interaction from creative prompting to spatial layout, to technical file management. Furthermore - all systems loses context at every step. When you drag an image out of Playground into Figma (or whatever space we use to save and share images), the image becomes "dumb." Figma doesnt know what prompt generated it. If you need to make a slight adjustment to the lighting or change something else, you have to jump back into Playground and hope the UI lets you scroll to the missing Prompt. The bridge between generation and execution is completely broken. ![A recent FLUX Project I worked on - impossible to do in the Playground](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/dcb297f8-3a9b-48e6-9823-1f2e77449001/Bildschirmfoto_2026-04-15_um_09.54.54.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4662CPTWCCK%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095703Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIDyi6ova11bl83yhDG%2BrqbbNy3Fs%2BuObthwckLx4p9PmAiBILFNw84%2B9gPdtwiecYz9KeNbjYxYtOkmBH5DMCm9YLir%2FAwgCEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMLG0TwBY%2FLgCYW0vjKtwDEKfbxgwCpqw3XQRTP9VlvVRmOkkmhWDU7HInHmnlD0zQf%2BX%2BvHfI1xiwBcimz5FJJVkrNtAq%2BYWvacHi8jMEg5InyrMTuiq4zj6%2B866Y8NgRBBYPWkL%2FwH80LNyXe0j2JWqdC4NTdd0DHWhtI5m1Lc9QMa4PSYfluxJ9MCskJ7Pi8mAGksASVqT0jWY77E%2FiLNDEMrPTyz5DEcGmSfvsvdt%2Fvglc8F3hPOeNZwFscWPDaY4%2FHbirrJ0QLhMhH%2BBeL1Kf4wOOIzWlj0U%2BtDiHm%2FP5TUbUXaKOE%2Bqh%2FtCyHz1YaZPusD3pAdHUYl0It1SiMW47c69GI3BQZHfPQCaRS4MYNS4CEGy%2BZqkP63y8ZFv8J3%2Bc2yD7U6SRZvWF5%2BzHMtTayln3QNMSe37W1cMIIiVYeN69FX8EXaOP1Te%2BcVEFtgtZa355ndwEz9YuIZIto5lq7g28N88NSl4GYuV3i%2Fi3T0UmHx%2BSHZjODhvLJ7HY2hZH4EaIks4qflbsdLRfAuOppOy3rxvkWaJs298nmdukw7ZWVLcdVr9GAtzH4aiiiYfT6XNENquP4qA4q2MeQXSxbEZo1s00gpo%2Ft7hM6a0UJMJ7y9zmKB1m%2FWfXBcAiFenNqJZw%2F5ijJZMw06%2BSzwY6pgF86GIPqqs4VfK%2FrmkdZYXVnxFD9rTmL%2FAMtDE8JaetWSxHBK6B1NEHzNxS77J7ztXEa5vlBh0S4IDzfmtSdtLXpB%2B8uJhOSqkc53aISpCK045%2Bn5QW%2BAPumg32C9L2q2kEe9qVGZ%2FB9u%2BHcu5tV1sUyg5kZkIZW3WKkDZN3MSlys9JzT7CMvJribwJR7M4nIMf%2Fl0qUipfx94re4w5%2Btps9e3kK3o9&X-Amz-Signature=e8f8c31cc6f05be1405c5951161526dabdc4b8f39efe0a98acac47ae17255e61&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) ## **Part 2: The First Principles of Visual Ideation ** If the chatbox is the wrong answer what does the right one look like? To get there we have to stop thinking about "talking to an agent" and start thinking about how creative thinking actually works. before software, before ai, before screens, before any of this. So if the chatbox fails - what replaces(d) it? The answer isnt found in better software or agents. Its found by stepping back further than that. Before the interface debate, before AI, before screens entirely and asking a simpler question: *how does creative thinking actually work?* ### **The Architecture of the Human Moodboard** Long before digital design tools existed creative professionals used physical space to think. They pinned images on the wall with polaroid photographs into massive corkboards. ![A oldschool in(finite) cana](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/d7437879-1a0c-4a1f-8430-c6b13a43aa72/1_ia4Z2bQWOTD_Ri14eXlrIg.webp?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4662CPTWCCK%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095703Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIDyi6ova11bl83yhDG%2BrqbbNy3Fs%2BuObthwckLx4p9PmAiBILFNw84%2B9gPdtwiecYz9KeNbjYxYtOkmBH5DMCm9YLir%2FAwgCEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMLG0TwBY%2FLgCYW0vjKtwDEKfbxgwCpqw3XQRTP9VlvVRmOkkmhWDU7HInHmnlD0zQf%2BX%2BvHfI1xiwBcimz5FJJVkrNtAq%2BYWvacHi8jMEg5InyrMTuiq4zj6%2B866Y8NgRBBYPWkL%2FwH80LNyXe0j2JWqdC4NTdd0DHWhtI5m1Lc9QMa4PSYfluxJ9MCskJ7Pi8mAGksASVqT0jWY77E%2FiLNDEMrPTyz5DEcGmSfvsvdt%2Fvglc8F3hPOeNZwFscWPDaY4%2FHbirrJ0QLhMhH%2BBeL1Kf4wOOIzWlj0U%2BtDiHm%2FP5TUbUXaKOE%2Bqh%2FtCyHz1YaZPusD3pAdHUYl0It1SiMW47c69GI3BQZHfPQCaRS4MYNS4CEGy%2BZqkP63y8ZFv8J3%2Bc2yD7U6SRZvWF5%2BzHMtTayln3QNMSe37W1cMIIiVYeN69FX8EXaOP1Te%2BcVEFtgtZa355ndwEz9YuIZIto5lq7g28N88NSl4GYuV3i%2Fi3T0UmHx%2BSHZjODhvLJ7HY2hZH4EaIks4qflbsdLRfAuOppOy3rxvkWaJs298nmdukw7ZWVLcdVr9GAtzH4aiiiYfT6XNENquP4qA4q2MeQXSxbEZo1s00gpo%2Ft7hM6a0UJMJ7y9zmKB1m%2FWfXBcAiFenNqJZw%2F5ijJZMw06%2BSzwY6pgF86GIPqqs4VfK%2FrmkdZYXVnxFD9rTmL%2FAMtDE8JaetWSxHBK6B1NEHzNxS77J7ztXEa5vlBh0S4IDzfmtSdtLXpB%2B8uJhOSqkc53aISpCK045%2Bn5QW%2BAPumg32C9L2q2kEe9qVGZ%2FB9u%2BHcu5tV1sUyg5kZkIZW3WKkDZN3MSlys9JzT7CMvJribwJR7M4nIMf%2Fl0qUipfx94re4w5%2Btps9e3kK3o9&X-Amz-Signature=35d55617c760fd44892f0d72828d5651abc26966e6489ea78cae8827bb879e1c&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) This is a cognitive necessity based on the theory of the **Extended Mind**. The human brain struggles to hold multiple complex visual images in its shortterm memory simultaneously. By placing items in physical space we offload that cognitive burden onto our environment. We use spatial juxtaposition and placing a harsh brutalist font directly next to a soft organic photo to instantly gauge harmony or tension. ### **Jobs to Be Done (JTBD) in Creative Collaboration** When we apply the "Jobs to Be Done" framework to enterprise design the inadequacy of the chat interface becomes even more clearer When a Marketing Director sits down to work, their JTBD is almost never "I want to generate a single, isolated 1024x1024 PNG of a dog riding a skateboard." Their JTBD is: "I need to orchestrate a marketing campaign with 40 different Flux Images. I need a primary hero image for the website, three vertical video variations for TikTok, a 3D product mockup for our investor deck, and a consistent color palette that ties them all together." A chatbox cannot deliver this. It delivers isolated assets and not a visual world. ### The “Flow” in Workflow As I already said: When I use the Playground or our API im stuck in a one-at-a-time mode: Input prompt, wait for result, and if I want to try something different, start a whole new process. Its typical of many AI design tools and it breaks my focus. Almost exactly one year ago something changed. Weavy and Flora were launched. Two Infinite Canvas UI - both have grown incredibly fast. Weavy has since been acquired by Figma. Flora recently closed its Series B round with \$45 million in new funding. With these infinite canvas I can run several ideas at once and see them develop side by side. This matches how I actually think when designing or protoyping - considering multiple options simultaneously rather than one after another. ![*A demo of Flora*](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/2eb9a63b-f8d6-4a17-98cd-58f751eb2b3c/optimized_Screenshot_2025-03-14_at_10.45.04_AM.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4662CPTWCCK%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095703Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCIDyi6ova11bl83yhDG%2BrqbbNy3Fs%2BuObthwckLx4p9PmAiBILFNw84%2B9gPdtwiecYz9KeNbjYxYtOkmBH5DMCm9YLir%2FAwgCEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIMLG0TwBY%2FLgCYW0vjKtwDEKfbxgwCpqw3XQRTP9VlvVRmOkkmhWDU7HInHmnlD0zQf%2BX%2BvHfI1xiwBcimz5FJJVkrNtAq%2BYWvacHi8jMEg5InyrMTuiq4zj6%2B866Y8NgRBBYPWkL%2FwH80LNyXe0j2JWqdC4NTdd0DHWhtI5m1Lc9QMa4PSYfluxJ9MCskJ7Pi8mAGksASVqT0jWY77E%2FiLNDEMrPTyz5DEcGmSfvsvdt%2Fvglc8F3hPOeNZwFscWPDaY4%2FHbirrJ0QLhMhH%2BBeL1Kf4wOOIzWlj0U%2BtDiHm%2FP5TUbUXaKOE%2Bqh%2FtCyHz1YaZPusD3pAdHUYl0It1SiMW47c69GI3BQZHfPQCaRS4MYNS4CEGy%2BZqkP63y8ZFv8J3%2Bc2yD7U6SRZvWF5%2BzHMtTayln3QNMSe37W1cMIIiVYeN69FX8EXaOP1Te%2BcVEFtgtZa355ndwEz9YuIZIto5lq7g28N88NSl4GYuV3i%2Fi3T0UmHx%2BSHZjODhvLJ7HY2hZH4EaIks4qflbsdLRfAuOppOy3rxvkWaJs298nmdukw7ZWVLcdVr9GAtzH4aiiiYfT6XNENquP4qA4q2MeQXSxbEZo1s00gpo%2Ft7hM6a0UJMJ7y9zmKB1m%2FWfXBcAiFenNqJZw%2F5ijJZMw06%2BSzwY6pgF86GIPqqs4VfK%2FrmkdZYXVnxFD9rTmL%2FAMtDE8JaetWSxHBK6B1NEHzNxS77J7ztXEa5vlBh0S4IDzfmtSdtLXpB%2B8uJhOSqkc53aISpCK045%2Bn5QW%2BAPumg32C9L2q2kEe9qVGZ%2FB9u%2BHcu5tV1sUyg5kZkIZW3WKkDZN3MSlys9JzT7CMvJribwJR7M4nIMf%2Fl0qUipfx94re4w5%2Btps9e3kK3o9&X-Amz-Signature=91cf9bd2038fb1a8be92fb559df0255251e652cb986de7e17241cacc537fbf46&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) The sauce is in how closely the Flora team worked with actual creative professionals to understand their workflow. They collaborated with New York Universitys Tisch School of the Arts, designfirm Pentagram, and other major creative institutions and agencies across the US. They are building it for real creative workflows because they are embedded in those communities. You can feel that closeness to the end user when you are using the product. It just makes sense. The lesson im taking away: In the world of AI powered tools, understanding your users deeply is (slowly) becoming more important than the underlaying models. Its not just about the Models anymore. 2cbc3702-22d5-8048-8eab-e0d261022b2a.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2cbc370222d580488eabe0d261022b2a as of 2025-12-22T16:59:42.279Z:

</properties>
<content>
**Location: **Freiburg/San Francisco 
**Team: **GTM team with strong partnership/dotted line to engineering
<empty-block/>
As our first **GTM Engineer**, you'll be the technical architect behind our revenue engine. This isn't a traditional RevOps or engineering role—it's both. You'll build the billing systems, data pipelines, and automation workflows that power our complex business model: usage-based API pricing, enterprise licensing, and self-serve Playground/Studio flows.
You'll work cross functionally to transform manual processes into scalable systems, turning messy data into actionable insights, and building the infrastructure that lets us grow 10x without breaking. If you love solving hard technical problems that directly impact revenue, thrive in ambiguity, and want to shape the GTM infrastructure at one of most exciting company at the cutting edge of the visual space
**This role is ideal for:** A technical builder who's energized by the intersection of code and commerce—someone who can debug a data pipeline in the morning and design a quote-to-cash workflow in the afternoon, all while understanding how it drives business outcomes.
<empty-block/>
## Key Responsibilities
### Billing & Revenue Infrastructure (30%)
- Design and implement scalable billing systems to support our complex pricing models (API usage-based, Enterprise licenses, Playground/studio self-serve through to sales led motion)
- Build automated workflows for invoice generation, usage tracking, and revenue recognition across our dual US/German structure
- Create integrations between billing systems, CRM, payment processors, and financial systems
- Develop dashboards and reporting tools for Finance team to track consumption, ARR, churn, and revenue metrics
- Ensure accurate data flow from API endpoints through to invoicing and revenue reporting
### Enterprise GTM Systems (30%)
- Build and maintain GTM tech stack integrations (CRM, contract/subscription management, CPQ, billing, data warehouse)
- Design automated workflows for enterprise sales processes: quote-to-cash, contract approvals, procurement
- Create tools for contract analysis, pricing optimization, and customer segmentation
- Implement data quality controls and governance frameworks to ensure CRM data integrity
- Build internal tools to support Revenue Operations (territory management, lead routing, quota tracking)
- Automate support process for self-serve customers for BFL services around Playground and API
### Analytics & Business Intelligence (20%)
- Design and maintain data pipelines that consolidate data from APIs, CRM, billing, and product analytics
- Create executive dashboards for board presentations and strategic planning
- Build self-service reporting tools for GTM, Business Operations, and Finance teams
- Implement customer health scoring, usage analytics, and expansion opportunity detection
- Support financial modeling and forecasting with clean, reliable data infrastructure
### Process Automation & Optimization (20%)
- Identify manual, repetitive workflows and build automated solutions
- Partner with RevOps and Finance to streamline procure-to-pay and order-to-cash processes
- Create documentation and training materials for internal systems and tools
- Continuously optimize system performance, data accuracy, and integration reliability
---
## Required Qualifications
### Technical Skills
- **3-5+ years** as a Software Engineer, Systems Engineer, or RevOps Engineer at a B2B AI or SaaS company
- **Programming proficiency:** Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, SQL 
- **CRM expertise:** Experience / familiarity with cloud based CRMs such as Attio, Salesforce, Hubspot
- **Integration platforms:** Hands-on experience with Workato, Zapier, Tray.io, or similar iPaaS tools
- **API development:** RESTful APIs, webhooks, OAuth, authentication protocols
- **Data pipelines:** Experience building ETL/ELT workflows, data transformation, and warehouse integration
- **Billing systems:** Familiarity with Stripe Billing, Metronome, Lago, Chargebee, or similar usage-based billing platforms
### Business & Domain Knowledge
- Experience with usage-based pricing, consumption billing, and complex contract structures
- Understanding of multi-jurisdictional business operations (US/EU structures a plus)
- Familiarity with build vs buy decisions and ability to help choose the best path at the right time
### Soft Skills
- **Cross-functional collaboration:** Ability to work effectively with Finance, Sales, Marketing, and Engineering
- **Business acumen:** Translate business requirements into technical solutions that drive revenue
- **Problem-solving:** Debug complex data flows and system integration issues independently
- **Communication:** Explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders
- **Attention to detail:** Ensure data accuracy and integrity across all revenue systems
- **Ownership mentality:** Take initiative to identify problems and implement solutions proactively
---
## Preferred Experience
- Experience at a high-growth startup scaling from \$1M to \$100M+ ARR
- Familiarity with API-first or usage based products
- Experience with data visualization tools (Tableau, Looker, Metabase)
- Knowledge of sales tax, VAT compliance, and multi-currency billing
- Prior experience in dual US/EU entity structures
---
## What You'll Build (Example Projects)
### Year 1 Priorities
1. **Automated Billing System:** Build end-to-end automation from API usage tracking → invoice generation → payment processing → revenue recognition
2. **Customer Segmentation Framework:** Create data models and dashboards to segment enterprise customers by industry, use case, contract size, and growth potential
3. **Finance Reporting Infrastructure:** Design automated monthly/quarterly reports for revenue, bookings, collections, and key metrics
4. **Contract Management System:** Build workflows for enterprise contract creation, approval, amendments, and renewals
5. **Data Warehouse Integration:** Create unified data pipeline connecting product analytics, CRM, billing, and finance systems
---
## Success Metrics
**Within 3 Months:**
- Audit current GTM systems and identify top 5 automation opportunities
- Build first integration between billing system and CRM
- Create quote to cash end-to-end framework and look at build vs buy opportunities
- Document current revenue data architecture and pain points
**Within 6 Months:**
- Reduce manual billing tasks by 70% through automation
- Implement automated usage-based invoice generation
- Create self-service analytics dashboards for Finance, Business Operations and GTM team
- Review and design subscription management process  
**Within 12 Months:**
- Enable real-time revenue visibility across the organization for all revenue types
- Support 10x growth in customer base without linear increase in ops headcount
- Reduce billing errors to \<1% through automated quality controls
- Build predictive models for churn and expansion opportunities
- Further automated and integrated customer support with the broader GTM motions
---
##
</content>
</page>

fe9db704-44c7-4503-9151-b879bb1db603.title: Global Expense & Travel Policy
fe9db704-44c7-4503-9151-b879bb1db603.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/fe9db70444c745039151b879bb1db603 as of 2026-04-15T10:03:34.036Z: {"title":"Global Expense & Travel Policy"} ### Welcome to BFL's expense policy We've designed these guidelines to make your work-related spending easy and hassle-free. General rule is: **Act in BFL’s best interests.** **Your Ramp card will be your primary method for handling business expenses and travel, reimbursements where needed and will be issued during your onboarding process.**
Remember, the key is to book early (min. 14 days in advance where possible) and spend wisely to avoid unnecessarily high costs and stretching to upper limit or beyond. If you need an exception, just chat with Sarah before booking. Flights and hotels tend to be more expensive on Ramp platform, please use your Ramp card on alternative booking sites. **Ramp = Primary payment method for all business expenses** - Software subscriptions and licenses - Office supplies and equipment (out of your \$2.5k allowance when you start) - Conference tickets and professional development - Business meetings and team events - Data roaming charges for business travel - Travel expenses - Accommodation - Meals while traveling (conferences, customer meetings, Freiburg trips) - Local transportation (taxis, ride-shares) during work trips - Any other business-related purchases **What the card should not be used for ** - Non-business streaming services or subscriptions like Home Wifi or Netflix, Spotify - Wifi at home - Personal purchases of any kind - Cash withdrawals or cash advances - Gift cards or prepaid cards - Political contributions - Splitting purchases to circumvent spending limits - Entertainment venues (clubs, bars) without clear business purpose - Cryptocurrency or gambling - Fuel for personal vehicles (use mileage reimbursement instead) - Family member travel or meals **All expenses \>\$75 require a receipt and memo. Ramp fetches receipts from your email.** *Note: Ramp doesn’t allow country or city specific policies.* **Hotels** {color="green_bg"} **Europe 🇪🇺& UK 🇬🇧** - Germany 🇩🇪 generally half the price of US rates - Major Business hubs (Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt) up to 250€ per night. - Secondary cities (such as Freiburg) up to €200 per night - **For Freiburg specifically, reasonable rooms for 125-150€ per night if you book on time, ****some suggestions**** below:** - Black F Tower or Black F House (use the code “CORP” during the booking process for a discount) - Aparthotel Adagio - The Cloud Suite Apartments - Hampton by Hilton Freiburg - Apartments for longer stays: - *Black F apartments & Black F House* - *Wohnen auf Zeit - Innenstadt-Appartements* - *Freiburg Apartments Friedrichring* - *Friedrich Boutique-Apartments* ***Your accommodation budget during onboarding is €2,000.*** ***For offsites, we encourage extending your stay by one week (before or after) and join us in Freiburg. Accommodation budget: €1,200. *** **Major 🇪🇺hubs:** - London, Paris and Amsterdam, the upper limit is €350/£300 per night **USA 🇺🇸** - Major Business hubs (NYC, SF/Palo Alto, LA, Miami) upper limit is \$350 per night - SF recommendations [here](/384da917594344d2bd0af44efd47e01f?pvs=25#e819cf489c6544eba5c8718abac75169)
BFL Corporate Pricing Options: - [**Luma Hotel **](https://be.synxis.com/?adult=1&arrive=2026-04-07&chain=19010&child=0¤cy=USD&depart=2026-04-08&hotel=35419&level=hotel&locale=en-US&productcurrency=USD&promo=FORESTB&rooms=1)15% off Best Available Rate. (10 min. walk from office) Contact: Jacques Rachal call/email if there is no availability and he will work to get you taken care of. [jacques.rachal@lumahotelsf.com](mailto:jacques.rachal@lumahotelsf.com) Direct 415-757-1437 - **Hotel Via** (Note this is directly across from the professional baseball park, so check the SF Giant’s schedule before booking here) - Use code: BFLABS when searching room availability to get the rates - Contact Brandi Rivera: [brandie@hotelviasf.com](mailto:brandie@hotelviasf.com) Direct: 415- 200-4979 - Negotiated rates: - **RATE: January 1, 2026 – March 31, 2026, April 1, 2026 – November 16, 2026** - South Beach King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$269.00 per night plus tax - Park View King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$289.00 per night plus tax - **RATE: April 1, 2026 – November 16, 2026** - South Beach King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$315.00 per night plus tax - Park View King/Queen/Two Queen Beds: \$389.00 per night plus tax - **Hyatt **- SF recommendations in the Welcome to SF [Notion page](https://www.notion.so/Welcome-to-San-Francisco-384da917594344d2bd0af44efd47e01f?source=copy_link#e819cf489c6544eba5c8718abac75169), but this link is good for any Hyatt properties not just SF - You need to link your BFL email to your Hyatt profile or create a new one - This is the link to use to get our corporate pricing: - [Black Forest Labs - Be More Here with Hyatt Leverage](https://www.hyatt.com/loyalty/en-US?corp_id=238828) - **Marriott **- SF recommendations in the Welcome to SF [Notion page](https://www.notion.so/Welcome-to-San-Francisco-384da917594344d2bd0af44efd47e01f?source=copy_link#e819cf489c6544eba5c8718abac75169), but this link is good for any Marriott properties not just SF - You will be getting an invite via your BFL email address to [Business access by Marriott Bonvoy](https://businessaccess.marriott.com/hotels)
- For secondary cities the upper limit for reimbursement is \$300 per night. *Need an exception? Just ask – we understand last minute travel for customers and conferences can get pricey.* **Travel** {color="green_bg"} - Plane ✈️ - Economy for short flights; Price guideline within Europe: \< \$350 return - Economy Premium for \> 4h trips - Long-haul flights should be booked as early as possible, ask for approval \> \$2,500 - Please always book return flights as they are significantly cheaper than individual flights - Car 🚗 - For group trips only. - Train 🚆: First choice for intra-Germany and Europe travel: book via Deutsche Bahn for travel within Germany. - First-class tickets for \>2 hour trips **Food & third party entertainment** {color="green_bg"} - Business related dinners & drinks with third parties or occasionally within the team should not exceed \> €/\$50 per head, otherwise ask for approval before. While this guideline aims to promote cost consciousness, we recognize that reasonable exceptions may arise based on business context, location, and circumstances. Use professional judgment and ensure expenses align with business objectives. - All attendees & purpose of the expense should be mentioned when submitting the receipt. **Workplace equipment** {color="green_bg"} - Your current laptop & mobile phone allowance stands at €2.5k (\$2.7k) including office equipment related expenses if you’re working out of SF or Freiburg office and is \$4k (€3.5k) if you’re remote. **Reimbursements** {color="green_bg"} All out of pocket expenses will be reimbursed via Ramp, linked to your bank account (which needs to be added in the system). Open the App, click + and select “new reimbursement” and upload the receipt to initiate the process. Happy smart spending!

# per-modality-modulation helps significantly tldr; comparisons in single block variants show that per-modality-modulation is quite important originally wanted to explore if there is any [degradation similar to what was observed for flux2.5](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C0A07D22HE1/1766358895.775129/1766358895.775129) resulting from separate q, k, v initialization. In the end that was not explicitly tested for, but having separate modulations for the different modalities outpaces all other architecture effects it seems. ## Variants Model Classes

Details in 1. QKV Projection - Separate (singleseq, modblock): Three separate linear layers, computed independently ```plain text q = self.q_proj(x) k = self.k_proj(x) v = self.v_proj(x) ``` - Fused (origblock, midblock): Single linear layer, then split ```plain text qkv, mlp = self.linear1(x).split([3*H, mlp_dim], dim=-1) q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3) ``` 1. Output Projection - SEPARATE (singleseq, modblock): Separate projections summed ```plain text output = self.attn_out(attn) + self.mlp_out(self.mlp_act(mlp)) ``` - FUSED (origblock, midblock): Concatenate then project ```plain text output = self.linear2(torch.cat([attn, self.mlp_act(mlp)], dim=-1)) ``` 1. Modulation - Per-modality (singleseq): Separate Modulation modules for each content modality + txt ```plain text self.single_stream_modulations = ModuleDict({ 'image': Modulation(...), 'video': Modulation(...), 'audio': Modulation(...), 'txt': Modulation(...), }) ``` - Shared (origblock, midblock, modblock): Single Modulation applied to concatenated sequence ```plain text self.single_stream_modulation = Modulation(...) # one shared ``` ## Results

# per-modality-modulation helps significantly tldr; comparisons in single block variants show that per-modality-modulation is quite important originally wanted to explore if there is any [degradation similar to what was observed for flux2.5](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C0A07D22HE1/1766358895.775129/1766358895.775129) resulting from separate q, k, v initialization. In the end that was not explicitly tested for, but having separate modulations for the different modalities outpaces all other architecture effects it seems. ## Variants Model Classes

Details in 1. QKV Projection - Separate (singleseq, modblock): Three separate linear layers, computed independently ```plain text q = self.q_proj(x) k = self.k_proj(x) v = self.v_proj(x) ``` - Fused (origblock, midblock): Single linear layer, then split ```plain text qkv, mlp = self.linear1(x).split([3*H, mlp_dim], dim=-1) q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3) ``` 1. Output Projection - SEPARATE (singleseq, modblock): Separate projections summed ```plain text output = self.attn_out(attn) + self.mlp_out(self.mlp_act(mlp)) ``` - FUSED (origblock, midblock): Concatenate then project ```plain text output = self.linear2(torch.cat([attn, self.mlp_act(mlp)], dim=-1)) ``` 1. Modulation - Per-modality (singleseq): Separate Modulation modules for each content modality + txt ```plain text self.single_stream_modulations = ModuleDict({ 'image': Modulation(...), 'video': Modulation(...), 'audio': Modulation(...), 'txt': Modulation(...), }) ``` - Shared (origblock, midblock, modblock): Single Modulation applied to concatenated sequence ```plain text self.single_stream_modulation = Modulation(...) # one shared ``` ## Results

The main advantage of singleseq seems to come from per-modality modulation, since modblock (which has separate projections + SwiGLU but shared modulation) performs similar to origblock/midblock. Also seems reasonable given that the separate vs fused choices should be equivalent up to initialization scales. 29bc3702-22d5-80c3-bd0f-ddf80d1aaeb9.title: FDE - Hiring process
29bc3702-22d5-80c3-bd0f-ddf80d1aaeb9.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/29bc370222d580c3bd0fddf80d1aaeb9 as of 2026-03-23T14:00:40.920Z: {"title":"FDE - Hiring process"} # Process Overview
**Round** **Facilitators** **Duration** **Notes / Resources**
Screening Recruiter 30 min
Experience & Behavioral 45 min
Sales Collab
(Senior Only)		 Sales / Partnership 45 min Senior candidates should go through an additional round with sales/partnership to confirm confidence with owning customer relationships & collaboration with sales
Technical Case & Problem Solving 45 min scenario based exercise, debugging an issue a customer may face
FDE Interviewing - Technical Cases
Onsite Freiburg / SF including culture fit with founder Full Day
# Round Details ## Interview #1: Pre-Screening **Culture based questions:
**Adaptability around high pressure situations.
Environment that you thrive in. **Technical knowledge:
**High level overview of their knowledge of deploying and finetuning GenAi Models.
Solving customer technical problems with examples. ## Interview #2: Peer Interview - Experience & Behavioral This round asks the candidate to present a recent technical project they're proud of, in significant detail. The goal is to assess technical depth, ownership, decision-making quality, and genuine engagement with their work.
**Opening prompt to candidate:** *"Tell me about your favourite recent technical project you worked on and are proud of. Walk me through the problem you were solving, the architecture of your solution, and the key decisions you made along the way. Go as deep as you can — we love details."*
Allow the candidate to present for \~5-10 minutes before steering with questions. Take notes on claims you want to probe later. Your aim as interviewer should be to: - Understand the problem and solution they are presenting in as much detail as possible (be curious!) - Test the candidates understanding for the technologies and design decisions involved in the solution they are presenting - Be the devils advocate and ask the most critical and “dumb” questions about the project the candidate is presenting Assess for the following: - How much did this person actually do versus observe or coordinate? - Can they explain implementation details, not just architecture diagrams? - Do they say "I" vs. "we" appropriately — taking credit where earned but acknowledging collaborators honestly? - Can they describe dead ends they personally hit and how they worked through them? - Do they know the gnarly edge cases and why certain parts were harder than expected? - Do they light up when describing the problem or the elegant parts of the solution? - Do they show curiosity about their own work — things they'd still like to explore or improve?

**Red flags:** Only able to describe the system at a high level. Can't answer "what was the hardest part for you personally?" with specifics. Attributes all key decisions to others when pressed.**
** Directions of questions you could ask: - Why did you take design decision x? - What tradeoffs did you have to make in y? - What would you do different when taking this decision next time? - How did you measure success of z? ## Interview #3: BFL Technical Scenario Goal: probe their problem-solving capabilities and domain expertise + working with clients Prismo Aspect Ratio Challenge FDE Interviewing - Technical Cases ## Onsite ### Onsite Technical Challenge Challenge repo: [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/mle-onsite](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/mle-onsite) **Requirements for challenge discussion:** *Good candidates should…* - … explain sampling pipeline fixes - … explain finetuning config changes (specifically in connected to the customer requirements described) - High res - Learning rate - … explain fine tuning data handling - did they add new synthetic data (e.g. for additional car colors)? - how did they label the data? - … be able to discuss REST API hosting challenges - what might be different challenges at larger scale & in prod? - … reason over agent architecture choice - Which tools are available to the agent & why? - Which agentic patterns ([e.g. loop, vs, sequential)](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents) & why? - … formulate a solid product vision for a conversational interface for image gen & edit ### Sales / Partnership Interview (during onsite) Your aim as interviewer should be to: - Understand the candidate's natural instinct for navigating customer relationships — even if they haven't formally done it before - Probe whether they can think commercially: understanding deal dynamics, stakeholder mapping, and what makes a customer successful (not just technically unblocked) - Test their ability to translate technical work into business value and communicate it to non-technical stakeholders - Gauge how quickly they could be trusted to represent BFL in a customer-facing context without heavy supervision Questions to ask: - "Walk me through a time you had to convince someone — a colleague, a manager, a user — to adopt a technical approach or tool you believed in. How did you frame the value?" - "A customer you own has gone quiet after a successful POC — they haven't expanded usage or responded to your last two messages. What do you do?" - "You're on a call with a customer who asks for a feature we don't have and won't build in the near term. How do you handle that conversation without losing the deal?" Assess for the following: - Can they think in terms of outcomes for the customer, not just tasks they completed? Do they naturally frame things around value and impact? - Do they show comfort with ambiguity and incomplete information — or do they freeze without a clear technical spec? - Can they read a room? Do they demonstrate awareness of different stakeholder motivations (technical buyer vs. economic buyer vs. end user)? - Do they show a bias toward action and ownership — "I would do X" rather than "I would escalate to someone"? - Are they coachable? When pushed back on an answer, do they adapt their thinking or get defensive? - Do they demonstrate genuine curiosity about the business side — or does commercial thinking feel foreign and uncomfortable? **Red flags:** Frames every answer purely in technical terms with no awareness of the business context. Can't articulate why a customer would care. Defaults to "I'd ask my manager" for any customer-facing scenario. Shows no curiosity about deal dynamics or partnership strategy. # Resources **Black Forest Labs🌲— Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) & Solutions Engineer Interview Preparation Guide**

- Which agentic patterns ([e.g. loop, vs, sequential)](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents) & why? - … formulate a solid product vision for a conversational interface for image gen & edit ### Sales / Partnership Interview (during onsite) Your aim as interviewer should be to: - Understand the candidate's natural instinct for navigating customer relationships — even if they haven't formally done it before - Probe whether they can think commercially: understanding deal dynamics, stakeholder mapping, and what makes a customer successful (not just technically unblocked) - Test their ability to translate technical work into business value and communicate it to non-technical stakeholders - Gauge how quickly they could be trusted to represent BFL in a customer-facing context without heavy supervision Questions to ask: - "Walk me through a time you had to convince someone — a colleague, a manager, a user — to adopt a technical approach or tool you believed in. How did you frame the value?" - "A customer you own has gone quiet after a successful POC — they haven't expanded usage or responded to your last two messages. What do you do?" - "You're on a call with a customer who asks for a feature we don't have and won't build in the near term. How do you handle that conversation without losing the deal?" Assess for the following: - Can they think in terms of outcomes for the customer, not just tasks they completed? Do they naturally frame things around value and impact? - Do they show comfort with ambiguity and incomplete information — or do they freeze without a clear technical spec? - Can they read a room? Do they demonstrate awareness of different stakeholder motivations (technical buyer vs. economic buyer vs. end user)? - Do they show a bias toward action and ownership — "I would do X" rather than "I would escalate to someone"? - Are they coachable? When pushed back on an answer, do they adapt their thinking or get defensive? - Do they demonstrate genuine curiosity about the business side — or does commercial thinking feel foreign and uncomfortable? **Red flags:** Frames every answer purely in technical terms with no awareness of the business context. Can't articulate why a customer would care. Defaults to "I'd ask my manager" for any customer-facing scenario. Shows no curiosity about deal dynamics or partnership strategy. # Resources **Black Forest Labs🌲— Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) & Solutions Engineer Interview Preparation Guide**

304c3702-22d5-81dd-bcb3-e095402bbfa0.title: Decision Framework
304c3702-22d5-81dd-bcb3-e095402bbfa0.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/304c370222d581ddbcb3e095402bbfa0 as of 2026-04-01T07:45:40.207Z: {"title":"Decision Framework"} A lightweight framework to help us move fast on decisions. Four questions, one owner, no unnecessary process. Consider the likely outcomes, their probabilities, and 2nd order effects. > **Core principle**: Speed is the default. Only add process when the stakes demand it. --- # Decision Matrix For decisions that are aligned with [mission & values:](/99f95b254b6c4351b17a2798684d10c3?pvs=25)
🔄 Reversible 🚪 Irreversible
**🟢 Small** ⚡ **Just do it** — No approval needed. Decide and move. ✅ **Gut-check** — Ping 1 person. If no objection in 24h, proceed.
**🟡 Medium** 📢 **Decide & inform** — Make the call, document reasoning, share with affected parties. 🤝 **Consult then decide** — Get 1–2 perspectives. Decision owner still decides.
**🔴 Large** 🤝 **Consult then decide** — Leadership discussion. Document rationale. One person owns it. 🎯 **Full leadership alignment** — Written proposal → Leadership review → Explicit sign-off.
> **Note:** If Question 4 flagged dependencies, add 1–3 days for coordination before the timeframes below kick in. # How It Works Ask four questions in order. The combination tells you how to proceed. ## Question 1: How big is this decision? Consider financial impact, number of people affected, and strategic importance. ### 🟢 Small - Incremental spend under \$3K (annualised equiv) - Tooling or vendor choice (non-critical) - Process tweaks within your team - Day-to-day prioritization calls ### 🟡 Medium - Incremental spend \$3K–\$25K (annualised equiv) - New feature prioritization (Eng or even research) - Cross-team process changes - Partner, vendor or integration decisions ### 🔴 Large - Incremental spend over \$25K (annualised equiv) - Strategic direction or positioning - Leadership or exec-level hires - Pricing model changes - Legal, compliance, or equity decisions - Anything materially affecting BFL's reputation, runway, or fundraising **If you're unsure about size, treat it as one level up.** --- ## Question 2: Is it easily reversible? Inspired by Bezos' Type 1 / Type 2 door framework. **🔄 Reversible (Type 2 — Two-way door)** Can be unwound or changed within weeks with minimal cost or disruption. *Examples: trying a new tool, launching a beta feature behind a flag, adjusting pricing on a trial basis* **🚪 Irreversible (Type 1 — One-way door)** Difficult or impossible to undo. Creates lasting commitments or precedents. *Examples: signing a multi-year contract, public pricing changes, equity grants, hiring, shutting down a product* --- ## Question 3: Does it align with our [mission & values](/99f95b254b6c4351b17a2798684d10c3?pvs=25)? This is a hard gate. Misalignment stops everything regardless of size. - **✅ Yes** → Proceed to Question 4 - **🤷 Unclear** → Pause. Post in the relevant slack channel with context. Get clarity within 24 hours. - **❌ No** → Stop. Raise with founders if you passionately think this is an exception (note, expect this to be a no). --- ## Question 4: Can you execute this yourself? Even aligned, well-sized decisions may depend on shared resources, budgets, or other teams. This question determines whether you can move independently or need to coordinate. ### 🙋 Self-contained You have the skills and expertise, explicit ownership, authority (*legally*), and access to execute without pulling in other teams or competing for shared resources. *Examples: choosing a simple SaaS tool, restructuring your own team's workflow, writing a customer proposal/agreeing basic terms* ### 🤝 Needs coordination Execution requires another team's time, a shared resource (e.g. talent acquisition, engineering capacity, legal review), or draws from a shared budget that may have competing priorities. *Examples: hiring (needs TA bandwidth + headcount sequencing), launching a feature (needs engineering prioritization), signing a new vendor contract (potentially needs legal/procurement - need to think when this is needed vs online sign-up)* **→ Before committing to the decision, validate ability to execute:** - **Identify the dependency.** Who or what do you need? Be specific: a person, a team, a budget line, a slot in a roadmap. - **Check capacity, not just permission.** The question isn't "are we allowed to" — it's "can we actually do this given current priorities?" - **Propose, don't assume.** Bring a lightweight ask to the resource owner: what you need, by when, and what it displaces. Let them flag conflicts. - **If capacity isn't available**, you have three options: (1) defer and sequence it, (2) reduce scope so it becomes self-contained, or (3) escalate the priority trade-off to leadership. **The decision matrix still applies** — but your timeframe extends to account for the coordination step. Add 2–5 days for dependency validation before the clock starts on execution. --- --- # Timeframes
Decision Type Self-contained Needs Coordination
⚡ Just do it Immediate +2 days for dependency check
✅ Gut-check 24 hours +2–3 days
📢 Decide & inform 1–2 days +3–5 days
🤝 Consult then decide 2–5 days +3–5 days
🎯 Full leadership alignment 1–2 weeks +1 week
--- # Inherent principles of the above 1. **Speed is the default.** Only add process when stakes demand it. 2. **Every decision has one owner.** Consulted ≠ consensus. 3. **Reversible decisions should be made in hours, not days.** 4. **Document the "why", not just the "what".** 5. **If you're unsure about size, treat it as one level up.** 6. **A fast "no" beats a slow "yes" to the wrong thing.** 7. **Check capacity, not just permission.** "Can we?" matters as much as "should we?". 8. **If you can't execute alone, bring a specific ask** — not an open-ended request. 9. **Own and learn from mistakes.** Mistakes happen. Focus on fixing, learning, and growing from those mistakes and making you and BFL even better.
Idea: Decision doc structure for large decisions ## Context - **What’s true today:** - **Why it matters now:** - **What we ultimately care about:** - *\[Activation / engagement / retention / revenue / reliability, etc.\]* - *\[1–2 concrete examples of outcomes\]* ## Decision we need to make - **Describe the decision we need to make** ## Variables that matter Examples: - ***Confidence level:*** - *\[Prior experience, references, deliverability, reliability, etc.\]* - ***Operational / self-serve requirements:**** * - *\[Who needs to run this? What level of support is required?\]* - ***Cost + ability to start small then scale:**** * - *\[Budget sensitivity, pricing model, contract terms\]* - ***Scale / migration risk:**** * - *\[If we choose a smaller tool, what’s the switching cost later?\]* - *(Optional) ****Integration requirements:**** * - *\[Data pipeline, Segment, warehouse, API needs, etc.\]* ## Options - **Option 1:** - **Option 2:** - **Option 3: ** ## Expected outcomes What scenarios you expect to happen and their likely probabilities ## Decision - **Chosen option and why** \[Option X\]

### Overview
**One-line description:** We’re making our models friendly to use (don’t need to be an prompt expert to get photorealistic results), while still being powerful (with new features like web/image search and transparent backgrounds).
A major upgrade to FLUX 2 Pro, Flex, and Max with improved prompt upsampling, auto aspect ratio inference, visual grounding, and transparent backgrounds — making our FLUX 2 models higher quality, easier to prompt, and more intelligent.
**Launch date:** April 28th, 2026 or May 2nd, 2026
**People involved:** Maxim, Scott, Alex, Owais, Stefan, Robin, Nihanth
## What problem we’re solving?
<callout icon="/icons/star_red.svg" color="red_bg">
	**Developers building on our models struggle to build useful product experiences that creators actually retain on.** 
	- Getting images that look photo-realistic and not AI slop requires expert prompting and alot of manual steps.
		*Amazon Alexa flagged a "baked" look that isn't professional-grade, VSCO reported color shifts ruining their filters, and Canva saw quality degrade over iterative edits. *
	- Images aren’t configurable or usable in a real workflow because models don’t remove backgrounds or give you the exact aspect ratio you need to post on social, edit in Figma etc.
		*Amazon Ads and Alexa both found that basic prompts produce unusable output, and Alexa asked how to generate clean transparent-background stickers for overlaying on photos. *
	- Model can’t search the web for real world references to create with (current events, specific locations, products)
</callout>
## Who are we building for
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**P0: **Developers with end users that aren’t prompt experts, but still need high fidelity outputs and more control (eg Krea, Freepik, Lovart, Figma, Adobe).
</callout>
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**P1: **Professional creatives that don’t use tools like ComfyUI, but can use tools like Figma, Weavy, and Krea. They need ease-of-use and the ability to create usable outputs for e-commerce, brand design, and advertising use cases. 
</callout>
## Messaging
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	### **High quality images with simple prompts. **
	FLUX 2.1 gives you photorealistic images by default, even if you use simple prompts.
	Users can also now control the generation to get the exact image they need: 
	- Remove backgrounds: create logos, graphic designs, character photos without a background. Add to an existing design file in Adobe, Figma, etc without needing to make manual edits.
	- Web and image search: refer to logos/characters/places directly in your prompt and the model will search the web for images of that thing to use as a reference image during generation. 
	- Get images in the exact aspect ratio you need (just specify “16:9” or “Instagram”)
</callout>
## What we're launching
We’re releasing upgraded 2.1 versions of **Pro, Flex, and Max**. Here’s what’s shipping:
**Web search and image search for recent things** (aka Visual Grounding): you don’t need to manually upload reference images of publicly known things anymore. Just refer to logos/characters/places directly in your prompt and the model will search the web for images of that thing to use them as a reference images during generation.

	## Why ship FLUX 2.1?
	Image generation is at an inflection point where it's slowly moving from "cool toy" to "default way to create" for professional workflows. But that transition only happens when the output is good enough that people stop going back to manual methods like photoshoots, design agencies, and hand editing. Today, our biggest customers still do things manually:
	- Amazon runs millions of ad creatives across languages and can't afford a prompting expert for each one
	- Canva and Snap need to serve non-technical end users who will abandon the feature if results look fake
	- E-commerce companies need product images that are accurate enough to actually sell things. 
	Every time the model garbles a product, shifts a color, or requires five prompt rewrites to get something usable, it pushes users back to the old way of doing things. 2.1 closes that gap by making the model smarter to handle the basics on its own so image generation is not just an experiment people try and give up on.
	#### **New prompt upsampling (PUP)**
	#### Higher realism
	Reduced bake and more photorealistic outputs across the board. Example: T2I reduced bake using the same prompt.

	#### Aspect ratio inference from the prompt
	Greatly improving quality of life and arena scores. It will be possible to prompt specific aspect ratio, i.e. “16:9” or “landscape”. If those are not present, the model will guess based on the prompt content i.e. it will guess 9:16 for a prompt “instagram screenshot”
	#### Visual grounding (aka Web Search)
	Model will identify named people/logos/characters/places in the prompt and will look online for the images of those to use them as a reference images during generation, i.e. for prompt “Robin Rombach holds the flag of Black Forest Labs”, model will find images of Robin and BFL’s logo and generate an image:
	<empty-block/>
	#### **Transparent background.**
	Background removal capability, allowing users to generate images with transparent backgrounds via a `background` parameter (`auto | transparent | opaque`).

	Parameters aligned with Google and OpenAI standards for easier integration.

### Overview
**One-line description:** We’re making our models friendly to use (don’t need to be an prompt expert to get photorealistic results), while still being powerful (with new features like web/image search and transparent backgrounds).
A major upgrade to FLUX 2 Pro, Flex, and Max with improved prompt upsampling, auto aspect ratio inference, visual grounding, and transparent backgrounds — making our FLUX 2 models higher quality, easier to prompt, and more intelligent.
**Launch date:** April 28th, 2026 or May 2nd, 2026
**People involved:** Maxim, Scott, Alex, Owais, Stefan, Robin, Nihanth
## What problem we’re solving?
<callout icon="/icons/star_red.svg" color="red_bg">
	**Developers building on our models struggle to build useful product experiences that creators actually retain on.** 
	- Getting images that look photo-realistic and not AI slop requires expert prompting and alot of manual steps.
		*Amazon Alexa flagged a "baked" look that isn't professional-grade, VSCO reported color shifts ruining their filters, and Canva saw quality degrade over iterative edits. *
	- Images aren’t configurable or usable in a real workflow because models don’t remove backgrounds or give you the exact aspect ratio you need to post on social, edit in Figma etc.
		*Amazon Ads and Alexa both found that basic prompts produce unusable output, and Alexa asked how to generate clean transparent-background stickers for overlaying on photos. *
	- Model can’t search the web for real world references to create with (current events, specific locations, products)
</callout>
## Who are we building for
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**P0: **Developers with end users that aren’t prompt experts, but still need high fidelity outputs and more control (eg Krea, Freepik, Lovart, Figma, Adobe).
</callout>
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**P1: **Professional creatives that don’t use tools like ComfyUI, but can use tools like Figma, Weavy, and Krea. They need ease-of-use and the ability to create usable outputs for e-commerce, brand design, and advertising use cases. 
</callout>
## Messaging
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	### **High quality images with simple prompts. **
	FLUX 2.1 gives you photorealistic images by default, even if you use simple prompts.
	Users can also now control the generation to get the exact image they need: 
	- Remove backgrounds: create logos, graphic designs, character photos without a background. Add to an existing design file in Adobe, Figma, etc without needing to make manual edits.
	- Web and image search: refer to logos/characters/places directly in your prompt and the model will search the web for images of that thing to use as a reference image during generation. 
	- Get images in the exact aspect ratio you need (just specify “16:9” or “Instagram”)
</callout>
## What we're launching
We’re releasing upgraded 2.1 versions of **Pro, Flex, and Max**. Here’s what’s shipping:
**Web search and image search for recent things** (aka Visual Grounding): you don’t need to manually upload reference images of publicly known things anymore. Just refer to logos/characters/places directly in your prompt and the model will search the web for images of that thing to use them as a reference images during generation.

				### Why Launch FLUX 2.1
				- Image generation is moving from "cool toy" to "default way to create" for professional workflows
				- Current customers like Amazon, Canva, Snap, and e-commerce companies still rely on manual methods because outputs aren't reliable enough
				- Every time the model produces unusable results, users revert to traditional methods
				- 2.1 makes the model smarter and less reliant on expert prompting to close the quality gap
				### Core Problems Being Solved
				- **Requires expert prompting**: Basic prompts produce unusable output; 2.1 adds better prompt upsampling, auto aspect ratio, grounding, and background removal
				- **AI-generated look**: Outputs have a "baked" appearance; new PUP produces more natural, photorealistic results
				- **Inaccurate representations**: Model mixes up product colors, proportions, and details; visual grounding searches the web so the model actually "sees" what it's generating
				### What's Shipping in 2.1
				- Upgraded versions of Pro, Flex, and Max simultaneously (models stay the same, logic changes)
				- New prompt upsampling for more realistic images and better character reference/text editing
				- Automatic aspect ratio inference from prompt content
				- Visual grounding that searches the web for reference images of named people, logos, characters, and places
				- Transparent background removal capability
				- API parameter alignment with Google and OpenAI standards
				### Technical and Legal Discussions
				- **Visual grounding risks**: Can directly copy watermarked images from web search and recreate people/IP with high accuracy; risk elevated because users may not understand images come from web, not model
				- **Moderation approach**: Output moderation still in place but input-side blocklist may need enhancement; LLMs can help with IP filtering in the prompt upsampling layer
				- **NSFW testing**: Still needed to identify edge cases in image search
				- **Communication strategy**: May need to manage risk through marketing/comms and FAQs explaining how visual grounding works
				### Evaluations and Testing
				- Amazon load tests scheduled for April 2-3
				- LM Arena whitelist ready; can submit immediately for weekend results
				- Playground Arena available but has UI issue to resolve
				- Endpoint improvements include GPT 5.4 swap (faster, same quality) and prompt tweaks to avoid copying reference images
				### Open Questions Discussed
				- **API parameters**: Whether to expose quality parameter (like GPT image) and grounding default on/off
				- **Image search API**: Currently using Serper API on ramp card (not production-ready); need to evaluate Google API for cost and reliability
				- **Pricing model**: Flat fee vs additional charges for grounding; need to decide across Pro/Flex/Max and implement pricing functions
				- **Demo experience**: Critical dependency for launch success; exploring chat UI for natural iteration and discovery (Prompt Party model)
				### Launch Timeline and Dependencies
				- Original target: April 14, 2026

	## Why ship FLUX 2.1?
	Image generation is at an inflection point where it's slowly moving from "cool toy" to "default way to create" for professional workflows. But that transition only happens when the output is good enough that people stop going back to manual methods like photoshoots, design agencies, and hand editing. Today, our biggest customers still do things manually:
	- Amazon runs millions of ad creatives across languages and can't afford a prompting expert for each one
	- Canva and Snap need to serve non-technical end users who will abandon the feature if results look fake
	- E-commerce companies need product images that are accurate enough to actually sell things. 
	Every time the model garbles a product, shifts a color, or requires five prompt rewrites to get something usable, it pushes users back to the old way of doing things. 2.1 closes that gap by making the model smarter to handle the basics on its own so image generation is not just an experiment people try and give up on.
	#### **New prompt upsampling (PUP)**
	#### Higher realism
	Reduced bake and more photorealistic outputs across the board. Example: T2I reduced bake using the same prompt.
	<columns>
		<column>
			<empty-block/>
			<empty-block/>
		</column>
		<column>
			<empty-block/>
		</column>
	</columns>
	#### Aspect ratio inference from the prompt
	Greatly improving quality of life and arena scores. It will be possible to prompt specific aspect ratio, i.e. “16:9” or “landscape”. If those are not present, the model will guess based on the prompt content i.e. it will guess 9:16 for a prompt “instagram screenshot”
	#### Visual grounding (aka Web Search)
	Model will identify named people/logos/characters/places in the prompt and will look online for the images of those to use them as a reference images during generation, i.e. for prompt “Robin Rombach holds the flag of Black Forest Labs”, model will find images of Robin and BFL’s logo and generate an image:
	<empty-block/>
	#### **Transparent background.**
	Background removal capability, allowing users to generate images with transparent backgrounds via a `background` parameter (`auto | transparent | opaque`).
	#### **API parameter alignment.** 
	Parameters aligned with Google and OpenAI standards for easier integration.
