<content>
<callout icon="🎯" color="green_bg">
	Everyone at BFL needs rapid, intuitive access to answers from all knowledge sources. 
</callout>
# Workflow Requirements
## Sales Requirements
<mention-user url="user://161d872b-594c-8178-82c9-000280a302d4"/> 
<empty-block/>
## Partnership Requirements
<mention-user url="user://161d872b-594c-8126-b71c-0002e426aee3"/> 
<empty-block/>
## Goal state & Hypothesis:
- One single interface to …
	- find all technical documentation
	- access all project & account work progress
- That will allow… 
	- rapid onboarding 
	- minimum effort & eng involvement to respond to tech questions
	- quick, async project & account work status checks (e.g.)
	- agentic workflow automation (e.g. create a blog post about our work with xyz)
- Ideally without building a new frontend, building on tools the team already uses
## Questions that our research interface should be able to answer
*Please add more! Doesn’t have to be structured, anything that comes to mind.*
- What is the status of customer abc?
- Customer xyz send me technical question abc, what should I respond?
- Create a blog post about our work with abc
- What are the next steps with customer abc
- What is the status of projec abc with customer xyz 
- What feedback did customer xyz give on Kontext 
- How can I solve technical issue xyx
- How do I raise quotas for my customer
- What is our default contract clause on abc 
# Prototype & Usage Examples
There is no point in overloading our team with additional custom front ends. Thus POCs all build on Claude Desktop as entry point because most folks are using it already.
- Claude Projects allows setting custom system prompts and sharing them with the whole team
- Connectors still need to be enabled individually in everyones environment
Two Prototypes realized as custom Claude projects:
- GTM Assistant (specifically for asking account related stuff): [Claude](https://claude.ai/project/0199863e-bcfa-701d-991a-860730d35f52)
- Notion Q&A (general Q&A such as tech questions from customers): [Claude](https://claude.ai/project/01994777-93fa-700b-ba99-565d0e2b04a7)

<content>
<callout icon="🎯" color="green_bg">
	Everyone at BFL needs rapid, intuitive access to answers from all knowledge sources. 
</callout>
# Workflow Requirements
## Sales Requirements
<mention-user url="user://161d872b-594c-8178-82c9-000280a302d4"/> 
<empty-block/>
## Partnership Requirements
<mention-user url="user://161d872b-594c-8126-b71c-0002e426aee3"/> 
<empty-block/>
## Goal state & Hypothesis:
- One single interface to …
	- find all technical documentation
	- access all project & account work progress
- That will allow… 
	- rapid onboarding 
	- minimum effort & eng involvement to respond to tech questions
	- quick, async project & account work status checks (e.g.)
	- agentic workflow automation (e.g. create a blog post about our work with xyz)
- Ideally without building a new frontend, building on tools the team already uses
## Questions that our research interface should be able to answer
*Please add more! Doesn’t have to be structured, anything that comes to mind.*
- What is the status of customer abc?
- Customer xyz send me technical question abc, what should I respond?
- Create a blog post about our work with abc
- What are the next steps with customer abc
- What is the status of projec abc with customer xyz 
- What feedback did customer xyz give on Kontext 
- How can I solve technical issue xyx
- How do I raise quotas for my customer
- What is our default contract clause on abc 
# Prototype & Usage Examples
There is no point in overloading our team with additional custom front ends. Thus POCs all build on Claude Desktop as entry point because most folks are using it already.
- Claude Projects allows setting custom system prompts and sharing them with the whole team
- Connectors still need to be enabled individually in everyones environment
Two Prototypes realized as custom Claude projects:
- GTM Assistant (specifically for asking account related stuff): [Claude](https://claude.ai/project/0199863e-bcfa-701d-991a-860730d35f52)
- Notion Q&A (general Q&A such as tech questions from customers): [Claude](https://claude.ai/project/01994777-93fa-700b-ba99-565d0e2b04a7)

303c3702-22d5-809f-bcb1-c09a1cdf7247.title: GTM interview prep package
303c3702-22d5-809f-bcb1-c09a1cdf7247.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/303c370222d5809fbcb1c09a1cdf7247 as of 2026-04-15T03:46:09.457Z: {"title":"GTM interview prep package"} ## Welcome Thanks for your interest in Black Forest Labs! We're a team of world-class researchers and engineers creating the generative models that power how people make images and video — tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started. Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity. This document gives you a quick overview of what to expect during our interview process so you can put your best foot forward. --- ## About the Role Our models are already seeing strong inbound demand, and we're expanding our commercial team to accelerate adoption across enterprise and strategic partners. As a **Senior Account Executive**, you'll translate deep technical interest into durable, long-term partnerships — especially across complex, non-standard engagements involving APIs, on-prem deployments, and custom licensing. You own the end-to-end commercial journey, working closely with research, engineering, and leadership to help customers move confidently from evaluation to production. We're looking for people who combine strong sales execution with genuine technical curiosity and sound commercial judgment. --- ## Interview Process Our process has five stages. We aim to move quickly and respect your time. **Stage 1 – Recruiter Screen (30 min)**
An introductory call focused on background, motivation for the role, and baseline technical understanding. **Stage 2 – First Team Interview (45 min)**
A deeper conversation with a member of the sales team covering your experience, technical fluency, and how you approach complex sales situations. We’ll ask behavioral questions grounded in real examples from your past work. **Stage 3 – Second Team Interview (30 min)**
A follow-up discussion with the sales team focused on different aspects of your experience, decision-making, and judgment in ambiguous or high-stakes scenarios. **Stage 4 – Culture Interview**
A conversation focused on vision, culture, long-term fit, and alignment on how we build and sell at Black Forest Labs. **Stage 5 – Onsite & Case Study**
You'll visit one of our offices and work through a practical case study. More details will be shared ahead of this stage. --- ## How to Prepare **Understand our product and space** Familiarize yourself with FLUX, how it compares within the generative image/video landscape, and the basics of diffusion models at a high level. You don’t need to be an ML engineer, but you should be comfortable speaking with technical buyers and decision-makers. **Prepare concrete examples** We use behavioral interviewing. Be ready to walk through real situations where you closed complex, multi-stakeholder deals, navigated long sales cycles, grew strategic accounts, built or improved commercial processes, or learned new technical concepts to drive outcomes. Structure your answers clearly: context, actions, results, and lessons learned. **Think commercially** We care about numbers. Be prepared to discuss deal sizes, timelines, revenue impact, and tradeoffs. Quantifying your work matters. **Show startup judgment** We’re scaling quickly and don’t have perfect structure everywhere. We value people who identify gaps, take ownership, and move things forward thoughtfully. If you’ve done that before, bring those examples. --- ## Logistics All roles are currently based out of our offices in **Freiburg, Germany** or **San Francisco, USA**. Please flag any location questions early in the process. --- ## Questions? Don't hesitate to reach out to your recruiter contact at any point. We're happy to help. **We're excited to get to know you — good luck!**

311c3702-22d5-81fa-b2cb-cc446435cdad.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/311c370222d581fab2cbcc446435cdad as of 2026-04-14T15:57:53.742Z: {"title":"GTM Team Meeting Notes"} **👤 Owner:** @Anthony Charbonnier - - Opens - Product update - - Deal updates - Hiring update --- # **April 7, 2026** {toggle="true"} *(Summary)* **👥 Present:** Anthony Charbonnier · Jakob Pörschmann · Stephan Lachmann · Alexander Thebelt · Owais Khan · Gigi Henze · Stephen Batifol · Aitana Giebels van Bekestein · Morgan ## 🏆 Team Recognition Alex: product photography breakthrough + Snap deal leadership. API team: 99%+ success rate on Amazon load test after an intensive week — benefits all customers. Isabella: strong AE candidate pipeline. Amanda: open weight license work flagged as critical for Q2. Sarah Cyro (product): unblocked LoRa functionality. ## 🧪 LoRa / Object Removal Demo LoRa trained on FLUX client 9B for Samsung + Runway use cases. Input: image + binary mask → seamless background replacement. 56% win rate vs Runway in human evals (200 images, 50 evaluators) — competitive with NanaBanana 2, faster and cheaper. Prompt inpainting also built for Wix partnership. All endpoints documented in Notion and ready. > **Gap:** Needs website integration for customer visibility and lead generation — Slack follow-up assigned. ## 🤝 Reseller Strategy Runway pushing daily for object removal endpoint access. Current handshake agreements lack structure and pricing discipline. Decision meeting tonight (Anthony, Amanda, Matt) to formalize the framework. > **Decision:** Deliver the endpoint but build proper commercial terms around it. Transparent communication with Runway while protecting BFL interests. ## 🛒 Amazon Load test: passed ✅. API performance significantly improved. Contract stuck on Amazon's side — service order sent 2 weeks ago, no redlines back. Aggressive SLA requirements received Friday (non-standard — won't become BFL standard). Training component still under negotiation. **Tomorrow's launch not happening** due to Amazon delays. SLA learnings will inform future enterprise deals. ## 📣 Marketing & Hiring Aitana joined as BFL's first dedicated marketing hire — seeking customer use case stories for website. Hugo Boss and Dutch Telecom already identified as candidates. New AE expected to sign within days. Owais newsletter content flagged as strong — should expand frequency + audience segmentation. ## Next Steps - [ ] LoRa website integration — Slack follow-up - [ ] Reseller strategy decision tonight (Anthony, Amanda, Matt) - [ ] Zalando legal call tomorrow 4 PM — Gigi joining for technical topics - [ ] Amazon: respond to SLA requirements + escalate training component - [ ] Customer story development with Aitana (Hugo Boss, Dutch Telecom) --- # **March 31, 2026** {toggle="true"} *(Summary)* *(Q1 closed — missed targets but strong foundation building for Q2. Major deals in motion across Amazon, Disney, Adobe, and Snap.)* ## 🏆 Team Recognition Gigi for exceptional Zalando demo and customer engagement. Stephan for enabling GTM to move faster on infra and teaching rather than just solving. Amanda for nailing the first GTM demo day presentation to Samsung. Sam for the Disney mega-proposal built in 2–3 days. Matt, Jakob, Ian, Alex for relentless work on Amazon. LD team for raw output volume and quality of customer feedback generated. ## 📊 Q1 Revenue & Pipeline ARR declined MoM: \~\$46M (Jan) → \~\$38M (Mar). Net new ARR: \$164K actual vs \$3M target — only 2 new logos (Runway, Forks). ByteDance collapsed \$6M → \$450K. License revenue flat since Aug 2025 — Chinese OS model competition increasing. > **Q2 churn incoming:** PhotoRoom (\$50K/mo) + Lightricks (\$80K/mo) turning off Flux 1 dev licenses. > **Root causes:** Team too small to cover existing accounts + inbound significantly lower post-Flux 1 era + Q1 deals (Amazon) slipped out of team's control. ## 🔥 Major Deal Updates **Amazon Alexa** — Beta ongoing; GA blocked by load test failures (timeout \>20s vs 20s threshold). SOF #5 pending legal review; sticking point: training on BFL data. Custom product photography endpoint delivering tomorrow. New opportunity: Amazon Kids (early conversations). Target: load test run Friday. **Disney** — Engagement across all BUs. 3-tier proposal sent: Tier 1 current dev models \~\$8M ACV; Tier 2 all dev models over 3yr \$18M→\$35M; Tier 3 Pro models on-prem (OpenAI-level partnership) — primary target. Robin met Disney head of BD in LA as first touchpoint. **Snap** — Actively reinventing pricing model with auto-encoders during live negotiations. **Adobe** — IP/legal complexity flagged: Adobe suggesting Flux derivatives via Foundry may not need "powered by Flux" branding — technically inaccurate. Mohan + Amanda working on a one-pager tying technical, legal, and commercial frameworks together. ## 👗 Virtual Try-On (Gigi) End-to-end LoRA solution built for Zalando: sub-1s, strong character + garment consistency. No competitor exists at this spec over API. Zalando: 5–20M daily page viewers — massive volume opportunity. Building public BFL shop demo for broader rollout. Next: explore public launch with a fashion brand partner (e.g. Freepik). ## 🏗️ Account Tiering Framework (Sam) New framework to protect SE time and maximize impact. P0 (e.g. Meta): 9-figure TCV, dedicated owners + founder sponsor. P1 (Adobe, Amazon, Snap): \$1M+ ARR / 8-figure TCV, dedicated SE + research POC. P2–P3: mid-range ARR, Slack channel + launch-time intensity. P4 long tail: reactivation only, no dedicated SE. SE engagement decisions based on use case impact × deal size. Note: SE co-creation can create IP/ownership complications — loop in Mohan or Amanda if in doubt. ## 🔓 Open Weights Initiative (Amanda) Launch delayed April 1 → \~April 6. New SKU structure: **Builder** (10K image limit, Klein models only, restricted use cases — automated flow replacing self-serve) + **Enterprise** (\$10K+/mo minimum, full model flexibility, SLA). Website updates, migration comms, and Builder flow all in progress. ## 🚀 FLUX 2.1 Launch Anticipated \~2 weeks from March 31. Improvements: better human rendering, less baking, easier prompting, better low-light, auto-resolution. Pricing still being worked out. GPT-4o image release adding urgency to evals. > **Request from Amanda:** Updated ELO scores + before/after examples needed for sales materials at launch. ## Next Steps - [ ] Amazon: Run load test Friday; resolve SOF #5 legal redlines; deliver product photography endpoint - [ ] Disney: Continue BU engagement; progress partnership proposal - [ ] Snap: Finalize pricing model and close - [ ] Virtual Try-On: Build public BFL shop demo; identify fashion brand for public launch; loop in Owais on marketing - [ ] Open Weights: Complete website updates, Builder SKU automation, migration comms by \~April 6 - [ ] FLUX 2.1: Resolve backend + pricing; prepare updated ELOs and sales materials - [ ] GTM: Begin Q2 vertical strategy — Media & Entertainment as first motion; outbound push into e-commerce/retail - [ ] Account framework: Publish tiering doc; align new AE hires on SE engagement rules # **March 24, 2026** {toggle="true"} ## 👋 New Team Member **Huachun j**oined as forward deployed ML engineer in SF ! ## 🏆 Team Recognition Ian: Amazon partnership setup and infra support. Gigi: major progress on try-on. Freddie: volunteered research support for Snap technical requirements. Isabella: hiring process improvements already visible. lex + Stephan: strong collaboration on Adobe Brand Brain — third Adobe project underway, new open source protocol for B2B marketing use case, endpoint delivered for POC testing. ## 🛠️ Infrastructure Update (Ian) GPU availability challenges: review deploys compete with prod — check utilization dashboard and use Kubernetes tools to monitor without waiting for full rollout. Simplified worker deployment system in development (template-based, automated logging, cleaner folder structure). DB querying limitations due to rapid growth — BigQuery too expensive, seeking alternatives. API architecture: Azure API cluster + separate worker clusters; long-term target is unified clusters to cut latency. ## 🤝 Amazon Alexa Load test delayed by 1 day (infra issues). Beta launch this week, GA 1 week after. Order form finalizing: 30% minimum commitment of max TPS, quarterly commits with 30-day notice for increases — risk-sharing model to protect against volume uncertainty. Technical: 20s timeout issue resolved (graceful error handling). Latency optimization ongoing, 2 PRs in progress. > **Key learning:** Educate customers on technical specs upfront. Product teams often lack deep knowledge — proactive guidance prevents model evaluation mistakes. ## 📊 Revenue & Pipeline March: \~\$500K shortfall expected. Gamma trending negative (capacity blocking testing). Client still not live. Upsides: ByteDance usage spike, TikTok US meeting Thursday; Samsung subsidiary (Shell) new lead identified. Adobe + resellers still on legacy endpoints — need marketing push + deprecation timeline clarity. > **Proposed:** Office hours for tier 1 strategic accounts to drive endpoint migration and prevent churn. ## ⚙️ Ops & Account Ownership Amber (RevOps) starts mid-April. [Excel-based account ownership audit in progress](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-nolfQ5Sr0P9wsEURJOCGFXZrz8TsQ76/edit?gid=1219653003#gid=1219653003) — moving from deal-level to account-level ownership. Sales team to review and claim accounts. Clean handoff planned for Amber. ## Next Steps - [ ] Finalize Amazon order form (minimum commitment structure) - [ ] Complete account ownership audit before Amber's start (mid-April) - [ ] Drive legacy endpoint migration — marketing push + deprecation timeline - [ ] Resolve fal / Klein 9B commercial use questions (OF requirement, LoRA rights, strategic stance) --- # **March 17, 2026** {toggle="true"} *(Summary)* ## 🏆 Team Recognition Alex delivered a strong Adobe demo in his 3rd week — challenging use cases, solid execution. Gigi's Zalando meeting went exceptionally well, partnership continuing with a case study in progress. We have real customers, real revenue, and real momentum, and we're looking for the right person who will take that foundation and build something exceptional on top of it. This is not a role for someone who wants to apply a standard SaaS sales playbook. Recognising that standard SaaS tooling and methodology will need to be adapted or replaced, and that the forecasting process itself needs to evolve continuously as the business scales and the revenue mix shifts - Create visibility into consumption trends at the account level that allows the team to act proactively — identifying accounts building toward significant scale, accounts showing signs of reduced engagement, and the leading indicators that distinguish the two - Partner closely with Finance to ensure revenue recognition and forecasting align across the business, and that the commercial team's view of pipeline translates into reliable financial planning inputs *ICP Definition & Segmentation* - Work with research, product and marketing leadership to define and continually refine our ideal customer profile — the market for foundational image models is evolving fast, and new use cases, buyer profiles, and competitive dynamics emerge regularly - Build segment-specific approaches that reflect actual buying behavior across agrentic, developer, mid-market, and enterprise customers - Help the team stay oriented around the right customers as the landscape shifts *Enterprise & Strategic Customer Engagement* - Lead executive-level relationships with our largest and most strategic customers, acting as a genuine partner to their technology and product leadership - Understand customer roadmaps deeply enough to surface where FLUX creates compounding value — not as a point vendor but as long-term infrastructure partner - Manage the complexity of accounts where consumption can shift rapidly based on model releases or changes in the customer's own product direction *Partnerships* - Define and evolve a partnership strategy that spans the full ecosystem: resellers and distributors, inference providers, creative platforms, and other strategic integrations - Recognise that each partnership type requires a different commercial and operational model. Does where they come from differ - eg selling large Oracle or Azure deployments given years of PMF vs someone who has needed to do something at a scrappy start-up* - *Where do they sit in overall US management? Are we looking for someone to be de facto country manager? * - *How do they sit in the broader company management framework? Do they influence or own marketing? How do we feel about the interaction with product - if there are inherent disagreements in direction on product vs sales-led GTM (eg focus on PLG vs SLG) how do we resolve and how do they sit hierarchically with Morgan?* - *How much do they have autonomy to reverse previous decisions? They're measured on ARR. Marketing is a peer function they collaborate with and influence but don't control. This is a VP Sales or CRO profile. - A full GTM leader owns revenue *and* marketing, brand, demand gen, developer relations, content, the lot… They're measured on both pipeline and market presence. This is closer to a CCO or President of GTM profile, and it's a materially harder search. Given we have no Marketing leader to navigate around, no existing structure to protect, and no political complexity in the handoff. The incoming person gets a clean slate to design how commercial and marketing functions relate to each other from the start

30bc3702-22d5-80c6-887a-fc9eec5bec26.title: How marketing is prioritizing
30bc3702-22d5-80c6-887a-fc9eec5bec26.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/30bc370222d580c6887afc9eec5bec26 as of 2026-03-04T11:40:28.293Z: {"title":"How marketing is prioritizing"} **Our focus for H1 2026 is to build quality awareness to increase model usage.** Win the position as the leader of building frontier models that are SOTA for quality and uniquely good for creative control at speed. We should be perceived as the “premium” brand that augments the human creator and honors the craft of making things — from movies and graphic design, to simulated worlds for robotics and games. We are anti-slop and anti-human replacement. We’ll measure this by increases in impressions, website visits, and models usage (via API or licensing) from current baselines. ---
Criterion Questions to ask Score (1–3)
**Goal alignment** Does it build awareness with frontier devs or pro creatives? Does the partner/channel have wide distribution or tight network effects? 1 = weak fit / 3 = strong fit
**Investment required** Can we run a lightweight test before committing? Does it match where our team has depth? 1 = high cost, unproven / 3 = low cost, testable
**Execution confidence** Do we have the experience and bandwidth to deliver a clean test? 1 = needs heavy external support / 3 = within team strengths
Any opportunity scoring 7–9 total: pursue. 4–6: deprioritize or redesign. 1–3: decline. # Prioritization framework ### Alignment with our goals Does it build awareness with frontier developers and professional creatives at scale? - Does the opportunity have wide distribution? Working with a partner like Krea has large distribution on social vs. a B2B enterprise company with very minimal reach. The difference between reaching hundreds of target users vs. thousands to millions. - Is a given community tightly networked and lead to a multiplier word-of-mouth effect that reaches thousands. eg community hosted events with 50 AI artists in SF leads to 100X reach via word-of-mouth or quality leads. - Weird cool ideas like a theater pop-up where people can stop by and watch a short AI film made by a creator in a cozy setting “BFL drive in theater”. Has potential to get shared heavily via word of mouth. --- ### Investment required Prioritize opportunities that allow us to test with lower spend instead of ones that require a large investment from day one. - We’d prioritize things like social, enterprise sales enablement, customer stories, working with a small group of influencers, supporting the community because they allow us to test raising awareness at scale quickly. - Investing \$100K in paid ads at this stage doesn’t make sense without having a destination product and a clear understanding of our customer acquisition cost + payback period --- ### Confidence level Are we confident in our ability to deliver a clean test given team’s experience and internal resourcing bandwidth. - Marketing/Growth team today has deeper experience in product/growth marketing, developer experience, brand, and supporting enterprise sales. We should lean into those strengths! Prioritize channels like social, brand campaigns, sales enablement, developer relations etc. - Channels like demand gen conferences/events, paid ads and SEO can be figured out, but would likely need the support of externals in a large way. --- ### Example scenario Nebius (one of BFL’s compute providers) has requested working on co-marketing and events with them for NVIDIA’s GTC conference. Their target audience is other research labs/researchers and their reach/distribution on social platforms is low (500 average views on YouTube). They don’t align with our goal of quality awareness with frontier developers and professional creatives at scale. So we’ll de-prioritize and turn down this opportunity. --- ### Other variables to think about - Do they fit with our brand values of SOTA models, augmenting humans, and leading with openness? Higgsfield is an anti-brand and we should avoid working with them. ### Exception cases - High-impact conferences where speaking gives us consistent credibility within the research community without paying large amounts for sponsorships or co-hosting.

</properties>
<content>
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Our focus for H1 2026 is to build quality awareness to increase model usage.**
	We’ll measure this by increases in impressions, website visits, and models usage (via API or licensing) from current baselines.
</callout>
# Three goals for marketing in H1 2026:
<callout icon="1️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Build **quality awareness** for BFL & FLUX 
	**Black Forest Labs as a frontier lab.**
	Core channels: Press, Podcasts, founder socials, Publish research, Website/Blog
	Content: Press articles, vision of “Why visual AI matters”, Research papers
	**FLUX models best for reliable creative control at speed.**
	Core channels: Socials, YouTube, influencers/community, co-marketing w/ partners
	Content: Customer stories, use cases, model launches, Website
</callout>
<callout icon="2️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Drive usage** & retention** for our models
	Drive conversions and engagement for the API:
	Core channels: Dev focused websites, docs, YouTube, socials, email, sales enablement
	Content: API docs, sales enablement/ABM, Website
</callout>
<callout icon="3️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Establish foundation of an **enterprise GTM **engine
	Core channels: Sales motion, emails to existing users, enterprise marketing
	Content: Customer Case Studies, sales enablement material on pitch, model battlecards, etc
</callout>
# Who are we building for?
<callout icon="/icons/card_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Primary: the frontier developers building AI apps**
	The "highest expectation developer" builds visual apps and tools that creatives use directly (directors, creators, enterprises, agents). They need a solid API with special customization features (like LoRA training) that helps them fine-tune their apps while keeping costs low and speed high. Their main goal is creating AI applications that users actually stick with and keep coming back to, and they work at companies like Krea, Flora, Meta, Notion, Adobe, and Figma.
	![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/f6b13b84-9793-4d69-805e-9bbcf6811979/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4664FB3OMUO%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095729Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJGMEQCICirWVw33%2BgXa4gPGPapE2x3sdxL1d%2FFc7YiaH1auNcHAiAMM5waL5ewxio5ACxJFHbDIva0GQEqqNaTLOu5Bm6FNCr%2FAwgCEAAaDDYzNzQyMzE4MzgwNSIM8tSlpLkVayZOwM9xKtwDoxpmcXoOvVog%2F4xNCgqa1YS0ZXBvwojcwb9phhfwU0WyjfA4rQqx8PCuLqj2gM39L62N8kQI3zC0JNDyNTN%2BY9Z9RHDPu5St8OS9fMx242jWOGbDqWu%2Foq9Mnty%2BC%2BM5A1KFu0ACvZ2qNQxen%2Fup%2BAUUGWjdzdHfbSpWv2ap9EVdUg4Fnh51esH5256mtArhlmXA9GCb%2B2tt%2FFf%2B%2BzcuVPJDIFkywP9hdxF%2FS0YRWUME52jmQE8vJGfo1ObMUbYufjQuZLLEVEyynZYyTPiaED%2BkoqNrO9HIHH7VIpVGuVVWW3KR2zJRZ2xqGteiegKW76hnnSlmD29J3ETILckWG3ujP%2BkiI7VAjFXO3pzwpVWsZN15pCc%2BeK27HnKR6dM2wRQBms%2FEI07%2BUYYmggoKKyGdJ4qH%2BDEMHKC0ThFZqyQ4Zfaw8LsIR93iavFyb4scjd6DIuH4oKqXrCU3losinBGUlFU9%2B8KrwJYhsIB%2B7eH9ARzgCIC9%2FZft4eszAk2xI0TM8AcvK8uYHGxc4fE8Ihy6SOQNd94h0PH5ORPBvObrCK7Q9HrEq6LU6XWM70VYW1kE7nHVKpABmET7jG7oOjHNuub2TxsUx%2BuX6FQTRrDOSXaiDFjW%2F5bUiuowq7CSzwY6pgFsHVy8rY5lFTvjt4ZXs8oaWuJLetnfhSnvAxjCrnjjJJL975OtY1PGVsP2qUQ2yD9hhS8dDS79NmZhO2uZkHEHrCaEj9abeFt1DjyfdPAjhHCBhMCPc2Kc%2FLrSYf8hSetnMAmFLm%2F1JvXKVEeSqdUgAtJavRt%2BI6Ea6yl1aY2x2WyfedpFRN1GsL8VepksWv6xTB%2FSOvxk27uN24BeGw8AbYgAmmLc&X-Amz-Signature=aa0907bdba8f3f57abfb4d1618e2601f3bb314c4bcfd1899030735cb7a81a979&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject)
</callout>
<callout icon="/icons/card_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Secondary: the advanced creative (developer+)**
	Should consistently choose FLUX models because they offer the best combination of creative control, speed, and quality. They fall into a few key groups: marketing teams (like those at BMW and Notion) creating brand ads and graphics, product designers using AI for prototyping ideas, and AI creators making visuals and videos for consumers (working at places like Disney or AI studios). They typically use professional tools like Adobe, Krea, or Flora at work. Advanced users work with tools like Comfy UI to fine-tune BFL models.
</callout>
**Who we’re not targeting right now: **Non-technical mass market (e.g. users of Canva, Lovable)
# What problems do they face?
<callout icon="/icons/star_red.svg" color="red_bg">
	**For the developer, it’s hard to build creative tools with AI features that users actually retain on.**
	Developers are still figuring out how to build creative AI tools with lasting user engagement. While tools like Gamma, Adobe Firefly, and Krea see high initial use, they're mostly used for one-off tasks like quick presentations or edits. The goal is to be essential for creating final, production-ready work with fast iteration.
</callout>
<callout icon="/icons/star_red.svg" color="red_bg">
	**For the creator, no model or tool has yet given them the quality, control, and speed they need to ship production ready content.**
	“It takes a lot of work to get it right if they’re being used for sequences where there needs to be a lot of consistency/control. It was over a month of work getting a video ad with Lewis Hamilton just right” — Perplexity Creative Director
</callout>
# How does BFL solve these problems?
<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	### **FLUX models are built for creative control. **
	FLUX models deliver consistent, high-fidelity output with reliable creative control. From character consistency across sequences to accurate text rendering and precise camera angles. You can edit and steer results in real-time, and iterate fast without losing quality. Plus, with open weights and LoRA training, you can own your entire pipeline and customize for your use case.
</callout>

# Three Core Narratives (WIP)
### Why does visual intelligence matter and the path to super intelligence. 
Visual intelligence is harder than language: language is an interface, while vision models reality itself: the geometry of objects, how they relate to each other, what happens when they interact, what stays the same over time and what changes. True intelligence requires understanding the physical world. When models learn to simulate reality (eg predicting what happens when objects collide, how shadows move, how scenes unfold) they develop the foundation for actual reasoning. 
Visual intelligence unlocks everything from content creation to generative UIs that render as fast as you think, to simulations that train robots and agents, to systems that can reason by running mental experiments about the physical world. 
Whoever builds the standard for visual intelligence defines the next platform, because it's the path from generation to reasoning to superintelligence. Black Forest is focused on* *building* the standard for visual intelligence. *The standard means high performance and quality, lean, open, fast, affordable, always available. Ridiculously easy to build on and get great results effortlessly.
**Core channels: **Podcasts, Press Coverage, Founder Writing/Blog, Awareness Campaigns

### Black Forest Labs has an insanely good developer experience
Anthropic and Vercel level developer experience that’s loved because it’s optimized for builders creating AI creative apps. BFL API uniquely good for customization, training LoRAs, latency/speed, cost, BFL Skills, Docs, FDEs for custom deployments.
**Core channels:** Developer Experience, Docs, support for agents like Claude Code, Hackathons, Prompt Guides, etc. 
# Core launches in H1 2026
- Major improvements and faster variants of core FLUX.2 image model (eg 4K generation, fast editing)
- API features (out-of-the box customization, latency improvements)
- Martin Scorsese commercial/campaign
- FLUX.3 (Video, Audio, and Image) launch. BFL becomes fully multimodal
## Hiring plan & Sarah thoughts  {toggle="true"}
	<empty-block/>
	We dont have a “destination product” and no PLG motion…
	## 1. No growth loops, everything is a funnel
	Every initiative is linear: spend money/effort → get impressions → hope people convert. **where is the compounding?** Where is the mechanism where a user of FLUX generates the next user of FLUX? Some concrete gaps:
	- **No viral/referral loop.** When a developer builds with FLUX, there's no systematic way that creates more FLUX developers. Think "Powered by FLUX" attribution in outputs, API response headers that credit the model, referral credits for API usage.
	- **No user-generated content loop.** The community is creating incredible FLUX content already, where's the infrastructure to capture that, amplify it, and turn it into acquisition? This should be a self-reinforcing engine, not just "social media 2x a week."
	- **No content loop from product usage.** Every image generated by FLUX is a potential marketing asset. Where's the gallery, the showcase, the share-to-social from playground?
	## 2. Pricing is unowned at bfl 
	for a company at \$100M ARR with usage based revenue, pricing and packaging is probably the single highest leverage growth initiative we could run
	- experimenting with reverse trials; Let developers hit the API with generous free credits, then convert based on experienced value rather than a paywall.
	- What's our expansion revenue playbook? How do you systematically move a developer from \$50/mo to \$500/mo to \$5K/mo? That's not in any initiative.
	- Where's usage-based pricing optimization? Even small changes to per-request pricing tiers can meaningfully shift revenue without any new user acquisition.
	## 3. Activation is under-defined
	We can "Optimize customer activation flow with customer.io" and some email lifecycle campaigns, but there's no clearly defined aha moment. what is the *specific action* that, once a developer takes it, predicts they'll retain at 30 days? Is it first successful API call? First LoRA trained? First production deployment? First 1,000 requests?
	Without that defined, our activation emails are guesswork. we are sending lifecycle campaigns without knowing what lifecycle milestone actually matters.
	## 4. Massive ToF bias
	Looking at our metrics table: 37M impressions, 550K website visitors, media coverage targets. 10K unique users retaining 30 days. We set the stats as reference point to test how hard they are to achieve. We are investing heavily in pouring water in the top while barely measuring or investing in the bucket itself. what we should be doing: 
	- Cohort retention analysis before spending on awareness. What do our 30/60/90 day retention curves actually look like by segment?
	- Activation rate optimization. What % of signups make their first API call? What % make 10 calls? This should be an initiative with a DRI, not a side project on customer.io.
	- Resurrection campaigns. we have \~8K unique users but presumably thousands of churned or dormant accounts. Reactivating existing users is 5-10x cheaper than acquiring new ones.
	## 5. No experimentation framework or growth engineering
	There's no initiative around building a culture of rapid experimentation. 
	- A growth engineering function yet to be build 
	- Weekly experiment velocity targets: how many tests are we running on onboarding, activation, conversion, retention?
	- A clear learning loop: hypothesis → test → measure → iterate
	The Scorsese campaign is a big, slow bet. important but we should pair that with 10-20 smaller, faster experiments running simultaneously.
	## 6. Developer experience as a growth channel, not support
	We talk about Anthropic/Vercel level developer experience as a theme. But the initiatives DB doesn't back it up with real investment. We don’t have initiatives around:
	- **Time-to-first-API-call optimisation: **what's the current time and how do you cut it in half?
	- **SDK quality and docs** as a top-of-funnel magnet 
	- **Template/starter projects** that show up in search and drive organic signups
	- **In-product growth hooks:** smart upsells when developers hit rate limits, usage dashboards that create urgency to upgrade
	## 7. Enterprise GTM has no PLG wedge
	Goal #3 is "establish foundation of an enterprise GTM engine" but<span discussion-urls="discussion://31bc3702-22d5-80f6-a095-001cd95d641d"> every initiative is sales-led (case studies, sales enablement, pitch decks</span>). the best enterprise deals start with a developer inside the company already using the product. Where's the bottom-up motion?
	- Track which companies have individual developers already on the API
	- Build internal sharing mechanics (team workspaces, usage reports that can be forwarded to a manager)
	- Create the "land" content that helps a developer inside an enterprise justify bringing BFL in
	We are building a brand marketing machine but we are not building a growth engine. 
	Brand gets us on the first conversation. PLG compounds it. Right now almost nothing in the our initiatives touches the product itself as a growth lever 
	next hires to push: **(1)** Define and instrument the activation metric, **(2)** Own pricing and run first packaging experiment, **(3)** Build one viral loop, even a simple one like shareable outputs with attribution.

<callout icon="/icons/star_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Our focus for H1 2026 is to build quality awareness to increase model usage.**
	We’ll measure this by increases in impressions, website visits, and models usage (via API or licensing) from current baselines.
</callout>
# Three goals for marketing in H1 2026:
<callout icon="1️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Build **quality awareness** for BFL & FLUX 
	**Black Forest Labs as a frontier lab.**
	Core channels: Press, Podcasts, founder socials, Publish research, Website/Blog
	Content: Press articles, vision of “Why visual AI matters”, Research papers
	**FLUX models best for reliable creative control at speed.**
	Core channels: Socials, YouTube, influencers/community, co-marketing w/ partners
	Content: Customer stories, use cases, model launches, Website
</callout>
<callout icon="2️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Drive usage** & retention** for our models
	Drive conversions and engagement for the API:
	Core channels: Dev focused websites, docs, YouTube, socials, email, sales enablement
	Content: API docs, sales enablement/ABM, Website
</callout>
<callout icon="3️⃣" color="green_bg">
	### Establish foundation of an **enterprise GTM **engine
	Core channels: Sales motion, emails to existing users, enterprise marketing
	Content: Customer Case Studies, sales enablement material on pitch, model battlecards, etc
</callout>
# Who are we building for?
<callout icon="/icons/card_green.svg" color="green_bg">
	**Primary: the frontier developers building AI apps**
	The "highest expectation developer" builds visual apps and tools that creatives use directly (directors, creators, enterprises, agents). They need a solid API with special customization features (like LoRA training) that helps them fine-tune their apps while keeping costs low and speed high. Their main goal is creating AI applications that users actually stick with and keep coming back to, and they work at companies like Krea, Flora, Meta, Notion, Adobe, and Figma.

# Three Core Narratives (WIP)
### Why does visual intelligence matter and the path to super intelligence. 
Visual intelligence is harder than language: language is an interface, while vision models reality itself: the geometry of objects, how they relate to each other, what happens when they interact, what stays the same over time and what changes. True intelligence requires understanding the physical world. When models learn to simulate reality (eg predicting what happens when objects collide, how shadows move, how scenes unfold) they develop the foundation for actual reasoning. 
Visual intelligence unlocks everything from content creation to generative UIs that render as fast as you think, to simulations that train robots and agents, to systems that can reason by running mental experiments about the physical world. 
Whoever builds the standard for visual intelligence defines the next platform, because it's the path from generation to reasoning to superintelligence. Black Forest is focused on* *building* the standard for visual intelligence. *The standard means high performance and quality, lean, open, fast, affordable, always available. Ridiculously easy to build on and get great results effortlessly.

	## 1. No growth loops, everything is a funnel
	Every initiative is linear: spend money/effort → get impressions → hope people convert. **where is the compounding?** Where is the mechanism where a user of FLUX generates the next user of FLUX? Some concrete gaps:
	- **No viral/referral loop.** When a developer builds with FLUX, there's no systematic way that creates more FLUX developers. Think "Powered by FLUX" attribution in outputs, API response headers that credit the model, referral credits for API usage.
	- **No user-generated content loop.** The community is creating incredible FLUX content already, where's the infrastructure to capture that, amplify it, and turn it into acquisition? This should be a self-reinforcing engine, not just "social media 2x a week."
	- **No content loop from product usage.** Every image generated by FLUX is a potential marketing asset. Where's the gallery, the showcase, the share-to-social from playground?
	## 2. Pricing is unowned at bfl 
	for a company at \$100M ARR with usage based revenue, pricing and packaging is probably the single highest leverage growth initiative we could run
	- experimenting with reverse trials; Let developers hit the API with generous free credits, then convert based on experienced value rather than a paywall.
	- What's our expansion revenue playbook? How do you systematically move a developer from \$50/mo to \$500/mo to \$5K/mo? That's not in any initiative.
	- Where's usage-based pricing optimization? Even small changes to per-request pricing tiers can meaningfully shift revenue without any new user acquisition.
	## 3. Activation is under-defined
	We can "Optimize customer activation flow with customer.io" and some email lifecycle campaigns, but there's no clearly defined aha moment. what is the *specific action* that, once a developer takes it, predicts they'll retain at 30 days? Is it first successful API call? First LoRA trained? First production deployment? First 1,000 requests?
	Without that defined, our activation emails are guesswork. we are sending lifecycle campaigns without knowing what lifecycle milestone actually matters.
	## 4. Massive ToF bias
	Looking at our metrics table: 37M impressions, 550K website visitors, media coverage targets. 10K unique users retaining 30 days. We set the stats as reference point to test how hard they are to achieve. We are investing heavily in pouring water in the top while barely measuring or investing in the bucket itself. what we should be doing: 
	- Cohort retention analysis before spending on awareness. What do our 30/60/90 day retention curves actually look like by segment?
	- Activation rate optimization. What % of signups make their first API call? What % make 10 calls? This should be an initiative with a DRI, not a side project on customer.io.
	- Resurrection campaigns. we have \~8K unique users but presumably thousands of churned or dormant accounts. Reactivating existing users is 5-10x cheaper than acquiring new ones.
	## 5. No experimentation framework or growth engineering
	There's no initiative around building a culture of rapid experimentation. 
	- A growth engineering function yet to be build 
	- Weekly experiment velocity targets: how many tests are we running on onboarding, activation, conversion, retention?
	- A clear learning loop: hypothesis → test → measure → iterate
	The Scorsese campaign is a big, slow bet. important but we should pair that with 10-20 smaller, faster experiments running simultaneously.
	## 6. Developer experience as a growth channel, not support
	We talk about Anthropic/Vercel level developer experience as a theme. But the initiatives DB doesn't back it up with real investment. We don’t have initiatives around:
	- **Time-to-first-API-call optimisation: **what's the current time and how do you cut it in half?
	- **SDK quality and docs** as a top-of-funnel magnet 
	- **Template/starter projects** that show up in search and drive organic signups
	- **In-product growth hooks:** smart upsells when developers hit rate limits, usage dashboards that create urgency to upgrade
	## 7. Enterprise GTM has no PLG wedge
	Goal #3 is "establish foundation of an enterprise GTM engine" but<span discussion-urls="discussion://31bc3702-22d5-80f6-a095-001cd95d641d"> every initiative is sales-led (case studies, sales enablement, pitch decks</span>). the best enterprise deals start with a developer inside the company already using the product. Where's the bottom-up motion?
	- Track which companies have individual developers already on the API
	- Build internal sharing mechanics (team workspaces, usage reports that can be forwarded to a manager)
	- Create the "land" content that helps a developer inside an enterprise justify bringing BFL in
	We are building a brand marketing machine but we are not building a growth engine. 
	Brand gets us on the first conversation. PLG compounds it. Right now almost nothing in the our initiatives touches the product itself as a growth lever 
	next hires to push: **(1)** Define and instrument the activation metric, **(2)** Own pricing and run first packaging experiment, **(3)** Build one viral loop, even a simple one like shareable outputs with attribution.

	- 2x dev rel this year
	- 2x dev experience this year
	- 1 more creative technologist

Things that we might talk about:
- Parallelization strategies such as DP (also HSDP / FSDP), TP, PP
- GPU compute hierarchies
- Efficient attention implementations 1. 45 mins coding with Tim  In this interview we will debug some Triton code together. If you are new to Triton, it might be helpful to take a look at the tutorials ([https://triton-lang.org/main/getting-started/tutorials/](https://triton-lang.org/main/getting-started/tutorials/)). That being said, I am happy to help you with the syntax. We mostly want to see that you understand the fundamentals of GPU compute hierarchies and are comfortable using them in practice. Specifically we will look at a part of FLUX1 inference ([https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux)), though it’s not required to review the architecture beforehand. 1. **Role Title:**
**Location:**
**About Black Forest Labs**
We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We’re creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.
Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.
**Why This Role**
A short, concrete explanation of *why this role exists right now*.
Answer one of:
- What bottleneck does this role remove?
- What breaks today without this role?
- Who moves faster once this person is hired?
**What You’ll Work On**
A concise list of the core problems this role is responsible for.
- Describe the actual work this role is responsible for
- Prioritize clarity over completeness
- Focus on problems, not personality traits
- Keep it concise and concrete
*(5–7 bullets max)*
Tools & Context - Role based title section (optional)
Only include if tools meaningfully define the role.
- Keep this short
- Orientation, not a checklist
**What We’re Looking For**
A combined experience and capability section.
- Evidence of doing work at meaningful scope, scale, or complexity
- Ability to operate in ambiguous, fast-changing environments
- Strong judgment around tradeoffs and failure modes
- Comfort working cross-functionally when needed
Then add 4–6 role-specific examples:
- For technical roles: systems, scale, tooling, debugging
- For non-technical roles: operations, execution, coordination, decision-making
**How We Work Together**
We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. Depending on your role, you’ll either join us in Freiburg or SF at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week), or work remotely with a monthly in-person week to stay connected. We’ll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we’ve structured things to make it accessible to all. We’ll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process.
**Everything we do is grounded in four values:**
- Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.
- Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.
- Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.
- Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.
**Closing**
If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, we’d love to hear from you.
(Optional, for some roles)
If you’d like to explore the kinds of systems and research this role supports:
– \[Link 1\]
Compensation
Please include base salary range for SF based roles + equity
</content>

**About Black Forest Labs**
We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We’re creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.
Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.
**Why This Role**
A short, concrete explanation of *why this role exists right now*.
Answer one of:
- What bottleneck does this role remove?

**What You’ll Work On**

**How We Work Together**
We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. Depending on your role, you’ll either join us in Freiburg or SF at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week), or work remotely with a monthly in-person week to stay connected. We’ll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we’ve structured things to make it accessible to all. We’ll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process.
**Everything we do is grounded in four values:**

## Strategic Objectives
<empty-block/>
**1. Market Dominance & Awareness**
**Primary Goal**: Achieve 50M+ earned reach [\[1\]](https://www.notion.so/27ec370222d580cbbf82cd6ad2ebecfb)
**Key Metrics**:
- **Media Coverage**: Tier 1 tech press coverage (TechCrunch, The Verge, Wired, Bloomberg)
- **Social Reach**: 50M+ impressions across X, LinkedIn, Reddit
- **Organic Buzz**: 1,000+ community-created examples shared within first week
- **Search Dominance**: "FLUX 2" and "visual AI" top 3 results on Google within 30 days
**Tactics**:
- Pre-brief tier 1 tech press with exclusive early access
- Coordinate customer announcements to drop same day as launch
- Creator/influencer preview program (2 weeks pre-launch)
- Technical paper + accessible explainer published simultaneously
---
**2. Category Leadership: Own "Visual AI" Narrative**
**Primary Goal**: Establish BFL as the definitive authority on open-weight visual AI
<empty-block/>
**Key Metrics**:
- **Thought Leadership**: 3+ technical blog posts published within launch month
- **Speaking Engagements**: Robin/Andi at 2+ major conferences within 60 days
- **Brand Association**: When people think "visual AI," they think FLUX first
- **Technical Authority**: Referenced in 10+ industry analyses/reports within 90 days
<empty-block/>
**Positioning Focus**:
- "Building visual AI into products" vs. "making pretty pictures"
- Open-weight innovation leadership
- Enterprise infrastructure provider (not consumer toy)
---
**3. Enterprise Customer Acquisition**
**Primary Goal**: Sign 5+ landmark enterprise customers within 90 days [\[1\]](https://www.notion.so/27ec370222d580cbbf82cd6ad2ebecfb)
**Key Metrics**:
- **Alpha Partners Converted**: 80% of alpha partners become paying customers
- **New Enterprise Deals**: 5+ new enterprises with \$100K+ annual contracts
- **Pipeline Generation**: 50+ qualified enterprise leads
- **Case Studies**: 5+ customer case studies published within 90 days
**Target Segments** [\[2\]](https://www.notion.so/223c370222d5800395bee4b2ed26e7eb):
- E-commerce platforms (product visualization at scale)
- Marketing agencies (rapid concept development)
- Media & entertainment (concept art, pre-visualization)
- OEM partners (device/platform integration)
---
**4. Developer & Community Engagement**
**Primary Goal**: Build the strongest visual AI developer community
**Key Metrics**:
- **GitHub Activity**: 10,000+ stars on FLUX 2 repo within 30 days
- **API Adoption**: 1,000+ developers using FLUX 2 API within first month
- **Community Projects**: 100+ "Built with FLUX 2" projects showcased
- **Discord/Community**: 5,000+ new community members within 60 days
**Tactics**:
- San Francisco hackathon (entire weekend) [\[3\]](https://www.notion.so/273c370222d5803894b1d5ddbec8d8c3)
- Open-weight model release (FLUX 2 \[dev\]) shortly after launch
- Developer documentation and tutorials day-zero
- "FLUX Button" integration toolkit for partners [\[4\]](https://www.notion.so/281c370222d580d2b165fb80f874395b)
---
**5. Day-Zero Partner Integrations**
**Primary Goal**: Launch with 10+ major platform integrations live
**Key Metrics**:
- **Platform Partners**: Microsoft, Adobe, NVIDIA, Amazon day-zero ready
- **Distribution**: FLUX 2 available in 5+ major AI platforms at launch
- **Co-Marketing**: 3+ joint press releases with strategic partners
- **API Traffic**: 1M+ API calls within first week
**Partner Priorities**:
- Adobe (creative tools integration)
- Microsoft (PowerPoint, Designer)
- NVIDIA (infrastructure optimization)
- Amazon (AWS marketplace)
- Figma, Pinterest, Meta properties
---
**6. Technical Performance Benchmarks**
**Primary Goal**: Establish FLUX 2 as clear quality leader in public benchmarks
**Key Metrics**:
- **Independent Evals**: Top 3 ranking on key benchmark leaderboards
- **Head-to-Head Wins**: Beat Nano Banana in 60%+ of blind comparisons
- **Speed Claims**: Verified 10x faster than GPT Image in third-party tests
- **Quality Ratings**: 4.5+ average rating in community comparisons
**Benchmark Focus**:
- Text rendering and typography
- Character consistency across images
- Physical accuracy and realism
- Multi-language prompting quality
---
**7. Revenue & Business Impact**
**Primary Goal**: \$50M/ XM+ ARR pipeline generated within 90 days
**Key Metrics**:
- **Q4 Revenue**: \$XM+ actual revenue from FLUX 2 in Q4 2025
- **Pipeline**: \$XM+ qualified pipeline within 90 days
- **Average Deal Size**: \$XK+ annual contract value
- **Conversion Rate**: X%+ of alpha users convert to paid
**Pricing Strategy**:
- Competitive vs. Nano Banana at API level
- Significant cost advantage for self-hosted at scale
- Enterprise custom pricing for 1M+ images/month
</content>
</page>

340c3702-22d5-8064-954c-c51ce9320131.title: [lmarena] Data Quality Assurance Protocol
340c3702-22d5-8064-954c-c51ce9320131.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/340c370222d58064954cc51ce9320131 as of 2026-04-13T18:05:38.814Z:
<page url="https://www.notion.so/340c370222d58064954cc51ce9320131">
<ancestor-path></ancestor-path>
<properties>
{"title":"\\[lmarena\\] Data Quality Assurance Protocol"}
</properties>
<content>
In this doc, we explore potential directions for leveraging user data from LMArena to improve BFL's models.
Data specifications for the initial tranche of 52k samples:
- 100% of the samples should correspond to the “Image Edit” task (no T2I for this tranche).
- The categorical distribution should approximately follow: 
	- 20% - Product Branding & Commercial
	- 15% - Overall
	- 15% - Photorealistic & Cinematic
	- 10% - Cartoon Anime & Fantasy
	- 10% - 3D imaging & modeling
	- 10% - Art
	- 10% - Portraits
	- 10%  - Text Rendering
- All the prompts should have at least 1 input image.
	- \>50% - exactly 1 image.
	- \>25% - exactly 2 images.
	- \>10% - 3 or more images.
- All input images should be filtered to include only high-quality images. The quality filters must ensure a minimum original resolution of at least 720p. Additionally, any user-uploaded images of poor quality should be proactively filtered out. 
- Deduplication: No two samples should share the same prompt or any of the input images to ensure thorough deduplication.
- If faces or product shots appear in any of the images, these should not be blurred. In general, all the samples where the images are blurred to hide PII should be filtered out.
- All prompts should be in English only for the first tranche (this restriction may be relaxed for subsequent tranches, depending on the results).
- Prompt quality: The prompts should be clear and relevant to the task. Users sometimes erroneously use t2i or i2v prompts for i2i tasks, and these must be filtered out.  Prompts should not mention specific aspect ratios or external model names (e.g., “reve-edit”).
- Prompt Alignment filters ensure the prompt and input image are semantically related. 
- NSFW filtering: Only samples classified as "safe" should be included. Both "borderline" and "unsafe" content must be removed.
- PII detection: Samples containing personally identifiable information must be filtered out.
- Blurred Face filtering: Remove any pairs where faces in the input images have been blurred to hide identity. Unblurred, naturally occurring faces are acceptable.
- Diversity: We are committed to ensuring the data distribution accurately represents the diverse use cases of our underlying user base.

raw.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/340c370222d58064954cc51ce9320131 as of 2026-04-13T18:05:38.814Z:

<properties>
{"title":"\\[lmarena\\] Data Quality Assurance Protocol"}
</properties>
<content>
In this doc, we explore potential directions for leveraging user data from LMArena to improve BFL's models.
Data specifications for the initial tranche of 52k samples:
- 100% of the samples should correspond to the “Image Edit” task (no T2I for this tranche).
- The categorical distribution should approximately follow: 
	- 20% - Product Branding & Commercial
	- 15% - Overall
	- 15% - Photorealistic & Cinematic
	- 10% - Cartoon Anime & Fantasy
	- 10% - 3D imaging & modeling
	- 10% - Art
	- 10% - Portraits
	- 10%  - Text Rendering
- All the prompts should have at least 1 input image.
	- \>50% - exactly 1 image.
	- \>25% - exactly 2 images.
	- \>10% - 3 or more images.
- All input images should be filtered to include only high-quality images. The quality filters must ensure a minimum original resolution of at least 720p. Additionally, any user-uploaded images of poor quality should be proactively filtered out. 
- Deduplication: No two samples should share the same prompt or any of the input images to ensure thorough deduplication.
- If faces or product shots appear in any of the images, these should not be blurred. In general, all the samples where the images are blurred to hide PII should be filtered out.
- All prompts should be in English only for the first tranche (this restriction may be relaxed for subsequent tranches, depending on the results).
- Prompt quality: The prompts should be clear and relevant to the task. Users sometimes erroneously use t2i or i2v prompts for i2i tasks, and these must be filtered out.  Prompts should not mention specific aspect ratios or external model names (e.g., “reve-edit”).
- Prompt Alignment filters ensure the prompt and input image are semantically related. 
- NSFW filtering: Only samples classified as "safe" should be included. Both "borderline" and "unsafe" content must be removed.
- PII detection: Samples containing personally identifiable information must be filtered out.
- Blurred Face filtering: Remove any pairs where faces in the input images have been blurred to hide identity. Unblurred, naturally occurring faces are acceptable.
- Diversity: We are committed to ensuring the data distribution accurately represents the diverse use cases of our underlying user base.

337c3702-22d5-8070-bacb-c53ad753c893.title: AI Engineer London | Talk
337c3702-22d5-8070-bacb-c53ad753c893.text: Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/337c370222d58070bacbc53ad753c893 as of 2026-04-08T16:07:17.754Z: {"title":"AI Engineer London \\| Talk"} 17 mins long ## Slide 1 - 4 Hello everyone, I am Stephen Batifol, I work in Developer & Creative Growth at BFL. Who here knows Black Forest Labs? And FLUX? BFL, who are we, funding etc, why are we here, why do we matter ## Slide 5 - what are we known for You may know us for our FLUX models, FLUX.1 was the first model of BFL and the one that really put us out there in the wild. It was the first model to just nail anatomy, and one that could also run on consumer hardware (show the numbers and amount of downloads of the model on HF in particular, also the number of derivatives created with that one.) We then released FLUX.1 Kontext, the first open editing model in the world. ## Slide 6 In november, we released FLUX.2, our latest family of model - in january we released Klein with 2 variants, 4B and 9B - making it possible for everyone to use it on their hardware. We have seen a lot of adoption for Klein and in particular from the community and the open-source world. (Show some really cool assets that people created and demos) Also show the number of downlaods we’ve had with FLUX.2 \[dev\] and Klein family. ## Slide 7 - What are we working on at the moment? BFL is first and foremost a research company, we are here to invent new technologies and new modalities. For example, we recently published a new version of our Klein variant, the “KV Cache” version. You might be familiar with KV cache when you hear LLMs, but it’s different in the Diffusion world - even if the models are Diffusion Transformers, they still process those differently. (show the way we process tokens in a normal model) Diffusion models are not generating a sequence left to right. They are running an iterative denoising process where the model is called over and over again on a changing state. Something can look static at the input and still not be static inside the transformer. This becomes even more relevant for image editing. You give the model one or more reference images, those references stay fixed for the entire denoising process, and yet the model keeps recomputing their representations at every step anyway. The instinct is still the same: cache the keys and values. That is where people usually start. It is also where it breaks. In a normal diffusion transformer, reference-image tokens are not actually stable across denoising steps. Cache them naively and you cache the wrong thing. The real change is not the cache itself. The real change is making the reference pathway stable enough to reuse across denoising steps. (Show the way it’s done with KV cache, what are we caching exactly) ## Slide 8 - KV Cache continue After those changes, the denoising loop splits into two phases. **Step 0:** run the model with the reference tokens present and build the cache from the reference-side computation. **Later steps:** stop recomputing that reference side from scratch. Reuse the cached reference information while continuing to update the actual image tokens being denoised. The references are static, so the model processes them once and then keeps using them, this means: - more reference images means more redundant work can be eliminated - the speedup grows as conditioning becomes a larger share of the total computation - multi-reference editing benefits the most (Maybe do a live demo here?) ## Slide 9 - Self Flow Another thing that differentiates us from the rest - we truly believe in Open-Research, we actually publish things, it’s the reason why we also push models in the open, and other components. For example, we recently published “Self Flow” (**Self-Supervised** Flow Matching for **Scalable** **Multi-Modal** Synthesis). It allows models to support both single-modality and joint multi-modal training. ## Slide 10 - Why Self Flow matters? If you aren’t aware, Generative models can be improved by aligning their internal features with the ones of a frozen image encoder. This poses a problem, those models don’t learn strong representations on their own, although they help for generation. 1. First, when using external alignment, it fails to keep up with the expected scaling laws. 2. This also fails to generalize across modalities: for video and audio generation, we find that it actually harms performance. 1. Making it less suitable for multi-modal models that must handle different data types. 3. On top of that, it’s hard to know which encoder will work best for a given task. This is why we believe it matters, Self-flow isn’t relying on those external encoders and naturally extends to more modalities. It supports both single-modality and joint multi-modal training. It also improves structural coherence, particularly for challenging structures like faces and hands, as well as text rendering accuracy and temporal consistency in videos. ## Slide 11 - Self Flow, Image Generation Here are some examples of Image generation, those have been trained on a small model and they would obviously look better if we were to train a model with more parameters but it’s to show you the idea. ## Slide 12 - Self Flow, Video Generation We can see that Video Generation is also improving, the coherence is better as well as the temporality ## Slide 13 - Self Flow, Video-Audio Generation ## Slide 14 - Self Flow, Actions And finally, we can see the the same model has learned Actions, so the model can not only generate better images, videos and audio, but on top of that, it can also worth with Actions. By also working on the Actions modality and robotics, we are already thinking about the future. With Self-flow and the different release such as KV cache, we aren’t only thinking of models for images or videos. ## Slide 15 - The future We are already thinking about the next modalities that we believe will change the world and the way we do things. Everything I have talked about today is here for 1 goal, the road to visual intelligence. We at BFL are focusing: Agents, World models, Robotics. Show the slide where we talk about World models, Agents, video models etc ## Slide 16 - Leave like a boss Thank you everyone, if you want to join us and do the best job of your career, we are hiring.

We then released FLUX.1 Kontext, the first open editing model in the world. ## Slide 6 In november, we released FLUX.2, our latest family of model - in january we released Klein with 2 variants, 4B and 9B - making it possible for everyone to use it on their hardware. We have seen a lot of adoption for Klein and in particular from the community and the open-source world. (Show some really cool assets that people created and demos) Also show the number of downlaods we’ve had with FLUX.2 \[dev\] and Klein family. ## Slide 7 - What are we working on at the moment? BFL is first and foremost a research company, we are here to invent new technologies and new modalities. For example, we recently published a new version of our Klein variant, the “KV Cache” version. You might be familiar with KV cache when you hear LLMs, but it’s different in the Diffusion world - even if the models are Diffusion Transformers, they still process those differently. (show the way we process tokens in a normal model) Diffusion models are not generating a sequence left to right. They are running an iterative denoising process where the model is called over and over again on a changing state. Something can look static at the input and still not be static inside the transformer. This becomes even more relevant for image editing. You give the model one or more reference images, those references stay fixed for the entire denoising process, and yet the model keeps recomputing their representations at every step anyway. The instinct is still the same: cache the keys and values. That is where people usually start. It is also where it breaks. In a normal diffusion transformer, reference-image tokens are not actually stable across denoising steps. Cache them naively and you cache the wrong thing. The real change is not the cache itself. The real change is making the reference pathway stable enough to reuse across denoising steps. (Show the way it’s done with KV cache, what are we caching exactly) ## Slide 8 - KV Cache continue After those changes, the denoising loop splits into two phases. **Step 0:** run the model with the reference tokens present and build the cache from the reference-side computation. **Later steps:** stop recomputing that reference side from scratch. Reuse the cached reference information while continuing to update the actual image tokens being denoised. The references are static, so the model processes them once and then keeps using them, this means: - more reference images means more redundant work can be eliminated - the speedup grows as conditioning becomes a larger share of the total computation - multi-reference editing benefits the most (Maybe do a live demo here?) ## Slide 9 - Self Flow Another thing that differentiates us from the rest - we truly believe in Open-Research, we actually publish things, it’s the reason why we also push models in the open, and other components. For example, we recently published “Self Flow” (**Self-Supervised** Flow Matching for **Scalable** **Multi-Modal** Synthesis). It allows models to support both single-modality and joint multi-modal training. ## Slide 10 - Why Self Flow matters? If you aren’t aware, Generative models can be improved by aligning their internal features with the ones of a frozen image encoder. This poses a problem, those models don’t learn strong representations on their own, although they help for generation. 1. First, when using external alignment, it fails to keep up with the expected scaling laws. 2. This also fails to generalize across modalities: for video and audio generation, we find that it actually harms performance. 1. Making it less suitable for multi-modal models that must handle different data types. 3. On top of that, it’s hard to know which encoder will work best for a given task. This is why we believe it matters, Self-flow isn’t relying on those external encoders and naturally extends to more modalities. It supports both single-modality and joint multi-modal training. It also improves structural coherence, particularly for challenging structures like faces and hands, as well as text rendering accuracy and temporal consistency in videos. ## Slide 11 - Self Flow, Image Generation Here are some examples of Image generation, those have been trained on a small model and they would obviously look better if we were to train a model with more parameters but it’s to show you the idea. ## Slide 12 - Self Flow, Video Generation We can see that Video Generation is also improving, the coherence is better as well as the temporality ## Slide 13 - Self Flow, Video-Audio Generation ## Slide 14 - Self Flow, Actions And finally, we can see the the same model has learned Actions, so the model can not only generate better images, videos and audio, but on top of that, it can also worth with Actions. By also working on the Actions modality and robotics, we are already thinking about the future. With Self-flow and the different release such as KV cache, we aren’t only thinking of models for images or videos. ## Slide 15 - The future We are already thinking about the next modalities that we believe will change the world and the way we do things. Everything I have talked about today is here for 1 goal, the road to visual intelligence. We at BFL are focusing: Agents, World models, Robotics. Show the slide where we talk about World models, Agents, video models etc ## Slide 16 - Leave like a boss Thank you everyone, if you want to join us and do the best job of your career, we are hiring.

In summary: There are two groups of tiers: online (hot, cool, and cold), and offline (archive). Cool/cold to hot is instant - moving a blob from the cool/cold tier to the hot tier is just a metadata operation. Since they're all online, there is no "rehydration" delay. When retrieving data from offline (archive) to online, that's when rehydration comes in, and could take up to 15 hours. You have the option of requesting a retrieval with high priority, which may complete in less than one hour. For costs, retrieving data from offline to online, there are early deletion plus data retrieval costs (e.g., standard and high priority).
