Intro and tell us about your role and the work you do at BFL?		 I lead infrastructure at Black Forest Labs. I joined about a year ago from a startup in the LLM serving and finetuning space which got acquired by AMD. At BFL, I'm responsible for our training infrastructure, API backend, and everything that takes our models from research to production at scale.

Black Forest Labs launched in August 2024. We're a small team, about 40 people split between our Freiburg office in Germany, on the edge of the Black Forest, and San Francisco. Our founding team is responsible for much of the original research that led to diffusion models. Many of them were behind the original Stable Diffusion models at Stability AI.

Since launch, our FLUX family of models has topped benchmarks for text-to-image and image-to-image editing quality. The FLUX family spans from open-weight models for on-premise deployments to high-performance models available via our API. Also these Pro Models are available direct from Azure Foundry. This gives customers flexibility to match their security, cost, and integration needs.
Working with a large cluster of GPUs is not the same as deploying general purpose compute infrastructure, walk us through some of your experiences as the team onboarded to Azure AI Infra cluster and how you scaled up to support training your Flux models? Timeline and journey slide You’re absolutely right. Working with large GPU clusters, bring about stresses the systems to its limits. From networking, to memory, to the compute layer. There are challenges in each of these areas. Azure has been our cloud partner since day 1. From H100s to being the first customer on the GB200 NVL72 cluster, Azure has supported throughout.

A case in point, with the GB200s especially, the rack topology and desnity becomes very important which is an anti-pattern to typical node levelVM allocation.

There was no existing playbook for rack-level allocation. We worked directly with Azure's CycleCloud team to develop a new allocation method they call scale_m1. Instead of requesting individual GPUs, we request complete racks.

The rack-level allocation and packing density was critical for maximizing performance on the NVL72 architecture.
What other considerations you had to make throughout the experience on Azure. Getting the infrastructure and related services right, is more than just the best GPUs. How has Azure’s AI infrastructure helped with your TTM goals. High level architecture slide, data pipeline flow and or other services used e.g. blob. Three things beyond the GPUs themselves: driver maturity, storage architecture, and monitoring.

**On drivers:** GB200 was brand new hardware. The entire Azure team plus NVIDIA worked together on providing new drivers, validation, and finding optimization best practices.

**On storage and networking:** Pre-training is intensive not just on GPUs but on storage and networking. We hit issues like partition thresholds and InfiniBand flapping. We've been working with Azure's Storage team to identify common hotpaths and implement pre-emptive load balancing for multi-node training runs.

**On monitoring, and resiliency: **It’s vital to have monitoring during training runs, especially production runs. Anything can go wrong when running month long training jobs, and figuring out the underlying problem, resolving it, and resuming the runs becomes very important.

One thing that people neglect is maintainence, it’s no secret that GPU servers might face hardware issues in their life-cycle, but with the rack density becoming so important for the NVL72, the removing of 1 node for maintenance, impacts the entire rack performance. Long story short, Azure’s over-allocation strategies allowed us to continue without impacting training speed.
How important to you was the orchestration experience of the large cluster?  Was there a benefit with Azure for the type of work you needed to do? Why did you choose Slurm as the job scheduler vs. some other solutions that we've seen customers use? Describe your experience with running Slurm on Azure with CycleCloud as the orchestration engine. Microsoft can show slide on different deployment options Orchestration was critical for GB200. We evaluated several options and chose to run Slurm on Azure CycleCloud.

The combination works well because Slurm is battle-tested for HPC workloads, and CycleCloud provides the cloud-native integration and understanding of Azure's infrastructure. The key was getting Slurm to understand GB200's rack topology.

Traditional slurm does not have native understanding of “racks”, and Cyclecloud worked with SchedMD to integrate block topology in slurm. Using that we were able to schedule jobs normally with slurm taking care of allocating over racks. Additionally, scaling of nodes happened in a rack-wise fashion using the scale_m1 technology.

We also worked closely with the Cyclecloud team, along with Davide, and Jesse, our dedicated Solutions engineers, to beef up the health agents to capture failures in the application layer too, making it much more reliable.

For a small team, this was much faster than building everything from scratch. We got the benefits of Slurm's mature scheduling plus Azure's infrastructure optimization.”
\[Matt to speak to the pace of silicon innovation these days, from A100s just a few years ago, to already talking about Vera Rubin\]
How has collaborating with Azure enabled you to swiftly access the latest NVIDIA GPUs? For instance, in what ways has being among the first to deploy the GB200 at a large scale boosted your performance and job throughput, and ultimately helped you stay at the leading edge of generative model training?		 BFL to share more about their journey with Flux and how its evolved over different versions I don’t think people really comprehend what a behemoth the GB200s are. 13.TB of HBM, with 576 TeraBYTES/s bandwidth, and double the FLOPs as the H100 gives massive improvement to training runs. Training in general (and this is true for both autoregressive models like LLMs and diffusion models), are compute bound, so with compute improvement, it shifts the training speed up quite a lot. Additionally, the extra HBM opens up the ability to “pack training of bigger models into lesser GPUs”, making it more efficient. Lastly, it allows to train with larger batch sizes, which generally helps with better model performance.


But with the bleeding edge, comes the teething problems, the GB200s are a very new technology, it differs from its predecessors not just due to more integrated rack layout, but also due to it being ARM based, having unified memory, the increased dependence of the NVLINK switches, etc. All this leads to dealing with new problems not present in older generations. Thankfully we have support from both Nvidia and Azure, to work on ironing out these issues.
For some of the Audience out there who are just starting out with AI infra for training, post training or inference workloads, what are your top 3 lessons learnt in this process? don’t save any of the gory details BFL top 3 lessons Three lessons from being first on GB200:

**First: Co-design with your cloud provider, don't just consume services.** When we faced issues with training run stability, we didn't file a support ticket. We sat down with Azure's CycleCloud team and co-developed tests to better capture errors before runs. We obsessed over collecting as much logs, and reporting, to share with Azure, to both understand the system better, and also accelerate them improving of the service. To Azure’s credit, the speed in improvement of the node health/resilience has been amazing. Treat your cloud provider as a true partner, you can get features built that solve your specific problems.

**Second: Budget time for immaturity on bleeding-edge hardware.** GB200 is incredibly powerful, but it was brand new. Drivers needed optimization. Documentation was sparse. We had to work closely with both Azure and NVIDIA teams to get everything production-ready. So if the compute speed up is 2x, factor in a cost for working through the kinks. This is not just in time, but also engineering manpower.

**Third: Optimize the entire system, not just GPU performance.** We initially obsessed over GPU metrics. But our most of our pain points came from networking, and storage. AI training is a system. You need to instrument the full pipeline, identify the true constraint, fix it, and repeat. The GPU is often not your bottleneck.

**unknown performance** post-sign (Sanjana hasn’t been engaged by MSFT sellers yet). - Need to clarify **seller incentives, routing, billing,** and enablement materials. - North-star example: **Anthropic × AWS** marketplace motion. - **Focus areas (near-term):** 1. **Microsoft in-product integration** (Copilot/Designer/PowerPoint) 2. **MaaS performance & scale** (seller motion, listings, regions, billing) 3. **Continued Infra stability** --- ## ### ** \| Microsoft / Clipchamp Prep** {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** , , **Draft Deck:** [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ZkvMb_qDBKwV9Xh4RarEo1uVUPXyQqdSNva1AtTVtWk/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ZkvMb_qDBKwV9Xh4RarEo1uVUPXyQqdSNva1AtTVtWk/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167) **Context** - Clipchamp (Microsoft’s quick & easy video editor tool) team visiting SF office. - Purpose: Preview of our **video roadmap**, not a formal pitch/demo. - Current status: No integration into MSFT products yet. - Reality: We don’t want this meeting but can’t pass it up → keep it light, don’t overshare. --- ### **Key Points from Discussion** - **Positioning** - Emphasize: we’re working on **foundational models**. - Model is particularly strong for **ideation** (fast iteration, previews). - Our differentiator: workflow speed + professional-grade ideation (generate low-res previews in \<10s → select → upscale). - **Content Strategy** - No need for full company overview. - Use **“cherries” = cherry-picked best content/results**. - Clarify: “Flux Video” (placeholder name) in training now → TBD if this exact model is released. - **Depth / Guardrails** - Important to **decide how much to share** (roadmap vs. technical detail). - Microsoft is contractually entitled to analyze once released, but not guaranteed reseller deal unless financials agreed. - Guidance needed from Axel: how deep to go, what not to reveal. - **Storyline (suggested)** 1. The BFL-specific clauses are on pages 122-124 of the EA Product Terms doc and start on page 89 for the MCA (when you export as PDF from the button at top right). Please be sure you’re using the “Present Day Terms” option when viewing/exporting. Let me know if this isn't what you were looking for.

4/2/2026 - [Today we're announcing 3 new world class MAI models, available in Foundry](https://microsoft.ai/news/today-were-announcing-3-new-world-class-mai-models-available-in-foundry/) **MAI-Image-2** has turbocharged image generation performance and speed on Copilot after debuting as a top 3 model family on the Arena.ai leaderboard. Users experience at least 2x faster generation times on Foundry and Copilot with similar quality, based on real-world production traffic data. Phased rollouts are also underway in Bing and PowerPoint. **MAI-Image-2** was created with photographers, designers, and visual storytellers that demand natural lighting, accurate skin tones and texture, and clear in-image text for diagrams, layouts, and graphics. Once again, speed and quality don’t come at higher costs – **MAI-Image-2** is offered at competitive price-to-performance. Customers are already embracing **MAI-Image-2 **for creative work. WPP, one of the world’s largest marketing and communications groups, is among the first enterprise partners building with **MAI-Image-2** at scale. “**MAI-Image-2** is a genuine game-changer. It’s a platform that not only responds to the intricate nuance of creative direction, but deeply respects the sheer craft involved in generating real-world, campaign-ready images,” said Rob Reilly, Global Chief Creative Officer, WPP. “WPP has some of the best creative talent in the world and **MAI-Image-2** is making them even better.”

### \| \[Internal Sync\] Bulleit (Katie) + Matt + Owais {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt, Owais - Bulleit: Katie ### **Microsoft PowerPoint Integration Launch Strategy** - Flux models now available to beta customers in PowerPoint - General availability rollout starts this week, 100% of customers by end of March - Currently white-labeled (no Black Forest Labs branding visible to users) - Future model picker feature will show Flux alongside OpenAI and potentially Microsoft’s own models - Goal: Make Flux the default option despite Microsoft’s OpenAI relationship - Advantage: Better pricing and speed compared to competitors ### **Announcement Timing & Approach** - Decided against GTC announcement (March) - Would get lost among Nvidia news - Clunky integration story with Azure/Nvidia - Separate Nemo Tron announcement already planned for GTC - Would force an early “preview” moment that weakens the eventual GA story - Preferred strategy: Wait for Microsoft’s broader rollout announcement - Higher impact when actual users can access the feature - Avoid preview fatigue from press (don’t pre-announce at GTC, then re-announce at GA) - Leverage Microsoft’s announcement for credibility and reach - Optimize for quality, enterprise-grade awareness vs. quick hype at GTC ### **Press & Marketing Strategy** - Target publications: Bloomberg, CNBC, Financial Times, Reuters - Position as enterprise validation story - Focus on “good enough for biggest company in the world” angle - Avoid consumer tech angle (TechCrunch, Mashable) - Timeline: 2-3 weeks lead time for press outreach - Need Microsoft’s explicit announcement plans first - Create own demo assets (Microsoft’s demos were “corporate AI slop”) ### **Next Steps** - Matt: Get Microsoft’s announcement timeline and plans - Katie: Prepare press strategy once Microsoft timeline confirmed - Team: Secure PowerPoint beta access for creating demo materials - Consider analyst briefings for enterprise lead generation ## :slack: Slack Message {toggle="true"} Hey [@Nadine](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U0A1NQX0S79) - Caught up with [@Owais](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U0A6T0CGUKU) and [@Katie](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U019P7EGL86) last week after we spoke with MSFT.Here's the thinking around GTM for Powerpoint at GTC: - **1. Skipping GTC as our launch moment: **Too much Nvidia noise, involving Nvidia into the story to get amplification via their channels is clunky. More importantly, teasing a preview at GTC would dilute the eventual GA announcement. - **2. Anchoring to Microsoft's PowerPoint GA rollout (currently planned for the week of April 8th) : **We announce when users can **actually access the feature**. GTC falls in the middle of Microsoft's rollout, the call to action would be unclear. Hitchhiking on Microsoft's comms gives us distribution and credibility. - **3. Model picker world. Flux as the default: **Right now customers would be unaware FLUX is powering the features. However, Microsoft is building a model picker that will be announced as part of this GA rollout. When this rolls out, customers can pick their model of choice. Our goal is to be the default pick. Will continue to push Microsoft on this. - **4. PR plan deferred pending Microsoft confirmation: **I'm working on getting clarity from MSFT on what will be included in their launch announcement around April 8th. Both teams are aligned on mentioning FLUX and Black Forest Labs. Our amplification strategy will depend on that. **Next step:** - Get alignment from Microsoft on their announcement plans. **On meetings with Microsoft Execs:** - That's a separate workstream. My counterparts are helping me understand who will be in attendance and then I'll make intros to find some available time. ### \| BFL / Powerpoint - GTM {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt, Owais - MSFT: - Matthew Hacker – Account Executive for BFL - Kostas Seleskerov – Group Product Manager, PowerPoint - Shilpi Gupta – Technical Program Manager, PowerPoint - Daniel Epstein – Technical Strategist (global team) - Davide Vanzo – HPC & AI Architect, GTC booth/content lead - Eric Van Aelstyn – Senior Product Marketing Manager, M365 Copilot - Lisa Svensson – Product Marketing, Microsoft 365 Consumer (PowerPoint PMM) ### **PowerPoint Integration Demo** - Three key experiences (all within agent mode): 1. Create presentation - contextual image generation based on slide content 2. Add image experience - generates relevant images without specific prompts 3. Edit image experience - multi-turn editing with natural language prompts - Agent mode is Microsoft’s new standard for PowerPoint creation/editing - Multiple prominent entry points planned - Zero query prompts feature “create presentation” and “create image” as hero prompts - Template picker includes branded templates for commercial users - Model picker coming soon - users will choose between available models - Works on both AI-generated and user-provided images ### **Current Availability & Rollout** - Currently live for Frontier audiences only - March rollout planned: - Gradual deployment starting at 10% across web, Windows, and Mac - Not a flip-switch launch - percentage-based rollout by market ### **Go-to-Market Plans** - Joint BFL + Microsoft narrative needed on Flux in PowerPoint and Agent Mode as the new default creation surface - Early focus on Frontier users as initial CTA during March rollout, then broader GA story once availability is high - GTC (March 16–19) discussed as a possible moment for: - Theater session at Microsoft’s booth (Davide coordinating) - Potential joint BFL/Microsoft presence and Nvidia tie-in if there’s a credible three-way story - Preference from both sides to time bigger public push to when most customers can actually use the feature, to avoid “too-early” announcement with no in-product experience - PR coordination to run through Eric (commercial), Lisa (consumer) and their PR teams, with alignment on: - Whether/when to call out Flux/BFL by name (especially once model picker ships) - How commercial vs consumer narratives differ ### **User Adoption & Use Cases** - Wide variety of users across industries - not niche, mainstream adoption - Highest usage among marketing teams, sales teams, and HR - Popular across commercial and consumer segments - Image generation already popular in Copilot chat surfaces - Document grounding (referencing other workspace files) in internal testing ### **Technical Capabilities & Limitations** - Contextual prompt formation based on slide content - Current limitations with Flux: - No transparency support (needed for icons) - Spelling errors in text-heavy infographics - Flux Pro now available - best model for typography - Faster models coming soon for near real-time editing ### **Next Steps** - Microsoft to provide demo videos via Teams channel - Joint go-to-market planning needed: - Align on public messaging timing - Consider GTC (March 16-19) announcement opportunity - PR coordination between teams required - Closer collaboration on model optimization and feedback - Teams channel setup for ongoing coordination (Owais needs Teams access) ### \| BFL / MSFT Weekly Sync {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt - MSFT: - Matt Hacker, Jordan Philipson, Leticia, Daniel Epstein **Agenda:** - Access to Frontier Program: [https://adoption.microsoft.com/files/copilot/Frontier_Getting-started-guide.pdf](https://adoption.microsoft.com/files/copilot/Frontier_Getting-started-guide.pdf) - In summary: There are two groups of tiers: online (hot, cool, and cold), and offline (archive). Cool/cold to hot is instant - moving a blob from the cool/cold tier to the hot tier is just a metadata operation. Since they're all online, there is no "rehydration" delay. When retrieving data from offline (archive) to online, that's when rehydration comes in, and could take up to 15 hours. You have the option of requesting a retrieval with high priority, which may complete in less than one hour. For costs, retrieving data from offline to online, there are early deletion plus data retrieval costs (e.g., standard and high priority). Intro and tell us about your role and the work you do at BFL?		 I lead infrastructure at Black Forest Labs. I joined about a year ago from a startup in the LLM serving and finetuning space which got acquired by AMD. At BFL, I'm responsible for our training infrastructure, API backend, and everything that takes our models from research to production at scale.

Black Forest Labs launched in August 2024. We're a small team, about 40 people split between our Freiburg office in Germany, on the edge of the Black Forest, and San Francisco. Our founding team is responsible for much of the original research that led to diffusion models. Many of them were behind the original Stable Diffusion models at Stability AI.

Since launch, our FLUX family of models has topped benchmarks for text-to-image and image-to-image editing quality. The FLUX family spans from open-weight models for on-premise deployments to high-performance models available via our API. Also these Pro Models are available direct from Azure Foundry. This gives customers flexibility to match their security, cost, and integration needs.
Working with a large cluster of GPUs is not the same as deploying general purpose compute infrastructure, walk us through some of your experiences as the team onboarded to Azure AI Infra cluster and how you scaled up to support training your Flux models? Timeline and journey slide You’re absolutely right. Working with large GPU clusters, bring about stresses the systems to its limits. From networking, to memory, to the compute layer. There are challenges in each of these areas. Azure has been our cloud partner since day 1. From H100s to being the first customer on the GB200 NVL72 cluster, Azure has supported throughout.

A case in point, with the GB200s especially, the rack topology and desnity becomes very important which is an anti-pattern to typical node levelVM allocation.

There was no existing playbook for rack-level allocation. We worked directly with Azure's CycleCloud team to develop a new allocation method they call scale_m1. Instead of requesting individual GPUs, we request complete racks.

The rack-level allocation and packing density was critical for maximizing performance on the NVL72 architecture.
What other considerations you had to make throughout the experience on Azure. Getting the infrastructure and related services right, is more than just the best GPUs. How has Azure’s AI infrastructure helped with your TTM goals. High level architecture slide, data pipeline flow and or other services used e.g. blob. Three things beyond the GPUs themselves: driver maturity, storage architecture, and monitoring.

**On drivers:** GB200 was brand new hardware. The entire Azure team plus NVIDIA worked together on providing new drivers, validation, and finding optimization best practices.

**On storage and networking:** Pre-training is intensive not just on GPUs but on storage and networking. We hit issues like partition thresholds and InfiniBand flapping. We've been working with Azure's Storage team to identify common hotpaths and implement pre-emptive load balancing for multi-node training runs.

**On monitoring, and resiliency: **It’s vital to have monitoring during training runs, especially production runs. Anything can go wrong when running month long training jobs, and figuring out the underlying problem, resolving it, and resuming the runs becomes very important.

One thing that people neglect is maintainence, it’s no secret that GPU servers might face hardware issues in their life-cycle, but with the rack density becoming so important for the NVL72, the removing of 1 node for maintenance, impacts the entire rack performance. Long story short, Azure’s over-allocation strategies allowed us to continue without impacting training speed.
How important to you was the orchestration experience of the large cluster?  Was there a benefit with Azure for the type of work you needed to do? Why did you choose Slurm as the job scheduler vs. some other solutions that we've seen customers use? Describe your experience with running Slurm on Azure with CycleCloud as the orchestration engine. Microsoft can show slide on different deployment options Orchestration was critical for GB200. We evaluated several options and chose to run Slurm on Azure CycleCloud.

The combination works well because Slurm is battle-tested for HPC workloads, and CycleCloud provides the cloud-native integration and understanding of Azure's infrastructure. The key was getting Slurm to understand GB200's rack topology.

Traditional slurm does not have native understanding of “racks”, and Cyclecloud worked with SchedMD to integrate block topology in slurm. Using that we were able to schedule jobs normally with slurm taking care of allocating over racks. Additionally, scaling of nodes happened in a rack-wise fashion using the scale_m1 technology.

We also worked closely with the Cyclecloud team, along with Davide, and Jesse, our dedicated Solutions engineers, to beef up the health agents to capture failures in the application layer too, making it much more reliable.

For a small team, this was much faster than building everything from scratch. We got the benefits of Slurm's mature scheduling plus Azure's infrastructure optimization.”
\[Matt to speak to the pace of silicon innovation these days, from A100s just a few years ago, to already talking about Vera Rubin\]
How has collaborating with Azure enabled you to swiftly access the latest NVIDIA GPUs? For instance, in what ways has being among the first to deploy the GB200 at a large scale boosted your performance and job throughput, and ultimately helped you stay at the leading edge of generative model training?		 BFL to share more about their journey with Flux and how its evolved over different versions I don’t think people really comprehend what a behemoth the GB200s are. 13.TB of HBM, with 576 TeraBYTES/s bandwidth, and double the FLOPs as the H100 gives massive improvement to training runs. Training in general (and this is true for both autoregressive models like LLMs and diffusion models), are compute bound, so with compute improvement, it shifts the training speed up quite a lot. Additionally, the extra HBM opens up the ability to “pack training of bigger models into lesser GPUs”, making it more efficient. Lastly, it allows to train with larger batch sizes, which generally helps with better model performance.


But with the bleeding edge, comes the teething problems, the GB200s are a very new technology, it differs from its predecessors not just due to more integrated rack layout, but also due to it being ARM based, having unified memory, the increased dependence of the NVLINK switches, etc. All this leads to dealing with new problems not present in older generations. Thankfully we have support from both Nvidia and Azure, to work on ironing out these issues.
For some of the Audience out there who are just starting out with AI infra for training, post training or inference workloads, what are your top 3 lessons learnt in this process? don’t save any of the gory details BFL top 3 lessons Three lessons from being first on GB200:

**First: Co-design with your cloud provider, don't just consume services.** When we faced issues with training run stability, we didn't file a support ticket. We sat down with Azure's CycleCloud team and co-developed tests to better capture errors before runs. We obsessed over collecting as much logs, and reporting, to share with Azure, to both understand the system better, and also accelerate them improving of the service. To Azure’s credit, the speed in improvement of the node health/resilience has been amazing. Treat your cloud provider as a true partner, you can get features built that solve your specific problems.

**Second: Budget time for immaturity on bleeding-edge hardware.** GB200 is incredibly powerful, but it was brand new. Drivers needed optimization. Documentation was sparse. We had to work closely with both Azure and NVIDIA teams to get everything production-ready. So if the compute speed up is 2x, factor in a cost for working through the kinks. This is not just in time, but also engineering manpower.

**Third: Optimize the entire system, not just GPU performance.** We initially obsessed over GPU metrics. But our most of our pain points came from networking, and storage. AI training is a system. You need to instrument the full pipeline, identify the true constraint, fix it, and repeat. The GPU is often not your bottleneck.

**Rough Notes** - first question: masked inpainting - Kontext trained for rectangles, esp good for text editing - Lots of excitement around infographics Appreciate that we focused on use cases (icons, scenarios Questions from MSFT: - How to handle inpainting? - When can they get API to run eval? - What is the performance (time to generate)? - Will it be possible to the get the images for icons in SVG? - Changing color palette changes the colors of the SVG - Leverage a lot of stock images, which come in different styles or don’t have all the context. Will be important to be able to change the images to match the styels or context. - Real-time suggestions in the side bar for editing - Hackathon would be helpful - Want images generated to feel like they were picked by a professional designer that fit the style and create cohesiveness. Feel like magic. - Images should be complementary vs literal representation (another idea for hackathon) - Worth spending lots of time in prompt upsampling. - When generating a deck, they know the context of the deck. How do they create bespoke images, icons, graphics? - Visual suggestions of how your slide could look. Want that to be faster. Faster models would be ideal. - Commanding - Via Copilot to use chat to manipulate image content. A key area they are investing in. - Upleveling without destroying. Next Session - Can MSFT share a sample presentation? We can then build a mock pipeline for how we would handle this. - Can BFL share the JSON schema? - BFL to share some samples from the demo last time. Async - Tackle logistics for the hackathon
### \| MSFT Quick Sync (During AMZN Sync) {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt, Sanjana, Andi ### Microsoft Situation - Designer team has gone silent after follow-up - Need escalation if no response by end of week - Flux Two demo opportunity to re-engage - They expressed interest in being launch partner - Could create urgency around partnership - Connected to compute decision timeline (one year out) ### Next Steps - [x] Matt: Follow up with Microsoft today, tease Flux.2 discussion ### \| BFL / MSFT - Weekly {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: Matt Smallwood, Sanjana Tandon - MSFT Account Team: - Matt Hacker - Account Executive at MSFT for past 1.5 years - Based Chicago - Jordan Philipson - Azure Specialist / Specialist of Cloud and AI - Based in Seattle - Can help set up technical sessions - Not on call Artem Lovan (Cloud Solutions Architect) **Agenda** - Travel: First week of November will be in Amsterdam - Meet and Greet with Matt - Slack Messages - We should share more for capacity planning - Had some challenges with this in the past - capacity planning needs - impact of video launch and impact to our business without additional capacity - no longer BFL + Msft weekly tech sync, no future growth planning - MSFT could support, they’d bring in Artem **Summary** - **Action Items** - **Rough Notes** - Do we have a separate engineering sync? - \[MH\] Not ongoing. Pivoted to something that included Nvidia - Future growth planning might be helpful. - Mike Gaal is on top of our account and keenly aware of usage. - Constant discussion internally around some of the issues we’ve encountered. ### \| Matt / Benjamin Gauthey {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** - BFL: - MSFT: - Benjamin Gauthey ### **Discussion Topics / Key Notes** - **Relationship Building** - Intro call with Benjamin (10 yrs at MSFT, joined via Clipchamp acquisition). - Benjamin’s org oversees video across Windows, M365, Office, PowerPoint, and Copilot. - **Microsoft Leadership Context** - Recent meeting 9/15 included Clipchamp CEO, Anna (Head of Product), JD (Head of Engineering). - Team impressed with Black Forest’s storyboard-first approach vs. direct text-to-video. - MSFT wants multiple model options beyond OpenAI (cost/performance flexibility). - **Current Priorities** - Image models (Designer) are foundation for video workflows. - Derek’s team owns orchestration for Designer; John Nack (handling evals) has left, transition underway. - Designer acts as an agent service—other teams call images first, then use in video creation. - **Video Model Opportunity** - Michelle’s team handles video creation products (Clipchamp + Copilot text-to-video). - They want a 45–60 min session (capabilities + Q&A), replaying last week’s overview for implementation team. - Deep dive session on use cases and integration design can follow later. - Microsoft recognizes adoption will take time; Q&A session is acceptable for now. - **Commercial & Technical Path** - Models deployed through Azure with secure MSFT tenants (compliance, Fortune 2000 coverage). - For MSFT products, models run on their GPUs with red-teaming before production. - Flux commercial agreement for images nearly complete. - Video model timeline still uncertain; early engagement important for planning. - Joint launch announcement goal for Flux 2 with Copilot/Clipchamp integration. --- ### **Action Items / Next Steps** - [ ] **Matt**: Coordinate 45–60 min presentation with Michelle’s implementation team (with Sumith, target next week). - [ ] **Matt + Benjamin**: Set monthly checkpoint cadence as model progresses. - [ ] **Matt**: Maintain collaboration with Derek’s team on Designer integration. - [ ] Revisit commercial discussion and video model economics once Flux image agreement finalizes.
**Rough Notes** - Last week was a good opportunity for the MSFT + Clipchamp Team to meet the team - Convinced from a leadership perspective that they want to work with us. - Very impressed with the team. - Love what they see what Flux , excited for the video model - Anna oversees all video products at MSFT - Michelle is the person to owns creation in Clipchamp or Copilot - Another team is focused on editing. - Want to partner with the best video, audio, image model. - Have a partnership with OpenAI’s Sora - Like our evals on image generating - Have a team focusing on the video product - Would like to do a similar session to what we did last week. They would be the team responsible for implementation - 45-60min intro session - Second next step would be to talk about what is possible, potential use cases, etc. - Want to work with the product as soon as they can - 1st scenario in Copilot, someone wants a video. When should they pull certain information from different sources. When do they use the BFL video model. - It’s okay that no additional progress has been made - Like the approach, ie. storyboarding, how it’s different from the market. - Be more of a Q&A. From there would be interested in a deeper dive. - Deep dive could be further out. But keep in mind that things take a while at Microsoft. - Will take time to put it into the product. - Image model - Are a sister team with Derek and Alex on Designer around all image generation. - When generating an video, might want to start with a image. - Images/FLUX are an ingredient. - Provider for images is design Update on Designer: - John left who was working on Evals - Derek’s team is taking that over Flow - \> Model is put on Azure → Made available internally or enternally via Foundry (deployed on GPU and paid on usage). For MSFT products, they take the model and put it on their own GPUs. Red team it Derek’s team is working on the orchestration. Next steps - Set up time with Product Team - Set up check points 1x1 as the model progresses
### \| Azure Foundry (MaaS) {toggle="true"} ### Attendees: - **BFL:** , - **Microsoft:** - **Nanditha Ram** (GTM/BD lead for AI Catalyst Team, building AI partner ecosystem. Formerly Google. Based in Seattle) - New org - AI Catalyst Team, working with VCs and enterprise companies to find the right distribution points (e.g Fal, Replicate, A16Z, etc) - connection points. Commonality there. - **Daniel Epstein** (Partner Technology Strategist. Based in Chicago.) - Background in broadcast and network media. - **Bella Valentini** (BD—helped on the deal; available for support. Based in LA.) ### Summary - **Formal handoff to execution**: MSFT AI Partner Catalyst (Nandita + Daniel) will own coordination across **Foundry reseller + product integrations** (Designer, Clipchamp), with BBE/BD still supporting. - **Cadence + operating model**: One coordinated forum spanning **Product Enablement / GTM / Distribution**, with a **Teams “Team” + channels** per workstream and a shared board (**Azure DevOps or GitHub Projects; or map to BFL’s tool if preferred**). - **Other Teams:** - **Designer**: Momentum improving (GPU constraints removed). Need steady **working-team cadence** to avoid stalls; MSFT to help “connect the dots” across internal product orgs. - **Clipchamp**: Awareness gap on model access; MSFT to connect the dots so the team can **test BFL models internally**. - **Reseller motion**: Live \~1 month but **little enablement done** yet. MSFT to share **telemetry dashboard** (weekly refresh) and early pipeline signals. - **Competitive positioning**: MSFT wants crisp **differentiation vs. “Nano Banana”** et al., plus **evals, prompts, and talk tracks** for field enablement. - **Roadmap**: **Flux 2 (text→image)** coming “soon”; **Video** in progress. C**ontractual renegotiation** required for video economics; **Flux 2** itself follows existing image model mechanics. ### Action Items / Next Steps **Microsoft** - [ ] **Spin up shared workspace**: Create a Teams space with channels per workstream (Designer, Clipchamp, Reseller/GTM) and propose a tracking board (Azure DevOps or GitHub Projects). - [ ] **Coordinate product orgs**: Daniel to plug into Designer and connect Clipchamp to internal access so they can test BFL models. - [ ] **Telemetry access**: Share telemetry dashboard links (from Malvika’s team) and ensure BFL can accept invites. - [ ] **Reseller signal**: Bring an early read on reseller motion (inbound activity, early pipeline) to next sync. - [ ] **Assign Partner Dev Specialist**: Replace Sarah’s role and introduce the new contact at/around the next meeting. - [ ] **GTM ideation**: Draft a 3-pronged approach (developer communities, startups, enterprise) to review with BFL post sharing of enablement materials. **BFL** - [ ] **Forward correspondence**: Share recent Designer (Derek’s team) and Clipchamp email threads with MSFT. - [ ] **Enablement materials**: Provide evals, prompt guides, and competitive positioning (esp. vs. Nano Banana) for MSFT field enablement. - [ ] **Hackathon**: Propose early-October dates, 3–4 prioritized use cases, and suggested attendees. - [ ] **Roadmap briefing**: Share demo clips/notes for Flux 2 and Video under NDA to help MSFT plan at future sync **Joint / Scheduling** - [ ] **Set cadence**: Align on a weekly sync starting the week of Sept 29. - Proposed times: Tue 9/30 (8–9am PT), Wed 10/1 (9–11am PT), Thu 10/2 (10–11am PT). ### \| Sumith Summary of Clipchamp Meeting {toggle="true"} - \~5 leadership crew of clipchamp came by the office, we had a kino session w/ [@Axel](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U06QDSK6MED) with a lunch follow-up. takeaways: - overall they found kino compelling, they were quite excited for the control/speed parts of it - for an integration with clipchamp (both video / image) – the most important factors & blockers, in order of priority, are i) compliance / safety – getting through msft’s RAI, ii) cost to afford their scale / budget, iii) least is performance / quality / control as long as its way off. don’t need bleeding edge quality. - It would be easiest to get the integration done if the cost can already be justified in the \$30/mo copilot sku - Higher cost can also be done but will take longer, they are considering higher tier skus for copilot where it could be slotted in - Said sora 1 integration didn’t happen mostly for a cost reason and quality is anyways toy-ish. Hypothetically if a sora 2 integration were to happen, it could be in a higher sku hence both cost / quality are no longer concerns. - For the compliance / safety / RAI, can already start working on it even if the model is still finishing up training – use an early ckpt to check it off - All stakeholders to be convinced are in the clipchamp team itself - VP (then ceo of clipchamp) said multiple times that they “haven’t fully onboarded to MSFT timelines” and can move in a much faster pace / help navigate msft processes if needed - There were a few discussions about efficient/smaller model that could be even cheaper or run on device etc and what our plans around those were - We could explore both images & videos. their CPO (Anna) was very keen and said she’ll initiate an email thread to follow-up with action items, [@Sanjana](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U087P9SULFJ) will loop you in to take it forward. doing an image integration seems no brainer and video one will let you guys decide - ❓Questions from Clipchamp: - How much revenue do we expect to drive from photo models vs video? - Why are we prioritizing steerability over speed, quality, cost? - Is there a single model or are they separate models? - What are our timelines on the video model? (Ask on two separate occasions) ### **Additional **[**Context shared over Slack**](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1758177708.103309/1758177708.103309)** ** **Sanjana🌴 **[Thursday at 1:34 AM](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1758184480.783209/1758177708.103309) [@Sumith](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U06PUJ0BT54) are they aware of our partnership with Foundry (so they can use image today on their own GPUs and pay us 11.2% of list price)? On video, we are contractually obligated to negotiate Foundry to also carry those models, and will hopefully arrive at a cost to them that they can stomach in the \$30/month copilot sku **Sumith **[Thursday at 10:47 AM](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1758217661.254099/1758177708.103309) > Nice! How much used is Clipchamp? If it's having decent distribution we can work with them to become a launch partner for the video model I think they are native video editors / video experience across all of msft (shipped in device, video features in copilot etc). I would say distribution would be massive. > @Sumith [@Sanjana](slackUser://black-forest-labs.slack.com/U087P9SULFJ) yes they are! lets connect with their cpo on the best of getting this through, seems just as promising as Designer if not more due to their agility to move fast they have a feature where they automatically create videos by pulling stock assets, adding voiceovers and stitching them together etc. images could be nice addition there as well ### \| Flux in MSFT Discussion Follow-Up {toggle="true"} Deck Shared: :google_slides_logo_-2014-2020-:[https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1NIn4r_Yme0CtN_M66cfl-rezCRwAh5OSzmAIEzxcH-s/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1NIn4r_Yme0CtN_M66cfl-rezCRwAh5OSzmAIEzxcH-s/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167) - Includes PPT specific use-cases + benchmarks ### Summary - **MSFT is bullish** on Flux for **PowerPoint/Copilot** scenarios, across two goals: - **1) Product Improvement **- Primary Use cases: 1) presentation-level styling, 2) icon generation at scale, 3) agent-generated multi-slide presentations, 4) multi-turn edits - 2) **Latency & cost** (GPU constraints are real at MSFT scale) - **Momentum:** - MSFT seemed really excited and engaged (big smiles throughout meeting). Want to build the best quality product with Flux. - GPU access hiccup (had 500 GPUs that were reassigned to another team). However, building and** testing is unblocked**; will send prototypes this week. - Eager to setup a hackathon between teams to identify what’s possible. Want to this ASAP. - **Immediate Next Steps:** - This Week: - **MSFT Send prioritized scenario list** (PPT restyle, icons, infographics) - **MSFT to share prototype links**. - Work with Asha/Bella on Flux-2 launch in Foundry - Next 30 days: - Host a joint hackathon in Mountain View between teams (target ASAP) - Next Month: - Coordinate onsite late October in Mountain View while Andi is in SF --- ### **What Microsoft said (key signals)** {toggle="true"} - **Goal Prioritization:** - 1) **Quality that improves the product for customers **(PowerPoint/Copilot) - **Priority scenarios (seemed similar to announcements from **[**Gamma 3.0**](https://gamma.app/insights/introducing-gamma-3-0)**):** - **Presentation-level restyle**: Style all slides to a reference image. - **Per-slide icon packs**: Generate **N icons** aligned to bullets based on the content. - **Agent-generation: **Collaborating with an agent to generate a 10-20 slide deck at a time. - **Infographics/diagrams**: Multi-turn editing + text fidelity. → Very important use case for Microsoft that they hope Flux2 can solve. - 2) **Latency & cost** (GPU constraints are real at MSFT scale) - **Momentum:** - Copilot/PowerPoint teams are excited and engaged (big smiles throughout meeting) - Want to build the best quality product with Flux - GPU access hiccup (had 500 GPUs that were reassigned to another team) - However, building and** testing is unblocked**; will send prototypes this week. - Eager to setup a hackathon between teams to identify what’s possible. Want to this ASAP. - **Risks** - **Lack of GPUs:** Internally struggling to secure GPUs. Had 500 secured which were given to another team at the last minute. - **Flux-2 timing:** Risk / concern of shipping Flux-1 right before Flux-2 and having duplicate work. - **Evals:** Our evals vs MSFT Evals - Nidhi mentioned they ran evals and were impressed with our performance. - MSFT is happy to **auto-route to Flux** where evals show clear win on **quality and/or cost/latency**. If results are a tie, they won’t switch as it’s not worth the effort. Need to know when to route to us vs GPT. --- ### **What we shared** {toggle="true"} - **Highlights:** - Playground Demo of Kontext - PowerPoint Specific Examples (All sub-10s operations in demo conditions) - Context-aware image generation/editing from PPTX parsing (text content, color schemes, image content) → prompt sampling (LLM-nano) → Flux prompt → write-back. - Bounding-box and masking options for localized edits - Transparent background pipeline (green-screen trick) - Human-preference evals showing Flux Kontext Pro on-par SOTA with much lower latency. - **Flux-2 preview:** \~2 months out. Focusing on maximizing quality (multi-image editing, stronger world understanding, long text, multilingual text). - We’ll discussed future updates and coordinating launch with Foundry. ### \| Matt / Sanjana Microsoft re: Azure Issue {toggle="true"} ## **People** - **Azure compute:** AM **Matthew Hacker**; BD lead **Mike Gaal**; AI Infra **Nidhi Chappell**. - **MaaS/Product:** **Bella Valentini**, **Rajat Gupta**; PMs **Derek Johnson**, **John Nack**; Strategy **Nanditha Ram**. ## Summary - **(Dave) Azure credits:** Received; no outstanding billing issue. - **(Patrick/Tim) Stability:** Azure infra issues appear **resolved** for now. - Weekly (Monday) acct syncs with Matthew Hacker (AM) exist but often light or cancelled. - **Delivery vs. config:** - GB200 delivery dates slipped (May/Jun) but were accepted by BFL - The **rack/config** delivered didn’t match the “standard” BFL expected, however **not explicitly contracted**. - Early instability expected given **new chips**; BFL didn’t seek 100% credits—argued for **shared risk**. - **SLAs/claims:** - **Not centrally tracked** today. - Need a clear, written SLA map + claims process with MSFT AM. - **Strategic posture / optionality:** - Contract through **end of next year**; shorter than the 3-yr push → preserves **flexibility**. - Switching clouds for **training** is **months of work**; should be pre-planned if pursued. - **GCP** product integrations less viable near-term; **AWS** marketplace strong but listing often tied to AWS compute usage (exceptions exist; bandwidth constrained). - **Product integration (Copilot/Designer/PowerPoint):** - Blocked by **model confidence** + **infra perception** - Continued relationship mgmt needed. - **Ownership shift:** Sanjana plans to step back from weekly infra meetings after transition to Matt. - **MaaS (Model-as-a-Service):** - Deal signed; **unknown performance** post-sign (Sanjana hasn’t been engaged by MSFT sellers yet). - Need to clarify **seller incentives, routing, billing,** and enablement materials. - North-star example: **Anthropic × AWS** marketplace motion. - **Focus areas (near-term):** 1. **Microsoft in-product integration** (Copilot/Designer/PowerPoint) 2. **MaaS performance & scale** (seller motion, listings, regions, billing) 3. **Continued Infra stability** --- ## ### ** \| Microsoft / Clipchamp Prep** {toggle="true"} **Attendees:** , , **Draft Deck:** [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ZkvMb_qDBKwV9Xh4RarEo1uVUPXyQqdSNva1AtTVtWk/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ZkvMb_qDBKwV9Xh4RarEo1uVUPXyQqdSNva1AtTVtWk/edit?slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167#slide=id.g361fd0d658a_0_167) **Context** - Clipchamp (Microsoft’s quick & easy video editor tool) team visiting SF office. - Purpose: Preview of our **video roadmap**, not a formal pitch/demo. - Current status: No integration into MSFT products yet. - Reality: We don’t want this meeting but can’t pass it up → keep it light, don’t overshare. --- ### **Key Points from Discussion** - **Positioning** - Emphasize: we’re working on **foundational models**. - Model is particularly strong for **ideation** (fast iteration, previews). - Our differentiator: workflow speed + professional-grade ideation (generate low-res previews in \<10s → select → upscale). - **Content Strategy** - No need for full company overview. - Use **“cherries” = cherry-picked best content/results**. - Clarify: “Flux Video” (placeholder name) in training now → TBD if this exact model is released. - **Depth / Guardrails** - Important to **decide how much to share** (roadmap vs. technical detail). - Microsoft is contractually entitled to analyze once released, but not guaranteed reseller deal unless financials agreed. - Guidance needed from Axel: how deep to go, what not to reveal. - **Storyline (suggested)** 1. We started with foundation models → image editing → now moving into video. 2. Goal: combine speed + professional workflow → unique differentiation vs. Runway, Sora. 3. Model structure: fast low-res previews → select → upscale. 4. Future potential: combine with kontext / image editing for richer workflows - **Meta** - We’ve often **overestimated MSFT teams’ technical depth** → keep explanations simple, anchor on outcomes. - Opportunity to reuse/adapt this deck for Adobe roadshow next week (likely higher integration potential). ### \| Context from Slack for Designer Team {toggle="true"} :slack: [Slack Link](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C07FKH3C36Y/1757916386.770019/1757916386.770019) **Resources Shared** [Prompting Guide - Image-to-Image - Black Forest Labs](https://docs.bfl.ai/guides/prompting_guide_kontext_i2i) [Prompting Guide - Text to Image - Quick Reference - Black Forest Labs](https://docs.bfl.ai/guides/prompting_summary) 📄** **[**FLUX.1 Kontext: Flow Matching for In-Context Image Generation and Editing in Latent Space**](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.15742) **Context** --- - Microsoft (via John Nack (9/15 is last day at Microsoft)) is running evals of **Flux Kontext** for image editing. - Their early results show mixed performance compared to competitors like **Qwen-Image** and **GPT-4o imagegen**. - Meeting with Microsoft scheduled for **Wednesday**; internal prep ongoing. --- ### **Key Points from Slack (shared by Sanjana)** - **Microsoft eval summary (John Nack via Derek’s team):** - Dataset: 100 prompts (face/product preservation + general edits). - Eval methods: - *Modification fidelity & visual quality* → BinaryEval (LLM-based). - *Preservation* → Segmentation Consistency, DINO similarity, AuraFace. - Results: - Flux Kontext **better than GPT-4o** at preserving non-edited regions. - **Worse than Qwen-Image** on prompt-following & modifications. - Missing real multi-turn (no conversation history support). Needs engineering work. - **Andi’s reaction:** - Need to **educate Microsoft** on our definition of “multiturn” (demo it). - Auto evals miss **image quality/artifacting**, where Flux is stronger. - Suggests **human eval** on Microsoft’s prompts if Flux \> Qwen. - Asked Sumith to confirm if Qwen vs Flux comparison already exists. - **Robin’s input:** - Suggest **deep dive into Microsoft’s actual prompts** (sampling settings may affect results). - Notes AuraFace was in BFL’s own tech report, so careful about contradicting. - **Jakob’s prep plan for Wednesday:** - Demo (PPT, contextual visualizations, transparent BG). - Editing live in PPT. - Benchmark slides (4o vs Flux Kontext Pro). - Add benchmarks vs Qwen using KontextBench + Microsoft’s eval setup. - Possibly share **eval scripts** so MSFT can run them themselves. --- ### **Implications for the Microsoft Relationship** - **Risk:** Microsoft’s evals currently favor Qwen over Flux. - **Opportunity:** Highlight Flux’s superior **quality/artifact handling** and **preservation**, plus human eval wins. - **Action Items:** - Run Qwen vs Flux benchmarks internally (Sumith). - Prepare clear **demo + benchmarks** for Wednesday. - Educate Microsoft on **multiturn editing definition**. - Ask for **Microsoft’s actual prompts** to rerun on Flux. - Package **eval scripts** for them (positions BFL as collaborative partner). ### \| Summary of Azure Issue for Matt {toggle="true"} ## **TL;DR** - **Severe instability + under-spec rack density** since early June led to major downtime and inefficiency. - **Credits/Relief secured:** \$1.8M (7/18), then **\$2.6M** (8/12) for June–mid-July **+ 100% discount on PAYGO GB200 through Sep 30** (RI charges still apply). - **Gaps:** Credits not yet visible in portal; mechanics/appearance unclear. No firm ETA to reach acceptable **rack density (≥16 nodes/rack)** or sustained stability. Open Questions: - Were credits applied? - Are we still having issues? - What is the status of the deployment? - Where can we track SLAs? - What’s the process for future claims? - Are we still meeting weekly? ## **Timeline & Key Events** - **Jun 27:** BFL escalates: delays, NCCL/NVLINK/networking errors; \<50% VMs usable for multi-node; requests compensation. - **Jun 30:** Azure AI Infra lead (Nidhi) engages; proposes **weekly call**; Nvidia’s Ian Buck available. - **Jul 18:** Microsoft offers **\$1.8M Azure credit**; asks about **returning \~1,500 H100s by 7/31** (planning). - **Jul 29:** Nidhi: **NVL72 unhealthy broadly** (not just BFL); owes better timeline. - **Jul 28 → Jul 28 email from Patrick:** BFL calculates **12.5% usable time in June**; billed ≈ **\$5.2M** (Jun–mid-Jul). Credit offered \~⅓ of cost; asks closer to **½**; details **rack density shortfall** and **median \~2h to node failure**; requests plan/commitment on density & reliability. - **Aug 11:** “Today’s cluster upgrade” expected to improve BFL-specific limits (e.g., full memory not usable). - **Aug 12:** Microsoft approves **\$2.6M credit** (June–mid-July) **+ 100% discount on PAYG GB200 usage through Sep 30**; BFL pays only RIs; on-demand GB200s free if MS requires on-demand usage. - **Aug 18:** BFL accepts moving forward with the June–mid-July credit. - **Aug 25:** BFL Finance (Dave) says **no credit visible in portal**; asks for **form/timing** (credit note vs. invoice deduction). **Mike**: Finance/billing (Matthew Beckett, Jordan Philipson) will walk through mechanics. ## **What’s actually broken (technical)** - **Usability:** Only **12.5% usable time in June**; frequent **node failures** (median \~2h to failure), unresponsive nodes. - **Density:** Racks far below **NVL72-like density**; averages around **\~9–10 nodes/rack** vs. target ≥16; efficiency losses confirmed by BFL tests and external validation. - **Stability:** CUDA/NCCL/NVLINK/network issues; large manual redeployments; multi-node training severely limited. ## **Commercial concessions to date** - **\$1.8M** credit (7/18) → superseded by - **\$2.6M** credit for **June–mid-July** (8/12). - **PAYG GB200 at 100% discount through Sep 30** (RIs still billable). - Promise to **guide SLA-bound credit requests** for future instability. ## **Open Items / Risks** - **Credit visibility & accounting:** Not showing in Azure portal yet; unclear **how/when** applied (credit memo vs. invoice deduction). - **Rack density & stability plan:** No **committed ETA** or milestone path to ≥16 nodes/rack and sustained stability. - **Cost leakage risk:** Even with PAYGO relief, **RI charges + inefficiency** could keep TCO elevated if density remains low. - **Relationship risk:** BFL flagged concern about **SOTA engineering support** and long-term partnership confidence. ## **Suggested next steps (owner → ask → outcome)** - **Finance (Dave) ↔ MS Billing (Beckett/Philipson):** Get a **written memo of credit application mechanics**, schedule of postings, and how it will reflect on specific subscription(s)/invoices. Confirm **dates and amounts**, and **evidence in portal**. - **Infra leads (Patrick/Tim) ↔ Nidhi/Kanchan:** Secure a **dated remediation plan** to reach **≥16 nodes/rack** (or agreed alternative) with **weekly milestones** (density, node failure MTBF, pass/fail gates). - **Cost tracking (BFL Finance):** Build a **variance tracker**: RI spend vs. expected, effective utilization, incremental cost due to sub-density. Tie to **make-good triggers**. - **SLA credits playbook:** Pre-agree **SLO/SLA thresholds** (e.g., uptime, node failure rate) that auto-trigger **credit amounts** without re-negotiation. - **H100 return audit:** Close the loop on **whether the 7/31 return** happened (or updated plan) and any downstream billing impacts.

33ac3702-22d5-8006-842a-dc3f7e38f039.title: FLUX 3 - Nailing Hero Use Cases
33ac3702-22d5-8006-842a-dc3f7e38f039.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/33ac370222d58006842adc3f7e38f039 as of 2026-04-07T19:44:09.329Z: {"title":"FLUX 3 - Nailing Hero Use Cases"} The purpose of this doc is to align on the use cases that we must nail with FLUX 3 to be competitive and get commercial success. ## What are the Priority Capabilities for FLUX 3? {toggle="true"} Tier 1 - Image to Video - Text to Image - Image to Image - Video to Video Tier 2 - Text to Video ## What are the Priority High Level Use Cases for FLUX 3? {toggle="true"} Tier 1 - Ecommerce - Advertising / MKG Tier 2 - Social Media ## What are the Priority Low Level Use Cases for Video? {toggle="true"} Tier 1
Photorealism The bar is "brand manager approves for a paid campaign without caveats" — not "impressive for AI." Audiences reject anything that looks synthetic.
Reference Object Fidelity Exact reproduction of labels, textures, colors, and proportions from the input image. Zero hallucination — a distorted logo on a product spin is a launch blocker.
Cross-Clip Consistency Same product or character looks identical across every clip in a campaign. 20 ad variants = pixel-consistent appearance in all 20.
Deterministic Camera Control Specifiable orbits, pans, zooms, tracking shots. E-commerce: smooth 360° with consistent lighting. Advertising: dolly, crane, rack focus.
Surgical Video Edits Swap backgrounds, product variants, or text overlays while everything else stays pixel-identical. Key constraint: fidelity preservation across multiple edit rounds with no drift. Video Kontext — unchanged regions are untouched, not re-generated.
Instant Edit Turnaround Edits like swapping a background or updating text should return in seconds, not trigger full video regeneration. Architecturally, edits must operate on existing latent representations, not re-run the full pipeline.
Video Style Transfer Apply color grading, stylistic filters, or brand aesthetics to existing footage without regenerating content.
Tier 2
Multi-Keyframe Generation Provide N keyframes (not just start or start+end) and the model generates coherent motion between all of them. Multi-keyframe unlocks precise narrative control — specify exact moments and the model fills transitions faithfully.
Typography & Animated Text Deterministic font, color, size, and animation style across campaign variants — variant #1's headline treatment = variant #20's. Text that appears, animates, and exits with transitions (fade, slide-in, typewriter, kinetic). Likely requires style-reference conditioning.
Motion Graphics & Animation Transitions (wipes, dissolves, geometric reveals), logo animations (scale up, particle assembly, draw-on), animated data (charts that build, counters, process flows), and kinetic effects on static assets (Ken Burns, parallax, dynamic cropping). Collapses post-production workflows into single generation calls.
Layer Compositing Semi-transparent overlays, lower thirds, badges, and UI elements composited into the scene. Most ad and social content is layered, not a single shot.
Tier 3
Custom Font Rendering Render specific brand fonts accurately. Likely requires font-conditioning input (upload font file) rather than prompt-based inference.
Multi-Angle Scene Generation Same scene from 3–5 camera positions for editorial cutting.
Useful references: - ## What are the Hard Constraints? {toggle="true"} - **Duration:** 45–60 seconds minimum. - **Resolution:** 1080p minimum. - **Aspect Ratios:** at least 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5. - **Speed:** Generation at least competitive with leading models, without being at the expense of quality. Editing near-real-time. ## What Good looks like for our Hero Use Cases? {toggle="true"}
Product 360° Spin (Ecommerce) A product (e.g., sneaker, handbag, electronics device) on a clean background does a smooth, complete 360° rotation. Logo, material details, and geometry stay pixel-perfect throughout. \~10 seconds.
**Maps to:** Reference Object Fidelity, Deterministic Camera Control
**Customer signal:** Photoroom (#1 pain point: product accuracy degrades during rotation), Walmart (abandoned 360° spins due to hallucination), Envato (product showcase is 83% of volume)
Fashion Virtual Model Walk (Ecommerce) An AI-generated model wearing a user's garment walks toward camera, pauses, turns, walks away. Garment drape, texture, and brand details stay consistent. 1:1 or 9:16 aspect ratio, \~8 seconds.
**Maps to:** Reference Object Fidelity, Cross-Clip Consistency, Photorealism
**Customer signal:** Photoroom (virtual model animation is #1 use case), Envato (bring-image-to-life is #2 use case)
Automotive Hero Shot (Advertising) A luxury car drives through a mountain road — tracking shot that follows the car laterally (Russian arm style). Reflections, paint finish, and wheel geometry stay accurate. \~10 seconds.
**Maps to:** Deterministic Camera Control, Reference Object Fidelity, Photorealism
**Customer signal:** Omnicom (#2 and #7 use cases — automotive key visuals and TVC motion; Russian arm specifically flagged as missing from all models)
Product in Lifestyle Context (Advertising) A warehouse product photo of a kitchen appliance is transformed into a lifestyle scene — the appliance sits on a counter, steam rises, hands interact with it. Natural, subtle movement — not exaggerated. \~15 seconds.
**Maps to:** Photorealism, Reference Object Fidelity, Surgical Video Edits
**Customer signal:** Walmart (#1 use case: raw warehouse images → lifestyle marketing video), Photoroom (unnatural/exaggerated movement is pain point #2).
Designed Social Ad from Product Image (Advertising / Social) From one product photo, generate a 15-second social-ready ad with motion graphics, animated headline, price badge, and CTA. Designed compositions with text and graphic overlays, not just camera shots. 9:16 primary, \~15 seconds.
**Maps to:** Motion Graphics & Animation, Typography & Animated Text, Multi-Keyframe Generation
**Customer signal:** Canva (#1 ask: coherent multi-shot generation), Walmart (promotional videos). Distinct from "Product in Lifestyle" — this is *designed* ad creative, not photorealistic footage.
Background Swap on Existing Video (V2V Editing) A product demo video where the background environment changes from a studio to a beach to a kitchen — while the foreground product and hand motion stay pixel-identical. \~10 seconds showing 3 variants.
**Maps to:** Surgical Video Edits, Instant Edit Turnaround
**Customer signal:** Omnicom (V2V localization: UK kitchen → Spanish kitchen), our V2V editing research (background swap is #1 editing use case)
Text & CTA Overlay Swap (V2V Editing) A promotional video where the headline text, price tag, and CTA button change between variants — "Save 20%" → "Spare 20%" → "Ahorre 20%" — while the video footage stays identical. Animated text elements (fade-in headlines, sliding price tags, pulsing CTA buttons) should render with typographic precision across all variants. \~6 seconds × 3 variants.
**Maps to:** Surgical Video Edits, Instant Edit Turnaround, Typography & Animated Text
**Customer signal:** Walmart (near-zero hallucination on text is #1 capability ask), Omnicom (screen content localization for Apple is #1 use case)
Style Transfer on Existing Footage (V2V Editing) Take raw footage of a product unboxing and apply a warm, cinematic color grade that matches a brand's visual identity. Same footage, 3 style variants side-by-side. \~8 seconds.
**Maps to:** Video Style Transfer
**Customer signal:** Omnicom (style transfer is a production need), our V2V research (style transfer & color grading is #3 editing use case)
