Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/270c370222d5801da30ad71d300fb1da as of 2026-04-16T14:13:26.649Z: {"Account Owners":[""],"Company":"Samsung Notes","Latest Status / Tasks":"","Partner Category":"OEM","Status":"Not started","Sub-item":["https://www.notion.so/344c370222d580288fa7e10a8edc8f97"],"url":"https://www.notion.so/270c370222d5801da30ad71d300fb1da"} **Latest Resources:** [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1uINdiDgn81sF5v_urm7uoTTyBKTdBCYEoT7UTN7qXgY/edit?slide=id.g3d1e2cd5592_0_151#slide=id.g3d1e2cd5592_0_151](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1uINdiDgn81sF5v_urm7uoTTyBKTdBCYEoT7UTN7qXgY/edit?slide=id.g3d1e2cd5592_0_151#slide=id.g3d1e2cd5592_0_151) ## Partner Overview ---
**Key Objectives**
Objective Status Expected Outcomes Details / Follow Ups
1. Win Galaxy Z Fold 8 (H2 2026) API integration for image generation & editing WIP Become BFL's first flagship device API integration April feature freeze likely unrealistic per Robin (Mar 25 HQ visit). Second window closes end of November. Inpainting (mask-based editing) is the most viable existing use case to replace. Image enhancement (moire/blur) is a net-new opportunity requiring finetuning — Samsung needs an endpoint to test ASAP. Character consistency is the primary gap flagged by Samsung in FLUX.2 testing. Pricing call \~Mar 30.
2. Secure weights license for Gallery stack + image enhancement use case WIP Anchor BFL inside Samsung's foundational image AI layer; licensing + self-hosting preferred by Samsung Samsung strongly interested in licensing (including Pro models) and self-hosting. Two finetuning paths on the table: BFL does it, or Samsung gets base weights + finetunes themselves. Samsung also asked about finetuning code/pipelines and safety checking components. FP4 (Blackwell) and fp8 inference of high interest for cost/latency. Pricing call \~Mar 30. NDA with R&D team needed ASAP.
3. Establish on-device model partnership (Samsung Mobile Cloud) In Progress Long-term on-device deployment of distilled BFL model (Klein 4B / NanoFLUX) across Samsung flagship lineup Klein 4B pitched for on-device; Galaxy Z Fold 8 (H2 2026) target device; working with Pruna; technical requirements still being scoped
4. Accelerate trust & executive relationship WIP Unlock faster decision-making at Samsung HQ (Korea); reduce startup risk perception Mark Kim (Samsung Next) used \$100mm ARR (Aug 2025) + \$300M Series B (Dec 2025) to address concerns with Minju about BFL stability; in-person Seoul meeting being explored
**Upcoming Events**
Date Event Name Purpose Attendees Action Items
Fri Mar 13, 2026 (8AM CET) Samsung MX Cloud Weights License Call Discuss technical details, customization (object removal, outpainting), and licensing structure for Gallery stack Robin Rombach, Jakob Pörschmann (BFL); Samsung MX Cloud team Jakob to drop object removal + outpainting examples in the deck; Amanda pulling together content
✅ Mar 25, 2026 In-Person Korea Visit (Completed) Executive relationship building; use case alignment; roadmap sharing Robin Rombach (BFL); \~10 Samsung Visual Solution + Tech Strategy members See Mar 25 meeting notes. NDA with R&D team, pricing proposals, finetuning demos, and endpoint access all outstanding.
\~Mar 30, 2026 Pricing Call (Samsung + BFL) Present API and licensing pricing proposals; align on commercial structure for inpainting + image enhancement use cases BFL (Amanda + Robin/Jakob); Samsung Visual Solution + MX Cloud teams BFL to prepare: waterfall API pricing, licensing options including Pro models, finetuning pricing options. Samsung to share volume estimates for inpainting ahead of call.
Recurring Dig Gaurang (UK) Sync UK-side relationship maintenance; Fold8 commercial progress Amanda, Digantam Gaurang Amanda syncing with Dig in London; get update on Korea visit timing
**Relationship History**
2025 - **Early 2025:** Robin had initial conversations with Samsung Next (Raymond Liao, Mark Kim). Discussed on-device potential and API path. Samsung indicated 6-month release cycles. Google identified as primary competitor. Notes: Samsung already using FLUX Schnell for TV screensavers. BFL provided API access to Samsung devs. Draft licensing agreement in place. - **Feb 2025:** Samsung + BFL Partnership Wishlist drafted (Sanjana Tandon). Core focus areas: image gen & editing for Galaxy phones (API preferred short-term), video gen & editing, Samsung internal use (Marketing, Ads, VD screensaver). - **Aug 2025:** Internal pricing analysis by Sanjana. Waterfall API pricing discussed. Samsung's expected usage: \~15.8M image generations/month for Style Transfer + \~10.4M/month for Mask-free Editing = \~26.2M/month combined. - **Sept 16, 2025:** Insight from Mark Kim (Samsung Next). Google charges Samsung \$0.01/generation. Samsung execs prefer to "chip away" from their Google search revenue lump sum rather than hold a separate contract line item. BFL contract timeline for January device launch still on track. - **Sept 22, 2025:** EXT Samsung Sync meeting (Flux 2). Key outcomes: Nano Banana update forced Samsung to retest all scenarios; competitive solutions now performing as well as Flux-Kontext. Samsung confirmed priority use cases: style transfer and mask-free editing. BFL previewed Flux.2 capabilities (4K native, multi-language rendering, 2–4x speed advantage). Samsung committed to apple-to-apple comparisons once early access available. Software freeze deadline: End of October 2025. - **Oct 2025:** Samsung testing window. BFL provided early access endpoint. Minju Seo (MX TSG) and R&D team in Korea evaluating. - **Oct 14–16, 2025:** Minju Seo responded (after Korean Thanksgiving delay). Engineering team feedback shared. Amanda responded clarifying Flux.2 capabilities and addressing open questions on quality vs. latency.
2026 - **Jan 2026:** Samsung internal testing in January. Internal consensus forming to implement FLUX.2 into devices alongside Nano Banana. Minju became unresponsive to Amanda and Andi via email. - **Jan 22, 2026 (GTM Pipeline):** Samsung Mobile listed as \$2.5M deal (Qualified), projected close 2025-12-31 (slipped). Still testing. Samsung raised concerns about BFL's ability to scale if rolled out widely across phones. Samsung asked about a mid-March Korea visit. - **Feb 5–11, 2026:** Dig Gaurang (Samsung UK) pushed for Andi to meet Samsung execs (EVP Ken Song + VP Min Ki Choi) visiting London Feb 26–27. Meeting location confirmed: Samsung R&D Institute UK (SRUK), Communications House, South Street, Staines-upon-Thames, Surrey TW18 4QE. - **Feb 19, 2026:** Mark Kim (Samsung Next) forwarded email from Minju Seo confirming January testing results and internal consensus developing around FLUX.2 + Nano Banana. Samsung inquired about BFL's 2025 revenue and M&A rumors (specifically Apple acquisition). Robin addressed using publicly available info: \~\$100mm ARR (Aug 2025), \$300M Series B (Dec 1, 2025). Samsung declined London in-person meeting. - **Mar 3, 2026:** Mark Kim confirmed (via email) that FLUX momentum is spreading internally at Samsung. Two parallel tracks now confirmed: (1) Fold8 API integration and (2) MX Cloud Gallery stack weights license ; separate teams, may eventually fold into one. **Key intelligence from Mark:** Google changed its contract with Samsung ; MX is now *directly charged* for Gemini services rather than costs being netted from Samsung's Google search revenue. Cost is higher than anticipated internally, driving Samsung to evaluate alternative models. Amanda: "excellent news ; we need to take advantage of the gap." - **Mar 10, 2026:** New Samsung MX Cloud team reached out expressing interest in licensing BFL model weights to upgrade the core Samsung Gallery editing stack across multiple devices. Call scheduled Fri Mar 13. - **Mar 13, 2026:** First technical call with Samsung MX Cloud team (Jaehoon Ko, Hyok Choi). Productive session — object removal with effect erasure confirmed as primary use case. Team shared example image pairs with BFL. Response: "really fruitful." - **Mar 25, 2026:** Robin visited Samsung HQ in Suwon. In-person meeting with \~10 members of the Visual Solution Team and Technology Strategy group. Warm, open, direct tone. Samsung presented failure cases of FLUX.2 \[pro\] — character inconsistency flagged as primary gap. Key outcomes: (1) Fold8 April freeze likely unrealistic but not impossible; (2) inpainting (mask-based editing) is the replaceable existing use case; (3) image enhancement (moire/blur removal) is a net-new opportunity requiring finetuning; (4) strong interest in licensing + self-hosting, including Pro models and finetuning pipelines; (5) FP4/fp8 inference on Blackwells of high interest; (6) pricing call set for \~March 30. NDA with R&D team to be signed ASAP.
**Their Relationship w/ Competitors / Notable Players**
Company Initiative / Announcement Considerations / Follow-up
Google (Nano Banana / Gemini) Samsung's CEO plans to double mobile devices running Galaxy AI (backed by Gemini) to **800 million** devices this year. Google charges Samsung **\$0.01/generation**. Google has now changed its contract: MX is directly charged for Gemini services rather than costs netting out of Samsung's Google search lump sum ; at a higher cost than anticipated. **This is BFL's key opening.** Samsung previously preferred to "chip away" at their Google revenue instead of holding a separate contract. The new direct-charge model makes BFL's offer structurally competitive for the first time. Nano Banana also forced a full retest of all scenarios in Sept 2025 ; quality parity is now achieved per Samsung's own evaluation.
Google (Nano Banana; on-device) Nano Banana model used for on-device inference across Samsung devices. Samsung evaluated Nano Banana alongside FLUX for on-device scenarios. BFL's on-device play is longer-term. Tough to win on API now given Google's embedded position, but on-device via Klein 4B / distilled models is a viable path ; especially with Pruna collaboration. NanoFLUX generates 512×512 images in \~2.5 seconds on mobile, proving feasibility.
**Integration Summary**
Surface Target Date Details & Follow-ups
Galaxy Z Fold 8; API (Image Gen & Editing) H2 2026 (Fall launch) BFL Flux.2 being evaluated for integration into Fold8 device launch. Primary use cases: style transfer, mask-free editing. \$2.5M deal in pipeline (Qualified). Evaluation ongoing with Minju Seo / R&D Korea team.
Galaxy AI; Portrait Studio (Photo Assist) TBD Converts image style when a human face is detected. Currently limited to human faces (4 presets). Samsung wants to expand to broader subject matter. BFL's style transfer capability well-suited.
Galaxy AI; Draw Assist TBD Text or image prompt input. Samsung considering expanding photo editor capabilities. BFL can support text-to-image and image-to-image workflows.
Galaxy Gallery Stack; Weights License (Inpainting + Image Enhancement) \~Mar 30 pricing call Two confirmed use cases from Mar 25 HQ visit: (1) **Inpainting / mask-based editing** — existing deployed use case, replaceable at any time if BFL matches quality + cost; (2) **Image enhancement** (moire/blur removal) — net-new use case replacing Samsung in-house stack, requires finetuning for character consistency. Samsung strongly prefers licensing + self-hosting. FP4 (Blackwell) and fp8 inference of strong interest. Pro model licensing also on the table. Finetuning code/pipelines and safety checking components also discussed. NDA with R&D team needed. Pricing call \~Mar 30.
Samsung TV; Screensavers Active (existing) Samsung already using FLUX Schnell for TV screensavers (Samsung VD). Existing relationship and technical integration.
Samsung Galaxy Books; Remaster Picture Tool TBD From wishlist: offer BFL models/tools on Galaxy Books within the Remaster Picture tool. Not yet formally pursued.
On-Device; Klein 4B (Galaxy Z Fold 8) H2 2026 • BFL pitching Klein 4B (distilled) for on-device deployment.
• Galaxy Z Fold 8 specs (unconfirmed): RAM 12GB or 16GB LPDDR5X, Storage 256GB/512GB/1TB, no dedicated GPU VRAM (shares system RAM).
• Previous on-device requirements based on SD 1.5 (outdated).
• Samsung tested Dev and Schnell for on-device; RAM size is the critical constraint.
**Agreement Overview**
Agreement Type Date Signed General Terms Considerations
Draft Licensing Agreement Not signed Drafted (as of early 2025); not progressed to execution • Sanjana’s handover notes reference a draft agreement on file.
API Access Active (informal) BFL API access provided to Samsung devs for testing • Not a commercial agreement; testing only.
• Commercial T&Cs needed.
NDA MX Mobile Team Complete
(Mar 2026)		 NDA signed with Samsung Mobile team • NDA now in place
**Key POCs** **Samsung Corporate / Ventures** JH Yoon ; Chief Executive Officer Albert Kim ; Head of Samsung Ventures Overseas Division Thomas Jueng ; Sr. Managing Director Raymond Liao ; Founding MD, Samsung Next Mark Kim ; Investment Manager, Samsung Next (key intelligence source; 650.390.5208 / [mark.kim@samsungnext.com](mailto:mark.kim@samsungnext.com)) **Samsung Mobile (MX) ; Tech Strategy** VP Min Ki Choi ; VP of AI Strategy, Samsung Mobile EVP Ken Song ; EVP, Tech Strategy (invited to London meeting around MWC; then cancelled their trip) Minju Seo ; MX TSG; primary R&D technical contact ([minjoo.seo@samsung.com](mailto:minjoo.seo@samsung.com)); has been unresponsive since Jan 2026 Jack Kim ; Samsung contracts team ([jack.kim@samsung.com](mailto:jack.kim@samsung.com)); involved when commercial terms are ready **Samsung UK** Digantam Gaurang ; Technology Sourcing (UK); BFL's main UK-side relationship contact
Customizations Object Removal + Outpainting
--- ## Pricing ---
**API Pricing: FLUX.2 Pro Waterfall (Updated)** ### Volume Assumptions - Samsung's projected usage (may be outdated): **\~26.2M images/month** — 15.8M style transfer (60%) + 10.4M mask-free editing (40%) - Use case is naturally limited to 1 reference image per generation based on in-app flow - Google was previously charging **\$0.01/generation** — our direct competitive benchmark - Samsung launches flagships **twice a year**; existing/deployed use cases can be swapped anytime (not tied to launch windows) ### Updated Waterfall Pricing — FLUX.2 Pro *Assumptions: 1 reference image per generation. Cost for FLUX.1 with 1 ref image: \$0.045 for res ≤ 1MP, up to \$0.135 for 3MP–4MP.*

--- ## Samsung Mobile Cloud /Infra *New initiative as of March 10, 2026. The Samsung Mobile Cloud team is interested in licensing BFL model weights specifically for on-device deployment, to power the Gallery editing stack across multiple Samsung devices. This is separate from the Fold8 API integration. Call scheduled Fri Mar 13 (8AM CET) with Robin + Jakob.* ---
**Agenda: Samsung Mobile Cloud ; Weights License Discussion** ### 1. Technology Roadmap ; What's Coming from BFL Introduce Samsung to BFL's forward-looking model roadmap relevant to on-device deployment. Key points to cover: - BFL's direction on **small, efficient models** (Klein 4B) and the trajectory toward distilled on-device variants - The **Pruna collaboration** for model compression and quantization; directly relevant to on-device feasibility - BFL's unique position: *no other lab* will be able to deliver the quality-to-efficiency ratio we can achieve for mobile-sized models at this stage ### 2. Gallery Applications ; Use Cases for On-Device Deployment Walk through the specific editing scenarios Samsung cares about for the Gallery app: - **Object removal** ; Jakob to bring examples; key requirement for Gallery editing stack - **Outpainting** ; Jakob to bring examples; confirmed interest from MX Cloud team - **Style transfer** ; Samsung found this "really really good"; 4 presets exist for human faces, want to expand to broader subject matter; BFL can deliver this - **Mask-free (natural language-based) editing** ; Major use case - **Inpainting** ; Address open question from last feedback: *how does the script capture inpainting/outpainting/edits as a full image?* - Samsung's current approach to **personalization** has hit limitations ; BFL's fine-tuning capabilities are a competitive differentiator here ### 3. Generating Emojis with BFL Models ; In-Line Creative Feature Present the opportunity for Samsung to deploy BFL models for **inline emoji / sticker generation** across their messaging and keyboard stack: - Users could generate custom emojis or expressive visual elements directly within Samsung's native keyboard or messaging surfaces - Aligns with Samsung's goal to expand Galaxy AI beyond photos into **communication and self-expression** - Latency requirement: image generation for communication has lower quality requirements ; latency matters more here; BFL can optimize for this use case specifically - Native **multi-language character rendering** (Korean, Thai, etc.) is a key BFL advantage ; directly relevant to Samsung's global device base ### 4. On-Device Model Capabilities ; How Capable Can It Be? Address Samsung's technical requirements and constraints for on-device inference: **Device specs (Galaxy Z Fold 8 ; unconfirmed, H2 2026):** - RAM: Up to 12 GB or 16 GB LPDDR5X - Storage: 256 GB, 512 GB, 1 TB - No dedicated GPU VRAM ; GPU shares system RAM (mobile SoC) - Previous on-device requirements Samsung shared were based on SD 1.5 (several years outdated ; no longer the right benchmark) **What we know about on-device feasibility:** - Samsung tested FLUX Dev and Schnell for on-device; RAM size is the critical constraint - NanoFLUX (from recent research) generates 512×512 images in \~**2.5 seconds** on mobile devices ; demonstrating on-device high-quality text-to-image is feasible - A **distilled Klein 4B** could substantially outperform NanoFLUX and enable editing (not just text-to-image) ; Freddy believes a good distillation of Klein 4B "could be much much better and enable editing" - Samsung is **open to changing their entire foundation model** ; the current foundation is not locked **What we need from Samsung to scope this properly:** - Exact device specs from the R&D team (Seong Ju's requirements were based on SD 1.5) - Max VRAM/memory Samsung is willing to allocate to the image model - Target latency per generation for their specific use cases - Which AI models are currently running on-device (to understand the memory budget) ### 5. Small Model Evolution ; Where Are We Headed? Paint the longer-term roadmap for Samsung's planning purposes: - BFL's small model strategy: Klein 4B today → continued distillation and quantization toward mobile-optimized variants - **Collaboration with Pruna** for efficient on-device compression ; Samsung should be aware this work is ongoing - Two paths for Samsung: (a) license weights + BFL handles model optimization for their device specs, or (b) Samsung's R&D team handles on-device conversion with BFL's technical support - From original Samsung feedback: they're interested in either *training a smaller model for a specific use case* or *replacing the foundation model entirely* to improve quality ; BFL can support both paths - On-device is a **multi-year commercial opportunity** ; Samsung expects any integration to continue across future flagship and non-flagship models, not just one device cycle
--- ## Meeting Notes ---
**Apr 16, 2026 - Amanda message to Minju (new main contact)** Hi Minju, Thank you for re-sharing the deck, and for the clarity on use cases across the teams. It's good to hear you will be our main point of contact going forward. I'm assuming this means you will manage our contact with the Technology Strategy team, the Visual Solution team, and the Cloud Infra teams? With that being said, I wanted to make sure you had context across all our current discussions with Samsung, and wanted to see if you had a preference on whether we should also include you in 3.) and 4.) below:**1. Samsung Mobile, Technology Strategy team **(contact: you): We have mainly discussed Flux.1 Kontext and Flux.2 API use for Galaxy S and Fold8 launches (use cases: style transfer, mask-free editing). **2. Samsing Mobile, Cloud Infra Team **(contact: Jaehoon)**: **We have discussed Flux.2 via API and Commercial Weights License (use cases: "Eraser" or inpainting/outpainting, **3. Cheil, New Tech Solution Team** (contact: Taegu Kang, [gugu.kang@samsung.com](mailto:gugu.kang@samsung.com)) We received interest in licensing our Flux.2 models for the creation of advertisement drafts and final commercial deliverables for 10+ major advertisers (To be used for various commercial purposes, including digital content, TV commercials, and event videos).**4. **[**Blueport**](https://www.blueport.co.kr/Index.aspx)**, Samsung Electronics** (Contact: Seungchang Baek, [geni.info@samsung.com](mailto:geni.info@samsung.com)) Blueport is currently licensing Flux.1 Kontext and Dev models on behalf of Samsung Electronics. They would now like access to Flux.2 models. Regarding your comments about the use cases and licensing: **1. "Eraser" (In/outpaining endpoint):** we delivered an update this week to Jaehoon that further improves object removal quality on the combined endpoint we previously shared. We also conducted a human evaluation benchmark against other dedicated object erasing workflows, and our results indicate that we outperform them. - **Our requests: **If there are any (open) datasets closer to your internal benchmarks that you'd like us to test against, we'd be happy to run additional evaluations and share them with you. As you mentioned, we assume the Visual Solutions team will do the evals - is there a rough timing on when they expect to complete those evals? It would also be helpful to understand whether the team would prefer a custom endpoint via our API or licensing options with support on fine-tuning from our team. If via the API, can you provide rough volume estimates? **2. "Remaster":** The team is working on a fine-tuned end-point to share with the Visual Solutions team to show what is possible. I understand the team wants to license our models and run this on-prem. The team can download the model weights via our [repo on HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs) - **Our request: **Can you please share a volume estimate so we can provide pricing options for licensing our model weights? Finally, could we schedule time next week for you and I to discuss progress on use cases and options for licensing our models? Given the number of teams and initiatives, it would be ideal to have time to discuss on a call to ensure we can stay aligned on what your teams need, and make sure we are prioritising accordingly.
**Mar 25, 2026 — Robin @ Samsung HQ, Suwon (In-Person)** *Source: Robin's debrief, March 25, 2026. Attendees: Robin Rombach (BFL) + \~10 Samsung people from the Visual Solution Team and Technology Strategy group.* **Tone & Setting** Open, direct, and warm. Some Samsung attendees are avid BFL fans — one said: *"I know every sentence of the latent diffusion paper."* Samsung presented a deck to Robin (not the other way around), which mostly contained **failure cases of FLUX.2 \[pro\] via API** across different image editing tasks. The biggest identified problem: **character inconsistency** (e.g. unintended changes to race/gender in outputs). **Fold8 Launch Window** Feature freeze is end of April. Robin's assessment: inclusion in this launch window is **"likely unrealistic but not impossible."** A second launch window closes end of November. Samsung launches flagships twice a year; existing/deployed use cases can be replaced at any time (not tied to new device launches), but new feature integrations are. **Key Discussion Points** - **Replacing existing Google use cases is hard.** Google updates their models every 3 months, and the evaluation overhead required to swap makes it difficult. For equal performance between BFL and competition, **cost becomes the determining factor**. - **Existing use case BFL could replace: mask-based image editing (inpainting).** This is a deployed use case not tied to a launch window — can be replaced anytime if BFL can match quality and cost. - **New net-new use case: image enhancement** — removing moire patterns and blurriness from photos (e.g. random shots in challenging conditions). This would replace Samsung's in-house stack entirely. However, FLUX.2 needs finetuning to solve this consistently — Samsung's deck showed too much variation in outputs and insufficient character consistency. - **Strong interest in licensing and self-hosting**, including licensing of Pro models. Two finetuning paths discussed: - (a) BFL performs the finetuning and delivers a custom model - (b) Samsung gets access to the base model weights and does finetuning themselves - Samsung asked whether **BFL provides finetuning code / pipelines** alongside the weights. - Samsung also asked about licensing **other parts of the pipeline**, such as safety checking. Robin indicated BFL is open to licensing those as well. - **FP4 inference on Blackwells** is very interesting to Samsung for cost and latency reasons; **fp8** also of interest. - Samsung wants **access to BFL's model roadmap** to plan future integrations. - **Video:** not interesting now (not "every day use"), but when Robin mentioned targeting **real-time editing**, they became more curious. Not near-term, but flagged as a future opportunity. **Robin's Assessment & Recommended Path Forward** BFL should prioritise supporting the **net-new image enhancement use case**. If BFL moves fast, there may be a chance to hit the end-of-April feature freeze, but Samsung needs an **API endpoint to test ASAP**. The finetuning could potentially be done via synthetic data simulating image degradations (moire, blur). BFL should also pursue the **inpainting use case** (mask-based editing). In combination with **fp8 or fp4 inference**, licensing should become commercially viable. Robin is open to **Pro model licensing** only if a meaningful contract is in sight. **Action Items** *Samsung to deliver to BFL:* - The presentation deck from today's meeting - Their future use cases - Rough volume estimates for inpainting *BFL to deliver to Samsung:* - API and licensing pricing proposals → **pricing call scheduled for \~March 30** - Before/after finetuning comparison demonstrating character consistency improvement (consider using virtual try-on examples) — to be shared with the full group - Updated inpainting demo - Any further examples demonstrating finetuning / customization value, especially re: character consistency *Both sides:* - **Sign NDA between BFL and Samsung R&D team ASAP** (separate from the MX NDA already in place)
**Mar 10, 2026 ; Samsung MX Cloud Weights License (Slack #customerdeals-partnerships)** A new team at Samsung is interested in licensing BFL model weights to upgrade their core Samsung "Gallery" editing stack across multiple devices. This deal could anchor BFL inside Samsung's foundational image AI layer rather than as a feature vendor for specific device launches (e.g., the Fold8, which we are currently being evaluated for as well). **Next steps:** Call scheduled Fri Mar 13 (8AM CET). Robin will join. They would like to discuss technical details of our models, possible customization for specific use cases (object removal, outpainting, etc.), and licensing structure. Jakob confirmed to join for customization discussion ; to drop object removal and outpainting examples in the deck. Amanda has started pulling together content for the presentation.
**Mar 3, 2026 ; Mark Kim Intelligence Update (via Email)** Mark Kim (Samsung Next) confirmed two parallel Samsung initiatives in response to Robin's check-in: 1. **Fold8 integration** and **MX Cloud licensing** are separate initiatives ; different teams within Samsung Mobile/MX. May eventually fold into one, but currently running in parallel. 2. **Google contract change confirmed:** Google has changed its contract with Samsung ; MX is now directly charged for Gemini services as opposed to costs being netted out of Samsung's search revenue. Cost is higher than anticipated internally. This is why MX is now looking for alternative models. *"This is a great opportunity for BFL to jump in."* (Robin forwarded to Amanda, Anthony, and Andi ; treat as confidential.) Mark still awaiting more information on Fold8 integration status.
**Feb 19, 2026 ; Mark Kim / Minju Seo Update (Samsung Next Email)** Mark Kim forwarded an inquiry from Minju Seo (MX TSG) about: (1) BFL's 2025 revenue, and (2) rumors of Apple acquisition interest. Mark's read: Samsung is gauging the stability of a potential commercial partnership ; a constant concern when working with startups. Mark's plan: share \~\$100mm ARR (publicly available, as of August 2025) and confirm no M&A rumors known to him personally. Robin agreed and pointed to the \$300M Series B ([bfl.ai/blog/our-300m-series-b](http://bfl.ai/blog/our-300m-series-b), Dec 1, 2025) as additional supporting information. Also in this thread (from Robin, Feb 19): Samsung declined the London in-person meeting. Amanda will sync with Dig and explore a replacement Korea meeting in March.
**Sept 22, 2025 ; EXT Samsung Sync (Flux 2 launch)** Agenda: (1) Discuss Samsung's experience with Kontext and feedback on pricing, (2) finalize use cases, (3) introduce Flux 2. **Samsung's Current State & Competition Update** - Working on business proposal and service integration use case scenarios - Nano Banana model update forced comprehensive retesting across all scenarios - Competitive solutions (Nano Banana) now performing as good as or better than Flux-Kontext per Samsung's evaluation - Taking significant time to evaluate best solution for user experience on specific Samsung devices project **Technical Requirements & Use Case Priorities** - Quality vs. latency depends heavily on use case: - Image editing: quality more important ; users can wait **10–20 seconds** for superior quality; **over 20 seconds** becomes problematic - Style transfer and mask-free editing remain key requirements - Image generation for communication: quality requirements are lower, latency matters more - Multi-language **rendering** is high priority ; they can translate prompts to English, but native character rendering in images is critical (Korean, Thai, etc.) - New use cases still being developed ; no additional scenarios to share at time of meeting **Flux 2 Model Preview & Capabilities** - Timeline for Flux release: **End of October to end of November** release - Early access availability: within 1–2 weeks for Samsung testing - Currently text-to-image (t2i) only (still in pre-training) - Image editing (i2i) capabilities being added in next 1–2 weeks - Native multi-reference support included - Key features Samsung found compelling: native multi-language prompting and character rendering (Korean, Thai, etc.) - Other Flux.2 characteristics discussed: - Better world knowledge and physics understanding - **4K resolution** native support - Structured JSON prompting for systematic control - Superior text rendering (outperforming GPT Image) - Performance advantage: **2–4x faster** than competition while maintaining quality parity **Critical Timeline & Next Steps** - Samsung flagship device launch: January 2025 \[S25 cycle at time of meeting\] - Software freeze: End of October 2025 - Need feature-complete, QA-ready version **2–3 weeks before freeze** - Latest handover: **October week 1–2** for Samsung testing - BFL follow-ups committed to: - Provide character rendering samples - Share Flux 2 evaluations when available - Set up early access endpoint for Samsung testing within 1–2 weeks - Samsung committed to: run apple-to-apple comparisons using their test sets once early access available
**Sept 16, 2025 ; Insights from Mark Kim (via Email)** *"As you may know, Samsung gets a lump sum payment from Google for making Google our default search engine. Whenever we have service-related costs, they get subtracted from that amount. For executives, they have a preference to 'chip away' from this expected revenue rather than having a separate contract in place that could be considered an expense item. I heard that Google is charging \$0.01 per generation.* *I think we should wait and see what they come back with. I don't think it's the commercial terms that's the issue. The image team also had early access to Google's image model. They're likely answering some questions from executives who may not have been fully plugged into the process but are now asking about Google's model after seeing the buzz around it.* *In terms of the timeline for contracts that need to be in place with partners for our January launch, we are still very much on pace."*

The new direct-charge model makes BFL's offer structurally competitive for the first time. Nano Banana also forced a full retest of all scenarios in Sept 2025 ; quality parity is now achieved per Samsung's own evaluation.
Google (Nano Banana; on-device) Nano Banana model used for on-device inference across Samsung devices. Samsung evaluated Nano Banana alongside FLUX for on-device scenarios. BFL's on-device play is longer-term. Tough to win on API now given Google's embedded position, but on-device via Klein 4B / distilled models is a viable path ; especially with Pruna collaboration. --- ## Pricing ---
**API Pricing: FLUX.2 Pro Waterfall (Updated)** ### Volume Assumptions - Samsung's projected usage (may be outdated): **\~26.2M images/month** — 15.8M style transfer (60%) + 10.4M mask-free editing (40%) - Use case is naturally limited to 1 reference image per generation based on in-app flow - Google was previously charging **\$0.01/generation** — our direct competitive benchmark - Samsung launches flagships **twice a year**; existing/deployed use cases can be swapped anytime (not tied to launch windows) ### Updated Waterfall Pricing — FLUX.2 Pro *Assumptions: 1 reference image per generation. Cost for FLUX.1 with 1 ref image: \$0.045 for res ≤ 1MP, up to \$0.135 for 3MP–4MP.*

**Licensing Pricing: Open Weights — FLUX.2 \[dev\] (Updated)** ### Why Licensing Samsung strongly prefers **licensing + self-hosting** over API access (confirmed Mar 25 HQ visit). This means Samsung licenses the weights and runs inference on their own infrastructure. Key implications: - Per-generation billing doesn't apply — flat annual license is the right structure - Samsung also asked about licensing **Pro models** and **finetuning code/pipelines** - Samsung asked about licensing **other pipeline components** (e.g. safety checking) — Robin indicated openness to this - Two finetuning paths on the table: (a) BFL does the finetuning, or (b) Samsung gets base weights and finetunes themselves ### Volume Assumptions - Samsung's CEO has targeted **800M Galaxy AI-enabled devices** in 2026 - If \~5% of Galaxy AI users generate 1 image/month → **\~40M generations/month** for flagship devices - 26M/month figure (from 2025) was likely Galaxy S-scale; Fold is a smaller launch - Estimated inference cost per image at Samsung's own infra: **\~\$0.03/image** ### Open Weights License — FLUX.2 \[dev\] (Proposed) *Structured per device family. --- ## Samsung Mobile Cloud /Infra *New initiative as of March 10, 2026. The Samsung Mobile Cloud team is interested in licensing BFL model weights specifically for on-device deployment, to power the Gallery editing stack across multiple Samsung devices. This is separate from the Fold8 API integration. Call scheduled Fri Mar 13 (8AM CET) with Robin + Jakob.* ---
**Agenda: Samsung Mobile Cloud ; Weights License Discussion** ### 1. Technology Roadmap ; What's Coming from BFL Introduce Samsung to BFL's forward-looking model roadmap relevant to on-device deployment. Key points to cover: - BFL's direction on **small, efficient models** (Klein 4B) and the trajectory toward distilled on-device variants - The **Pruna collaboration** for model compression and quantization; directly relevant to on-device feasibility - BFL's unique position: *no other lab* will be able to deliver the quality-to-efficiency ratio we can achieve for mobile-sized models at this stage ### 2. Gallery Applications ; Use Cases for On-Device Deployment Walk through the specific editing scenarios Samsung cares about for the Gallery app: - **Object removal** ; Jakob to bring examples; key requirement for Gallery editing stack - **Outpainting** ; Jakob to bring examples; confirmed interest from MX Cloud team - **Style transfer** ; Samsung found this "really really good"; 4 presets exist for human faces, want to expand to broader subject matter; BFL can deliver this - **Mask-free (natural language-based) editing** ; Major use case - **Inpainting** ; Address open question from last feedback: *how does the script capture inpainting/outpainting/edits as a full image?* - Samsung's current approach to **personalization** has hit limitations ; BFL's fine-tuning capabilities are a competitive differentiator here ### 3. Generating Emojis with BFL Models ; In-Line Creative Feature Present the opportunity for Samsung to deploy BFL models for **inline emoji / sticker generation** across their messaging and keyboard stack: - Users could generate custom emojis or expressive visual elements directly within Samsung's native keyboard or messaging surfaces - Aligns with Samsung's goal to expand Galaxy AI beyond photos into **communication and self-expression** - Latency requirement: image generation for communication has lower quality requirements ; latency matters more here; BFL can optimize for this use case specifically - Native **multi-language character rendering** (Korean, Thai, etc.) is a key BFL advantage ; directly relevant to Samsung's global device base ### 4. On-Device Model Capabilities ; How Capable Can It Be? Address Samsung's technical requirements and constraints for on-device inference: **Device specs (Galaxy Z Fold 8 ; unconfirmed, H2 2026):** - RAM: Up to 12 GB or 16 GB LPDDR5X - Storage: 256 GB, 512 GB, 1 TB - No dedicated GPU VRAM ; GPU shares system RAM (mobile SoC) - Previous on-device requirements Samsung shared were based on SD 1.5 (several years outdated ; no longer the right benchmark) **What we know about on-device feasibility:** - Samsung tested FLUX Dev and Schnell for on-device; RAM size is the critical constraint - NanoFLUX (from recent research) generates 512×512 images in \~**2.5 seconds** on mobile devices ; demonstrating on-device high-quality text-to-image is feasible - A **distilled Klein 4B** could substantially outperform NanoFLUX and enable editing (not just text-to-image) ; Freddy believes a good distillation of Klein 4B "could be much much better and enable editing" - Samsung is **open to changing their entire foundation model** ; the current foundation is not locked **What we need from Samsung to scope this properly:** - Exact device specs from the R&D team (Seong Ju's requirements were based on SD 1.5) - Max VRAM/memory Samsung is willing to allocate to the image model - Target latency per generation for their specific use cases - Which AI models are currently running on-device (to understand the memory budget) ### 5. Small Model Evolution ; Where Are We Headed? Paint the longer-term roadmap for Samsung's planning purposes: - BFL's small model strategy: Klein 4B today → continued distillation and quantization toward mobile-optimized variants - **Collaboration with Pruna** for efficient on-device compression ; Samsung should be aware this work is ongoing - Two paths for Samsung: (a) license weights + BFL handles model optimization for their device specs, or (b) Samsung's R&D team handles on-device conversion with BFL's technical support - From original Samsung feedback: they're interested in either *training a smaller model for a specific use case* or *replacing the foundation model entirely* to improve quality ; BFL can support both paths - On-device is a **multi-year commercial opportunity** ; Samsung expects any integration to continue across future flagship and non-flagship models, not just one device cycle
--- ## Meeting Notes ---
**Apr 16, 2026 - Amanda message to Minju (new main contact)** Hi Minju, Thank you for re-sharing the deck, and for the clarity on use cases across the teams. It's good to hear you will be our main point of contact going forward. I'm assuming this means you will manage our contact with the Technology Strategy team, the Visual Solution team, and the Cloud Infra teams? With that being said, I wanted to make sure you had context across all our current discussions with Samsung, and wanted to see if you had a preference on whether we should also include you in 3.) and 4.) below:**1. Samsung Mobile, Technology Strategy team **(contact: you): We have mainly discussed Flux.1 Kontext and Flux.2 API use for Galaxy S and Fold8 launches (use cases: style transfer, mask-free editing). **2. Samsing Mobile, Cloud Infra Team **(contact: Jaehoon)**: **We have discussed Flux.2 via API and Commercial Weights License (use cases: "Eraser" or inpainting/outpainting, **3. Cheil, New Tech Solution Team** (contact: Taegu Kang, [gugu.kang@samsung.com](mailto:gugu.kang@samsung.com)) We received interest in licensing our Flux.2 models for the creation of advertisement drafts and final commercial deliverables for 10+ major advertisers (To be used for various commercial purposes, including digital content, TV commercials, and event videos).**4. **[**Blueport**](https://www.blueport.co.kr/Index.aspx)**, Samsung Electronics** (Contact: Seungchang Baek, [geni.info@samsung.com](mailto:geni.info@samsung.com)) Blueport is currently licensing Flux.1 Kontext and Dev models on behalf of Samsung Electronics. They would now like access to Flux.2 models. Regarding your comments about the use cases and licensing: **1. "Eraser" (In/outpaining endpoint):** we delivered an update this week to Jaehoon that further improves object removal quality on the combined endpoint we previously shared. We also conducted a human evaluation benchmark against other dedicated object erasing workflows, and our results indicate that we outperform them. - **Our requests: **If there are any (open) datasets closer to your internal benchmarks that you'd like us to test against, we'd be happy to run additional evaluations and share them with you. As you mentioned, we assume the Visual Solutions team will do the evals - is there a rough timing on when they expect to complete those evals? It would also be helpful to understand whether the team would prefer a custom endpoint via our API or licensing options with support on fine-tuning from our team. If via the API, can you provide rough volume estimates? **2. "Remaster":** The team is working on a fine-tuned end-point to share with the Visual Solutions team to show what is possible. I understand the team wants to license our models and run this on-prem. The team can download the model weights via our [repo on HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs) - **Our request: **Can you please share a volume estimate so we can provide pricing options for licensing our model weights? Finally, could we schedule time next week for you and I to discuss progress on use cases and options for licensing our models? Given the number of teams and initiatives, it would be ideal to have time to discuss on a call to ensure we can stay aligned on what your teams need, and make sure we are prioritising accordingly.
**Mar 25, 2026 — Robin @ Samsung HQ, Suwon (In-Person)** *Source: Robin's debrief, March 25, 2026. Attendees: Robin Rombach (BFL) + \~10 Samsung people from the Visual Solution Team and Technology Strategy group.* **Tone & Setting** Open, direct, and warm. Some Samsung attendees are avid BFL fans — one said: *"I know every sentence of the latent diffusion paper."* Samsung presented a deck to Robin (not the other way around), which mostly contained **failure cases of FLUX.2 \[pro\] via API** across different image editing tasks. The biggest identified problem: **character inconsistency** (e.g. unintended changes to race/gender in outputs). **Fold8 Launch Window** Feature freeze is end of April. Robin's assessment: inclusion in this launch window is **"likely unrealistic but not impossible."** A second launch window closes end of November. Samsung launches flagships twice a year; existing/deployed use cases can be replaced at any time (not tied to new device launches), but new feature integrations are. **Key Discussion Points** - **Replacing existing Google use cases is hard.** Google updates their models every 3 months, and the evaluation overhead required to swap makes it difficult. For equal performance between BFL and competition, **cost becomes the determining factor**. - **Existing use case BFL could replace: mask-based image editing (inpainting).** This is a deployed use case not tied to a launch window — can be replaced anytime if BFL can match quality and cost. - **New net-new use case: image enhancement** — removing moire patterns and blurriness from photos (e.g. random shots in challenging conditions). This would replace Samsung's in-house stack entirely. However, FLUX.2 needs finetuning to solve this consistently — Samsung's deck showed too much variation in outputs and insufficient character consistency. - **Strong interest in licensing and self-hosting**, including licensing of Pro models. Two finetuning paths discussed: - (a) BFL performs the finetuning and delivers a custom model - (b) Samsung gets access to the base model weights and does finetuning themselves - Samsung asked whether **BFL provides finetuning code / pipelines** alongside the weights. - Samsung also asked about licensing **other parts of the pipeline**, such as safety checking. Robin indicated BFL is open to licensing those as well. - **FP4 inference on Blackwells** is very interesting to Samsung for cost and latency reasons; **fp8** also of interest. - Samsung wants **access to BFL's model roadmap** to plan future integrations. - **Video:** not interesting now (not "every day use"), but when Robin mentioned targeting **real-time editing**, they became more curious. Not near-term, but flagged as a future opportunity. **Robin's Assessment & Recommended Path Forward** BFL should prioritise supporting the **net-new image enhancement use case**. If BFL moves fast, there may be a chance to hit the end-of-April feature freeze, but Samsung needs an **API endpoint to test ASAP**. The finetuning could potentially be done via synthetic data simulating image degradations (moire, blur). BFL should also pursue the **inpainting use case** (mask-based editing). In combination with **fp8 or fp4 inference**, licensing should become commercially viable. Robin is open to **Pro model licensing** only if a meaningful contract is in sight. **Action Items** *Samsung to deliver to BFL:* - The presentation deck from today's meeting - Their future use cases - Rough volume estimates for inpainting *BFL to deliver to Samsung:* - API and licensing pricing proposals → **pricing call scheduled for \~March 30** - Before/after finetuning comparison demonstrating character consistency improvement (consider using virtual try-on examples) — to be shared with the full group - Updated inpainting demo - Any further examples demonstrating finetuning / customization value, especially re: character consistency *Both sides:* - **Sign NDA between BFL and Samsung R&D team ASAP** (separate from the MX NDA already in place)
**Mar 10, 2026 ; Samsung MX Cloud Weights License (Slack #customerdeals-partnerships)** A new team at Samsung is interested in licensing BFL model weights to upgrade their core Samsung "Gallery" editing stack across multiple devices. This deal could anchor BFL inside Samsung's foundational image AI layer rather than as a feature vendor for specific device launches (e.g., the Fold8, which we are currently being evaluated for as well). **Next steps:** Call scheduled Fri Mar 13 (8AM CET). Robin will join. They would like to discuss technical details of our models, possible customization for specific use cases (object removal, outpainting, etc.), and licensing structure. Jakob confirmed to join for customization discussion ; to drop object removal and outpainting examples in the deck. Amanda has started pulling together content for the presentation.
**Mar 3, 2026 ; Mark Kim Intelligence Update (via Email)** Mark Kim (Samsung Next) confirmed two parallel Samsung initiatives in response to Robin's check-in: 1. **Fold8 integration** and **MX Cloud licensing** are separate initiatives ; different teams within Samsung Mobile/MX. May eventually fold into one, but currently running in parallel. 2. **Google contract change confirmed:** Google has changed its contract with Samsung ; MX is now directly charged for Gemini services as opposed to costs being netted out of Samsung's search revenue. Cost is higher than anticipated internally. This is why MX is now looking for alternative models. *"This is a great opportunity for BFL to jump in."* (Robin forwarded to Amanda, Anthony, and Andi ; treat as confidential.) Mark still awaiting more information on Fold8 integration status.
**Feb 19, 2026 ; Mark Kim / Minju Seo Update (Samsung Next Email)** Mark Kim forwarded an inquiry from Minju Seo (MX TSG) about: (1) BFL's 2025 revenue, and (2) rumors of Apple acquisition interest. Mark's read: Samsung is gauging the stability of a potential commercial partnership ; a constant concern when working with startups. Mark's plan: share \~\$100mm ARR (publicly available, as of August 2025) and confirm no M&A rumors known to him personally. Robin agreed and pointed to the \$300M Series B ([bfl.ai/blog/our-300m-series-b](http://bfl.ai/blog/our-300m-series-b), Dec 1, 2025) as additional supporting information. Also in this thread (from Robin, Feb 19): Samsung declined the London in-person meeting. Amanda will sync with Dig and explore a replacement Korea meeting in March.
**Sept 22, 2025 ; EXT Samsung Sync (Flux 2 launch)** Agenda: (1) Discuss Samsung's experience with Kontext and feedback on pricing, (2) finalize use cases, (3) introduce Flux 2. **Samsung's Current State & Competition Update** - Working on business proposal and service integration use case scenarios - Nano Banana model update forced comprehensive retesting across all scenarios - Competitive solutions (Nano Banana) now performing as good as or better than Flux-Kontext per Samsung's evaluation - Taking significant time to evaluate best solution for user experience on specific Samsung devices project **Technical Requirements & Use Case Priorities** - Quality vs. latency depends heavily on use case: - Image editing: quality more important ; users can wait **10–20 seconds** for superior quality; **over 20 seconds** becomes problematic - Style transfer and mask-free editing remain key requirements - Image generation for communication: quality requirements are lower, latency matters more - Multi-language **rendering** is high priority ; they can translate prompts to English, but native character rendering in images is critical (Korean, Thai, etc.) - New use cases still being developed ; no additional scenarios to share at time of meeting **Flux 2 Model Preview & Capabilities** - Timeline for Flux release: **End of October to end of November** release - Early access availability: within 1–2 weeks for Samsung testing - Currently text-to-image (t2i) only (still in pre-training) - Image editing (i2i) capabilities being added in next 1–2 weeks - Native multi-reference support included - Key features Samsung found compelling: native multi-language prompting and character rendering (Korean, Thai, etc.) - Other Flux.2 characteristics discussed: - Better world knowledge and physics understanding - **4K resolution** native support - Structured JSON prompting for systematic control - Superior text rendering (outperforming GPT Image) - Performance advantage: **2–4x faster** than competition while maintaining quality parity **Critical Timeline & Next Steps** - Samsung flagship device launch: January 2025 \[S25 cycle at time of meeting\] - Software freeze: End of October 2025 - Need feature-complete, QA-ready version **2–3 weeks before freeze** - Latest handover: **October week 1–2** for Samsung testing - BFL follow-ups committed to: - Provide character rendering samples - Share Flux 2 evaluations when available - Set up early access endpoint for Samsung testing within 1–2 weeks - Samsung committed to: run apple-to-apple comparisons using their test sets once early access available
**Sept 16, 2025 ; Insights from Mark Kim (via Email)** *"As you may know, Samsung gets a lump sum payment from Google for making Google our default search engine. Whenever we have service-related costs, they get subtracted from that amount. For executives, they have a preference to 'chip away' from this expected revenue rather than having a separate contract in place that could be considered an expense item. I heard that Google is charging \$0.01 per generation.* *I think we should wait and see what they come back with. I don't think it's the commercial terms that's the issue. The image team also had early access to Google's image model. They're likely answering some questions from executives who may not have been fully plugged into the process but are now asking about Google's model after seeing the buzz around it.* *In terms of the timeline for contracts that need to be in place with partners for our January launch, we are still very much on pace."*

Higher output resolutions add moderate latency. A 4200x3095 output takes roughly **50-55 seconds** end-to-end. --- ## How it works 1. **Provide an input image and canvas size** - Your image is centered on a canvas at `width` x `height`. FLUX.2 Pro fills the surrounding area with contextually coherent content, guided by an optional prompt (auto-upsampled by VLM). 2. **Request high-res output** - Set `output_width` and `output_height` to receive the final result at up to **4200x3095** (\~13 megapixels). The model generates at canvas resolution and natively produces the high-res deliverable. 3. **Get your result** - The final image passes through content moderation and is delivered as a signed URL. `width`/`height` control the generation canvas and are subject to the standard FLUX.2 Pro megapixel limit (\~9 MP). `output_width`/`output_height` control the final deliverable size and are **not** subject to this limit - the model handles the upscaling to the requested resolution natively. Omit them to receive the image at canvas resolution. --- ## ⚠️ Please note - This endpoint is designed for **testing and evaluation** with Netflix. Do not use for production traffic. - You will need a **special BFL-provided API key** - your regular API key will not work. - This is part of our demo and staging environment. The endpoint is **rate limited**. - High-res output requests are processed sequentially on dedicated infrastructure. - The endpoint follows the standard FLUX outpainting API contract with the addition of `output_width` / `output_height` for high-res output. - Both `outpainting` (Flex-based) and `outpainting-pro` (Pro-based) endpoints support high-res output. --- ## Get started **1. Get your API key** from your BFL account team. You will need a project-specific key. **2. Submit an outpainting + upscale request** ```bash IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/input.png | tr -d '\n')" B64_TMP=$(mktemp) echo "$IMAGE_BASE64" > "$B64_TMP" jq -n \ --rawfile img "$B64_TMP" \ '{ prompt: "A vibrant underwater scene with colorful tropical fish and coral reef", input_image: ($img | rtrimstr("\n")), width: 1408, height: 1024, output_width: 4200, output_height: 3095, output_format: "png" }' > /tmp/outpaint_request.json rm -f "$B64_TMP" curl -sk -X POST "$BASE/partners/preview/outpainting-pro" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY" \ --data-binary @/tmp/outpaint_request.json ``` This returns a task ID and a polling URL: ```json {"id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx", "polling_url": "..."} ``` **3. Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sk "$BASE/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, grab the high-res image URL from `result.sample`. --- ## Available parameters
**Parameter** **Type** **Default** **Description**
`input_image` string *required* Base64-encoded input image to outpaint from
`width` integer - Canvas width for outpainting generation (min 64)
`height` integer - Canvas height for outpainting generation (min 64)
`prompt` string auto-generated Text prompt guiding how new areas are filled. "OUTPAINT" is prepended automatically. If omitted, a quality-focused default is used.
`output_width` integer - Final output width (max 4200). Omit for canvas-resolution output.
`output_height` integer - Final output height (max 3095). Omit for canvas-resolution output.
`bbox_x1` integer centered Left offset (px) of input image on canvas. Negative values allowed.
`bbox_y1` integer centered Top offset (px) of input image on canvas. Negative values allowed.
`auto_crop` boolean false Crop input image to canvas bounds if it extends beyond edges
`prompt_upsampling` boolean true Upsample the prompt via VLM before inference
`output_format` string `"png"` `"png"` or `"jpeg"`
> `output_width` and `output_height` must both be provided for high-res output. When omitted, the endpoint returns the outpainted image at canvas resolution (`width` x `height`) - identical to the standard outpainting endpoint. --- ## Python quick start ```python import base64, os, time, requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} def encode_image(path: str) -> str: with open(path, "rb") as f: return base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() # Submit outpainting + upscale resp = requests.post( f"{BASE}/partners/preview/outpainting-pro", headers=HEADERS, json={ "input_image": encode_image("scene.png"), "width": 1408, "height": 1024, "prompt": "Expand the scene naturally with consistent lighting and perspective", "output_width": 4200, "output_height": 3095, "output_format": "png", }, verify=False, ).json() task_id = resp["id"] poll_url = resp.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") print(f"Task submitted: {task_id}") # Poll while True: result = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}, verify=False).json() if result["status"] == "Ready": img_url = result["result"]["sample"] with open("output_4200x3095.png", "wb") as f: f.write(requests.get(img_url).content) print("Saved: output_4200x3095.png") break elif result["status"] in ("Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated"): print(f"Failed: {result['status']}") break time.sleep(3) ``` --- ## Key details
**Endpoint (Pro)** `/partners/preview/outpainting-pro`
**Endpoint (Flex)** `/partners/preview/outpainting`
**Auth** `X-Key` header with your BFL API key
**Max output** 4200 x 3095 (\~13 MP)
**Output formats** PNG, JPEG

**Prompt:** *"Epic space battle with a fighter spacecraft firing engines through an explosive debris field, distant capital ships, volumetric explosions, stars and nebula in the background, cinematic sci-fi"* ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/fb16a0ae-200d-4416-9d10-9504ca5a7d95/space_output.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4666GMDQCNP%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095749Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQC8LlKybNdi1iCnMjDYXjDnM55kir7QMcex%2FfbbalmSbgIhAKBMfQAQ4EN9G4dcE7bcC5Ml5aVRnnGtiiXYbJENaUBuKv8DCAIQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgyIKd44K3611I1b95gq3AOgHjBj9zfYoZv29ZwLme%2BLG1d67bfLDbCxkON67d08eeVV2eefKcAU6KrPvNQo6e4GchHeMJVANgo4O9vo0SY0XcJ81AVDUtlZ3PfgzYQR%2BIj7v8BFqMxc41mVLbvTXGr%2FbyLwcfC4KR8Pvw2QX1kqdK4BF7wC6%2BY2BJNum0qfRNfCkQ4kuR9As1So%2BuXkT9asRbXhBCjmvqGlIi50dnGQdCD6xTL7ZyRpgSP%2FpAEc8ySlYAMnA9%2F%2B3%2Fjl4xLZPGmH80ESgDJOPvGcZ2f4qDzhaavwr9Srqr%2FfqsUfYBAW6jWctmm7gOvN68tJzRRz9CWbimsz%2F8xtqzvDMKBvj6EgwBbtkvBDHg%2FOwUV2xPl8Dl%2B3YcgVVu5nRi8FDv%2FfTpFde%2FRkUhlFpHMhfvvvtM9a7j9fOBcZ8GpRls%2F56i6%2B42JvBVQLjR8npYMMKzGSgcqVGjFRbv8gxAehFV5rjqLdw7%2BTPA1OpihVHovD23Za6cDAEH0jomjJ4vB6EWM9h79NLPi1irCLTO80tCbS4GJXMvmqJAu%2B2%2Bc%2Ft2Q5Vxpuwm1BQAwW8etmoIfoaAsa%2FyG%2BDig7PMCPeePjuyh53BvwzEzjts5Vg3oUb2X%2FWc0rnvmWR791aRwmM3QNGTD1rpLPBjqkASz3Bx4peFpsnjNqmWqeUm6iuID0sF4851bvJ%2FG8jxNHvvzjLcAjCZl6IXqHNZmm%2Flz5sjPuI91wvh7YS%2B2pnbAI8%2BaZlNKy%2FwKw6H3K7B92vB8LYQ8OjKc7tgSSVf7Y%2BLjy4rOPimSe2%2FkVWsidr9VDGmxe94HFOBOyviWjwCfj3OmAnGRARyfj3W%2FP%2B8Ruv8hGKICKeESrcmC5txEitC78Fn6t&X-Amz-Signature=3957d5aff6317704cb1bfaeebdc8d4f968d31a0d0bb94c0305702503772ef95b&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) > **Output - 4200 x 3095** --- ## Latency Benchmark
**Input Size** **Canvas** **Final Output** **End-to-end**
1000x638 1408x1024 1408x1024 \~32s
1000x638 1408x1024 **4200x3095** \~55s
838x585 1408x1024 **4200x3095** \~55s
995x588 1408x1024 **4200x3095** \~55s
684x513 1408x1024 **4200x3095** \~50s
Higher output resolutions add moderate latency. A 4200x3095 output takes roughly **50-55 seconds** end-to-end. --- ## How it works 1. **Provide an input image and canvas size** - Your image is centered on a canvas at `width` x `height`. FLUX.2 Pro fills the surrounding area with contextually coherent content, guided by an optional prompt (auto-upsampled by VLM). 2. **Request high-res output** - Set `output_width` and `output_height` to receive the final result at up to **4200x3095** (\~13 megapixels). The model generates at canvas resolution and natively produces the high-res deliverable. 3. **Get your result** - The final image passes through content moderation and is delivered as a signed URL. `width`/`height` control the generation canvas and are subject to the standard FLUX.2 Pro megapixel limit (\~9 MP). `output_width`/`output_height` control the final deliverable size and are **not** subject to this limit - the model handles the upscaling to the requested resolution natively. Omit them to receive the image at canvas resolution. --- ## ⚠️ Please note - This endpoint is designed for **testing and evaluation** with Netflix. Do not use for production traffic. - You will need a **special BFL-provided API key** - your regular API key will not work. - This is part of our demo and staging environment. The endpoint is **rate limited**. - High-res output requests are processed sequentially on dedicated infrastructure. - The endpoint follows the standard FLUX outpainting API contract with the addition of `output_width` / `output_height` for high-res output. - Both `outpainting` (Flex-based) and `outpainting-pro` (Pro-based) endpoints support high-res output. --- ## Get started **1. Get your API key** from your BFL account team. You will need a project-specific key. **2. Submit an outpainting + upscale request** ```bash IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/input.png | tr -d '\n')" B64_TMP=$(mktemp) echo "$IMAGE_BASE64" > "$B64_TMP" jq -n \ --rawfile img "$B64_TMP" \ '{ prompt: "A vibrant underwater scene with colorful tropical fish and coral reef", input_image: ($img | rtrimstr("\n")), width: 1408, height: 1024, output_width: 4200, output_height: 3095, output_format: "png" }' > /tmp/outpaint_request.json rm -f "$B64_TMP" curl -sk -X POST "$BASE/partners/preview/outpainting-pro" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY" \ --data-binary @/tmp/outpaint_request.json ``` This returns a task ID and a polling URL: ```json {"id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx", "polling_url": "..."} ``` **3. Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sk "$BASE/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, grab the high-res image URL from `result.sample`. --- ## Available parameters
**Parameter** **Type** **Default** **Description**
`input_image` string *required* Base64-encoded input image to outpaint from
`width` integer - Canvas width for outpainting generation (min 64)
`height` integer - Canvas height for outpainting generation (min 64)
`prompt` string auto-generated Text prompt guiding how new areas are filled. "OUTPAINT" is prepended automatically. If omitted, a quality-focused default is used.
`output_width` integer - Final output width (max 4200). Omit for canvas-resolution output.
`output_height` integer - Final output height (max 3095). Omit for canvas-resolution output.
`bbox_x1` integer centered Left offset (px) of input image on canvas. Negative values allowed.
`bbox_y1` integer centered Top offset (px) of input image on canvas. Negative values allowed.
`auto_crop` boolean false Crop input image to canvas bounds if it extends beyond edges
`prompt_upsampling` boolean true Upsample the prompt via VLM before inference
`output_format` string `"png"` `"png"` or `"jpeg"`
> `output_width` and `output_height` must both be provided for high-res output. When omitted, the endpoint returns the outpainted image at canvas resolution (`width` x `height`) - identical to the standard outpainting endpoint. --- ## Python quick start ```python import base64, os, time, requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} def encode_image(path: str) -> str: with open(path, "rb") as f: return base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() # Submit outpainting + upscale resp = requests.post( f"{BASE}/partners/preview/outpainting-pro", headers=HEADERS, json={ "input_image": encode_image("scene.png"), "width": 1408, "height": 1024, "prompt": "Expand the scene naturally with consistent lighting and perspective", "output_width": 4200, "output_height": 3095, "output_format": "png", }, verify=False, ).json() task_id = resp["id"] poll_url = resp.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") print(f"Task submitted: {task_id}") # Poll while True: result = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}, verify=False).json() if result["status"] == "Ready": img_url = result["result"]["sample"] with open("output_4200x3095.png", "wb") as f: f.write(requests.get(img_url).content) print("Saved: output_4200x3095.png") break elif result["status"] in ("Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated"): print(f"Failed: {result['status']}") break time.sleep(3) ``` --- ## Key details
**Endpoint (Pro)** `/partners/preview/outpainting-pro`
**Endpoint (Flex)** `/partners/preview/outpainting`
**Auth** `X-Key` header with your BFL API key
**Max output** 4200 x 3095 (\~13 MP)
**Output formats** PNG, JPEG

Main process now [here](slackMessage://black-forest-labs.slack.com/C06PQ6N99P1/1775859939.740589/1775859939.740589). Compiled from shop proposals. GPU counts assume 8 GPUs per node where proposals specify nodes. ## Active Shops
# Shop Lead(s) Min GPUs Ideal GPUs Notes
1 Multimodal Concept Flow Adi 64 GPUs (8 nodes) 256 GPUs (32 Nodes) For explorations (3 months). Scaling up with 64 nodes
2 RL Post-Training Ravi TBD TBD No compute section in proposal
3 Distillation Axel, (Griffin) 64-128 (8-16 nodes) 256 (32 nodes) Exploration: 8-16 nodes \~2 months; Scale-up: 32 nodes \~2-4 weeks per modality
4a Long Context: Architecture Dominik, (Jonas) TBD TBD No compute section in proposal
4b Long Context: RAG + Persistent State Hila 64 256 \~16 nodes per small training run, joint training of two models
4c Long Context: Perceiver Style Freddy, (Tim) 64 256 Needs multimodal data, large-scale video pretraining
4d Adaptive Memory / Streaming Cheng, (Ruben) 16 64 Post-training + serving system
5 Physical AI / Action Prediction Sumith, (Harry), (Niklas), (Vikash), (Patrick) 64 256 Data pipeline processing can use CPU; model training is GPU-heavy
6 Reasoning Flux Rinon 80 (10 nodes) 192 (24 nodes) VRAM hungry -- multi-pass unrolling requires sharding across \~4 nodes minimum
7 VAE/SSL Pre-training Suraj, Gaetan 32-64 64-128 Phase 1 exploration ongoing, scale-up phase will need significant compute

## Summary **Known minimum total: 352-416 GPUs** / **Known ideal total: 1280 GPUs** Shops 1, 2, 4a, 7, 8 have not specified GPU requirements yet. ## Unassigned Researchers Researchers without a shop (Dustin, Zion, and potentially others) -- proposal: allocate a small permanent pool (e.g. 2-3 nodes / 16-24 GPUs) plus access to leftover compute. ## Open Questions - GB200 vs B200 cluster distribution per shop - Data movement between clusters (blocker for some people to switch) - Several shops (1, 2, 4a, 7, 8) still need to specify compute requirements - How to handle preemption when shops exceed their minimum allocation
