## Narrative Stories have always inspired humanity to understand the world around them. From ancient paintings of hunts, The Iliad, books of the world’s great religions, to modern sci-fi. The craft of bringing these stories to life, visually in an image or movie, lets people feel the story as a lived experience. We can simulate and learn from the scenarios in a story. The dark side of tribalism in Gangs of New York, the desire to not be ordinary in Goodfellas, the power of greed in the Wolf of Wall Street. If you give storytellers and builders better tools — in our case frontier visual models — higher levels of craft can emerge. Especially when people want to tell stories visually. FLUX models should be reliable tools: fast enough to iterate, controllable enough to direct, and consistent enough to refine an idea. And that will stay true as we move into multimodal models for visual intelligence, from images to real-time video and action prediction. Our models should be tested by creators with the highest standards. That’s why we’re excited to call Martin Scorsese an advisor to Black Forest Labs. He cares deeply about honoring the craft of cinema, wants to use AI to create more, and keep human creation at the center. This video takes you inside a working storyboarding session we did with him and our FLUX models. It was magical to see him bring ideas that were trapped in his mind to life within a few minutes. The results also met his famously stringent quality bar. We think there are many creators in the world that still haven’t gotten to tell their stories. The models and tools we build should help millions of new creators come online. --- ## Goal of the campaign **Positioning goal**: This video becomes the first impactful milestone that positions BFL as the “premium” brand on the path to multi-modality. BFL augments the human creator and honors the craft of making things. Perception should be that our models are used by the creators with the highest standards (Martin Scorsese), while still democratizing access to creators that didn’t have the means (also why we’re pushing towards multi-modality). Maintain a clear understanding that this is a real investor/advisor partnership.

**Metrics goal** - Generate **5–8M impressions** - **+63,000 incremental** **website sessions** over 14 days (a +30% lift) - **2–5k unique demo users** in the first 14 days ## Messaging ### Martin Scorsese is an advisor to Black Forest Labs Martin Scorsese has spent six decades shaping how the world sees stories. We're thrilled he's now helping us shape Black Forest Labs as an advisor and investor. He describes FLUX as a “a kind of cinematic intelligence”. This video takes you inside a working storyboarding session we did with Martin Scorsese and our FLUX models. It was magical to see him bring ideas that were trapped in his mind to life within a few minutes that also met his famously stringent quality bar. ### Alt headlines - Martin Scorsese storyboards with FLUX - Martin Scorsese partners with Black Forest Labs - FLUX x Martin Scorsese - Black Forest Labs x Martin Scorsese ## Launch Strategy - Show that this isn’t just a one-off paid endorsement. Announce that Martin Scorsese has been an investor and advisor who’s been helping us for awhile now. - Hint at BFL going multi-modal soon (video, audio) given Scorsese is a filmmaker. We believe the future is visual intelligence and that’s what we’re building to. - CTA is a simple demo app for storyboarding with “FLUX by Black Forest Labs” watermarked image outputs. - Storyboarding showcase series on social after the launch - Tackle the expected negative sentiment from the creative community by being transparent, re-sharing our belief in open source models that the community makes their own, and working with some of the most creative people in the industry. ## Channels - Press: proactively target “higher taste” publications like NY Times, Variety, maybe Bloomberg Media. - Marty posting the video on his socials - X: 30 second trailer + full video posted same day, paid boosting of 30 second trailer 3-4 days after launch - LinkedIn: 30 second trailer + full video posted same day, paid boosting of 30 second trailer 3-4 days after launch - Instagram: Core video posted on account, share via snippet formats in Instagram stories throughout the week - YouTube: 30 second trailer + full video posted same day, paid boosting of 30 second trailer 3-4 days after launch - Robin’s socials: Speak to what it was like working with Scorsese for a day and the magic Robin’s continuously amazed by in the models - A16Z Socials: Partner with New Media team to amplify via their channels - Website: Blog + banner - Community/Influencers: TBD if possible - BFL Blog: Full narrative (above) of why we partnered with Scorsese, our values of augmenting the human creators etc. ## Crisis comms Press? - Proactive vs. inbound? - There’s no story here for most press—the story would be a major launch, or lots of creative backlash, or actually using the model in a real workflow, etc. But without those, there’s no angle. That said, we could position this into e.g. a longform interview with Marty and Robin in Variety. A meditation on how creators might interact with AI. High-risk / high-reward. It depends on Marty’s availability / willingness for these kinds of appearances. Headlines we want to avoid investor/ advisor announcement? - need to be careful in calling him an "investor and advisor" while simultaneously using him as a marketing vehicle - makes it hard to separate the commercial relationship from the creative endorsement. People will ask whether he's genuinely using FLUX in his workflow or if this was a produced session for the camera. The "it's not a paid endorsement" framing actually draws (potentially) more attention to the transactional nature Cinematic intelligence - we like it, but its also loaded. It positions AI generated images as having creative judgment, which will provoke strong reactions from filmmakers and artists who see intelligence and taste as distinctly human. It could easily become the pull quote in a critical article Human replacement - could be risky: right now it says "storyboards today, your entire job tomorrow.” Ben made some suggestions in comms doc for this
Archive The AI generation universe is filled with slop-piness. Copyright violations of Brad Pitt and Tom Cruise, cheap sexual videos that get clicks, ads that overwhelm the eyes and never stop coming. Each generation of generative AI fills our feeds with images that look more like each other than like the work of any individual using them. Great for memes, but quickly abandoned. The trendy word for this is *slop*. Generative AI has been filling up our feeds lately with images that might be great for memes, but are quickly forgotten. frontier models for visual creation will naturally bring out the most a higher level of taste and craft. in values of taste, craft, and augmenting humans that have stories to tell. Especially when they want to tell that story visually. It makes us reflect on what traits we see in ourselves in those characters. Sometimes it inspires us to be better or to do worse. But at the very least we get to understand and have empathy for other people we may have never even tried to understand (the drug addict, the veteran with PTSD, the black scientist facing racism in the 1960s). Visual storytelling allows us humans to simulate and learn from scenarios that we might be in (maybe not John Wick though 🙂). The evolution of a family in Godfather, the desire to not be ordinary in Goodfellas, a person being overtaken by greed in the Wolf of Wall Street. It makes us reflect on what traits we see in ourselves in those characters. Sometimes it inspires us to be better or to do worse. But at the very least we get to understand and have empathy for other people we may have never even tried to understand (the drug addict, the veteran with PTSD, the black scientist facing racism in the 1960s). Iteration during the discovery part of the creative process should feel unencumbered by waiting or worrying about cost. Black Forest Labs builds AI models that generate visual outputs. How those models work and how we build them speaks to our values. We want to augment creators, not replace them. We want to give humans open access to a technology we think is way too powerful to be in the hands of just a few. That’s why be build models that are at the frontier for quality, but also maximally controllable/customizable. Many of our best models are also released as open source under an Apache license so the creator community can make them their own, improve them, and call us out on improvements we need to make. When our team builds models, we’re always pushing to make large leaps at the frontier in quality that comes with high customizability, speed, and lower cost. Iteration during the discovery part of the creative process should feel unencumbered by waiting or worrying about cost. It’s not our place to judge what’s art or creativity. ## Narrative Stories have always inspired humanity to understand the world around them. From ancient paintings of hunts, The Iliad, books of the world’s great religions, to modern sci-fi. The craft of bringing these stories to life, visually in an image or movie, lets people feel the story as a lived experience. We can simulate and learn from the scenarios in a story. The dark side of tribalism in Gangs of New York, the desire to not be ordinary in Goodfellas, the power of greed in the Wolf of Wall Street. If you give storytellers and builders better tools — in our case frontier visual models — higher levels of craft can emerge. Especially when people want to tell stories visually. FLUX models should be reliable tools: fast enough to iterate, controllable enough to direct, and consistent enough to refine an idea. And that will stay true as we move into multimodal models for visual intelligence, from images to real-time video and action prediction. Our models should be tested by creators with the highest standards. That’s why we’re excited to call Martin Scorsese an advisor to Black Forest Labs. He cares deeply about honoring the craft of cinema, wants to use AI to create more, and keep human creation at the center. This video takes you inside a working storyboarding session we did with him and our FLUX models. It was magical to see him bring ideas that were trapped in his mind to life within a few minutes. The results also met his famously stringent quality bar. We think there are many creators in the world that still haven’t gotten to tell their stories. The models and tools we build should help millions of new creators come online. --- ## Goal of the campaign **Positioning goal**: This video becomes the first impactful milestone that positions BFL as the “premium” brand on the path to multi-modality. BFL augments the human creator and honors the craft of making things. Perception should be that our models are used by the creators with the highest standards (Martin Scorsese), while still democratizing access to creators that didn’t have the means (also why we’re pushing towards multi-modality). Maintain a clear understanding that this is a real investor/advisor partnership.

**Metrics goal** - Generate **5–8M impressions** - **+63,000 incremental** **website sessions** over 14 days (a +30% lift) - **2–5k unique demo users** in the first 14 days ## Messaging ### Martin Scorsese is an advisor to Black Forest Labs Martin Scorsese has spent six decades shaping how the world sees stories. We're thrilled he's now helping us shape Black Forest Labs as an advisor and investor. He describes FLUX as a “a kind of cinematic intelligence”. This video takes you inside a working storyboarding session we did with Martin Scorsese and our FLUX models. It was magical to see him bring ideas that were trapped in his mind to life within a few minutes that also met his famously stringent quality bar. ### Alt headlines - Martin Scorsese storyboards with FLUX - Martin Scorsese partners with Black Forest Labs - FLUX x Martin Scorsese - Black Forest Labs x Martin Scorsese ## Launch Strategy - Show that this isn’t just a one-off paid endorsement. Announce that Martin Scorsese has been an investor and advisor who’s been helping us for awhile now. - Hint at BFL going multi-modal soon (video, audio) given Scorsese is a filmmaker. We believe the future is visual intelligence and that’s what we’re building to. - CTA is a simple demo app for storyboarding with “FLUX by Black Forest Labs” watermarked image outputs. - Storyboarding showcase series on social after the launch - Tackle the expected negative sentiment from the creative community by being transparent, re-sharing our belief in open source models that the community makes their own, and working with some of the most creative people in the industry. ## Channels - Press: proactively target “higher taste” publications like NY Times, Variety, maybe Bloomberg Media. - Marty posting the video on his socials - X: 30 second trailer + full video posted same day, paid boosting of 30 second trailer 3-4 days after launch - LinkedIn: 30 second trailer + full video posted same day, paid boosting of 30 second trailer 3-4 days after launch - Instagram: Core video posted on account, share via snippet formats in Instagram stories throughout the week - YouTube: 30 second trailer + full video posted same day, paid boosting of 30 second trailer 3-4 days after launch - Robin’s socials: Speak to what it was like working with Scorsese for a day and the magic Robin’s continuously amazed by in the models - A16Z Socials: Partner with New Media team to amplify via their channels - Website: Blog + banner - Community/Influencers: TBD if possible - BFL Blog: Full narrative (above) of why we partnered with Scorsese, our values of augmenting the human creators etc. ## Crisis comms Press? - Proactive vs. inbound? - There’s no story here for most press—the story would be a major launch, or lots of creative backlash, or actually using the model in a real workflow, etc. But without those, there’s no angle. That said, we could position this into e.g. a longform interview with Marty and Robin in Variety. A meditation on how creators might interact with AI. High-risk / high-reward. It depends on Marty’s availability / willingness for these kinds of appearances. Headlines we want to avoid investor/ advisor announcement? - need to be careful in calling him an "investor and advisor" while simultaneously using him as a marketing vehicle - makes it hard to separate the commercial relationship from the creative endorsement. People will ask whether he's genuinely using FLUX in his workflow or if this was a produced session for the camera. The "it's not a paid endorsement" framing actually draws (potentially) more attention to the transactional nature Cinematic intelligence - we like it, but its also loaded. It positions AI generated images as having creative judgment, which will provoke strong reactions from filmmakers and artists who see intelligence and taste as distinctly human. It could easily become the pull quote in a critical article Human replacement - could be risky: right now it says "storyboards today, your entire job tomorrow.” Ben made some suggestions in comms doc for this

Copyright violations of Brad Pitt and Tom Cruise, cheap sexual videos that get clicks, ads that overwhelm the eyes and never stop coming. Each generation of generative AI fills our feeds with images that look more like each other than like the work of any individual using them. Great for memes, but quickly abandoned. The trendy word for this is *slop*. Generative AI has been filling up our feeds lately with images that might be great for memes, but are quickly forgotten. frontier models for visual creation will naturally bring out the most a higher level of taste and craft. in values of taste, craft, and augmenting humans that have stories to tell. The evolution of a family in Godfather, the desire to not be ordinary in Goodfellas, a person being overtaken by greed in the Wolf of Wall Street. Iteration during the discovery part of the creative process should feel unencumbered by waiting or worrying about cost. Black Forest Labs builds AI models that generate visual outputs. How those models work and how we build them speaks to our values. We want to augment creators, not replace them. We want to give humans open access to a technology we think is way too powerful to be in the hands of just a few. That’s why be build models that are at the frontier for quality, but also maximally controllable/customizable. Many of our best models are also released as open source under an Apache license so the creator community can make them their own, improve them, and call us out on improvements we need to make. When our team builds models, we’re always pushing to make large leaps at the frontier in quality that comes with high customizability, speed, and lower cost. Take a look at our current org chart [HERE](/17bc370222d580d7b8a9f0471ff142b5?pvs=25). During your first week, - Complete [**this onboarding check-list**](/275c370222d580ee9fccdc96ebf1160b?pvs=25). You should receive this in your email inbox as well. - You'll have a welcome session with our CEO Robin or someone else from the leadership team, where you'll learn about BFL models, our tech, and meet key members of your team. - Play around with our models in the [Playground](https://playground.bfl.ai/) We highly value regular check-ins, transparent communication and personal connections: - On the third Wednesday of every month, we hold our **BFL Monthly All Hands**, where we share company-wide updates, insights from each department, and a look at our roadmap to bring everyone on the same page. - Thursday [Demo Days ](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zWq8j56FWv6OODq9XehLBCk0zOkkTpCAnXEOkE7XjTI/edit?gid=0#gid=0)where you can present anything you’ve been working on without prep, occasionally we also have customers come in to share feedback. - We encourage active participation in team meetings and discussions. - In-person company wide offsites 2x a year → Our next Offsite is first week of October - We have a public #private_dms channel on Slack Finding answers: - Our single point of access to any information and questions is Claude. Find more information on how to use it effectively to find answers ###
Take time to explore our documentation: (deprecated, needs rework, don’t use Forest Labs Section) (For SF hotel bookings, we have corporate rates at Marriott Bonvoy and others, which you should receive an email to sign up with your BFL email - Details in the above expense & travel policy) Let us know if you need anything else! BFL Team

### Problems we’re solving **Real-time/fast image generation has always come at the cost of production-ready quality. ** - Teams want to customize models for their specific styles, brands, or use cases but can't afford the compute ### Solution and positioning ### FLUX.2 \[klein\] is our fastest image model yet. FLUX.2 \[klein\] unifies real time image generation and editing in a single, compact model. Delivering state-of-the-art quality with end-to-end inference in less than a second. Enabling interactive workflows, real-time previews, and latency-critical applications. **Core features** - \[Super fast and super high quality (for both text to image and image editing\] **Use Cases** 1. **Use Case 1:** 2. **Use Case 2:** 3. **Use Case 3:** ### Messaging ### Blazing fast. Beautiful. Klein delivers stunning, professional-quality visuals in under a second, making it 30%+ faster than any competing model at this quality level with better realism and more output diversity. While other models force you to choose between speed and quality…… ### **Images generated instantly — without sacrificing quality. ** FLUX.2 \[klein\] gives you blazing fast generation so you can iterate on your idea without pausing. It unifies real time image generation and editing in a single, compact model. Delivering state-of-the-art quality with end-to-end inference in less than a second. Built for the next generation of interactive applications, run on consumer hardware. ### Built to fine-tune and run locally. 25bc3702-22d5-80bb-8bb6-f88f582b9b31.title: Which Flux Model for which use case?
25bc3702-22d5-80bb-8bb6-f88f582b9b31.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/25bc370222d580bb8bb6f88f582b9b31 as of 2026-03-27T15:43:47.301Z: {"Verification":"expired","title":"Which Flux Model for which use case?"} Benefits & highlights of each model and when to recommend them by use case. ## **TLDR;** 1. Recommended Standard for most Usecases = Flux.2 \[pro\] 2. Best Model = Flux.2 \[max\] 3. Fastest = Flux.2 \[schnell\] (Upcoming Model) 4. Cheapest = look it up for [API pricing](https://bfl.ai/pricing) & [licensing pricing](https://bfl.ai/licensing) 5. High resolution = Flux.2 \[pro\] Ultra (up to 4 megapixel, all other images 1 mp) 6. Edits = Flux.2 \[flex\] 7. Saturated style (liked by consumers) = Flux.2 \[pro\] 8. Self-host = Flux.2 \[dev\] or Flux.2 \[klein\] (upcoming) 9. How does moderation work? [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-Fn8bdZzxT5nWCfprIx_eLM7QahgZmysrKC9EknGfRU/edit?tab=t.0](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-Fn8bdZzxT5nWCfprIx_eLM7QahgZmysrKC9EknGfRU/edit?tab=t.0) **→ Flux.2 \[pro\] is our Flagship workhorse model, in most cases you cannot do much wrong recommending that one!** Model Strengths and Limitations, New data source, and New data source ## Deployment Recommendations Sometimes we provide inference containers or code that customers deploy directly on their infrastructure. If they ask about number of GPUs to use for their deployment, this is usually what we recommend:
Model # of GPUs Type of GPU Additional Considerations
FLUX.2 \[pro\] 4 H100, H200 or GB200 Fewer GPUs could lead to Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors for larger images or higher numbers of reference images, as well as higher latency. Smaller GPUs (in terms of memory) could suffer from the same issue.
FLUX.2 \[flex\] 4 H200 or GB200 H100 GPUs don’t suffice for the current setup in terms of memory. Fewer and smaller GPUs might suffer from increased latency and OOM errors.
FLUX.2 \[klein\] 4B & 9B 1 H100, H200 or GB200 Klein can run on a single GPU. Using more than a single GPU will not reduce latency further, and smaller GPUs could suffer from OOM errors.
## FLUX Model Names and what they mean - Number = version & sub version (.1, 1.1, .2) - \[pro\] vs \[dev\] = closed source (API) vs. open weights (licensing & self-host) - Ultra = High resolution (currently up to 4 megapixel) - Raw = Fine-tuned for ultra realistic output ## FLUX .2 FLUX.2 \[max\] - Top-Tier-Quality Image Generation and Editing FLUX.2 Prompting Guide \[WIP\] ## [FLUX.1 Kontext](/1fcc370222d580e2af0df93271590e2b?pvs=25) FLUX.1 Kontext \[max\] - Doesn’t do much for edits - basically built on pro and has a model behind it and picks what it thinks are best. (secret) - Thats why it costs more - Helps a lot more with text to image - Likely better for text FLUX.1 Kontext \[pro\] - best overall for price and performance likley (don’t share this with customers!!!) FLUX.1 Kontext \[dev\] (open weights - [FLUX non-commercial license](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux/blob/main/model_licenses/LICENSE-FLUX1-dev)) ## FLUX1.1 FLUX1.1 \[pro\] - more stylized and less resolution FLUX1.1 \[pro\] Ultra - Based off 1.1. It can go much higher resolution than every model. - Ultra can do 4mp (2k res) image so resolution is way higher. - Still very fast speed. - Worse at listening and prompt following than Kontext (personal preference) FLUX1.1 \[pro\] Raw & ## FLUX.1 Flux .1 pro is sunsetted. Please don’t include it in any new agreements! ~~FLUX.1 \[pro\]~~ ~~FLUX.1 \[dev\] (open weights - ~~[~~FLUX non-commercial license~~](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux/blob/main/model_licenses/LICENSE-FLUX1-dev)~~)~~ ~~FLUX.1 \[schnell\] (open source - ~~[~~Apache2.0 License~~](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/apache-2.0/)~~) ~~ ## FLUX.1 Tools **pro series** Flux .1 Tools pro series are sunsetted. Please dont include them in any new agreements! FLUX.1 Fill \[pro\] ~~FLUX.1 Canny \[pro\]~~ ~~FLUX.1 Depth \[pro\]~~ ~~FLUX.1 Redux \[pro\]~~ **dev series** (open weights - [FLUX non-commercial license](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux/blob/main/model_licenses/LICENSE-FLUX1-dev)) FLUX.1 Fill \[dev\] FLUX.1 Canny \[dev\] FLUX.1 Depth \[dev\] FLUX.1 Redux \[dev\] FLUX.1 Canny LoRA FLUX.1 Depth LoRA

317c3702-22d5-8181-9b87-f70eb21df4cf.text:

{"title":"Customer Use Case Interview — Question Bank & Template"}
</properties>
<content>
**Purpose:** Structured question bank for L1 discovery sessions with FLUX.3 Early Access partners. Goal is to learn about video (+audio) use cases and pain points to directly inform posttraining dataset creation.
---
## How to Use This Document
The goal of this is to collect structured feedback from customers on the most important video (+audio) use cases and pain points to directly inform posttraining dataset creation. Keep it simple and focused on learning. Each session should be 30–45 minutes with the customer's product and/or engineering POC. The account manager leads; research/product joins where relevant. **Important: Make sure you’re getting a senior product person that does not only manage one product but that oversees an area as broad as possible . This will help us getting feedback that is really representative of the entire product portfolio and not only of a single product thereof.**
Before the session, the account manager should fill in the **Pre-Session Brief** section with what we already know about the customer. During the session, work through the question bank in order — skip sections that don't apply. After the session, write up findings in the **Post-Session Summary** section and share the summary here on this [notion page](/318c370222d5803da700f7f72eb9d466?pvs=25) (you find it at the bottom of this page) and the in the following thread [https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C0AE7J27UDP/p1772528393725649](https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C0AE7J27UDP/p1772528393725649) 
**Key principle:** For every use case or pain point the customer describes, ask them to share a visual example — a video clip, screenshot, reference output, or failed generation. These samples are a central output of the session.
---
## Pre-Session Brief (fill before the call)
**Customer:** \[Name\]
**Account Manager:** \[Name\]
**BFL Attendees:** \[Names + roles\]
**Customer Attendees:** \[Names + roles\]
**Date:** \[Date\]
**Current BFL products in use:** \[e.g. FLUX.2 Pro, Kontext, etc.\]
**Current ARR / volume:** \[If known\]
**Industry / vertical:** \[e.g. creative tools, e-commerce, entertainment, social media\]
**What we already know about their use cases:** \[Pre-fill from account history, Slack threads, prior syncs\]
**Open questions going in:** \[What specifically do we want to learn from this customer?\]
---
## Question Bank
### 1 - Current State & Video Importance
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand how central video (and audio) is in their product roadmap and current stack.
</callout>
**1.1** How important is video generation to your product today vs. 6–12 months from now? Is it already in production, in prototyping, or still in the exploration phase? How important is it compared to image generation/image editing?
**1.2** What role does audio play alongside video in your use cases? Do you need synchronized audio (speech, music, sound effects), or is video-only sufficient for now?
**1.3** Which video/audio generation models or tools are you currently using (internal or third-party)? What made you choose them?
**1.4** How does image generation fit into your video workflows today? For example, do you generate stills first and then animate, or do you go directly to video?
### 2 - Use Cases & Applications
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Map the specific video (+audio) use cases they care about most, with concrete examples. This will be the central part of the assessment, since the visual examples of what great and what failure looks like, will tell how (and how not) the data distribution should be for the customer)
</callout>
**Important: **Customers often confuse use cases with model capabilities. So please make sure you’re making them aware of the difference. 
**Examples for use cases:**
- product marketing
- pre-visualization for a motion picture
- synth-to-real for video games 
**Examples of model capabilities:**
- text-to-video+audio
- image-to-video+audio
- video-to-video
**Questions:**
**2.1** Walk us through your top 3 video generation use cases in order of priority. For each one: What is the input? What is the desired output? Who is the end user?
**2.2** *For each use case:* Can you show us a reference example of what "great" looks like? This could be an existing output you're happy with, a competitor output, a mockup, or a reference video from another source. *(Encourage them to share screen or - better - send files.)*
**2.3** *For each use case:* Can you show us a current output that falls short? What specifically is wrong with it? *(Ask them to share the actual failed/subpar generation if possible.)*
**2.4** Are there video use cases you've explored but abandoned because no model could handle them well enough? What were they?
**2.5** What video durations matter most to you? (e.g. 2–5 seconds for product clips, 15–30 seconds for social, 60+ seconds for longer content)
**2.6** What resolutions and aspect ratios do you need for video? Is there a minimum quality bar for production use (e.g. 1080p, 4K)?
**2.7** List the 3 model capabilities that are the most important ones to you 
### 3 - Pain Points with Existing Models
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand where current models fail in their production environment. These pain points directly inform posttraining priorities.
</callout>
**3.1** What are the top 3 things that frustrate you most about the video models you're currently using? For each, can you share a specific example — ideally a video sample or screenshot that shows the problem?
**3.2** How would you rate current models on the following dimensions? For any that score poorly, can you show us an example?
- Visual quality / realism
- Motion quality and naturalness
- Temporal consistency (objects/characters staying consistent across frames)
- Text/typography rendering in video
- Character/identity consistency
- Prompt adherence (does the output match what you asked for?)
- Resolution and detail
- Speed / latency
- Audio quality and synchronization (if applicable)
**3.3** Are there specific types of content where models consistently fail? (e.g. hands, faces, complex camera movements, specific materials/textures, brand-specific elements)
**3.4** Do you experience issues with controllability? For example: camera angle control, subject motion control, pacing, or editing-style cuts.
### 3.5 - Camera Controls & Conditioning Preferences
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand how customers want to control camera behavior in generated video — this is a critical input for how we design camera conditioning in FLUX.3.
</callout>
**3.5.1** How important is camera control to your use cases today? Is it a must-have for production, a nice-to-have, or not currently a priority?
**3.5.2** What camera movements matter most to you? (e.g. static/locked shot, pan, tilt, zoom, dolly, orbit, crane, handheld/shaky, drone-style)
**3.5.3** How would you ideally specify camera behavior? For example:
- Natural language descriptions in the prompt (e.g. "slow dolly in")
- Structured parameters (e.g. a dropdown or JSON with angle, movement type, speed)
- Reference video or image as a camera style guide
- Keyframe-based camera path definition
- Something else?
**3.5.4** Do you need control over the starting camera angle or framing? (e.g. close-up, wide shot, bird's eye, POV) How would you want to set that?
**3.5.5** Beyond camera, what other types of generation controls are most valuable to you? (e.g. subject motion speed, expression control, lighting direction, style/mood locking, negative prompting for video)
**3.5.6** Are there specific controllability failures you've hit with current models — where the camera or subject did something unexpected? Can you share an example output?
### 4 - What "Winning" Looks Like
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand the customer's definition of success so we can measure whether FLUX.3 nails their requirements.
</callout>
**4.1** If you could wave a magic wand and have the perfect video model, what would it do that nothing on the market does today?
**4.2** What would it take for you to move your primary video generation workload to FLUX.3? What are the must-haves vs. nice-to-haves?
**4.3** How do you evaluate video models internally? Do you have benchmarks, eval sets, or A/B testing frameworks? Would you be open to sharing these with us (under NDA)?
**4.4** Are there competitive models or products that you consider the current gold standard for your use case? What specifically makes them good? *(Ask for sample outputs if possible.)*
### 5 - Sample Collection Ask
<empty-block/>
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Get those samples! Explicitly ask for visual materials we can use to understand their requirements. This is the most actionable output of the session.
</callout>
**5.1** Can you share 5–10 example outputs that represent your most important use cases — both good and bad examples? For bad examples, annotate what's wrong.
**5.2** Can you share reference videos (from any source) that represent the quality bar and style you're targeting?
**5.3** If you have prompts or input specifications that consistently produce poor results with current models, can you share those?
**5.4** Can you share any internal evaluation criteria, rubrics, or scoring frameworks you use to assess video quality?
<empty-block/>
**Video prompts & samples!!!**
---
### 6 — Pricing Model Preferences for Video Generation
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand how customers currently pay for video generation and what billing structures feel most natural for their workflows, to inform how we design FLUX.3 pricing.
</callout>
**6.1** How are you currently billed for video generation by your existing providers? *(e.g. per second of output, per generation attempt, per resolution tier, flat monthly subscription, compute/GPU time)*
**6.2** Which pricing unit feels most intuitive for video in your workflow : per second of output, per clip regardless of length, per resolution, or something else?
**6.3** How does resolution and duration factor into your expectations around pricing tiers? Would you expect a 4K, 30-second clip to be priced differently from a 1080p, 5-second one?
<empty-block/>
---
## Post-Session Summary (fill after the call)
**Date:** \[Date\]
**Key Use Cases Identified (ranked by priority):**
1. \[Use case\] - \[brief description, input → output\]
2. \[Use case\]
3. \[Use case\]
**Top Model Capabilities (ranked by importanvce):**
1. \[Capability\]
2. \[Capability\]
3. \[Capability\]
**Top Pain Points (ranked by severity):**
1. \[Pain point\] - \[which models affected, example shared? Y/N\]
2. \[Pain point\]
3. \[Pain point\]
<empty-block/>
**Video Importance Level:** \[Critical / High / Medium / Exploratory\]
**Audio Relevance:** \[Yes — synchronized / Yes — separate / Not relevant\]
**Key Competitive Models Mentioned:** \[List\]
**Visual Examples Received:** \[List files/links received\]
**Visual Examples Promised (follow up needed):** \[List what they said they'd send\]
**Surprising Insights or Unmet Needs:** \[Anything unexpected\]
**Follow-Up Actions:**
- [ ] \[Action item — owner — deadline\]
- [ ] \[Action item — owner — deadline\]
---
## Outreach Message Template (for scheduling the session)
Hi \[Name\],
We're in the early stages of building FLUX.3 — our next-generation multimodal model spanning image, video, and audio — and we're inviting a small number of partners to shape its development through structured feedback sessions.
We'd love to set up a 30–45 min session with your product and/or engineering team to understand your most important use cases for video (+audio) generation and where current models fall short. Your input will directly inform how we build FLUX.3.
To make the session as productive as possible, it would be great if your team could come prepared with a few concrete examples — reference videos, current outputs (good and bad), or descriptions of use cases you'd like to see nailed. Visual samples are especially valuable.
This is under NDA and limited to a small group of partners. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through what participation looks like.
\[Account Manager\]
---
## Tips for Interviewers
Always push for specifics over generalities. When a customer says "quality isn't good enough," ask "can you show me a specific output where quality fell short?" The samples and examples they share are more valuable than verbal descriptions.
Don't pitch FLUX.3 capabilities during the session. The goal is to listen and learn, not to sell. If they ask about FLUX.3 specs or timeline, keep it high-level and redirect to their needs.
Spend the most time on Sections 2 and 3 (Use Cases and Pain Points). These directly feed posttraining dataset decisions. Sections 1 and 4 are context-setting; Section 5 helps calibrate expectations.
If the customer mentions audio needs, dig in — this is a newer area and we have less signal. Understand whether they need lip-sync, sound effects, music, voiceover, or ambient audio.
After the session, share the summary in #dev_flux3 within 24 hours so research can act on it quickly.
<empty-block/>
---
## Summary Page
<page url="https://www.notion.so/318c370222d5803da700f7f72eb9d466">Customer Use case/Pain Points/Capability Needs Summary</page>
</content>
</page>

{"title":"Customer Use Case Interview — Question Bank & Template"}
</properties>
<content>
**Purpose:** Structured question bank for L1 discovery sessions with FLUX.3 Early Access partners. Goal is to learn about video (+audio) use cases and pain points to directly inform posttraining dataset creation.
---
## How to Use This Document
The goal of this is to collect structured feedback from customers on the most important video (+audio) use cases and pain points to directly inform posttraining dataset creation. Keep it simple and focused on learning. Each session should be 30–45 minutes with the customer's product and/or engineering POC. The account manager leads; research/product joins where relevant. **Important: Make sure you’re getting a senior product person that does not only manage one product but that oversees an area as broad as possible . This will help us getting feedback that is really representative of the entire product portfolio and not only of a single product thereof.**
Before the session, the account manager should fill in the **Pre-Session Brief** section with what we already know about the customer. During the session, work through the question bank in order — skip sections that don't apply. After the session, write up findings in the **Post-Session Summary** section and share the summary here on this [notion page](/318c370222d5803da700f7f72eb9d466?pvs=25) (you find it at the bottom of this page) and the in the following thread [https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C0AE7J27UDP/p1772528393725649](https://black-forest-labs.slack.com/archives/C0AE7J27UDP/p1772528393725649) 
**Key principle:** For every use case or pain point the customer describes, ask them to share a visual example — a video clip, screenshot, reference output, or failed generation. These samples are a central output of the session.
---
## Pre-Session Brief (fill before the call)
**Customer:** \[Name\]
**Account Manager:** \[Name\]
**BFL Attendees:** \[Names + roles\]
**Customer Attendees:** \[Names + roles\]
**Date:** \[Date\]
**Current BFL products in use:** \[e.g. FLUX.2 Pro, Kontext, etc.\]
**Current ARR / volume:** \[If known\]
**Industry / vertical:** \[e.g. creative tools, e-commerce, entertainment, social media\]
**What we already know about their use cases:** \[Pre-fill from account history, Slack threads, prior syncs\]
**Open questions going in:** \[What specifically do we want to learn from this customer?\]
---
## Question Bank
### 1 - Current State & Video Importance
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand how central video (and audio) is in their product roadmap and current stack.
</callout>
**1.1** How important is video generation to your product today vs. 6–12 months from now? Is it already in production, in prototyping, or still in the exploration phase? How important is it compared to image generation/image editing?
**1.2** What role does audio play alongside video in your use cases? Do you need synchronized audio (speech, music, sound effects), or is video-only sufficient for now?
**1.3** Which video/audio generation models or tools are you currently using (internal or third-party)? What made you choose them?
**1.4** How does image generation fit into your video workflows today? For example, do you generate stills first and then animate, or do you go directly to video?
### 2 - Use Cases & Applications
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Map the specific video (+audio) use cases they care about most, with concrete examples. This will be the central part of the assessment, since the visual examples of what great and what failure looks like, will tell how (and how not) the data distribution should be for the customer)
</callout>
**Important: **Customers often confuse use cases with model capabilities. So please make sure you’re making them aware of the difference. 
**Examples for use cases:**
- product marketing
- pre-visualization for a motion picture
- synth-to-real for video games 
**Examples of model capabilities:**
- text-to-video+audio
- image-to-video+audio
- video-to-video
**Questions:**
**2.1** Walk us through your top 3 video generation use cases in order of priority. For each one: What is the input? What is the desired output? Who is the end user?
**2.2** *For each use case:* Can you show us a reference example of what "great" looks like? This could be an existing output you're happy with, a competitor output, a mockup, or a reference video from another source. *(Encourage them to share screen or - better - send files.)*
**2.3** *For each use case:* Can you show us a current output that falls short? What specifically is wrong with it? *(Ask them to share the actual failed/subpar generation if possible.)*
**2.4** Are there video use cases you've explored but abandoned because no model could handle them well enough? What were they?
**2.5** What video durations matter most to you? (e.g. 2–5 seconds for product clips, 15–30 seconds for social, 60+ seconds for longer content)
**2.6** What resolutions and aspect ratios do you need for video? Is there a minimum quality bar for production use (e.g. 1080p, 4K)?
**2.7** List the 3 model capabilities that are the most important ones to you 
### 3 - Pain Points with Existing Models
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand where current models fail in their production environment. These pain points directly inform posttraining priorities.
</callout>
**3.1** What are the top 3 things that frustrate you most about the video models you're currently using? For each, can you share a specific example — ideally a video sample or screenshot that shows the problem?
**3.2** How would you rate current models on the following dimensions? For any that score poorly, can you show us an example?
- Visual quality / realism
- Motion quality and naturalness
- Temporal consistency (objects/characters staying consistent across frames)
- Text/typography rendering in video
- Character/identity consistency
- Prompt adherence (does the output match what you asked for?)
- Resolution and detail
- Speed / latency
- Audio quality and synchronization (if applicable)
**3.3** Are there specific types of content where models consistently fail? (e.g. hands, faces, complex camera movements, specific materials/textures, brand-specific elements)
**3.4** Do you experience issues with controllability? For example: camera angle control, subject motion control, pacing, or editing-style cuts.
### 3.5 - Camera Controls & Conditioning Preferences
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand how customers want to control camera behavior in generated video — this is a critical input for how we design camera conditioning in FLUX.3.
</callout>
**3.5.1** How important is camera control to your use cases today? Is it a must-have for production, a nice-to-have, or not currently a priority?
**3.5.2** What camera movements matter most to you? (e.g. static/locked shot, pan, tilt, zoom, dolly, orbit, crane, handheld/shaky, drone-style)
**3.5.3** How would you ideally specify camera behavior? For example:
- Natural language descriptions in the prompt (e.g. "slow dolly in")
- Structured parameters (e.g. a dropdown or JSON with angle, movement type, speed)
- Reference video or image as a camera style guide
- Keyframe-based camera path definition
- Something else?
**3.5.4** Do you need control over the starting camera angle or framing? (e.g. close-up, wide shot, bird's eye, POV) How would you want to set that?
**3.5.5** Beyond camera, what other types of generation controls are most valuable to you? (e.g. subject motion speed, expression control, lighting direction, style/mood locking, negative prompting for video)
**3.5.6** Are there specific controllability failures you've hit with current models — where the camera or subject did something unexpected? Can you share an example output?
### 4 - What "Winning" Looks Like
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand the customer's definition of success so we can measure whether FLUX.3 nails their requirements.
</callout>
**4.1** If you could wave a magic wand and have the perfect video model, what would it do that nothing on the market does today?
**4.2** What would it take for you to move your primary video generation workload to FLUX.3? What are the must-haves vs. nice-to-haves?
**4.3** How do you evaluate video models internally? Do you have benchmarks, eval sets, or A/B testing frameworks? Would you be open to sharing these with us (under NDA)?
**4.4** Are there competitive models or products that you consider the current gold standard for your use case? What specifically makes them good? *(Ask for sample outputs if possible.)*
### 5 - Sample Collection Ask
<empty-block/>
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Get those samples! Explicitly ask for visual materials we can use to understand their requirements. This is the most actionable output of the session.
</callout>
**5.1** Can you share 5–10 example outputs that represent your most important use cases — both good and bad examples? For bad examples, annotate what's wrong.
**5.2** Can you share reference videos (from any source) that represent the quality bar and style you're targeting?
**5.3** If you have prompts or input specifications that consistently produce poor results with current models, can you share those?
**5.4** Can you share any internal evaluation criteria, rubrics, or scoring frameworks you use to assess video quality?
<empty-block/>
**Video prompts & samples!!!**
---
### 6 — Pricing Model Preferences for Video Generation
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Goal
	Understand how customers currently pay for video generation and what billing structures feel most natural for their workflows, to inform how we design FLUX.3 pricing.
</callout>
**6.1** How are you currently billed for video generation by your existing providers? *(e.g. per second of output, per generation attempt, per resolution tier, flat monthly subscription, compute/GPU time)*
**6.2** Which pricing unit feels most intuitive for video in your workflow : per second of output, per clip regardless of length, per resolution, or something else?
**6.3** How does resolution and duration factor into your expectations around pricing tiers? Would you expect a 4K, 30-second clip to be priced differently from a 1080p, 5-second one?
<empty-block/>
---
## Post-Session Summary (fill after the call)
**Date:** \[Date\]
**Key Use Cases Identified (ranked by priority):**
1. \[Use case\] - \[brief description, input → output\]
2. \[Use case\]
3. \[Use case\]
**Top Model Capabilities (ranked by importanvce):**
1. \[Capability\]
2. \[Capability\]
3. \[Capability\]
**Top Pain Points (ranked by severity):**
1. \[Pain point\] - \[which models affected, example shared? Y/N\]
2. \[Pain point\]
3. \[Pain point\]
<empty-block/>
**Video Importance Level:** \[Critical / High / Medium / Exploratory\]
**Audio Relevance:** \[Yes — synchronized / Yes — separate / Not relevant\]
**Key Competitive Models Mentioned:** \[List\]
**Visual Examples Received:** \[List files/links received\]
**Visual Examples Promised (follow up needed):** \[List what they said they'd send\]
**Surprising Insights or Unmet Needs:** \[Anything unexpected\]
**Follow-Up Actions:**
- [ ] \[Action item — owner — deadline\]
- [ ] \[Action item — owner — deadline\]
---
## Outreach Message Template (for scheduling the session)
Hi \[Name\],
We're in the early stages of building FLUX.3 — our next-generation multimodal model spanning image, video, and audio — and we're inviting a small number of partners to shape its development through structured feedback sessions.
We'd love to set up a 30–45 min session with your product and/or engineering team to understand your most important use cases for video (+audio) generation and where current models fall short. Your input will directly inform how we build FLUX.3.
To make the session as productive as possible, it would be great if your team could come prepared with a few concrete examples — reference videos, current outputs (good and bad), or descriptions of use cases you'd like to see nailed. Visual samples are especially valuable.
This is under NDA and limited to a small group of partners. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through what participation looks like.
\[Account Manager\]
---
## Tips for Interviewers
Always push for specifics over generalities. When a customer says "quality isn't good enough," ask "can you show me a specific output where quality fell short?" The samples and examples they share are more valuable than verbal descriptions.
Don't pitch FLUX.3 capabilities during the session. The goal is to listen and learn, not to sell. If they ask about FLUX.3 specs or timeline, keep it high-level and redirect to their needs.
Spend the most time on Sections 2 and 3 (Use Cases and Pain Points). These directly feed posttraining dataset decisions. Sections 1 and 4 are context-setting; Section 5 helps calibrate expectations.
If the customer mentions audio needs, dig in — this is a newer area and we have less signal. Understand whether they need lip-sync, sound effects, music, voiceover, or ambient audio.
After the session, share the summary in #dev_flux3 within 24 hours so research can act on it quickly.
<empty-block/>
---

Answers to these questions should be the basis to understand customization potential & effective SE engagement. We have a Notes Template (called ”FLUX Use Case Qualification”) to automate note taking for these use case qualification calls. ## Overview - What does their platform do / What are they building? - What service / product do they provide? - Who are their users? - *Internal vs. external?* - *Consumer vs. Prosumer vs. companies?* - What do the users create / what are common final outputs? - *Ideally, concrete examples* - Are they already using visual AI models? - *Which other models are they using today?* - *What are their main pain points with those models?* - How strategic is image gen to their core business? - What happens to their business if the image generation quality/speed degrades? - What KPIs are they tracking? ## FLUX Integration - How are they integrating visual AI models in their product? - Who writes the prompt? - *End user writes full prompt vs. prompt template that is defined by customer only filled with end users details? * - Simple prompting interface (similar to playground) vs. prompt presets integrated in product functionality? - *“Integrated preset” could be a button that triggers a certain pre-written prompt, without exposing the prompt to the user.* - *e.g. consider virtual try on. A user could upload an image an click try on button. The platform could fully abstract away the prompt from the user.* - More complex workflow? - *Where is the prompting complexity managed in the usual case (user vs. workflow)?* - How can users customize models? - *Upload their own data to finetune?* - *If yes, what type of data do they upload?* - Which API / User Interface do they use? - Reseller vs. BFL directly vs. competitor API - Misc. SaaS UI vs. Playground - Which requirements do they have in terms of (input and) output resolutions? - What are their preferred aspect ratios? - How are they exposing visual AI models to their internal/external users? - *UI vs API vs something else* - *(if UI) Would they be interested in BFL helping them to build a customized UI?* ## Visual Examples SEs need visual examples for **every** use case, before starting to work on it. **Generally we need to know what they tried so far:** - Which models did they try so far & with which parameter settings? - Playground vs. API vs. self-hosted - Reseller vs. BFL platform - Which prompts & inputs did they try so far? - What are the core quality bars we need to meet? - What are the common errors? - What are the no-gos? - What already works well out of the box? **Please ask the customer / partner to share a drive / zip folder with:** - Examples of desired output images (including prompts & input reference images) - Examples of undesired output images (including prompts & input reference images) ## Volume Estimation - How many images are they looking to generate per day / month?

Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/32ec370222d580cda806c600a8e064ad as of 2026-03-31T15:38:53.557Z: {"title":"\\[Product Shop\\] Standard User Interface for Video Models"} > *We build the standard for visual intelligence.

***The standard **means high performance and quality, lean, open, fast, affordable, always available; not clunky – a beautiful, minimalistic, reliable, no-bullshit product which makes it a no-brainer to use because it is so ridiculously easy to build on and get good results.

**Visual intelligence** is the ability to understand and simulate (i.e. create) the underlying geometry, relationships, and interactions between objects in a physical universe. True intelligence will require reasoning across all of these domains, and an understanding of what is persistent over time and what not.

A truly visually intelligent system can simulate the physical world, and enable both humans and agents to explore it, interact with it, and learn from it. ### Goal We need to build the best and most intuitive user experiences around FLUX 3. We need to start exploring directions right away and build for future. #### What is UI/UX? The UI layer is our abstraction to make the value proposition of our model capabilities easy to grasp. We see it already today with some of our customized endpoints: Endpoints are abstract and not necessarily intuitive. We can make clients understand our capabilities WAY easier, if we just showcase the intended use and what it actually generates within a frontend. We see this pattern already today with images and this will be even more amplified once we add more modalities on the input and output. ### Why? - ### What is / (not) the shop? - ### Our path 1. **Competitor & market analysis:
**Check every possible model and product in the world to understand their strengths and weaknesses. 2. **User interviews:
**Talk to creators and power users to understand what are their pain points, what’s working and what’s not working. 3. **Build with insights:
**Coding is not the challenge, building the right thing is. We need to understand the gaps in the workflows from super users and address them in our product. 4. **Feedback research:
**As an outcome, build Product x Research muscle. Regular exchange between product and research, where user and use-case insights inform training priorities and model capabilities shape product direction. ### Team Team of 5 from each department **Product:** **FDE:** **Creative Tech:** **GTM / Sales:** TBD **Research:** TBD ## Questions - Realtime support
Will FLUX 3 be real-time? if so how? - Where will this application live in?
Is it Playground or separate standalone app? - ## Action Items - Finalize the question bank - all - - Tasks Tracker

305c3702-22d5-8027-a797-d9083e34f7e9.title: 🌲✨ The BFL North Star: Towards the Standard for Visual Intelligence
305c3702-22d5-8027-a797-d9083e34f7e9.text: Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/305c370222d58027a797d9083e34f7e9 as of 2026-03-09T08:49:29.141Z: {"title":"🌲✨ The BFL North Star: Towards the Standard for Visual Intelligence"} Visual intelligence is harder than language: Language is an interface, while vision models reality itself. Whoever solves this first defines the next platform. To that end, our north star is: *We build the standard for visual intelligence.* **The standard **means high performance and quality, lean, open, fast, affordable, always available; not clunky – a beautiful, minimalistic, reliable, no-bullshit product which makes it a no-brainer to use because it is so ridiculously easy to build on and get good results. **Visual intelligence** is the ability to understand and simulate (i.e. create) the underlying geometry, relationships, and interactions between objects in a physical universe. True intelligence will require reasoning across all of these domains, and an understanding of what is persistent over time and what not. A truly visually intelligent system can simulate the physical world, and enable both humans and agents to explore it, interact with it, and learn from it. # **How will we get there? ** *A*** ***research perspective.* Through *capable, fast, controllable, and interactive generative models* that have a persistent memory state and produce consistent outputs. These models will become increasingly multimodal: *Everything in → Everything out* To realize this goal, we will adopt unified conditioning across text, images, video, audio and actions. This matters, because the world is inherently multimodal: Structure is learned from images, spatial relationships are learned from image and video, causal relationships from actions and video, and timing from audio, etc. A model trained on all conditions simultaneously builds a richer internal world model than one trained on a single modality (e.g. images) alone. Practically, this means we potentially add auxiliary loss functions on other input modalities like text or actions. For practical reasons, we focus on output quality for natural data (image, video, then audio) first, rather than doing both text modeling and pixel creation at the same time. We will have to put significant work into the memory layer, which is currently the sequence context window. # **Applications we’ll unlock along the way** *(this list is by no means complete)* As these models become increasingly multimodal, they will enable new applications along the way that support our business and grow our community: **Content creation.** Where we already have significant market share. Extend the lead. **Generative UIs.** Rendering, placement, and mockups in real time—as fast as you can think. The memory layer enables users to "browse" through design choices. Potentially paired with audio. Clearest near-term enterprise value beyond content creation. **Simulation.** Fast models with action inputs, consistent outputs and persistent memory. In the short term, enable new interactive experiences in gaming and film with fast, controllable, and personalized visual engines. **Automation. **Beyond that, train agents and robots in generated environments. For example, simulation helps self-driving scale, enables advanced web agents, and helps automate complex manufacturing. Demonstrating a path towards real-world impact in domains beyond content creation could unlock significant markets. **Understanding/Perception.** Combining representation learning with generative abilities. Unlocks novel tasks: perception, object recognition and visual reasoning. Large multimodal models will begin to reason over video rollouts / simulations. Computer use in agents will be amplified by fast, efficient perception models. # **Image as our Foundation** Image modeling is the foundation of our business, our revenue engine and proof point. As we expand into other modalities, our image quality should compound. For example, video dynamics improve spatial understanding and image editing, while audio context increases temporal coherence. This is how we will maintain our lead in image: We are not splitting our focus, but compounding it. Models get smarter overall and benefit from transfer learning. # **Our approach** **Always exploring.**** **We do not care about diffusion vs autoregression vs transfusion vs normalizing flows etc. Whatever it takes, we will explore all viable approaches. **Always shipping. **Importantly, however, we need to keep shipping. Execution speed matters. *Our moat is velocity. We ship faster because **we own the full stack from research to API.* **Always optimizing.**** **Always optimize the tuple of *latency - controllability - quality - consistency*. Everything else should improve as a consequence of this. **Always here. **Building the standard for visual intelligence requires resources. To keep our frontier research sustainable, we need smart and ambitious people, capital, compute, and data. In order to acquire these, we need to build a scalable business, while keeping our research-first culture. **Always open. **We believe that sharing AI innovation openly is good for the world, now and in the future. Open models build trust, attract talent, and create ecosystems that proprietary systems cannot. Projects that defined previous platforms—Linux, Android, CUDA, the web itself—won by being open. We intend to do the same for visual intelligence. From the Black Forest into the World. Feedback

Whoever solves this first defines the next platform. To that end, our north star is: *We build the standard for visual intelligence.* **The standard **means high performance and quality, lean, open, fast, affordable, always available; not clunky – a beautiful, minimalistic, reliable, no-bullshit product which makes it a no-brainer to use because it is so ridiculously easy to build on and get good results. **Visual intelligence** is the ability to understand and simulate (i.e. create) the underlying geometry, relationships, and interactions between objects in a physical universe. True intelligence will require reasoning across all of these domains, and an understanding of what is persistent over time and what not. A truly visually intelligent system can simulate the physical world, and enable both humans and agents to explore it, interact with it, and learn from it. # **How will we get there? ** *A*** ***research perspective.* Through *capable, fast, controllable, and interactive generative models* that have a persistent memory state and produce consistent outputs. These models will become increasingly multimodal: *Everything in → Everything out* To realize this goal, we will adopt unified conditioning across text, images, video, audio and actions. This matters, because the world is inherently multimodal: Structure is learned from images, spatial relationships are learned from image and video, causal relationships from actions and video, and timing from audio, etc. A model trained on all conditions simultaneously builds a richer internal world model than one trained on a single modality (e.g. images) alone. Practically, this means we potentially add auxiliary loss functions on other input modalities like text or actions. For practical reasons, we focus on output quality for natural data (image, video, then audio) first, rather than doing both text modeling and pixel creation at the same time. We will have to put significant work into the memory layer, which is currently the sequence context window. # **Applications we’ll unlock along the way** *(this list is by no means complete)* As these models become increasingly multimodal, they will enable new applications along the way that support our business and grow our community: **Content creation.** Where we already have significant market share. Extend the lead. **Generative UIs.** Rendering, placement, and mockups in real time—as fast as you can think. The memory layer enables users to "browse" through design choices. Potentially paired with audio. Clearest near-term enterprise value beyond content creation. **Simulation.** Fast models with action inputs, consistent outputs and persistent memory. In the short term, enable new interactive experiences in gaming and film with fast, controllable, and personalized visual engines. **Automation. **Beyond that, train agents and robots in generated environments. For example, simulation helps self-driving scale, enables advanced web agents, and helps automate complex manufacturing. Demonstrating a path towards real-world impact in domains beyond content creation could unlock significant markets. **Understanding/Perception.** Combining representation learning with generative abilities. Unlocks novel tasks: perception, object recognition and visual reasoning. Large multimodal models will begin to reason over video rollouts / simulations. Computer use in agents will be amplified by fast, efficient perception models. # **Image as our Foundation** Image modeling is the foundation of our business, our revenue engine and proof point. As we expand into other modalities, our image quality should compound. For example, video dynamics improve spatial understanding and image editing, while audio context increases temporal coherence. This is how we will maintain our lead in image: We are not splitting our focus, but compounding it. Models get smarter overall and benefit from transfer learning. # **Our approach** **Always exploring.**** **We do not care about diffusion vs autoregression vs transfusion vs normalizing flows etc. Whatever it takes, we will explore all viable approaches. **Always shipping. **Importantly, however, we need to keep shipping. Execution speed matters. *Our moat is velocity. We ship faster because **we own the full stack from research to API.* **Always optimizing.**** **Always optimize the tuple of *latency - controllability - quality - consistency*. Everything else should improve as a consequence of this. **Always here. **Building the standard for visual intelligence requires resources. To keep our frontier research sustainable, we need smart and ambitious people, capital, compute, and data. In order to acquire these, we need to build a scalable business, while keeping our research-first culture. **Always open. **We believe that sharing AI innovation openly is good for the world, now and in the future. Open models build trust, attract talent, and create ecosystems that proprietary systems cannot. Projects that defined previous platforms—Linux, Android, CUDA, the web itself—won by being open. We intend to do the same for visual intelligence. From the Black Forest into the World. Feedback

VSCO wanted to change that. The solution: FLUX.1 Kontext \[Pro\] delivers what photographers actually need—semantic understanding that distinguishes intentional artistic choices (grain, light patterns) from unwanted distractions. The result:
→ One-tap removal of power lines, people, and distractions
→ Context-aware edits that preserve texture and artistic intent
→ Zero prompt engineering required—select, edit, done *"FLUX understands what photographers need preserved—the texture, the feeling, the artistic intent."*
— Eric Wittman, CEO VSCO What made this work wasn't just the model. It was the partnership. BFL's Solutions Engineering team worked hands-on with VSCO to optimize workflows, plan features, and solve technical blockers together. AI that feels like a natural extension of tools photographers already trust—not another technical system to master. Read the full case study: \[link\] ### Version 2: **VSCO is bringing desktop-grade AI photo editing to 300M mobile photographers—powered by FLUX.** FLUX.1 Kontext \[Pro\] delivers what photographers actually need: semantic understanding that preserves intentional artistic choices while removing distractions with a single tap. No prompt engineering. No technical expertise. Select, edit, done. *"FLUX understands what photographers need preserved—the texture, the feeling, the artistic intent."*
— Eric Wittman, CEO VSCO Read the full case study: \[link\] ### People to link [https://www.linkedin.com/in/ericjwittman/](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ericjwittman/) --- --- # Content Outline (notes - not to be published) ## Headline *VSCO Brings Desktop-Quality AI Photo Editing to mobile for 300M Photographers with FLUX* ## Subheadline *Combining VSCOs UI and workflow innovation with BFLs state of the art research and hands on partnership approach, opens a new era of photo editing.* ## Section 1: The Platform Barrier ### What Capability Was Previously Platform-Limited - Professional object removal required hours of manual clone/heal work on desktop - Complex masking and blending skills needed for natural-looking results - Mobile editing apps lacked the sophistication for professional removal - Photographers increasingly mobile-first but chained to desktop for finishing - 18-month evaluation journey demonstrated the challenge of finding AI with true quality preservation - VSCO + FLUX proving: AI can match human expertise while preserving artistic vision **Pull Quote:** *"FLUX understands what photographers need preserved—the texture, the feeling, the artistic intent"* ## Section 2: The AI-Powered Breakthrough **\[300 words\]** ### Why AI Models Enable Mobile Professional Editing - **Context Understanding**: FLUX.1 \[Kontext\] understands image semantics, not just pixels—enabling intelligent removal vs. traditional clone/heal tools - **Quality Preservation**: AI maintains texture, lighting, and artistic intent that manual mobile tools couldn't achieve - **Instant Processing**: Complex removal that took hours manually now happens in seconds via AI - **No Manual Skill Required**: AI eliminates need for precise masking and blending expertise - **Consistent Results**: FLUX delivers professional output regardless of user skill level or device ### AI Integration Architecture - **Model Selection Journey**: 1. Initial validation: FLUX Schnell in Canvas (mood boarding) proved quality 2. Perfect fit: FLUX.1 Kontext \[Pro\] 3. Immediate recognition: Quality difference apparent from first tests - **Intelligent Processing Pipeline**: - Custom segmentation models identify objects precisely - Object detection suggests common removals automatically - FLUX.1 Kontext \[Pro\] performs removal while preserving image character - Professional upscaling ensures output quality - --- ## Section 3: The User Experience Revolution **\[250 words\]** ### Before: Complex Desktop Workflows - Transfer photos from mobile to computer - Open heavyweight desktop software (Photoshop, Lightroom) - Hours of manual clone/heal work requiring precision and skill ### After: AI-Powered Mobile Experience - Open photo directly in VSCO AI Lab (iOS) - Tap or brush to select unwanted objects - FLUX.1 \[Kontext\] understands scene context and removes intelligently - AI preserves surrounding textures, lighting, and atmosphere - Continue editing in same creative session - Share directly to portfolio or social - Complete workflow where creativity happens—on mobile - **Mobile-First Design**: AI handles heavy lifting, mobile handles interaction - **Prompt-Free Innovation**: Users select objects visually, AI handles complex scene understanding - **Familiar Tools, AI Power**: Brush/lasso tools everyone knows, powered by FLUX's intelligence ## Section 4: BFL's Excellence in Models and Partnership **\[250 words\]** ### The Model Quality That Made the Difference - **18-Month Validation**: VSCO tested every major AI provider - **Immediate Recognition**: First test with FLUX showed quality gap vs. alternatives - **Proven Track Record**: FLUX Schnell success in Canvas built confidence for expansion - **Technical Superiority**: Understanding context and preserving artistic intent - **Consistent Excellence**: Quality maintained across varied photography styles ### Beyond the API: Hands-On Integration Support - **Human Connection**: Direct access to BFL Solutions Engineers & Forward Deployed Engineers - **Real-Time Problem Solving**: Issues addressed in hours/days, not weeks - **Optimization Partnership**: Joint work on mobile performance and quality - **Rapid Iteration**: Feedback implemented quickly for continuous improvement ### Why This Partnership Model Works - **Shared Mission**: Both companies committed to empowering creators - **Technical + Creative**: BFL brings AI innovation & implementation excellence, VSCO brings creator understanding - **Future Alignment**: Roadmaps developed collaboratively, not in isolation **Partnership Quote:** *"BFL doesn't just provide models—they're invested in co-shaping our photographers' success"* ## Conclusion: Transforming Creative Work Through Partnership **\[150 words\]** ### The Photographer Impact - Hours returned to creativity instead of tedious editing - 300M photographers gaining professional capabilities - Creative momentum preserved through mobile-first workflow ### The Success Formula Proven - **Superior AI**: FLUX understands artistic intent, not just commands - **Intuitive UI**: Patent-pending design makes AI feel like simple tools - **Natural Workflow**: Edit where creativity happens—on location, in the moment - **Result**: Professional quality without professional complexity ### BFL's Unique Value - Industry-leading model quality validated through 18-month search - Hands-on partnership approach accelerating innovation - Genuine investment in photographer success, not just API delivery - Continuous improvement through real-world feedback **The breakthrough**: Making AI feel like a natural extension of tools photographers already trust, not a technical system to master. **The result**: Wedding photographers now edit during cocktail hour. Travel photographers perfect shots while still at the location. Edit time reduction comes not just from AI speed, but from eliminating the friction between creative vision and technical execution. The distinction adds confusion without adding value for readers. Most people outside BFL don't know these are different functions, and frankly, they don't need to. What matters is that BFL provided hands-on technical partnership.
