Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sk "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key: $BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, grab the expanded image URL from `result.sample` — it's a full-resolution PNG with seamlessly generated content filling the new canvas area. --- ## Python quick start ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import base64 import os import time import requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" PARTNER = "" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} # Prompt is optional; the backend prepends "OUTPAINT" automatically. PROMPT = "expand background, woman standing in front of greek temple." IMAGE_PATH = "" WIDTH, HEIGHT = 1024, 1024 BBOX_X1 = 100 # None = center horizontally BBOX_Y1 = 50 # None = center vertically AUTO_CROP = False OUTPUT = "output.png" with open(IMAGE_PATH, "rb") as f: image_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() payload = { "prompt": PROMPT, "input_image": image_b64, "auto_crop": AUTO_CROP, "output_format": "png", } payload.update({"width": WIDTH, "height": HEIGHT}) if BBOX_X1 is not None: payload["bbox_x1"] = BBOX_X1 if BBOX_Y1 is not None: payload["bbox_y1"] = BBOX_Y1 resp = requests.post( f"{BASE}/partners/{PARTNER}/outpainting", headers=HEADERS, json=payload, verify=False, ).json() try: task_id = resp["id"] except Exception as e: print(f"Error getting task id: {e}") print(resp) exit(1) poll_url = resp.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") print(f"Task submitted: {task_id}") while True: result = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}, verify=False).json() if result["status"] == "Ready": img_url = result["result"]["sample"] with open(OUTPUT, "wb") as f: f.write(requests.get(img_url).content) print(f"Saved: {OUTPUT}") break if result["status"] in ("Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated", "Task not found"): print(f"Failed: {result['status']}") break time.sleep(1) ``` --- ## Details: API and Training: The `pydantic` model used to construct the outpainting request. You have three options: - **Let the endpoint handle padding (centered)** — provide your image, set `width` and `height`, and leave `bbox_x1` / `bbox_y1` as `None`. The image will be centered on the new canvas automatically (legacy behaviour). - **Place the image at a custom position** — set `bbox_x1` and `bbox_y1` to control exactly where the top-left corner of your input image lands on the canvas (negative values are allowed). Optionally enable `auto_crop=True` to crop any overflow instead of raising an error. ```python class PartnerOutpaintingInputs(BaseModel): """Input model for partner outpainting endpoint. The caller provides a prompt, an input image, and target dimensions. The image is placed on a white canvas at (width, height) before being sent to the Flex finetuned model. bbox_x1 / bbox_y1 set the top-left corner of the input image on the canvas in pixels (may be negative). When both are None the image is centered (legacy behaviour). """ prompt: Optional[str] = Field( default=None, description=( "Text prompt for outpainting. The trigger word 'OUTPAINT' is prepended " "automatically if absent. Defaults to a quality-focused outpainting prompt." ), ) input_image: str = Field(description="Base64-encoded input image.") width: Optional[int] = Field( default=None, ge=64, description="Target output width." ) height: Optional[int] = Field( default=None, ge=64, description="Target output height." ) bbox_x1: Optional[int] = Field( default=None, description=( "Left offset (px) of input image top-left corner on the canvas. " "Negative values are allowed. None = center horizontally." ), ) bbox_y1: Optional[int] = Field( default=None, description=( "Top offset (px) of input image top-left corner on the canvas. " "Negative values are allowed. None = center vertically." ), ) auto_crop: bool = Field( default=False, description=( "If True, crop the input image to the canvas bounds when it " "extends beyond the edges. If False, an error is raised instead." ), ) output_format: Optional[OutputFormat] = Field(default=OutputFormat.png) ``` The model was trained on green, blue, and magenta masks and performs best with those colors. In practice, however, any solid color with sufficient contrast against the rest of the image should work reliably. ```python MASK_COLORS = { "GREEN": (0, 255, 0), "BLUE": (0, 0, 255), "MAGENTA": (255, 0, 255), } ``` ## Key details

312c3702-22d5-8028-9c20-fad64ab5fadc.title: Multimodal Concept Flow
312c3702-22d5-8028-9c20-fad64ab5fadc.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/312c370222d580289c20fad64ab5fadc as of 2026-04-12T15:47:44.689Z: {"title":"**Multimodal Concept Flow**"} # Overview At BFL we are setting the standard for visual intelligence and embracing the every-thing-in every-thing-out multimodal training and generation — all modalities are treated as first class citizens. However, this is not the case in practice: we are lacking behind in the language domain by treating text as a merely conditioning signal for image (soon video and audio) generation. Our models do not generate text and have limited understanding capabilities of the text modality beyond treating it as a conditional signal for denoising. This is in opposition to our north start: The standard for Visual Intelligence cannot be set with lacking understanding. We cannot keep solely relying on our generation capabilities and neglecting the understanding component of intelligence. # Current Landscape The current landscape have been moving fast in the direction of unification of *understanding* and *generation — they are not in contradiction with one another. Rather, they benefit from each other *\[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\]. Most works have been unifying understanding and generation is a non-organic way: understanding is modeled auto-regressively and generation using flow-matching. Thus, a unified model needs to be trained with two separate losses operating on two different paradigms. Although this is a step in the right direction, there are sill room for improvement. # Main Goal Multimodal inputs → ONE Backbone, Same Loss across all inputs → Multimodal output (generation/understanding - text is also part of the output). For Flux3 we are moving closer to this direction. However, we not capitalizing on text generation, i.e. understanding. We need to change this for upcoming releases. # Measuring succes - At least on par performance with comparable model on - Generation *(GenEval, CoCo FID)* - and Understanding benchmarks (MS-COCO, VQA) - Favorable scaling laws and stable training - Paper out # Head count & compute: - 2 - 3 people - Exploration: At least 16 B200 nodes - best 32 B200 nodes for 3 months - Scale-up: 64 nodes for 1.5 months # Idea - Multimodal Concept Flow (MCF) The main roadblock for this clean solution which led to the dual loss formulation in current approaches is the inherent discrete nature of language — In contrast to other modalities (images, videos, audio) which can be modeled in a continuous latent spaces on top which we can train a FM model, text is still widely modeled in the token space; even for language diffusion models \[8, 9\]. Some works starting exploring the idea of latent language diffusion \[10, 11, 12\]. Other explored the idea of a shred multimodal latent space \[3\] but was limited to understanding tasks and autoregressive regime. The best of my knowledge, we are the first to propose to propose a unified multimodal understanding and generation system operating entirely in joint concept space with a single Flow Matching loss. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/a526574a-9ea9-4d15-841d-882a3502e1af/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZHLJOKSQ%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095902Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQDx%2Bi%2BVSXVGaLSNUlvgyAE5Ob8y3z%2FJ%2BrZDFxkZXrrr4gIhAJGXLxaQcqboewbE4aSfMnsyd%2FsYayk8fOmU0d0OglwkKv8DCAIQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgwZ2F40xl6gsRvwRIgq3AOXKm195Jn5fpwFVXFffeit1dKtOfA3aI3PUtzV%2F%2F5xrU2j7J959PblIGFRlp8%2FPY3jgftBQidkaX2TMqSAUvoYIsMQZnGDvLOjRarT90qdCw5sV%2BHP8QoGSfkLrLviIeQnDlAq%2FOps60nGPQ74uxjh8qioDIfUxv1UWUHnr%2FvXTlOWhyskRp9j9LyCUPTbwb7M0%2FSSo6D2xmCiYHa0c0Py87fLVCkQaIhCQrIA9gHalnUquQ4WjCHFPDSyU9bnQYHJS8PTy8Xl6AwhAU%2BF4Tkaawz8Oc9zULAFhADeKMZsfiZk2obw%2BnQfTufnvbW2TieBsyHO7EL%2Bd4M6Vm5wxx%2FvfmAvDAZFxs41P60sc5ObePNdX1VzPhr1fsKENbioJ2xvaiL4mFdPE2puwEfwKYu%2BYYwIS%2FViS8WO3e%2BW7lyv0M%2FTTuRh6a4N6YT3kXLNGE8nbGUWUOTkiiWfFar0%2Fg5oJvSDFIK2NOWMTXbeMITjJ8mxXPVP5lHJHs52yM8xqEj8FP%2FnEeFhrpW%2Fmeivos586TvgFgvvGgvrAfy5PvmiMZ%2BGE06hw8KNfVIw80mFVHdXnBgyfYsgC77wWDySfuqig0mMvnHCxm8UQWFwE9teWzwqFYOhNWSl5zp1ajCrsJLPBjqkAdqJf3C7rIFtQtcqZYX%2BRDthxP2FfhfGg4BsYAw69eS9CSUn1Dz%2FId1WO3KUGM6%2FbTi0QV2N2H%2BRDgBkW1CjX2RX8BJzpzCKJLPZ3P7LUc47ZWLXE%2BtSjb35CYQt4sjEE4enZ7o8g6kmIGZzYYsZHlhAInrgfXTkIMuBtca9BD%2FlCADnXV3ysGuu89WqnqriW4EsWHkw5wYT%2FB8k949zc3zPpKsa&X-Amz-Signature=937aa3c65930f8f3d304f33b46314480413c2454f6ac1b9ad86aefbec0cd4085&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) # Training ### Stage 1 — Train QFormer (seq-v-SONAR)
Maps DINO patch features to an ordered sequence of SONAR concept embeddings.
One concept per caption sentence. Trained with MSE + contrastive loss. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/6c09cf5c-e453-4cb7-a8d3-a614b347b926/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZHLJOKSQ%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095902Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQDx%2Bi%2BVSXVGaLSNUlvgyAE5Ob8y3z%2FJ%2BrZDFxkZXrrr4gIhAJGXLxaQcqboewbE4aSfMnsyd%2FsYayk8fOmU0d0OglwkKv8DCAIQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgwZ2F40xl6gsRvwRIgq3AOXKm195Jn5fpwFVXFffeit1dKtOfA3aI3PUtzV%2F%2F5xrU2j7J959PblIGFRlp8%2FPY3jgftBQidkaX2TMqSAUvoYIsMQZnGDvLOjRarT90qdCw5sV%2BHP8QoGSfkLrLviIeQnDlAq%2FOps60nGPQ74uxjh8qioDIfUxv1UWUHnr%2FvXTlOWhyskRp9j9LyCUPTbwb7M0%2FSSo6D2xmCiYHa0c0Py87fLVCkQaIhCQrIA9gHalnUquQ4WjCHFPDSyU9bnQYHJS8PTy8Xl6AwhAU%2BF4Tkaawz8Oc9zULAFhADeKMZsfiZk2obw%2BnQfTufnvbW2TieBsyHO7EL%2Bd4M6Vm5wxx%2FvfmAvDAZFxs41P60sc5ObePNdX1VzPhr1fsKENbioJ2xvaiL4mFdPE2puwEfwKYu%2BYYwIS%2FViS8WO3e%2BW7lyv0M%2FTTuRh6a4N6YT3kXLNGE8nbGUWUOTkiiWfFar0%2Fg5oJvSDFIK2NOWMTXbeMITjJ8mxXPVP5lHJHs52yM8xqEj8FP%2FnEeFhrpW%2Fmeivos586TvgFgvvGgvrAfy5PvmiMZ%2BGE06hw8KNfVIw80mFVHdXnBgyfYsgC77wWDySfuqig0mMvnHCxm8UQWFwE9teWzwqFYOhNWSl5zp1ajCrsJLPBjqkAdqJf3C7rIFtQtcqZYX%2BRDthxP2FfhfGg4BsYAw69eS9CSUn1Dz%2FId1WO3KUGM6%2FbTi0QV2N2H%2BRDgBkW1CjX2RX8BJzpzCKJLPZ3P7LUc47ZWLXE%2BtSjb35CYQt4sjEE4enZ7o8g6kmIGZzYYsZHlhAInrgfXTkIMuBtca9BD%2FlCADnXV3ysGuu89WqnqriW4EsWHkw5wYT%2FB8k949zc3zPpKsa&X-Amz-Signature=d4fa807034a05b6961a35a5816d0a9b06a229993a3651bb74a9e7cec511c014f&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) ```python class QFormer(nn.Module): def __init__(self, n_max=6, d_dino=768, d_sonar=1024, n_heads=8, n_layers=6): super().__init__() # N_max learnable query tokens, positionally conditioned self.query_tokens = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(n_max, d_sonar)) self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(n_max, d_sonar) # cross-attention to DINO patch tokens self.cross_attn_layers = nn.ModuleList([ CrossAttentionLayer(d_sonar, d_dino, n_heads) for _ in range(n_layers) ]) # project to SONAR dimension (if d_sonar != d_dino, already same here) self.proj = nn.Linear(d_sonar, d_sonar) def forward(self, z_rae, n_active): """ z_rae: (B, 256, 768) DINO patch tokens n_active: (B,) number of active queries per example returns: (B, N_max, 1024) concept embeddings """ B = z_rae.shape[0] pos = torch.arange(self.query_tokens.shape[0], device=z_rae.device) q = self.query_tokens + self.pos_embed(pos) # (N_max, 1024) q = q.unsqueeze(0).expand(B, -1, -1) # (B, N_max, 1024) for layer in self.cross_attn_layers: q = layer(q, z_rae) # cross-attend to DINO return self.proj(q) # (B, N_max, 1024) ``` ```python def train_qformer(qformer, dino, sonar_text_encoder, dataloader, λ=0.1): """ dataloader yields: (image, [sent_1, sent_2, ..., sent_N]) curriculum: stage 1 coarse (CC12M), stage 2 medium (ShareGPT4V), stage 3 fine (DOCCI) """ for images, caption_sentences in dataloader: B = images.shape[0] # --- encode image with frozen DINO --- with torch.no_grad(): z_rae = dino(images) # (B, 256, 768) # --- encode each sentence with frozen SONAR --- # caption_sentences: list of lists, shape (B, N_i) # pad to N_max, record active counts z_text, n_active, mask = sonar_encode_batch( sonar_text_encoder, caption_sentences ) # (B, N_max, 1024) # --- QFormer forward --- z_img = qformer(z_rae, n_active) # (B, N_max, 1024) # --- per-position MSE loss (active positions only) --- L_mse = (((z_img - z_text) ** 2) * mask.unsqueeze(-1)).mean() # --- contrastive loss --- # positives: (ẑ_i, z_i) for each active position # negatives: (ẑ_i, z_j≠i) within image + across images in batch L_con = info_nce_loss(z_img, z_text, mask) loss = L_mse + λ * L_con ``` ## Stage 2 — Train Image Decoder DiT
A DiT that denoises DINO patch tokens conditioned on SONAR concept embeddings.
Uses flow matching loss. RAE ViT decoder is frozen and used only at inference.
```python class ImageDecoderDiT(nn.Module): def __init__(self, d_rae=768, n_patches=256, d_sonar=1024, d_model=1024, n_heads=16, n_layers=12): super().__init__() # project RAE patch tokens to DiT hidden dim self.patch_embed = nn.Linear(d_rae, d_model) self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(n_patches, d_model) self.time_embed = TimestepEmbedding(d_model) # DiT blocks with cross-attention to SONAR concepts self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([ DiTBlock(d_model, n_heads, d_sonar) # cross-attn to concepts for _ in range(n_layers) ]) self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_rae) # back to 768d def forward(self, z_t, t, concept_embeddings): """ z_t: (B, 256, 768) noisy DINO latent t: (B,) timestep in [0,1] concept_embeddings:(B, N, 1024) SONAR image concepts (conditioning) returns: (B, 256, 768) predicted velocity """ B, P, _ = z_t.shape pos = torch.arange(P, device=z_t.device) x = self.patch_embed(z_t) + self.pos_embed(pos) t_emb = self.time_embed(t) # (B, d_model) for block in self.blocks: x = block(x, t_emb, concept_embeddings) # cross-attn to concepts return self.out_proj(x) # (B, 256, 768) def train_image_decoder(dit, dino, qformer, dataloader, σ_aug=0.1): """ dataloader yields: (image, captions) no pixel supervision needed — only FM loss in DINO latent space """ opt = AdamW(dit.parameters(), lr=1e-4) for images, captions in dataloader: with torch.no_grad(): # frozen DINO: get patch tokens (target latent) z_rae = dino(images) # (B, 256, 768) # frozen QFormer: get concept conditioning z_img_concepts = qformer(z_rae, ...) # (B, N, 1024) # noise augmentation on concepts (robustness to FM imperfection) σ = torch.abs(torch.randn(1) * σ_aug) z_img_concepts = z_img_concepts + σ * torch.randn_like(z_img_concepts) # --- flow matching --- t = torch.rand(images.shape[0]) # (B,) in [0,1] ε = torch.randn_like(z_rae) z_t = (1 - t[:, None, None]) * z_rae + t[:, None, None] * ε # target velocity v_target = ε - z_rae # DiT prediction v_pred = dit(z_t, t, z_img_concepts) loss = F.mse_loss(v_pred, v_target) ``` ## Stage 3 — Train FM Transformer
Joint flow matching over mixed-modality concept sequences. Learns the joint distribution p(image concepts, text concepts). Single FM loss, no modality-specific objectives. ```python class FMTransformer(nn.Module): def __init__(self, d_sonar=1024, d_model=2048, n_heads=16, n_layers=24): super().__init__() self.input_proj = nn.Linear(d_sonar, d_model) self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(1024, d_model) # max sequence length self.time_embed = TimestepEmbedding(d_model) # full bidirectional attention — no causal mask self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([ TransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads) for _ in range(n_layers) ]) self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_sonar) def forward(self, x_t, t_per_position): """ x_t: (B, L, 1024) noisy concept sequence (mixed modalities) t_per_position: (B, L) timestep per position (0 = clean/fixed) returns: (B, L, 1024) predicted velocity per position """ B, L, _ = x_t.shape pos = torch.arange(L, device=x_t.device) x = self.input_proj(x_t) + self.pos_embed(pos) t_emb = self.time_embed(t_per_position) # (B, L, d_model) x = x + t_emb for block in self.blocks: x = block(x) # bidirectional attention return self.out_proj(x) # (B, L, 1024) def train_fm_transformer(fm, dino, qformer, sonar_enc, dataloader, p_uncond=0.10): """ dataloader yields: (image, multi_sentence_caption) Training regime (addresses train-inference mismatch): ~10% joint noising — both modalities noised, learns p(z_img, z_text) enables CFG at inference ~45% text→image — text clean (t=0), image noised trains generation pathway ~45% image→text — image clean (t=0), text noised trains understanding pathway Rationale: at inference one modality is always fully clean (t=0). If we only noise both during training the model never sees a perfectly clean conditioning signal → distribution shift. The 10% joint rate mirrors typical CFG dropout and is sufficient to learn the joint for guidance; the conditional regimes directly match the inference setting. """ opt = AdamW(fm.parameters(), lr=1e-4) for images, captions in dataloader: with torch.no_grad(): # encode image → concept sequence z_rae = dino(images) z_img = qformer(z_rae, ...) # (B, N, 1024) # encode caption → concept sequence z_text = sonar_encode_sentences( sonar_enc, captions ) # (B, M, 1024) B = z_img.shape[0] N = z_img.shape[1] M = z_text.shape[1] # concatenate into one sequence x = torch.cat([z_img, z_text], dim=1) # (B, N+M, 1024) # --- regime sampling ------------------------------------------------ r = random.random() if r < p_uncond: # joint — unconditional: noise all positions t = torch.rand(B, N + M) elif r < p_uncond + (1 - p_uncond) / 2: # text→image generation: text clean, image noised t_img = torch.rand(B, N) t_text = torch.zeros(B, M) t = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) else: # image→text understanding: image clean, text noised t_img = torch.zeros(B, N) t_text = torch.rand(B, M) t = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) # -------------------------------------------------------------------- ε = torch.randn_like(x) x_t = (1 - t.unsqueeze(-1)) * x + t.unsqueeze(-1) * ε v_target = ε - x v_pred = fm(x_t, t) loss = F.mse_loss(v_pred, v_target) ``` ## Training Order and Dependencies - Stage 1: Train QFormer
depends on: DINO (frozen), SONAR encoder (frozen)
data: image + multi-sentence captions
output: seq-v-SONAR → \[ẑ_1...ẑ_N\] per image - Stage 2: Train Image Decoder DiT
depends on: DINO (frozen), QFormer (frozen), RAE decoder (frozen)
data: images only — no captions needed
output: DiT that denoises DINO latents conditioned on SONAR concepts

↓ (can be parallel with Stage 2) - Stage 3: Train FM Transformer
depends on: DINO (frozen), QFormer (frozen), SONAR encoder (frozen)
data: paired image-caption data
output: joint FM model over image + text concept sequences
## ** Key Properties**
Property Description
**Single loss** Pure FM loss everywhere — no CE, no KL, no reconstruction loss during FM training
**Unified space** All modalities live in SONAR 1024d — no modality gap
**Parallel generation** All N concepts denoised simultaneously — no sequential bottleneck
**Language agnostic** SONAR covers 1500 languages zero-shot
**Modular** Each component trains independently, frozen during downstream stages
**Interpretable** Any image concept ẑ_i can be decoded to text via SONAR decoder
**No AR loss** Unlike Transfusion, v-LCM — purely generative via FM
**Bidirectional** FM transformer uses full attention — concepts inform each other during denoising
# Inference ## Image Captioning ```python @torch.no_grad() def generate_caption(image, dino, qformer, fm, sonar_dec, N=3, T=50): """ image: (1, 3, H, W) N: number of caption sentences to generate T: number of FM denoising steps """ # 1. encode image to clean concept embeddings (conditioning) z_rae = dino(image) # (1, 256, 768) z_img = qformer(z_rae, n_active=N) # (1, N, 1024) # 2. initialize text concepts as pure noise z_text = torch.randn(1, N, 1024) # (1, N, 1024) # 3. FM denoising — image concepts fixed (t=0), text concepts noisy dt = 1.0 / T for step in range(T, 0, -1): t_img = torch.zeros(1, N) # image positions: clean t_text = torch.full((1, N), step / T) # text positions: noisy x_t = torch.cat([z_img, z_text], dim=1) # (1, 2N, 1024) t_all = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) # (1, 2N) v = fm(x_t, t_all) # (1, 2N, 1024) v_text = v[:, N:, :] # velocity for text only # euler step on text positions only z_text = z_text - dt * v_text # (1, N, 1024) # 4. decode each concept embedding to a sentence sentences = [ sonar_dec(z_text[:, i, :], target_lang="eng_Latn") for i in range(N) ] return sentences ``` ## Image Generation from Text
```python @torch.no_grad() def generate_image(sentences, sonar_enc, fm, dit, rae_decoder, N=None, T_fm=50, T_dit=50): """ sentences: list of strings (caption sentences) T_fm: FM denoising steps (concept space) T_dit: DiT denoising steps (pixel space) """ M = len(sentences) N = N or M # image concepts = text concepts # 1. encode text to clean concept embeddings (conditioning) z_text = sonar_enc(sentences) # (1, M, 1024) # 2. initialize image concepts as pure noise z_img = torch.randn(1, N, 1024) # ── LEVEL 1: denoise image concepts in SONAR space ────────────── dt = 1.0 / T_fm for step in range(T_fm, 0, -1): t_text = torch.zeros(1, M) # text: clean t_img = torch.full((1, N), step / T_fm) # image: noisy x_t = torch.cat([z_img, z_text], dim=1) t_all = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) v = fm(x_t, t_all) v_img = v[:, :N, :] z_img = z_img - dt * v_img # (1, N, 1024) # z_img now contains clean image concept embeddings # ── LEVEL 2: denoise RAE latent conditioned on image concepts ──── z_rae = torch.randn(1, 256, 768) # init DINO latent dt2 = 1.0 / T_dit for step in range(T_dit, 0, -1): t = torch.full((1,), step / T_dit) v = dit(z_rae, t, z_img) # cross-attn to concepts z_rae = z_rae - dt2 * v # ── decode RAE latent to pixels ────────────────────────────────── image = rae_decoder(z_rae) # (1, 3, H, W) return image ``` # References \[1\] Chameleon Team (2024). *Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818) \[2\] Zhou, C. et al. (2024). *Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images with One Multi-Modal Model. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11039](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11039) \[3\] Qiu, Y. et al. (2026). *Unified Vision–Language Modeling via Concept Space Alignment. *[https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01096](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01096) \[4\] He, J. et al. (2025). *FlowTok: Flowing Seamlessly Across Text and Image Tokens. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10772](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10772) \[5\] Liu. Z, et al. (2025). *Tuna: Taming Unified Visual Representations for Native Unified Multimodal Models. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02014](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02014) \[6\] Tong. S, et al. (2026). *Beyond Language Modeling: An Exploration of Multimodal Pre-training. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03276) \[7\] Wang. Y, et al. (2025). *Unified Reward Model for Multimodal Understanding and Generation. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05236](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05236) \[8\] Arriola. M, et al (2025). *Encoder-Decoder Diffusion Language Models for
Efficient Training and Inference*. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22852](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22852) \[9\] Nie. S, et al. (2025). *Large Language Diffusion Models*. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09992](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09992) \[10\] Lovelace. J, et al. (2023). *Latent Diffusion for Language Generation.* [https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09462](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.09462) \[11\] Meshchaninov. V, et al. (2025). *Cosmos: Compressed and Smooth Latent Space for Text Diffusion Modeling. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21170](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21170) \[12\] Zhang. Y, et al. (2023). PLANNER: Generating Diversified Paragraph via Latent Language Diffusion Model. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02531](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02531)

Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/312c370222d580289c20fad64ab5fadc as of 2026-04-12T15:47:44.689Z: {"title":"**Multimodal Concept Flow**"} # Overview At BFL we are setting the standard for visual intelligence and embracing the every-thing-in every-thing-out multimodal training and generation — all modalities are treated as first class citizens. However, this is not the case in practice: we are lacking behind in the language domain by treating text as a merely conditioning signal for image (soon video and audio) generation. Our models do not generate text and have limited understanding capabilities of the text modality beyond treating it as a conditional signal for denoising. This is in opposition to our north start: The standard for Visual Intelligence cannot be set with lacking understanding. We cannot keep solely relying on our generation capabilities and neglecting the understanding component of intelligence. # Current Landscape The current landscape have been moving fast in the direction of unification of *understanding* and *generation — they are not in contradiction with one another. Rather, they benefit from each other *\[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\]. Most works have been unifying understanding and generation is a non-organic way: understanding is modeled auto-regressively and generation using flow-matching. Thus, a unified model needs to be trained with two separate losses operating on two different paradigms. Although this is a step in the right direction, there are sill room for improvement. # Main Goal Multimodal inputs → ONE Backbone, Same Loss across all inputs → Multimodal output (generation/understanding - text is also part of the output). For Flux3 we are moving closer to this direction. However, we not capitalizing on text generation, i.e. understanding. We need to change this for upcoming releases. # Measuring succes - At least on par performance with comparable model on - Generation *(GenEval, CoCo FID)* - and Understanding benchmarks (MS-COCO, VQA) - Favorable scaling laws and stable training - Paper out # Head count & compute: - 2 - 3 people - Exploration: At least 16 B200 nodes - best 32 B200 nodes for 3 months - Scale-up: 64 nodes for 1.5 months # Idea - Multimodal Concept Flow (MCF) The main roadblock for this clean solution which led to the dual loss formulation in current approaches is the inherent discrete nature of language — In contrast to other modalities (images, videos, audio) which can be modeled in a continuous latent spaces on top which we can train a FM model, text is still widely modeled in the token space; even for language diffusion models \[8, 9\]. Some works starting exploring the idea of latent language diffusion \[10, 11, 12\]. Other explored the idea of a shred multimodal latent space \[3\] but was limited to understanding tasks and autoregressive regime. The best of my knowledge, we are the first to propose to propose a unified multimodal understanding and generation system operating entirely in joint concept space with a single Flow Matching loss. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/a526574a-9ea9-4d15-841d-882a3502e1af/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZHLJOKSQ%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095902Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQDx%2Bi%2BVSXVGaLSNUlvgyAE5Ob8y3z%2FJ%2BrZDFxkZXrrr4gIhAJGXLxaQcqboewbE4aSfMnsyd%2FsYayk8fOmU0d0OglwkKv8DCAIQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgwZ2F40xl6gsRvwRIgq3AOXKm195Jn5fpwFVXFffeit1dKtOfA3aI3PUtzV%2F%2F5xrU2j7J959PblIGFRlp8%2FPY3jgftBQidkaX2TMqSAUvoYIsMQZnGDvLOjRarT90qdCw5sV%2BHP8QoGSfkLrLviIeQnDlAq%2FOps60nGPQ74uxjh8qioDIfUxv1UWUHnr%2FvXTlOWhyskRp9j9LyCUPTbwb7M0%2FSSo6D2xmCiYHa0c0Py87fLVCkQaIhCQrIA9gHalnUquQ4WjCHFPDSyU9bnQYHJS8PTy8Xl6AwhAU%2BF4Tkaawz8Oc9zULAFhADeKMZsfiZk2obw%2BnQfTufnvbW2TieBsyHO7EL%2Bd4M6Vm5wxx%2FvfmAvDAZFxs41P60sc5ObePNdX1VzPhr1fsKENbioJ2xvaiL4mFdPE2puwEfwKYu%2BYYwIS%2FViS8WO3e%2BW7lyv0M%2FTTuRh6a4N6YT3kXLNGE8nbGUWUOTkiiWfFar0%2Fg5oJvSDFIK2NOWMTXbeMITjJ8mxXPVP5lHJHs52yM8xqEj8FP%2FnEeFhrpW%2Fmeivos586TvgFgvvGgvrAfy5PvmiMZ%2BGE06hw8KNfVIw80mFVHdXnBgyfYsgC77wWDySfuqig0mMvnHCxm8UQWFwE9teWzwqFYOhNWSl5zp1ajCrsJLPBjqkAdqJf3C7rIFtQtcqZYX%2BRDthxP2FfhfGg4BsYAw69eS9CSUn1Dz%2FId1WO3KUGM6%2FbTi0QV2N2H%2BRDgBkW1CjX2RX8BJzpzCKJLPZ3P7LUc47ZWLXE%2BtSjb35CYQt4sjEE4enZ7o8g6kmIGZzYYsZHlhAInrgfXTkIMuBtca9BD%2FlCADnXV3ysGuu89WqnqriW4EsWHkw5wYT%2FB8k949zc3zPpKsa&X-Amz-Signature=937aa3c65930f8f3d304f33b46314480413c2454f6ac1b9ad86aefbec0cd4085&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) # Training ### Stage 1 — Train QFormer (seq-v-SONAR)
Maps DINO patch features to an ordered sequence of SONAR concept embeddings.
One concept per caption sentence. Trained with MSE + contrastive loss. ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/6c09cf5c-e453-4cb7-a8d3-a614b347b926/image.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB466ZHLJOKSQ%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T095902Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQDx%2Bi%2BVSXVGaLSNUlvgyAE5Ob8y3z%2FJ%2BrZDFxkZXrrr4gIhAJGXLxaQcqboewbE4aSfMnsyd%2FsYayk8fOmU0d0OglwkKv8DCAIQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgwZ2F40xl6gsRvwRIgq3AOXKm195Jn5fpwFVXFffeit1dKtOfA3aI3PUtzV%2F%2F5xrU2j7J959PblIGFRlp8%2FPY3jgftBQidkaX2TMqSAUvoYIsMQZnGDvLOjRarT90qdCw5sV%2BHP8QoGSfkLrLviIeQnDlAq%2FOps60nGPQ74uxjh8qioDIfUxv1UWUHnr%2FvXTlOWhyskRp9j9LyCUPTbwb7M0%2FSSo6D2xmCiYHa0c0Py87fLVCkQaIhCQrIA9gHalnUquQ4WjCHFPDSyU9bnQYHJS8PTy8Xl6AwhAU%2BF4Tkaawz8Oc9zULAFhADeKMZsfiZk2obw%2BnQfTufnvbW2TieBsyHO7EL%2Bd4M6Vm5wxx%2FvfmAvDAZFxs41P60sc5ObePNdX1VzPhr1fsKENbioJ2xvaiL4mFdPE2puwEfwKYu%2BYYwIS%2FViS8WO3e%2BW7lyv0M%2FTTuRh6a4N6YT3kXLNGE8nbGUWUOTkiiWfFar0%2Fg5oJvSDFIK2NOWMTXbeMITjJ8mxXPVP5lHJHs52yM8xqEj8FP%2FnEeFhrpW%2Fmeivos586TvgFgvvGgvrAfy5PvmiMZ%2BGE06hw8KNfVIw80mFVHdXnBgyfYsgC77wWDySfuqig0mMvnHCxm8UQWFwE9teWzwqFYOhNWSl5zp1ajCrsJLPBjqkAdqJf3C7rIFtQtcqZYX%2BRDthxP2FfhfGg4BsYAw69eS9CSUn1Dz%2FId1WO3KUGM6%2FbTi0QV2N2H%2BRDgBkW1CjX2RX8BJzpzCKJLPZ3P7LUc47ZWLXE%2BtSjb35CYQt4sjEE4enZ7o8g6kmIGZzYYsZHlhAInrgfXTkIMuBtca9BD%2FlCADnXV3ysGuu89WqnqriW4EsWHkw5wYT%2FB8k949zc3zPpKsa&X-Amz-Signature=d4fa807034a05b6961a35a5816d0a9b06a229993a3651bb74a9e7cec511c014f&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) ```python class QFormer(nn.Module): def __init__(self, n_max=6, d_dino=768, d_sonar=1024, n_heads=8, n_layers=6): super().__init__() # N_max learnable query tokens, positionally conditioned self.query_tokens = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(n_max, d_sonar)) self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(n_max, d_sonar) # cross-attention to DINO patch tokens self.cross_attn_layers = nn.ModuleList([ CrossAttentionLayer(d_sonar, d_dino, n_heads) for _ in range(n_layers) ]) # project to SONAR dimension (if d_sonar != d_dino, already same here) self.proj = nn.Linear(d_sonar, d_sonar) def forward(self, z_rae, n_active): """ z_rae: (B, 256, 768) DINO patch tokens n_active: (B,) number of active queries per example returns: (B, N_max, 1024) concept embeddings """ B = z_rae.shape[0] pos = torch.arange(self.query_tokens.shape[0], device=z_rae.device) q = self.query_tokens + self.pos_embed(pos) # (N_max, 1024) q = q.unsqueeze(0).expand(B, -1, -1) # (B, N_max, 1024) for layer in self.cross_attn_layers: q = layer(q, z_rae) # cross-attend to DINO return self.proj(q) # (B, N_max, 1024) ``` ```python def train_qformer(qformer, dino, sonar_text_encoder, dataloader, λ=0.1): """ dataloader yields: (image, [sent_1, sent_2, ..., sent_N]) curriculum: stage 1 coarse (CC12M), stage 2 medium (ShareGPT4V), stage 3 fine (DOCCI) """ for images, caption_sentences in dataloader: B = images.shape[0] # --- encode image with frozen DINO --- with torch.no_grad(): z_rae = dino(images) # (B, 256, 768) # --- encode each sentence with frozen SONAR --- # caption_sentences: list of lists, shape (B, N_i) # pad to N_max, record active counts z_text, n_active, mask = sonar_encode_batch( sonar_text_encoder, caption_sentences ) # (B, N_max, 1024) # --- QFormer forward --- z_img = qformer(z_rae, n_active) # (B, N_max, 1024) # --- per-position MSE loss (active positions only) --- L_mse = (((z_img - z_text) ** 2) * mask.unsqueeze(-1)).mean() # --- contrastive loss --- # positives: (ẑ_i, z_i) for each active position # negatives: (ẑ_i, z_j≠i) within image + across images in batch L_con = info_nce_loss(z_img, z_text, mask) loss = L_mse + λ * L_con ``` ## Stage 2 — Train Image Decoder DiT
A DiT that denoises DINO patch tokens conditioned on SONAR concept embeddings.
Uses flow matching loss. RAE ViT decoder is frozen and used only at inference.
```python class ImageDecoderDiT(nn.Module): def __init__(self, d_rae=768, n_patches=256, d_sonar=1024, d_model=1024, n_heads=16, n_layers=12): super().__init__() # project RAE patch tokens to DiT hidden dim self.patch_embed = nn.Linear(d_rae, d_model) self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(n_patches, d_model) self.time_embed = TimestepEmbedding(d_model) # DiT blocks with cross-attention to SONAR concepts self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([ DiTBlock(d_model, n_heads, d_sonar) # cross-attn to concepts for _ in range(n_layers) ]) self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_rae) # back to 768d def forward(self, z_t, t, concept_embeddings): """ z_t: (B, 256, 768) noisy DINO latent t: (B,) timestep in [0,1] concept_embeddings:(B, N, 1024) SONAR image concepts (conditioning) returns: (B, 256, 768) predicted velocity """ B, P, _ = z_t.shape pos = torch.arange(P, device=z_t.device) x = self.patch_embed(z_t) + self.pos_embed(pos) t_emb = self.time_embed(t) # (B, d_model) for block in self.blocks: x = block(x, t_emb, concept_embeddings) # cross-attn to concepts return self.out_proj(x) # (B, 256, 768) def train_image_decoder(dit, dino, qformer, dataloader, σ_aug=0.1): """ dataloader yields: (image, captions) no pixel supervision needed — only FM loss in DINO latent space """ opt = AdamW(dit.parameters(), lr=1e-4) for images, captions in dataloader: with torch.no_grad(): # frozen DINO: get patch tokens (target latent) z_rae = dino(images) # (B, 256, 768) # frozen QFormer: get concept conditioning z_img_concepts = qformer(z_rae, ...) # (B, N, 1024) # noise augmentation on concepts (robustness to FM imperfection) σ = torch.abs(torch.randn(1) * σ_aug) z_img_concepts = z_img_concepts + σ * torch.randn_like(z_img_concepts) # --- flow matching --- t = torch.rand(images.shape[0]) # (B,) in [0,1] ε = torch.randn_like(z_rae) z_t = (1 - t[:, None, None]) * z_rae + t[:, None, None] * ε # target velocity v_target = ε - z_rae # DiT prediction v_pred = dit(z_t, t, z_img_concepts) loss = F.mse_loss(v_pred, v_target) ``` ## Stage 3 — Train FM Transformer
Joint flow matching over mixed-modality concept sequences. Learns the joint distribution p(image concepts, text concepts). Single FM loss, no modality-specific objectives. ```python class FMTransformer(nn.Module): def __init__(self, d_sonar=1024, d_model=2048, n_heads=16, n_layers=24): super().__init__() self.input_proj = nn.Linear(d_sonar, d_model) self.pos_embed = nn.Embedding(1024, d_model) # max sequence length self.time_embed = TimestepEmbedding(d_model) # full bidirectional attention — no causal mask self.blocks = nn.ModuleList([ TransformerBlock(d_model, n_heads) for _ in range(n_layers) ]) self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_sonar) def forward(self, x_t, t_per_position): """ x_t: (B, L, 1024) noisy concept sequence (mixed modalities) t_per_position: (B, L) timestep per position (0 = clean/fixed) returns: (B, L, 1024) predicted velocity per position """ B, L, _ = x_t.shape pos = torch.arange(L, device=x_t.device) x = self.input_proj(x_t) + self.pos_embed(pos) t_emb = self.time_embed(t_per_position) # (B, L, d_model) x = x + t_emb for block in self.blocks: x = block(x) # bidirectional attention return self.out_proj(x) # (B, L, 1024) def train_fm_transformer(fm, dino, qformer, sonar_enc, dataloader, p_uncond=0.10): """ dataloader yields: (image, multi_sentence_caption) Training regime (addresses train-inference mismatch): ~10% joint noising — both modalities noised, learns p(z_img, z_text) enables CFG at inference ~45% text→image — text clean (t=0), image noised trains generation pathway ~45% image→text — image clean (t=0), text noised trains understanding pathway Rationale: at inference one modality is always fully clean (t=0). If we only noise both during training the model never sees a perfectly clean conditioning signal → distribution shift. The 10% joint rate mirrors typical CFG dropout and is sufficient to learn the joint for guidance; the conditional regimes directly match the inference setting. """ opt = AdamW(fm.parameters(), lr=1e-4) for images, captions in dataloader: with torch.no_grad(): # encode image → concept sequence z_rae = dino(images) z_img = qformer(z_rae, ...) # (B, N, 1024) # encode caption → concept sequence z_text = sonar_encode_sentences( sonar_enc, captions ) # (B, M, 1024) B = z_img.shape[0] N = z_img.shape[1] M = z_text.shape[1] # concatenate into one sequence x = torch.cat([z_img, z_text], dim=1) # (B, N+M, 1024) # --- regime sampling ------------------------------------------------ r = random.random() if r < p_uncond: # joint — unconditional: noise all positions t = torch.rand(B, N + M) elif r < p_uncond + (1 - p_uncond) / 2: # text→image generation: text clean, image noised t_img = torch.rand(B, N) t_text = torch.zeros(B, M) t = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) else: # image→text understanding: image clean, text noised t_img = torch.zeros(B, N) t_text = torch.rand(B, M) t = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) # -------------------------------------------------------------------- ε = torch.randn_like(x) x_t = (1 - t.unsqueeze(-1)) * x + t.unsqueeze(-1) * ε v_target = ε - x v_pred = fm(x_t, t) loss = F.mse_loss(v_pred, v_target) ``` ## Training Order and Dependencies - Stage 1: Train QFormer
depends on: DINO (frozen), SONAR encoder (frozen)
data: image + multi-sentence captions
output: seq-v-SONAR → \[ẑ_1...ẑ_N\] per image - Stage 2: Train Image Decoder DiT
depends on: DINO (frozen), QFormer (frozen), RAE decoder (frozen)
data: images only — no captions needed
output: DiT that denoises DINO latents conditioned on SONAR concepts

↓ (can be parallel with Stage 2) - Stage 3: Train FM Transformer
depends on: DINO (frozen), QFormer (frozen), SONAR encoder (frozen)
data: paired image-caption data
output: joint FM model over image + text concept sequences
## ** Key Properties**
Property Description
**Single loss** Pure FM loss everywhere — no CE, no KL, no reconstruction loss during FM training
**Unified space** All modalities live in SONAR 1024d — no modality gap
**Parallel generation** All N concepts denoised simultaneously — no sequential bottleneck
**Language agnostic** SONAR covers 1500 languages zero-shot
**Modular** Each component trains independently, frozen during downstream stages
**Interpretable** Any image concept ẑ_i can be decoded to text via SONAR decoder
**No AR loss** Unlike Transfusion, v-LCM — purely generative via FM
**Bidirectional** FM transformer uses full attention — concepts inform each other during denoising
# Inference ## Image Captioning ```python @torch.no_grad() def generate_caption(image, dino, qformer, fm, sonar_dec, N=3, T=50): """ image: (1, 3, H, W) N: number of caption sentences to generate T: number of FM denoising steps """ # 1. encode image to clean concept embeddings (conditioning) z_rae = dino(image) # (1, 256, 768) z_img = qformer(z_rae, n_active=N) # (1, N, 1024) # 2. initialize text concepts as pure noise z_text = torch.randn(1, N, 1024) # (1, N, 1024) # 3. FM denoising — image concepts fixed (t=0), text concepts noisy dt = 1.0 / T for step in range(T, 0, -1): t_img = torch.zeros(1, N) # image positions: clean t_text = torch.full((1, N), step / T) # text positions: noisy x_t = torch.cat([z_img, z_text], dim=1) # (1, 2N, 1024) t_all = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) # (1, 2N) v = fm(x_t, t_all) # (1, 2N, 1024) v_text = v[:, N:, :] # velocity for text only # euler step on text positions only z_text = z_text - dt * v_text # (1, N, 1024) # 4. decode each concept embedding to a sentence sentences = [ sonar_dec(z_text[:, i, :], target_lang="eng_Latn") for i in range(N) ] return sentences ``` ## Image Generation from Text
```python @torch.no_grad() def generate_image(sentences, sonar_enc, fm, dit, rae_decoder, N=None, T_fm=50, T_dit=50): """ sentences: list of strings (caption sentences) T_fm: FM denoising steps (concept space) T_dit: DiT denoising steps (pixel space) """ M = len(sentences) N = N or M # image concepts = text concepts # 1. encode text to clean concept embeddings (conditioning) z_text = sonar_enc(sentences) # (1, M, 1024) # 2. initialize image concepts as pure noise z_img = torch.randn(1, N, 1024) # ── LEVEL 1: denoise image concepts in SONAR space ────────────── dt = 1.0 / T_fm for step in range(T_fm, 0, -1): t_text = torch.zeros(1, M) # text: clean t_img = torch.full((1, N), step / T_fm) # image: noisy x_t = torch.cat([z_img, z_text], dim=1) t_all = torch.cat([t_img, t_text], dim=1) v = fm(x_t, t_all) v_img = v[:, :N, :] z_img = z_img - dt * v_img # (1, N, 1024) # z_img now contains clean image concept embeddings # ── LEVEL 2: denoise RAE latent conditioned on image concepts ──── z_rae = torch.randn(1, 256, 768) # init DINO latent dt2 = 1.0 / T_dit for step in range(T_dit, 0, -1): t = torch.full((1,), step / T_dit) v = dit(z_rae, t, z_img) # cross-attn to concepts z_rae = z_rae - dt2 * v # ── decode RAE latent to pixels ────────────────────────────────── image = rae_decoder(z_rae) # (1, 3, H, W) return image ``` # References \[1\] Chameleon Team (2024). *Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09818) \[2\] Zhou, C. et al. (2024). *Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images with One Multi-Modal Model. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11039](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11039) \[3\] Qiu, Y. et al. (2026). *Unified Vision–Language Modeling via Concept Space Alignment. *[https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01096](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01096) \[4\] He, J. et al. (2025). *FlowTok: Flowing Seamlessly Across Text and Image Tokens. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10772](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10772) \[5\] Liu. Z, et al. (2025). *Tuna: Taming Unified Visual Representations for Native Unified Multimodal Models. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02014](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02014) \[6\] Tong. S, et al. (2026). *Beyond Language Modeling: An Exploration of Multimodal Pre-training. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03276) \[7\] Wang. Y, et al. (2025). *Unified Reward Model for Multimodal Understanding and Generation. *[https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05236](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05236) \[8\] Arriola. M, et al (2025). *Encoder-Decoder Diffusion Language Models for
Efficient Training and Inference*. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22852](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22852) \[9\] Nie. S, et al. (2025). *Large Language Diffusion Models*. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09992](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09992) \[10\] Lovelace. J, et al. 32fc3702-22d5-8050-8235-e658c1acd49f.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/32fc370222d580508235e658c1acd49f as of 2026-04-02T22:11:55.700Z: {"title":"Technical Project Discussion — Interview Guide (Infrastructure)"} Evaluate the candidate’s technical ownership, decision-making, and ability to deeply understand and reflect on complex systems they’ve built. This is a deep dive into ONE past project. Focus on: - ownership and contributions - system design and architecture - technical decision-making and tradeoffs - debugging and problem-solving - ability to reflect and improve systems ## What Good Looks Like Strong candidates will: - clearly explain a complex system end-to-end - demonstrate real ownership (not just participation) - explain why decisions were made (not just what) - discuss tradeoffs and alternatives - walk through real failures or challenges - reflect on what they would do differently ## Core Question Here's how we'll structure it: you'll have about 15 minutes to walk me through the project uninterrupted - the architecture, the key decisions you made, the trade-offs, and the challenges. I won't cut in during that time. After that, I'll go deep with questions for about 20 minutes. Then we'll end with a retro - how you'd approach it differently today. We'll save the last 5 minutes for your questions. Any questions before we start?"

"Go ahead - take a moment to think about which project you want to walk me through. It should be something where you made meaningful technical decisions and faced real constraints. Ready when you are." "Hi \[name\], welcome. I'm \[your name\] - I'm on \[team\], focused on \[responsibilities\]. Today's format is a bit different from a typical interview. I want to hear you go really deep on one project - the most technically complex thing you've worked on, ideally in the ML infrastructure space. No slides needed; I care about the substance, not the presentation.
Candidate Presentation (15 min) > Do not interrupt during this phase. Your job is to listen and take notes. If they go off on a tangent, let them - it often reveals what they actually care about. If they finish early (under 8 min), that's a signal in itself.
What to listen for? - Depth markers - note when you hear these - Do they lead with "what" or "why"? Strong candidates explain reasoning before mechanics. - Do they name specific systems, numbers, constraints - or stay at abstract level? - Do they acknowledge trade-offs unprompted, or present everything as the obvious right call? - Do they mention other teams, stakeholders, pushback? Or present as if they worked in a vacuum? - How do they talk about failure? Do they surface it voluntarily, minimize it, or skip it entirely? - Note-taking prompts (jot for Q&A) - Any decision they made that sounds under-explained - you'll push on this - Any number that sounds impressive - verify it. - Any team dynamic they glossed over - ask about it - Any technology choice that wasn't justified — surface it
Deep Q&A ( \~ 20 min) ”Thanks - really interesting. I'm going to go deep now. Some of my questions will be about things you mentioned, some will push into areas you didn't cover. There are no trick questions - I just want to understand how you think.”
Q1: Architecture and design decisions - “You chose \[X\]. Walk me through why that over \[Y\]”
Frame it as - "You mentioned \[decision\]. What were the real alternatives you considered, and what ruled them out?" - "At the time, what were you most uncertain about in that choice?" - "If someone on your team pushed back on that approach, what would their strongest argument have been?"
Listen for - Can they steelman the alternative? Weak candidates can only defend their choice, not articulate the opponent's case. - Is their reasoning based on data/constraints, or post-hoc rationalization? - Positives: - Names concrete constraints that drove the choice - Acknowledges what they gave up - Negatives: - Every choice was "obvious" or "best practice"
Q2: Scale and constraints - “What broke first as this scaled, and how did you know it was going to break before it did?”
Variations - "What were the hard limits of your design - the ceiling you knew you'd eventually hit?" - "What assumptions in your architecture would have needed to change at 10x the load?" - "How did you validate it would hold at scale before you committed to it?"
Listen for - Do they have mental models for failure modes, or did they discover problems reactively? - Can they distinguish what they knew vs. what they discovered?
Positives - Anticipates bottlenecks before they happened - Has numbers - not just "it scaled well"
- Negatives - Can only describe what broke, not why it was going to
Q3: Hardest technical problem - “What was the single hardest problem you hit, and walk me through how you actually solved it step by step”
Push on process, not just outcome - "Walk me through your debugging process - what did you try first, what eliminated what?" - "What was your hypothesis going in, and when did it turn out to be wrong?" - "How long did it take, and what eventually cracked it?"
Listen for - Do they have a systematic method, or did they stumble into the answer? - Can they reconstruct their mental state at the time - not just the clean retrospective version?
Positives: - Describes what they ruled out and why - Admits they were wrong initially

Variations - "Who pushed back hardest on your approach, and what was their concern?" - "How did you get alignment when teams had different priorities or timelines?" - "Was there a decision you made that someone else owned - how did you navigate that?"

2b1c3702-22d5-8046-a04d-ea40a9b77d26.title: Large-scale Video Data Project
2b1c3702-22d5-8046-a04d-ea40a9b77d26.text: Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2b1c370222d58046a04dea40a9b77d26 as of 2025-11-22T02:06:56.522Z: {"title":"Large-scale Video Data Project"} We are in the process of acquiring O(100 PiB) of video data - There is 1.4BN videos available from wyndlabs. We need to decide how much we would like to acquire. I think we should do some cost modeling for different dataset scales and do the maximum we are comfortable spending. - is also acquiring a large common crawl video set. Action items: - PR and link current Captioning workflow - Next step: Can we optimize speed? - reaching out to storage companies (don’t exactly remember the names) Questions to answer: - Where are we storing the data? - To answer this we first need to figure out where we want to train with this data. My assumption is ideally everywhere. - How does transfer work? - How are we storing the data? - For Azure Blob storage a flat structure is better. - Processing of the data to prepare for training - Captioning - How long does it take given how many GPUs? - Do we have the final setup that we are confident with? In the past we have wasted quite a bit compute on re-captioning. - Clipping - How long does it take given how many CPUs? - Other processing steps: embedding computation, motion scores - How long does it take give how many GPUs - Training - Will the amount of training compute we have available be a factor in the size of our datasets.

{"title":"Research Data Requests"}
</properties>
<content>
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	**Why do we need this doc?**
	We have various means to acquire post training data, among them
	- the dataworks team 
	- 3rd party vendors and partners
	- our own automatic data pipelines
	- data from our products 
	- Open source datasets
	The purpose of this doc is to get an overview of the requests that come from various teams (input from those teams), map them to one or more channels to acquire them and assign an owner to use that channel to get it.  
</callout>
## How does this work?
**Research Team Members**
- put in a new request by filling in the fields `Name` , `Domain` , `Quantity needed` , `Requesting Person`  (aka their name) and optionally `Examples` / `Online Examples` ,`How do we get it` (in case there’s already an idea) and `Data Category`
- in the card, write a short description on `Why do we need this?`  and `How will this help us improve?` + add any helpful visual examples.
Like this, we always have a good overview of what we need and we can build data focused shops, go buy the data at some 3rd party, use the dataworks team or build the dataset from user data.
## What happens after we have got some data?
After we’ve created a new dataset (either internally or bought externally) we should ablate how well this dataset is suited for training. For this we usually have two means:
- using human voters to compare the new dataset with existing ones (e.g. for synthetic datasets)
- training a model on the data and comparing it to a baseline without that data
## What if I’m working on a dataset myself atm?
please put it in (in this case the `Requesting Person`  would be the one under `Assigned To` ), so others know it and an potentially also use it . Like this we can avoid doing work twice.
## Dataworks Post-Training Data Viewer
[baseline-streamlit.tunnel.bfl.ai](https://baseline-streamlit.tunnel.bfl.ai/) contains a viewer into the data that’s currently annotated by dataworks. This can be used to close the feedback loop between people requesting data and the dataworks team, to make sure what’s collected and annotated is aligned with what’s needed.

The `object://` protocol is a convenience alias that resolves to the **default** storage for the current cluster: - On H200 → `nebius-us://` - On B200 → `nebius-israel://` - On GB200 → `azure-us://` ### How to Access Use `fsspec`-based access throughout the codebase: ```markup from utils.environment import prepare_env_for_blob # sets up credentials for all backends import fsspec # Use the cluster's default object storage fsspec.open("object://bucket/path/to/file") # Or be explicit about which region fsspec.open("nebius-us://bucket/path/to/file") # H200 (US) fsspec.open("nebius-israel://bucket/path/to/file") # B200 (Israel) fsspec.open("azure-us://container/path/to/file") # GB200 (Azure) ``` You can also use the helper: ```markup from utils.environment import fs_from_path fs, path = fs_from_path("object://bucket/path/to/file") ``` There is also a CLI wrapper for quick operations: ```markup python -m utils.fs ls nebius-us:// # list buckets python -m utils.fs ls azure-us://image-datasets/precomputed # list contents python -m utils.fs head nebius-us://bucket/path/to/file.txt # preview file python -m utils.fs copy nebius-us://bucket/file.txt /tmp/local # download ``` ### Interactive Browser To browse storage interactively (vim-style `hjkl` navigation): ```markup python scripts/storage_browser.py # pick a backend ``` Keybindings: `w`/`s` or arrows to move up/down, `d`/Enter to enter a directory, `a`/Delete to go back, `/` to filter, `i` for file info, `q` to quit. ### H200 vs B200: Different S3 Regions Both Nebius clusters use S3, but they are **separate buckets in separate regions**. 1. Recruiter screen
2. Vibe check with Freddy (30 mins)
3. Tech interview with Griffin (45 mins)
This session evaluates your ability to implement key deep learning components in PyTorch with a focus on correctness and efficiency. You'll work in a shared Google Colab environment, completing a live coding exercise.
1. Onsite
You'll work on a focused research implementation task that mirrors the type of work we do at BFL. The task involves reading and understanding a recent research paper, implementing a core analysis from it, and running experiments with a pretrained model.
Expect to spend \~5 hours of focused work debugging practical issues (memory constraints, data loading, etc.), presenting your findings, and proposing extensions or alternative approaches. The goal isn't perfection—it's to see how you think through problems, implement ideas, and communicate your process.
You'll have access to compute resources and can use any tools/libraries you're comfortable with. We'll also have lunch with the team and wrap up with a 30-minute team fit conversation.
</content>

# **Head of Finance MOC**
### **Mission**
- Build and scale a world-class finance function to support Black Forest Labs' rapid growth to 100m ARR+
- Drive strategic financial planning and controls across our global operations while preparing the company for future growth milestones: we always want to be fundraising ready
- Partner with leadership to optimise our dual revenue streams from API and licensing models, cash flow planning/compute/ fundraising planning
In a nutshell, we are looking for a generalist who is hungry:
-
	![]()
	Strategic financial planning /FP&A who can go deep on financial modeling, build our budget, track metrics
-
	![]()
	(Up) Scaling financial processes and systems
-
	![]()
	Accounting DNA for managing accounting operations and monthly bookkeeping with external accounting firm
-
	![]()
	Liquidity and cash flow management
-
	![]()
	Can work independently without a large team around them
-
	![]()
	Maintains agility needed for continued growth: international expansion, sophisticated financial planning
-
	![]()
	Can run EY finance ops workstreams
### **Outcomes (Next 12-18 Months)**
### Financial Planning & Strategy
- Develop and maintain comprehensive financial models and rolling forecasts aligned with company strategy
- Lead consolidated reporting and financial planning across international entities
- Drive strategic initiatives including pricing strategies and long-term financial planning
- Partner with leadership to provide actionable financial insights for decision-making
### Operations & Infrastructure
- Design and implement scalable financial controls and accounting infrastructure
- Oversee core financial operations (AR/AP, bookkeeping, reconciliation)
- Manage cash flow optimization and treasury operations
- Establish efficient, scalable finance ops processes for BFL's continued growth
### Compliance & External Relations
- Lead tax strategy and compliance efforts with EY and other partners
- Oversee global IP structure and transfer pricing implementation
- Ensure regulatory compliance across all jurisdictions
- Manage relationships with key financial partners and vendors
### Team Building & Leadership
- Work independently for 6-12 months and collaborate with external accounting and tax advisory firms
- Create effective working relationships with CEO, Chief of Staff, Sales
- Establish finance as a trusted strategic partner to the business
### **Core Competencies**
### Technical Excellence
- Deep expertise in SaaS/AI finance, particularly with usage-based, API and software licensing models
- Strong foundation in GAAP/IFRS with international accounting experience
- Proven ability to build financial systems and controls from the ground up
- Experience with modern finance tech stack implementation
### Strategic Leadership
- Track record of being a strategic partner to CEOs/founders in high-growth technology companies
- Ability to translate financial concepts for technical and non-technical stakeholders
- Experience in scaling finance operations internationally
- Strong analytical skills with focus on business impact and actionable insights
### Cultural Fit & Working Style
- Comfort with ambiguity and rapid change typical of AI/ML technology companies
- Hands-on leader willing to both set strategy and execute on tactical needs
- Interest in AI/ML technology and BFL position in the market
### Must-Have Qualifications
- 5-10 years of relevant FP&A experience in B2B software/technology companies
- Experience managing international financial operations and entities
- Professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACCA, or equivalent)
- Track record implementing financial systems and controls
- Experience with both API and software licensing revenue models
### Nice-to-Have Qualifications
- German language proficiency
- Prior experience in AI/ML companies
- Background in venture-backed startups
### **Success Metrics (First Year)**
1. Implementation of scalable financial planning and reporting processes
2. Establishment of international entity / IP structure with EY and controls
3. Runs monthly closing bookkeeping independently
4. Revamp Financial systems like ERP
### Resources Required
- Systems implementation budget
- Travel budget for time at international offices
- Professional services budget (audit, tax, advisory)
### Reporting & Relationships
- Reports to: CEO
- Key Relationships: Chief of Staff, Legal, Sales
- Not expected to build a large team around them for a while
</content>
</page>

2f0c3702-22d5-8073-9b20-f5f9d6646d0a.title: Strategic finance/FP&A
2f0c3702-22d5-8073-9b20-f5f9d6646d0a.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2f0c370222d580739b20f5f9d6646d0a as of 2026-03-31T15:37:00.872Z: {"title":"Strategic finance/FP&A"} ## The Role We're looking for a strategic finance leader who can bring structure to high-growth chaos. As our first dedicated FP&A, you'll be the financial architect behind our scaling decisions—translating our rapid growth into clear financial frameworks, building robust planning processes, and partnering with leadership to make disciplined decisions about where and how to invest. This is a high-impact, hands-on role. You'll own the company's financial planning muscle, work directly with finance leadership and executive team, and have visibility into every major business decision. You'll be comfortable operating across our US and German entities, understanding the complexities of international operations, and building scalable processes that work across borders. If you're energized by turning ambiguity into clarity, love building systems from scratch, and want direct impact on a fast-scaling AI company, we'd love to meet you. ## What You'll Do ### Core Responsibilities **Financial Planning & Forecasting** - Own and drive the full planning cycle: annual operating plans, quarterly forecasts, rolling projections, and long-range strategic planning - Build and maintain sophisticated financial models covering revenue (API, Playground, Enterprise), expenses, headcount, GPU compute costs and model building complexity as well as cash flow across the group. - Lead scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for major decisions (GPU provider contracts, go-to-market expansion, pricing frameworks) - Drive continuous improvement in forecast accuracy as the business scales **Business Partnership** - Partner with GTM leadership on revenue forecasting, customer segmentation economics, pricing strategy, and capacity planning - Collaborate with Engineering on GPU compute optimization, infrastructure planning, and R&D investment allocation - Support Product on feature prioritization, monetization analysis, and competitive positioning - Translate strategy into financial reality—surfacing tradeoffs, forcing clarity, and ensuring alignment between ambition and resources **Performance Management & Insights** - Deliver monthly and quarterly business reviews with variance analysis, KPIs, and actionable insights - Build executive dashboards that track key metrics: ARR growth, customer cohort economics, gross margins, burn rate, runway - Analyze the P&L across our multiple revenue streams and identify opportunities for margin expansion and efficiency - Help craft compelling financial narratives for board meetings, investor updates, and strategic planning sessions **Systems & Process Excellence** - Design and implement scalable FP&A processes that work with a growing, fast moving company in a new space - Partner with Accounting to ensure close process efficiency, data integrity, and reporting consistency - Drive automation and AI enablement across financial planning and reporting - Build the infrastructure (tools, templates, workflows) needed to support 3-5x growth **Strategic Initiatives** - Support high-impact projects: pricing optimization, enterprise contract structuring, M&A evaluation, fundraising support - Work with Rev Ops in building customer segmentation frameworks and analyze unit economics by customer type, geography, and product ## What Success Looks Like ### First 30 Days - Learn & Assess - Understand our business model deeply: revenue streams, customer base, pricing mechanics, cost structure - Audit existing financial models, forecasts, and reporting processes—identify gaps and quick wins - Build relationships with key stakeholders: Chief of Staff, Engineering leads and founders - Gain fluency in our GPU compute economics and infrastructure costs - Deliver initial observations and recommendations on planning process improvements ### First 60 Days - Build & Improve - Own the next quarterly forecast cycle end-to-end with improved accuracy and granularity - Establish monthly business review cadence with consistent KPIs, variance analysis, and executive reporting - Create or significantly enhance core financial models: revenue by stream, customer cohort analysis, headcount planning, cash flow forecasting - Implement 2-3 quick process improvements that increase efficiency or data quality - Partner with GTM on refined revenue forecasting methodology incorporating pipeline visibility - Begin designing the framework for annual planning cycle ### First 90 Days - Lead & Scale - Lead any reforecasting process with bottoms-up input from all departments - Help craft board-ready materials demonstrating financial performance, trends, and strategic recommendations - Establish yourself as the trusted financial advisor to executive team and department leaders - Deliver tangible business impact: better decisions, clearer tradeoffs, improved forecast accuracy, or process efficiency gains - Identify and begin implementing 1-2 strategic initiatives (pricing optimization, customer segmentation economics, scenario planning framework) ## What You Bring ### Essential Requirements **Experience** - 6-10 years in FP&A, corporate finance, investment banking, consulting, or strategic finance - Minimum 4 years hands-on FP&A experience at a high-growth company - Proven track record owning full planning cycles (annual budgeting, quarterly forecasts, long-range planning) - Experience with B2B AI or SaaS or technology businesses; understanding of subscription economics, usage-based pricing, and enterprise sales - Comfort with international operations or multi-entity financial structures **Technical Skills** - Advanced Excel/Google Sheets with strong financial modeling capabilities—you can build complex models from scratch - Experience with modern finance tech stack and curiosity around AI improvements and possibilities against legacy tech stack incumbents - Understanding of SaaS metrics: ARR/MRR, NDR, CAC, LTV, payback period, gross margin, Rule of 40 and ideally experience with consumption based metrics - Ability to work with large datasets, perform variance analysis, and build dashboards - Financial statement literacy and understanding of US GAAP **Interview Process** Screening First interview: Dave Arkell Second interview: Sarah/ Adam- Aim to asses cultural fit/values alignment things to test for: Suggest Sarah test agency/speed and Adam test culture and prioritisation - **High agency/ownership** - *Tell me about a time you identified a problem at work that wasn't in your job description and fixed it anyway. What happened?* - *Give me an example of a decision you made with limited information that turned out to be right — and one that turned out to be wrong. What did you do differently after the second one?* - *When did you last disagree with your manager about how to approach something? What did you do?* - *Tell me about a project you owned end to end. What would have happened if you hadn't pushed it forward?* - *Have you ever taken on a responsibility that was clearly above your pay grade/scope? What drove you to do it?* - **Operating with ambiguity and speed** - *How do you personally decide when you have enough information to act versus when to keep gathering data?* - *Tell me about a time a key assumption in your plan turned out to be wrong mid-execution. What did you do?* - *Tell me about a time you had to present a forecast you weren't fully confident in. How did you frame it, and what happened?* - *Have you ever been pressured to move faster on a model or report than you were comfortable with? How did you handle it?* - *When do you think it's acceptable to present numbers you know are directionally right but not fully reconciled? Where do you draw the line?* - *Give me an example of a financial analysis you did that turned out to be more precise than the situation actually needed. What would you do differently?* - *How do you decide what level of detail is enough in a model — and how has that judgment changed over your career?* - **Prioritisation under pressure** - *Walk me through a month-end close or forecast cycle where everything went wrong at the same time. What did you triage and why?* - *Tell me about a time a senior stakeholder asked for a completely new analysis mid-cycle. How did you balance that with existing commitments?* - *What's the thing you most consistently have to let go of — in terms of quality or completeness — when time is short? Does that bother you?* - **BFL specific cultural fit** - *What do you find genuinely interesting about what BFL is building? What aspect of the product or technology have you spent time trying to understand?* - *Have you ever had to get your head around a completely new technical domain quickly — compute infrastructure, a new business model, a new regulatory regime? How did you go about it?* - *Tell me about a time you worked closely with engineers or researchers who thought very differently from you. What did you learn, and what friction did you encounter?* - *What does "good" look like to you in a fast-scaling company — and how is that different from a large, established one?* - *When have you had to push back on something senior leadership wanted to do? How did you frame it?* Third interview: Robin - looking at how well he could work with them Case study on-site

**Case Study** 1. Revenue forecasting 1. Give historic MRR reporting (and caveat that there are billing errors) 2. Show historical trends with both our and other model releases 3. Give roadmap of next model releases 4. Show sales headcount evolution 5. Ask to produce a revenue forecast for the next 6 months based on those inputs 1. Cost planning 1. Attached are our historic costs, current headcount evolution and some of our broader strategies/bets that we may be considering. Put together a template for us to be able to model costs and how we can quickly assess some of the cost options. Things to include as part of case study 1. Include inference being RI 2. include historical GPU purchases plus tracking of storage 3. Show some historical data acquisition costs 4. Show historical headcount with some degree of roster 5. Brief comments on rent and other overheads as well as travel philosophy 6. Legal being high given complexity and risks of an AI business Case study - master **Tiffany Kha- **Case study Case study - Markus Tiffany Kha (AC Feedback)

Finance state of 
**What we manage in house vs in house? **
- Taxes and IP (EY US and Germany) 
- Accounting US (Attivo) 
- Accounting Germany (Wenzel & Decker) 
- Cash management & treasury (in house, no tools) 
- FP&A (in-house, no tools) 
- Expense management + accounts payable (Ramp)
	- Accounts payable now managed by Attivo 
<empty-block/>
**Which email should be used for bills BFL has to pay if I sign a new contract or complete a form? **
accounting@blackforestlabs.ai
<empty-block/>
**Where do i send invoices that I received and needs to be paid? **
[accounting@blackforestlabs.ai](mailto:accounting@blackforestlabs.ai) + [blackforestlabs@ap.ramp.com](mailto:blackforestlabs@ap.ramp.com)
*If you include Ramp in the email invoices will automatically get fetched to Ramp and make the life easier for our accountants *
*PLEASE also share the email address of our key contact/ finance team of our new vendor. We need to add the email address to Ramp when we set up a new vendor. *
<empty-block/>
**How do bills get approved? **
Currently via Slack / Ramp integration by Sarah, Robin and Andi until we define new thresholds for certain departments. 
/

**But you don't want "boring enterprise marketing"** (no generic ABM/field programs) **We want ** - **Showcase-first marketing**: Demos, examples, "wow" moments that sell themselves - **Creator partnerships** but for B2B use cases - Showcase what's possible with FDE (example galleries, case studies with actual output) - Integration guides and reference architectures - "How we solved X for Y" content that's visually compelling - Demo environment that sales can customize per prospect **Priority 2: Developer Marketing → Enterprise Conversion** - Technical content that attracts developers who work at target enterprises - Open source examples, benchmarks, comparisons - Community that surfaces enterprise buyers (like Vercel, Hugging Face model) **Priority 3: Creative Brand that Sells Enterprise** - Visual excellence that differentiates from OpenAI/Google/Runway - Product launches that create buzz (not press releases, but "events") - Executive thought leadership that's actually interesting ## We DON'T need: - Pure PLG/growth marketer (Marta's core strength) - Demand gen for outbound motions - Traditional enterprise marketing (Natalie's strength) ### We DO need: **Technical Product Marketer with Creative Sensibility** Someone who can: 1. **Translate technical capability into compelling use cases** (FDE solutions marketing) 2. **Create showcase content** that makes complex tech feel magical (11Labs model) 3. **Enable sales without owning sales** (materials, demos, customer stories) 4. **Build developer → enterprise funnel** (technical content that attracts enterprise developers) 5. **Make enterprise buyers feel cool** (not corporate) ### Marta (Mirage → Captions): **Strengths reconsidered:** - ✅ Visual AI creative storytelling - ✅ Can make technical products feel exciting - ✅ Creator partnerships could work for B2B (game studios, production companies using FLUX) **New concerns:** - ❌ Her 90-day plan is consumer/creator-focused, not FDE-enablement - ❌ No solutions marketing or technical sales support experience - ❌ Playground/Studio focus when that's unproven ROI **Could work IF**: We redirect her from consumer creator marketing → B2B creative partnerships (agencies, studios, production companies as showcase customers) ### Natalie (Enterprise SaaS): **Strengths reconsidered:** - ✅ Solutions marketing for enterprise - ✅ Enables sales without boring corporate marketing - ✅ Multi-stakeholder technical products **Concerns remain:** - ❌ Doesn't know visual AI / creative space - ❌ Track record is more traditional B2B, not "cool enterprise" ### Iva (Meta → Aleph Alpha): **Strengths reconsidered:** - ✅ **B2B product marketing at scale** (Meta ads platform) - ✅ **Technical solutions** (retail, conversion data products) - ✅ **Developer → enterprise motion** (Meta's model) - ✅ **Currently at AI company** (Aleph Alpha = enterprise AI) **New appreciation:** - Meta ads platform = technical product sold to enterprises through self-serve → high-touch - Product marketing for conversion data = solutions marketing for technical use cases - Central Europe lead = multi-stakeholder, complex sales support **Reevaluated fit:** - ✅ Can do FDE solutions marketing (has technical product marketing background) - ✅ Understands developer → enterprise funnel (Meta's core motion) - ✅ Won't do boring enterprise marketing (came from product-led culture) - ❓ Unknown: Can she make it feel "cool" or will it be technical but corporate? ### Marta: 70% "Engine" fit, 20% Enterprise/Partner fit - **Nails:** Inbound, lifecycle, PLG infrastructure - **Weak:** Outbound, demand gen, enterprise, partners - **Would need:** Someone else to eventually own enterprise/partner marketing ### Natalie: 40% "Engine" fit, 80% Enterprise/Partner fit - **Nails:** Outbound, demand gen, enterprise, partners - **Weak:** PLG/growth infrastructure, inbound (in self-serve context) - **Would need:** Growth engineers to own PLG infrastructure ### Iva: 60% "Engine" fit, 60% Enterprise/Partner fit - **Covers:** Inbound (performance), lifecycle (funnels), enterprise (B2B product mktg), partners (platform experience) - **Weaker:** Pure PLG creativity, but has technical chops - **Most balanced** but not exceptional at either

263c3702-22d5-80ab-861e-fc5b0ae49f50.title: Engineering Dev Setup
263c3702-22d5-80ab-861e-fc5b0ae49f50.text: Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/263c370222d580ab861efc5b0ae49f50 as of 2025-10-03T06:00:13.014Z: {"title":"Engineering Dev Setup"} This is a perpetually WIP doc. As a new hire it is your sacred duty to pay it forward by adding any undocumented tribal knowledge you uncover during your onboarding. # Codebase and Dev Cluster 1. Clone the [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/) repo into your local workspace 1. If you can’t open this link, ask to add your github to the BFL org 2. Ask to add you to the cluster 1. Read through the documentation about this here: [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/docs/cluster.md](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/docs/cluster.md) 3. Follow the schwarzwald [readme](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/README.md) to set up your python virtual environment 4. If you’re working on Backend, clone the [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/hoellental) repo as well and read through it’s readme # Development Patterns ### IDE and Remote Dev Use whatever IDE you’d like, but we do have company Cursor plan. If you’re a Claude Code enjoyer that’s also supported. The recommended coding practice is to code on your local machine, use `rsync` to push changes to the GPU cluster, then execute code on the GPU node. There is a custom script that executes `rsync` specifically for this: [https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/31c2d7063336b8408798f976349e13d772e8ffce/sync.sh](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/31c2d7063336b8408798f976349e13d772e8ffce/sync.sh). This has a couple benefits: - If you want to install a system-level package (e.g. node.js for Claude Code or oh-my-zsh) it’s a bit of a headache on the GPU cluster. Instead, you can do this on your local machine and get your dev setup exactly how you want it without having to configure the GPU cluster. - You’re decoupled from network issues. You only need good enough internet to `rsync`, ssh, and kick off the script. ### Long-Running Jobs on the Cluster If you need to execute a long-running job on the GPU cluster, we recommend using tmux as follows: 1. ssh into a login node 2. Start a new tmux session 3. Run `./schwarzwald/scripts/getgpu_gb200.sh` to grab a GPU node 4. Kick off your script 5. Detach and reattach to/from your tmux session at will! This is needed because we don’t ssh directly into GPU nodes, and instead they are managed and cleaned up by some otherworldly process. Running `getgpu_gb200.sh` in a tmux session persists your connection to the GPU node, else the node will be cleaned up.
