--- ## Get started in 30 seconds **1. Get your API key** from your BFL account team. You will need a specific partner key for this or access to the “preview” deployment (`PARTNER="preview"`). **2. Submit a removal request** Provide your image and a black/white mask where white pixels mark the object to remove. The server applies a green fill to the masked region, optionally dilates the mask, and runs FLUX Klein 9B with a fixed object-removal LoRA. No prompt is needed — the model uses a built-in removal instruction. ```bash IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/image.png | tr -d '\n')" MASK_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/mask.png | tr -d '\n')" IMG_TMP=$(mktemp) MASK_TMP=$(mktemp) echo "$IMAGE_BASE64" > "$IMG_TMP" echo "$MASK_BASE64" > "$MASK_TMP" jq -n \ --rawfile img "$IMG_TMP" \ --rawfile mask "$MASK_TMP" \ '{ image: ($img | rtrimstr("\n")), mask: ($mask | rtrimstr("\n")), dilate_pixels: 5, output_format: "png" }' > /tmp/removal_request.json rm -f "$IMG_TMP" "$MASK_TMP" curl -sk -X POST "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/object-removal" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" \ --data-binary @/tmp/removal_request.json ``` This returns a task ID and a polling URL: ```json {"id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx", "polling_url": "..."} ``` **3. Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sk "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, grab the cleaned image URL from `result.sample` — it’s a full-resolution PNG with the masked object removed. --- ## Python quick start ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import base64 import os import time import requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" PARTNER = "" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} IMAGE_PATH = "input.png" MASK_PATH = "mask.png" # White (255) = remove, Black (0) = keep DILATE_PIXELS = 5 # Expand mask edges for cleaner removal OUTPUT = "output.png" with open(IMAGE_PATH, "rb") as f: image_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() with open(MASK_PATH, "rb") as f: mask_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() payload = { "image": image_b64, "mask": mask_b64, "dilate_pixels": DILATE_PIXELS, "output_format": "png", } resp = requests.post( f"{BASE}/partners/{PARTNER}/object-removal", headers=HEADERS, json=payload, verify=False, ).json() try: task_id = resp["id"] except Exception as e: print(f"Error getting task id:{e}") print(resp) exit(1) poll_url = resp.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") print(f"Task submitted:{task_id}") while True: result = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}, verify=False).json() if result["status"] == "Ready": img_url = result["result"]["sample"] with open(OUTPUT, "wb") as f: f.write(requests.get(img_url).content) print(f"Saved:{OUTPUT}") break if result["status"] in ("Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated", "Task not found"): print(f"Failed:{result['status']}") break time.sleep(1) ``` --- ## Details: API and Mask The `pydantic` model used to construct the object-removal request: ```python class PartnerObjectRemovalInputs(BaseModel, ImageValidationMixin): """Input model for partner object-removal endpoint. The caller provides an image and a black/white mask where white pixels mark the object to be removed. The server applies a green fill to the masked region before forwarding to the Klein 9B pipeline with a fixed object-removal LoRA. """ image: str = Field(description="Base64-encoded input image.") mask: str = Field( description=( "Base64-encoded black/white mask. White (255) pixels indicate " "the object to remove; black (0) pixels are preserved. " "Must have the same dimensions as the input image." ), ) dilate_pixels: int = Field( default=0, ge=0, le=100, description=( "Number of pixels to dilate the mask by before removal. " "Dilation helps the model fully cover object edges. Default 0." ), ) output_format: Optional[OutputFormat] = Field(default=OutputFormat.png) ``` ### Mask guidelines - **Format**: Black and white PNG at the same resolution as the input image. - **White (255)** = pixels to remove. **Black (0)** = pixels to keep. - The server converts the mask to a green fill internally — the caller only sends a binary mask. - **Dilation** (`dilate_pixels`): Expanding the mask by a few pixels typically improves removal quality by ensuring the model fully covers object edges. The optimal value depends on how well your masks capture the whole object. For typical SAM (Segment Anything) masks, we recommend `5` as a starting point. ### Tips for best results - Use a mask that fully covers the object that you want to remove. In case you worry that the mask is leaving an edge, you can enlarge it using `dilate_pixels` . - For objects with **soft edges** (hair, fur, smoke) that are often not fully enclosed by a mask, use a higher `dilate_pixels` value (15–20). - The model was trained on images at **\~1 megapixel** across 9 aspect ratios from 1:2 to 2:1. Images close to these resolutions produce the best results. Images that deviate significantly in aspect ratio or total resolution may see reduced quality. --- ## Key details
**Endpoint** `https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/object-removal`
**Auth** `X-Key` header with your BFL API key
**Input** Base64-encoded image + base64-encoded binary mask (same dimensions)
**Output** PNG & JPG (RGB)
**Prompt** Fixed internally — no user prompt needed
**Model** FLUX Klein 9B with object-removal LoRA

--- ## Get started in 30 seconds **1. Get your API key** from your BFL account team. You will need a specific partner key for this or access to the “preview” deployment (`PARTNER="preview"`). **2. Submit a removal request** Provide your image and a black/white mask where white pixels mark the object to remove. The server applies a green fill to the masked region, optionally dilates the mask, and runs FLUX Klein 9B with a fixed object-removal LoRA. No prompt is needed — the model uses a built-in removal instruction. ```bash IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/image.png | tr -d '\n')" MASK_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/mask.png | tr -d '\n')" IMG_TMP=$(mktemp) MASK_TMP=$(mktemp) echo "$IMAGE_BASE64" > "$IMG_TMP" echo "$MASK_BASE64" > "$MASK_TMP" jq -n \ --rawfile img "$IMG_TMP" \ --rawfile mask "$MASK_TMP" \ '{ image: ($img | rtrimstr("\n")), mask: ($mask | rtrimstr("\n")), dilate_pixels: 5, output_format: "png" }' > /tmp/removal_request.json rm -f "$IMG_TMP" "$MASK_TMP" curl -sk -X POST "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/object-removal" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" \ --data-binary @/tmp/removal_request.json ``` This returns a task ID and a polling URL: ```json {"id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx", "polling_url": "..."} ``` **3. Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sk "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, grab the cleaned image URL from `result.sample` — it’s a full-resolution PNG with the masked object removed. --- ## Python quick start ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import base64 import os import time import requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" PARTNER = "" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} IMAGE_PATH = "input.png" MASK_PATH = "mask.png" # White (255) = remove, Black (0) = keep DILATE_PIXELS = 5 # Expand mask edges for cleaner removal OUTPUT = "output.png" with open(IMAGE_PATH, "rb") as f: image_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() with open(MASK_PATH, "rb") as f: mask_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() payload = { "image": image_b64, "mask": mask_b64, "dilate_pixels": DILATE_PIXELS, "output_format": "png", } resp = requests.post( f"{BASE}/partners/{PARTNER}/object-removal", headers=HEADERS, json=payload, verify=False, ).json() try: task_id = resp["id"] except Exception as e: print(f"Error getting task id:{e}") print(resp) exit(1) poll_url = resp.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") print(f"Task submitted:{task_id}") while True: result = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}, verify=False).json() if result["status"] == "Ready": img_url = result["result"]["sample"] with open(OUTPUT, "wb") as f: f.write(requests.get(img_url).content) print(f"Saved:{OUTPUT}") break if result["status"] in ("Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated", "Task not found"): print(f"Failed:{result['status']}") break time.sleep(1) ``` --- ## Details: API and Mask The `pydantic` model used to construct the object-removal request: ```python class PartnerObjectRemovalInputs(BaseModel, ImageValidationMixin): """Input model for partner object-removal endpoint. The caller provides an image and a black/white mask where white pixels mark the object to be removed. The server applies a green fill to the masked region before forwarding to the Klein 9B pipeline with a fixed object-removal LoRA. """ image: str = Field(description="Base64-encoded input image.") mask: str = Field( description=( "Base64-encoded black/white mask. White (255) pixels indicate " "the object to remove; black (0) pixels are preserved. " "Must have the same dimensions as the input image." ), ) dilate_pixels: int = Field( default=0, ge=0, le=100, description=( "Number of pixels to dilate the mask by before removal. " "Dilation helps the model fully cover object edges. Default 0." ), ) output_format: Optional[OutputFormat] = Field(default=OutputFormat.png) ``` ### Mask guidelines - **Format**: Black and white PNG at the same resolution as the input image. - **White (255)** = pixels to remove. **Black (0)** = pixels to keep. - The server converts the mask to a green fill internally — the caller only sends a binary mask. - **Dilation** (`dilate_pixels`): Expanding the mask by a few pixels typically improves removal quality by ensuring the model fully covers object edges. The optimal value depends on how well your masks capture the whole object. For typical SAM (Segment Anything) masks, we recommend `5` as a starting point. ### Tips for best results - Use a mask that fully covers the object that you want to remove. In case you worry that the mask is leaving an edge, you can enlarge it using `dilate_pixels` . - For objects with **soft edges** (hair, fur, smoke) that are often not fully enclosed by a mask, use a higher `dilate_pixels` value (15–20). - The model was trained on images at **\~1 megapixel** across 9 aspect ratios from 1:2 to 2:1. Images close to these resolutions produce the best results. Images that deviate significantly in aspect ratio or total resolution may see reduced quality. --- ## Key details
**Endpoint** `https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/object-removal`
**Auth** `X-Key` header with your BFL API key
**Input** Base64-encoded image + base64-encoded binary mask (same dimensions)
**Output** PNG & JPG (RGB)
**Prompt** Fixed internally — no user prompt needed
**Model** FLUX Klein 9B with object-removal LoRA

225c3702-22d5-80f0-a1a4-f84df8910ac3.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/225c370222d580f0a1a4f84df8910ac3 as of 2026-04-01T12:42:58.035Z: {"title":"Onboarding Cheat Sheet"} ## Cloning the repository: follow [this guide](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/generating-a-new-ssh-key-and-adding-it-to-the-ssh-agent) to add your **public ssh key **(can generate with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`) to your github account to allow cloning. when cloning, **use the ssh command**. e.g.: `git clone git@github.com:black-forest-labs/schwarzwald.git` # **Working with the servers:** ### **Gaining access to the cluster (only once per (computer, cluster)): ** request a team member to give access to the cluster using the public key (`.pub`) ### Setting up your virtual environment: Follow the [instructions on the README](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/tree/hila/multimodal_clip?tab=readme-ov-file#installation) activate venv: `source .venv/bin/activate` ## h100 allocating an interactive node:
`./scripts/getgpu.sh [number of gpus (default=1)]` running your training code on the interactive node with a config yaml: `bash `[`interactive.sh`](http://interactive.sh/)` ` # gb200 cluster start each python command with `PYTHONPATH=src` allocating an interactive node: `./scripts/getgpu_gb200.sh 1` ### launching runs: follow [this README](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/pull/595/files) notice that** jobs may restart and run from scratch**, in this case, use the [modified sbatch script here](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/pull/581/files#diff-2b6152f1bb6bd00966b8c375e6355dc6cb661e1850f0377eb41d773da6c2aca5R109) resuming a run: make sure that path_to_your_run_dir contains also the configs (not the ckpt dir) ` --resume --seed 42` ### evaluating an imagenet run: only works from a login node (not arm) 1. activate dominik’s env:`source /shared/home/dominik/internal/schwarzwald/.venv/bin/activate` 2. launch a run to evaluate your checkpoint:
`TARGET_VENV=/shared/home/dominik/src/schwarzwald-envs/sw0605 CH=4 PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/evalt2i/sample.py -l -s -name test -ip` (the ip flag indicates that this is imagenet testing, for T2I don’t pass anything) to view the graphs for the FIDs (with streamlit): `PYTHONPATH=src streamlit run ./scripts/evalt2i/streamlit_metrics.py` ## **Port mapping examples:** h100: `ssh -i /.ssh/id_ed25519 -J `[`@h100cluster-login.bfl.ml`](mailto:hila@h100cluster-login.bfl.ml)` -L 8501:localhost:8501 @slurmcluster-hpc-4` gb200: `ssh -i /.ssh/id_ed25519 -J @gb200-login-1 -L 8502:localhost:8501 @ccw1-gpu-31 ` ## Data debugging 1. use the `test_data` script to make sure everything works properly:
`PYTHONPATH=src python ./scripts/data/test_data.py ` 2. it is recommended to write a streamlit app to visualize your data, an example can be found [here](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/pull/593/files#diff-01f1c5cc6a487e7316c5c01b8e222c066a740d8e428cc69a77370d2cebb22bb5) ## Distributed training ### Distributed Data Parallel - model is duplicated on gpus - data is distributed across gpus use `bfl.modules.distributed.ddp.apply_ddp` (where the model is defined, e.g., model.yaml). for example: `strategy_config: ` `strategy_target: bfl.modules.distributed.ddp.apply_ddp ` `param_dtype: float32` ### Fully Sharded Data Parallel (model sharding) - Model parameters are sharded across devices (not replicated like DDP) - Gradients and optimizer states are also sharded - Parameters are gathered only when needed for computation - Much lower memory usage per device compared to DDP need to wrap the model blocks with fsdp, see parallel dit example:
[github.com](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/src/bfl/modules/distributed/parallelize_dit.py#L135) need to define the strategy in the config (where the model is defined, e.g., model.yaml):
[github.com](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/main/configs/baselines/t2i/model.yaml#L192) ## loading distributed checkpoints use the convert function in `scripts.checkpoint.convert` to convert the distributed checkpoint to a `safetensors` checkpoint: `convert("/step-/model", target="/")` if you want your checkpoint to be saved with a certain format: `convert("/step-/model", target="/model.safetensors")` ## Logging start logging ui command (this will give a port on which the ui will be hosted, do port mapping to see it locally): `streamlit run src/sbord/slimboard.py` all the logs should be under **/blob/raw/\ (not shared) to save space. set up a symbolic link from logs to /blob/raw/\:** `ln -s /blob/raw//06_2025/ logs` once in the logging ui, place the path to the log under `/blob/raw//06_2025/`. get log path from job id: `bash scripts/logof.sh` ## masterboard logging you can open a tunnel (and keep it up) to view logs and share them with others. 1. start a masterboard using
`PYTHONPATH=src streamlit run src/sbord/masterboard.py` (use ctrl Z + bg to run this in the background) 2. start a tunnel to your masterboard:
`/shared/bin/bfltunnel.sh -l -h ` new tunnel setup: ```plain text 1. Start tmux session 2. In one window start streamlit app on some port streamlit run src/sbord/masterboard.py --server.port 7509 3. In another window start the tunnel script ./scripts/bfltunnel.sh -l 7509 -h masterboard-${USER}, make sure they have same port 4. the tunnel script will ask you for a passworrd twice, it's there in 1password. Look for bfltunnel 5. Once you enter it, the script would have given you an access url, which would look like https://masterboard-${USER}.tunnel.bfl.ai, you can now access the streamlit app at this url. 6. The webpage will also ask for a login name and password, check the 1password for BFL Tunnel Web Auth, it has the login name and password. ``` ## deployment ### deployment launch (from the login node with the starter env) 1. convert your checkpoint to a consolidated one (see loading distributed checkpoints) 2. use the converted checkpoint to deploy your model (from login node with the starter env):
`TARGET_VENV=/blob-dataloading/raw/home/pesser/containers/bfl-25.06-00.sqsh CKPT_PATH= python -m serving.deploy --deploy_id start --model_configs configs/projects/2025_04_motion_ablations/sampling_configs/pln_1gpu.yaml --num_workers=1 --worker_world_size=1` 3. test your deployment (and possibly share url with others): `python -m serving.deploy --deploy_id ` (this also allows to see how many tasks are in the queue of the deployment (under queues)) 4. to cancel all tasks:
`curl -X POST `[`/purge`](http://ccw1-d16d-4:8136/purge) the `api_url` can be found with `python -m serving.deploy --deploy_id ` 5. to clean previous deployments:
`python -m serving.deploy --deploy_id delete && python -m serving.deploy cleanup --dry_run False` ### deployment logs deployment logs can be found under `~/.sws//worker-logs/` (for example when serving a checkpoint for eval/ launching an eval run) ## debugging ### PDB add breakpoint:
`torch.distributed.breakpoint()` then type `up` to start debugging type `l` to see the code lines you are running at ### Streamlit [Example script to visualize data](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/schwarzwald/blob/hila/multimodal_clip/scripts/data/visualize_data.py) and play with the model. Run with: `CH=4 streamlit run scripts/data/visualize_data.py ./configs/baselines/t2i/model.yaml` ## evaluation from served checkpoint kino: `PYTHONPATH=src python src/projects/p_2025_03_viz/sampling_batch/sample_from_prompts.py --name= --deployment ` example: `PYTHONPATH=src python src/projects/p_2025_03_viz/sampling_batch/sample_from_prompts.py /blob/raw/home/hila/video_prompts/videojam.txt /blob/raw/hila/outputs/videojam/kino_lemur_8_nodes_50k/ --name=kino_lemur_8_nodes_50k --deployment kino_lemur_8_nodes_50k`

335c3702-22d5-807c-83f7-c6fdcfbc4918.title: Eu5 keda issues
335c3702-22d5-807c-83f7-c6fdcfbc4918.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/335c370222d5807c83f7c6fdcfbc4918 as of 2026-04-01T03:28:22.599Z: {"title":"Eu5 keda issues"} eu2 kubectl -n keda run dns-test --rm -it --restart=Never \\
--image=busybox -- nslookup broker.production
Server: 169.254.25.10
Address: 169.254.25.10:53 - \* server can't find broker.production: NXDOMAIN - \* server can't find broker.production: NXDOMAIN pod "dns-test" deleted from keda namespace
pod keda/dns-test terminated (Error) kubectl -n keda describe pod -l app=keda-operator \| grep -E "Start Time\|Started\|Restart Count"
Start Time: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 06:56:31 -0500
Started: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 02:11:34 -0400
Started: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 02:11:08 -0400
Restart Count: 2 eu5 kubectl -n keda run dns-test --rm -it --restart=Never \\
--image=busybox -- nslookup broker.production
Server: 10.96.0.10
Address: 10.96.0.10:53 - \* server can't find broker.production: NXDOMAIN - \* server can't find broker.production: NXDOMAIN pod "dns-test" deleted from keda namespace
pod keda/dns-test terminated (Error) check operator uptime kubectl -n keda describe pod -l app=keda-operator \| grep -E "Start Time\|Started\|Restart Count"
Start Time: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 03:33:50 -0400
Started: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 03:33:59 -0400
Started: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 03:33:57 -0400
Restart Count: 1 **eu2** — operator last restarted **March 24**, 7 days ago. Scaler has been running continuously since then, coasting on state initialized after the last restart. At that point DNS may have resolved via some transient condition, or the scaler cached a successful connection early on. **eu5** — operator last restarted **March 31 at 03:33**, which is today. Fresh restart → scaler rebuilt from scratch → DNS lookup attempted → NXDOMAIN → immediate TriggerError. ## The Full Story ### Background: What KEDA does KEDA watches a RabbitMQ queue and scales a Deployment up or down based on queue depth. Every 15 seconds the KEDA operator pod makes an HTTP request to the RabbitMQ management API (`broker.production:15672`) to check how many messages are waiting. If it can't reach RabbitMQ, it can't scale — and that's exactly what broke. --- ### The infrastructure setup RabbitMQ doesn't run inside the GPU cluster. It runs on an external API cluster, connected to the cluster via Tailscale. The Tailscale operator creates an egress proxy that makes the external node reachable inside the cluster via a Kubernetes Service: `broker.production
→ ExternalName Service
→ ts-broker-pks4k.tailscale.svc.cluster.local (Tailscale proxy pod)
→ 100.94.93.125 (RabbitMQ node on the Tailscale mesh)
→ port 15672 (RabbitMQ management API)` This works fine for application pods — Celery workers connecting to RabbitMQ on port 5672 have no issues. The problem is specific to KEDA polling port 15672. --- ### The DNS problem Every pod in Kubernetes gets a `/etc/resolv.conf` injected by kubelet. The critical part is the `search` list, which defines shorthand suffixes the resolver appends when you use a short hostname: `# Pod in the 'production' namespace
search production.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local

# Pod in the 'keda' namespace
search keda.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local` When you query a short name like `broker.production`, the resolver works through the search list in order, appending each suffix until it gets a hit: **From a pod in the ****`production`**** namespace:** 1. `broker.production.production.svc.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN (non existing domain) 2. `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` → ✅ **resolves** — returns the Tailscale CNAME **From a pod in the ****`keda`**** namespace:** 1. `broker.production.keda.svc.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN 2. `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN 3. `broker.production.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN 4. `broker.production` (absolute) → NXDOMAIN 5. **All attempts exhausted → NXDOMAIN** The reason step 2 fails from `keda` is that `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` isn't the actual FQDN — the real name is `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` only because `production` is the namespace. The resolver from `keda` has no way to know that `production` in `broker.production` is a namespace qualifier rather than part of the hostname. Even though the ScaledObject lives in the `production` namespace, **the HTTP request is made by the KEDA operator pod, which runs in the ****`keda`**** namespace**. That's the mismatch — the ScaledObject namespace is irrelevant to where DNS queries originate from. --- ### Why it showed as `context deadline exceeded` instead of `NXDOMAIN` You'd expect a clean DNS error, but instead got: `context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)` This is because Go's DNS resolver works through all four search domains sequentially, and each failed lookup has its own network round-trip and timeout. By the time all four NXDOMAIN responses come back and the resolver gives up, the KEDA HTTP client's overall request timeout has already fired — so the error surfaces as a connection timeout rather than a DNS failure. This made it look like a network connectivity problem rather than a DNS resolution problem, which is why the initial investigation focused on Tailscale, NetworkPolicies, and port exposure. --- ### Why eu5 was broken but eu2 wasn't Both clusters have identical setups — same short hostname in the ScaledObject trigger, same KEDA namespace, same NXDOMAIN from `keda`. But their failure state diverged based on operator uptime:
Cluster Operator last restart Status
eu5 March 31 (today) ❌ Broken immediately
eu2 March 24 (7 days ago) ✅ Appeared healthy
Every time the KEDA operator restarts, it rebuilds all scalers from scratch, which triggers a fresh DNS lookup for every ScaledObject trigger host. eu5 restarted today, hit NXDOMAIN immediately, and entered a permanent `TriggerError` loop — rebuilding the scaler every 15 seconds, failing DNS every time, generating 112+ error events over 9 hours. eu2 restarted 7 days ago. At that point the DNS lookup either succeeded transiently, or the scaler initialized successfully via some other path, and has been coasting on that cached state ever since — no restart means no fresh DNS lookup means no failure. The moment eu2's operator restarts for any reason (node pressure, upgrade, OOM kill), it will hit the exact same failure. --- ### The fix Use the fully qualified domain name in the ScaledObject trigger host: yaml `# Before — breaks from any namespace other than 'production'
Host: http://guest:guest@broker.production:15672/

# After — works from any namespace, always unambiguous
Host: http://guest:guest@broker.production.svc.cluster.local:15672/` An FQDN bypasses the search domain logic entirely — the resolver sends exactly one query and gets the answer back immediately, regardless of which namespace the caller is in. This is the correct pattern for any cross-namespace service reference in Kubernetes, not just KEDA triggers. Potential reasons why other clusters work In this case, CoreDNS (Kubernetes' internal DNS server at `10.96.0.10`) is the authoritative server for `cluster.local`. When KEDA's resolver asked it about `broker.production.keda.svc.cluster.local`, CoreDNS checked its records and responded NXDOMAIN — not "I don't know", but "I know for a fact this doesn't exist." Same for each subsequent search domain attempt. The distinction matters because NXDOMAIN is a definitive negative answer, not a timeout or network error. It's what made the `context deadline exceeded` error misleading — the failure wasn't a network problem at all, DNS was working correctly and answering quickly. It was just answering "no" four times in a row fast enough that the cumulative lookup time consumed the HTTP client's timeout budget before a successful resolution was ever possible. Scarier statements The HPA has been successfully scaling continuously for **7d20h** — which traces back almost exactly to March 24 when the operator last restarted. The scaler has been alive and working without interruption since then. This confirms the hypothesis completely. eu2 works because: 1. Operator restarted March 24 2. Scaler initialized — DNS lookup for `broker.production` happened to succeed at that moment (most likely the search domain fallback completed before the timeout, or there was a transient condition that allowed it) 3. Scaler has been **continuously active** ever since — queue never drained to zero, so KEDA never marked the scaler inactive, never tore it down, never rebuilt it 4. No rebuild = no fresh DNS lookup = never hits NXDOMAIN again The continuous scaling activity is the key — if the queue had ever gone quiet long enough for KEDA to mark the ScaledObject inactive, it would have torn down the scaler and rebuilt it on the next poll cycle, hitting NXDOMAIN and breaking exactly like eu5. So eu2 isn't structurally different at all. It's just been busy enough that KEDA has never had a reason to reinitialize the scaler since March 24. **It's genuinely one quiet period away from breaking.** {color="red"} Final update for now update to hosts in some scaled objects looks like it triggered the others to become healthy clauds explanation makes sense to me --- --- When you updated one ScaledObject, it triggered the KEDA operator to reconcile that object, which caused it to **reload all scalers for that namespace**, not just the one you modified. KEDA's operator uses a shared scaler cache per namespace. When any ScaledObject in the namespace is modified: 1. Operator receives the reconcile event 2. Rebuilds the scaler cache for the namespace 3. In doing so, re-initializes scalers for **all** ScaledObjects in that namespace 4. All of them get fresh DNS lookups using the now-correct FQDN from the updated object But wait — the other ScaledObjects still have the short hostname `broker.production` in their specs. So why did they become healthy? Most likely explanation: **the reconcile loop warmed up the DNS cache**. When KEDA rebuilt the scaler for your updated object using the FQDN, CoreDNS cached the resolved IP. When the other scalers were rebuilt milliseconds later using the short hostname, the DNS search domain expansion completed fast enough (hitting the CoreDNS cache) before the HTTP timeout fired — succeeding where before it was timing out. Verify the other ScaledObjects still have the short hostname: bash `kubectl -n production get scaledobject -o json | \

Started: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 03:33:57 -0400
Restart Count: 1 **eu2** — operator last restarted **March 24**, 7 days ago. Scaler has been running continuously since then, coasting on state initialized after the last restart. At that point DNS may have resolved via some transient condition, or the scaler cached a successful connection early on. **eu5** — operator last restarted **March 31 at 03:33**, which is today. Fresh restart → scaler rebuilt from scratch → DNS lookup attempted → NXDOMAIN → immediate TriggerError. ## The Full Story ### Background: What KEDA does KEDA watches a RabbitMQ queue and scales a Deployment up or down based on queue depth. Every 15 seconds the KEDA operator pod makes an HTTP request to the RabbitMQ management API (`broker.production:15672`) to check how many messages are waiting. If it can't reach RabbitMQ, it can't scale — and that's exactly what broke. --- ### The infrastructure setup RabbitMQ doesn't run inside the GPU cluster. It runs on an external API cluster, connected to the cluster via Tailscale. The Tailscale operator creates an egress proxy that makes the external node reachable inside the cluster via a Kubernetes Service: `broker.production
→ ExternalName Service
→ ts-broker-pks4k.tailscale.svc.cluster.local (Tailscale proxy pod)
→ 100.94.93.125 (RabbitMQ node on the Tailscale mesh)
→ port 15672 (RabbitMQ management API)` This works fine for application pods — Celery workers connecting to RabbitMQ on port 5672 have no issues. The problem is specific to KEDA polling port 15672. --- ### The DNS problem Every pod in Kubernetes gets a `/etc/resolv.conf` injected by kubelet. The critical part is the `search` list, which defines shorthand suffixes the resolver appends when you use a short hostname: `# Pod in the 'production' namespace
search production.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local

# Pod in the 'keda' namespace
search keda.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local` When you query a short name like `broker.production`, the resolver works through the search list in order, appending each suffix until it gets a hit: **From a pod in the ****`production`**** namespace:** 1. `broker.production.production.svc.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN (non existing domain) 2. `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` → ✅ **resolves** — returns the Tailscale CNAME **From a pod in the ****`keda`**** namespace:** 1. `broker.production.keda.svc.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN 2. `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN 3. `broker.production.cluster.local` → NXDOMAIN 4. `broker.production` (absolute) → NXDOMAIN 5. **All attempts exhausted → NXDOMAIN** The reason step 2 fails from `keda` is that `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` isn't the actual FQDN — the real name is `broker.production.svc.cluster.local` only because `production` is the namespace. The resolver from `keda` has no way to know that `production` in `broker.production` is a namespace qualifier rather than part of the hostname. Even though the ScaledObject lives in the `production` namespace, **the HTTP request is made by the KEDA operator pod, which runs in the ****`keda`**** namespace**. That's the mismatch — the ScaledObject namespace is irrelevant to where DNS queries originate from. --- ### Why it showed as `context deadline exceeded` instead of `NXDOMAIN` You'd expect a clean DNS error, but instead got: `context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)` This is because Go's DNS resolver works through all four search domains sequentially, and each failed lookup has its own network round-trip and timeout. By the time all four NXDOMAIN responses come back and the resolver gives up, the KEDA HTTP client's overall request timeout has already fired — so the error surfaces as a connection timeout rather than a DNS failure. This made it look like a network connectivity problem rather than a DNS resolution problem, which is why the initial investigation focused on Tailscale, NetworkPolicies, and port exposure. --- ### Why eu5 was broken but eu2 wasn't Both clusters have identical setups — same short hostname in the ScaledObject trigger, same KEDA namespace, same NXDOMAIN from `keda`. But their failure state diverged based on operator uptime:
Cluster Operator last restart Status
eu5 March 31 (today) ❌ Broken immediately
eu2 March 24 (7 days ago) ✅ Appeared healthy
Every time the KEDA operator restarts, it rebuilds all scalers from scratch, which triggers a fresh DNS lookup for every ScaledObject trigger host. eu5 restarted today, hit NXDOMAIN immediately, and entered a permanent `TriggerError` loop — rebuilding the scaler every 15 seconds, failing DNS every time, generating 112+ error events over 9 hours. eu2 restarted 7 days ago. At that point the DNS lookup either succeeded transiently, or the scaler initialized successfully via some other path, and has been coasting on that cached state ever since — no restart means no fresh DNS lookup means no failure. The moment eu2's operator restarts for any reason (node pressure, upgrade, OOM kill), it will hit the exact same failure. --- ### The fix Use the fully qualified domain name in the ScaledObject trigger host: yaml `# Before — breaks from any namespace other than 'production'
Host: http://guest:guest@broker.production:15672/

# After — works from any namespace, always unambiguous
Host: http://guest:guest@broker.production.svc.cluster.local:15672/` An FQDN bypasses the search domain logic entirely — the resolver sends exactly one query and gets the answer back immediately, regardless of which namespace the caller is in. This is the correct pattern for any cross-namespace service reference in Kubernetes, not just KEDA triggers. Potential reasons why other clusters work In this case, CoreDNS (Kubernetes' internal DNS server at `10.96.0.10`) is the authoritative server for `cluster.local`. When KEDA's resolver asked it about `broker.production.keda.svc.cluster.local`, CoreDNS checked its records and responded NXDOMAIN — not "I don't know", but "I know for a fact this doesn't exist." Same for each subsequent search domain attempt. The distinction matters because NXDOMAIN is a definitive negative answer, not a timeout or network error. It's what made the `context deadline exceeded` error misleading — the failure wasn't a network problem at all, DNS was working correctly and answering quickly. It was just answering "no" four times in a row fast enough that the cumulative lookup time consumed the HTTP client's timeout budget before a successful resolution was ever possible. Scarier statements The HPA has been successfully scaling continuously for **7d20h** — which traces back almost exactly to March 24 when the operator last restarted. The scaler has been alive and working without interruption since then. This confirms the hypothesis completely. eu2 works because: 1. Operator restarted March 24 2. Scaler initialized — DNS lookup for `broker.production` happened to succeed at that moment (most likely the search domain fallback completed before the timeout, or there was a transient condition that allowed it) 3. Scaler has been **continuously active** ever since — queue never drained to zero, so KEDA never marked the scaler inactive, never tore it down, never rebuilt it 4. No rebuild = no fresh DNS lookup = never hits NXDOMAIN again The continuous scaling activity is the key — if the queue had ever gone quiet long enough for KEDA to mark the ScaledObject inactive, it would have torn down the scaler and rebuilt it on the next poll cycle, hitting NXDOMAIN and breaking exactly like eu5. So eu2 isn't structurally different at all. It's just been busy enough that KEDA has never had a reason to reinitialize the scaler since March 24. **It's genuinely one quiet period away from breaking.** {color="red"} Final update for now update to hosts in some scaled objects looks like it triggered the others to become healthy clauds explanation makes sense to me --- --- When you updated one ScaledObject, it triggered the KEDA operator to reconcile that object, which caused it to **reload all scalers for that namespace**, not just the one you modified. KEDA's operator uses a shared scaler cache per namespace. When any ScaledObject in the namespace is modified: 1. Operator receives the reconcile event 2. Rebuilds the scaler cache for the namespace 3. In doing so, re-initializes scalers for **all** ScaledObjects in that namespace 4. All of them get fresh DNS lookups using the now-correct FQDN from the updated object But wait — the other ScaledObjects still have the short hostname `broker.production` in their specs. So why did they become healthy? Most likely explanation: **the reconcile loop warmed up the DNS cache**. When KEDA rebuilt the scaler for your updated object using the FQDN, CoreDNS cached the resolved IP. When the other scalers were rebuilt milliseconds later using the short hostname, the DNS search domain expansion completed fast enough (hitting the CoreDNS cache) before the HTTP timeout fired — succeeding where before it was timing out. Verify the other ScaledObjects still have the short hostname: bash `kubectl -n production get scaledobject -o json | \
jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name + ": " + (.spec.triggers[].metadata.host // "no host")'` If they do, they're still latently broken — next time the scaler cache is cold and CoreDNS cache is empty, they'll fail again. Update all of them to the FQDN regardless of their current healthy status.

```bash
docker image prune -a --filter "until=72h" -f && docker builder prune -a --filter "until=72h" -f && sudo systemctl status actions.runner.*
```
fixing containerd
**Check:**
bash
check 
```bash
ls -la /var/lib/containerd && ls -la /mnt/containerd && sudo systemctl is-active containerd
```
If `/mnt/containerd` is a self-referential symlink (`/mnt/containerd -> /mnt/containerd`) and containerd is inactive, proceed with fix.
**Fix:**
bash
```bash

```
Verify the server block appears in `ctr version` output — that confirms containerd is up and the socket is live.

32ec3702-22d5-805a-8d00-d2f791511656.title: FLUX for prompt inpainting
32ec3702-22d5-805a-8d00-d2f791511656.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/32ec370222d5805a8d00d2f791511656 as of 2026-03-25T11:16:57.481Z: {"title":"FLUX for prompt inpainting"} **Fill any masked region with AI-generated content guided by your text prompt** — powered by FLUX Klein 9B. Describe what you want to see and FLUX will seamlessly fill the masked area with contextually coherent content that matches the surrounding scene. Perfect for creative editing and adding new elements to existing photos. --- ## Get started in 30 seconds **1. Get your API key** from your BFL account team. You will need a specific partner key for this or access to the “preview” deployment (`PARTNER="preview"`). **2. Submit an inpainting request** Provide your image, a black/white mask where white pixels mark the region to fill, and a text prompt describing what should appear there. The server applies a contrastive fill color to the masked region, prepends `FILL:` to your prompt, optionally dilates the mask, and runs FLUX Klein 9B with a fixed prompt-inpainting LoRA. ```bash IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/image.png | tr -d '\n')" MASK_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/mask.png | tr -d '\n')" IMG_TMP=$(mktemp) MASK_TMP=$(mktemp) echo "$IMAGE_BASE64" > "$IMG_TMP" echo "$MASK_BASE64" > "$MASK_TMP" jq -n \ --rawfile img "$IMG_TMP" \ --rawfile mask "$MASK_TMP" \ '{ image: ($img | rtrimstr("\n")), mask: ($mask | rtrimstr("\n")), prompt: "a red sports car", dilate_pixels: 5, output_format: "png" }' > /tmp/inpaint_request.json rm -f "$IMG_TMP" "$MASK_TMP" curl -sk -X POST "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/prompt-inpainting" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" \ --data-binary @/tmp/inpaint_request.json ``` This returns a task ID and a polling URL: ```json {"id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx", "polling_url": "..."} ``` **3. Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sk "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, grab the inpainted image URL from `result.sample` — it’s a full-resolution PNG with the masked region filled according to your prompt. --- ## Python quick start ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import base64 import os import time import requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" PARTNER = "" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} IMAGE_PATH = "input.png" MASK_PATH = "mask.png" # White (255) = inpaint, Black (0) = keep PROMPT = "a red sports car" # Describe what should fill the masked region DILATE_PIXELS = 5 # Expand mask edges for cleaner inpainting OUTPUT = "output.png" with open(IMAGE_PATH, "rb") as f: image_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() with open(MASK_PATH, "rb") as f: mask_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() payload = { "image": image_b64, "mask": mask_b64, "prompt": PROMPT, "dilate_pixels": DILATE_PIXELS, "output_format": "png", } resp = requests.post( f"{BASE}/partners/{PARTNER}/prompt-inpainting", headers=HEADERS, json=payload, ).json() try: task_id = resp["id"] except Exception as e: print(f"Error getting task id:{e}") print(resp) exit(1) poll_url = resp.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") print(f"Task submitted:{task_id}") while True: result = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}).json() if result["status"] == "Ready": img_url = result["result"]["sample"] with open(OUTPUT, "wb") as f: f.write(requests.get(img_url).content) print(f"Saved:{OUTPUT}") break if result["status"] in ("Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated", "Task not found"): print(f"Failed:{result['status']}") break time.sleep(1) ``` --- ## Details: API and Mask The `pydantic` model used to construct the prompt-inpainting request: ```python class PartnerPromptInpaintingInputs(BaseModel, ImageValidationMixin): """Input model for partner prompt-inpainting endpoint. The caller provides an image, a black/white mask marking the region to inpaint, and a text prompt describing the desired fill content. The server applies a contrastive fill colour to the masked region and prepends 'FILL:' to the prompt before forwarding to the Klein 9B pipeline with a fixed prompt-inpainting LoRA. """ image: str = Field(description="Base64-encoded input image.") mask: str = Field( description=( "Base64-encoded black/white mask. White (255) pixels indicate " "the region to inpaint; black (0) pixels are preserved. " "Must have the same dimensions as the input image." ), ) prompt: str = Field( description="Text prompt describing the desired content for the masked region.", ) dilate_pixels: int = Field( default=0, ge=0, le=100, description=( "Number of pixels to dilate the mask by before inpainting. " "Dilation helps the model fully cover object edges. Default 0." ), ) seed: Optional[int] = Field( default=None, description="Optional seed for reproducibility.", ) output_format: Optional[OutputFormat] = Field(default=OutputFormat.png) ``` ### Mask guidelines - **Format**: Black and white PNG at the same resolution as the input image. - **White (255)** = pixels to inpaint (fill with new content). **Black (0)** = pixels to keep. - The server automatically picks a contrastive fill color (green, blue, or magenta) based on image content — the caller only sends a binary mask. - **Dilation** (`dilate_pixels`): Expanding the mask by a few pixels can improve edge blending. For typical SAM masks, we recommend `5` as a starting point. ### Prompt guidelines - Describe **what you want to appear** in the masked region, not what you want removed. - Keep prompts concise and descriptive: `"a tabby cat sitting on the grass"` works better than `"replace the object with a cat"`. - The `FILL:` prefix is added automatically — do not include it in your prompt. ### Tips for best results - Use a mask that fully covers the region you want to fill and is reasonably sized for the object(s) you plan to inpaint. Use `dilate_pixels` to expand it if needed. - This form of inpainting does not preserve what is in the masked region, but re-creates content based on the prompt you give such that it fills in seamlessly. - The model was trained on images at **\~1 megapixel** across 9 aspect ratios from 1:2 to 2:1. Images close to these resolutions produce the best results. - For reproducible results, set the `seed` parameter to a fixed integer value. --- ## Key details
**Endpoint** `https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/prompt-inpainting`
**Auth** `X-Key` header with your BFL API key
**Input** Base64-encoded image + base64-encoded binary mask (same dimensions) + text prompt
**Output** PNG & JPG (RGB)
**Prompt** User-provided — `FILL:` prefix is added automatically
**Seed** Optional integer for reproducibility
**Model** FLUX Klein 9B with prompt-inpainting LoRA

You will need a specific partner key for this or access to the “preview” deployment (`PARTNER="preview"`). **2. Submit an inpainting request** Provide your image, a black/white mask where white pixels mark the region to fill, and a text prompt describing what should appear there. The server applies a contrastive fill color to the masked region, prepends `FILL:` to your prompt, optionally dilates the mask, and runs FLUX Klein 9B with a fixed prompt-inpainting LoRA. ```bash IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/image.png | tr -d '\n')" MASK_BASE64="$(base64 < /path/to/mask.png | tr -d '\n')" IMG_TMP=$(mktemp) MASK_TMP=$(mktemp) echo "$IMAGE_BASE64" > "$IMG_TMP" echo "$MASK_BASE64" > "$MASK_TMP" jq -n \ --rawfile img "$IMG_TMP" \ --rawfile mask "$MASK_TMP" \ '{ image: ($img | rtrimstr("\n")), mask: ($mask | rtrimstr("\n")), prompt: "a red sports car", dilate_pixels: 5, output_format: "png" }' > /tmp/inpaint_request.json rm -f "$IMG_TMP" "$MASK_TMP" curl -sk -X POST "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/prompt-inpainting" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" \ --data-binary @/tmp/inpaint_request.json ``` This returns a task ID and a polling URL: ```json {"id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx", "polling_url": "..."} ``` **3. Poll for your result** ```bash curl -sk "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/v1/get_result?id=YOUR_TASK_ID" \ -H "X-Key:$BFL_API_KEY" ``` When `status` is `"Ready"`, grab the inpainted image URL from `result.sample` — it’s a full-resolution PNG with the masked region filled according to your prompt. --- ## Python quick start ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import base64 import os import time import requests API_KEY = os.environ["BFL_API_KEY"] BASE = "https://labs.us2.bfl.ai" PARTNER = "" HEADERS = {"X-Key": API_KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"} IMAGE_PATH = "input.png" MASK_PATH = "mask.png" # White (255) = inpaint, Black (0) = keep PROMPT = "a red sports car" # Describe what should fill the masked region DILATE_PIXELS = 5 # Expand mask edges for cleaner inpainting OUTPUT = "output.png" with open(IMAGE_PATH, "rb") as f: image_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() with open(MASK_PATH, "rb") as f: mask_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() payload = { "image": image_b64, "mask": mask_b64, "prompt": PROMPT, "dilate_pixels": DILATE_PIXELS, "output_format": "png", } resp = requests.post( f"{BASE}/partners/{PARTNER}/prompt-inpainting", headers=HEADERS, json=payload, ).json() try: task_id = resp["id"] except Exception as e: print(f"Error getting task id:{e}") print(resp) exit(1) poll_url = resp.get("polling_url", f"{BASE}/v1/get_result?id={task_id}") print(f"Task submitted:{task_id}") while True: result = requests.get(poll_url, headers={"X-Key": API_KEY}).json() if result["status"] == "Ready": img_url = result["result"]["sample"] with open(OUTPUT, "wb") as f: f.write(requests.get(img_url).content) print(f"Saved:{OUTPUT}") break if result["status"] in ("Error", "Request Moderated", "Content Moderated", "Task not found"): print(f"Failed:{result['status']}") break time.sleep(1) ``` --- ## Details: API and Mask The `pydantic` model used to construct the prompt-inpainting request: ```python class PartnerPromptInpaintingInputs(BaseModel, ImageValidationMixin): """Input model for partner prompt-inpainting endpoint. The caller provides an image, a black/white mask marking the region to inpaint, and a text prompt describing the desired fill content. The server applies a contrastive fill colour to the masked region and prepends 'FILL:' to the prompt before forwarding to the Klein 9B pipeline with a fixed prompt-inpainting LoRA. """ image: str = Field(description="Base64-encoded input image.") mask: str = Field( description=( "Base64-encoded black/white mask. White (255) pixels indicate " "the region to inpaint; black (0) pixels are preserved. " "Must have the same dimensions as the input image." ), ) prompt: str = Field( description="Text prompt describing the desired content for the masked region.", ) dilate_pixels: int = Field( default=0, ge=0, le=100, description=( "Number of pixels to dilate the mask by before inpainting. " "Dilation helps the model fully cover object edges. Default 0." ), ) seed: Optional[int] = Field( default=None, description="Optional seed for reproducibility.", ) output_format: Optional[OutputFormat] = Field(default=OutputFormat.png) ``` ### Mask guidelines - **Format**: Black and white PNG at the same resolution as the input image. - **White (255)** = pixels to inpaint (fill with new content). **Black (0)** = pixels to keep. - The server automatically picks a contrastive fill color (green, blue, or magenta) based on image content — the caller only sends a binary mask. - **Dilation** (`dilate_pixels`): Expanding the mask by a few pixels can improve edge blending. For typical SAM masks, we recommend `5` as a starting point. ### Prompt guidelines - Describe **what you want to appear** in the masked region, not what you want removed. - Keep prompts concise and descriptive: `"a tabby cat sitting on the grass"` works better than `"replace the object with a cat"`. - The `FILL:` prefix is added automatically — do not include it in your prompt. ### Tips for best results - Use a mask that fully covers the region you want to fill and is reasonably sized for the object(s) you plan to inpaint. Use `dilate_pixels` to expand it if needed. - This form of inpainting does not preserve what is in the masked region, but re-creates content based on the prompt you give such that it fills in seamlessly. - The model was trained on images at **\~1 megapixel** across 9 aspect ratios from 1:2 to 2:1. Images close to these resolutions produce the best results. - For reproducible results, set the `seed` parameter to a fixed integer value. --- ## Key details
**Endpoint** `https://labs.us2.bfl.ai/partners/$PARTNER/prompt-inpainting`
**Auth** `X-Key` header with your BFL API key
**Input** Base64-encoded image + base64-encoded binary mask (same dimensions) + text prompt
**Output** PNG & JPG (RGB)
**Prompt** User-provided — `FILL:` prefix is added automatically
**Seed** Optional integer for reproducibility
**Model** FLUX Klein 9B with prompt-inpainting LoRA

Target 5-6B total → very roughly one month of pretraining - note: pumpkin currently transcodes to jpeg90, in future, keep original encoding (unless it’s obscure) - Typography - Rendered Rich Text dataset for pretraining, scale to theoretic O(1B) of on-the-fly images - iterate on categories for videos & improve split for midtraining - Get to 1B good clips - Proper diversity filtering - iterating on all filters - Video Editing - i2v: same targets as for image editing - + video to video editing - editing that actually changes the video - attribute editing - camera angle - global changes - reference insertion (multiref equivalent) i+v2v - everything else probably a i2v case - Audio - get first hire and start collecting some initial sets - target: full pre, mid, post set - Interleaved data / VLM / Image and Video understanding - Text - get first hire and start collecting some initial sets - target: full pre, mid, post set - Game-Engine-Model-Data “World-Models” - Software that captures video & keystroke - pay people to play games - SVG / Vector graphics - Exploratory 1M set - use for logo set The People’s Needs

📍 Room Overview Refer to the **floor plan below** to find where each room is located before booking. > ![](https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/d47c9781-7a36-4f60-98ec-c16fd7b286a6/4afed8c9-39c0-4bc0-ac84-73be5d62c077/The_Bow_4OG_Floor_Plan.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Content-Sha256=UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD&X-Amz-Credential=ASIAZI2LB4665BGR3FHE%2F20260419%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260419T100043Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Security-Token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEDkaCXVzLXdlc3QtMiJIMEYCIQCMwS%2FEXBQHQu5RnCVchRyrW0kYBOil7gAYzwueTDcANQIhAPCIMYKwQkzPv%2FjQ%2FiFh7PolrbjiSIjb6ARmH73sK%2Fy%2FKv8DCAIQABoMNjM3NDIzMTgzODA1IgyBbY3dnlBQXT5A4OYq3AN1u6CCDbq7qVJghFSYmWYSWGogfErF49%2BIT%2BsZq8mu33CPdgoW6yxxL%2FrndebmjUJTKGgif7kVSotKYOVsisNnmp9bEFgpFsq1Huup8Cl6djJGhw8O%2FX49yUOYXNXP6dwgRkZyGVw%2Fl6GLcRwi3lD%2FKmhyUgdsPbojoLtEDtc3pybhC1txjDFRBtNZ3zimqeW4DsVanWFDLm9h8zHTApagC9INFYeN%2BNcuBCZultuMGZZX%2BmFennK%2BjxCYPu6JIT%2BQlLl%2FOEhoeqdN2b5J6NDEYDAieoEGcgqGUdaTEloh7LljnjYFa5F%2B7iTs%2FYe%2FvFK9Jrm2khy3RQCkXQsdqUZEsehIQXmJFhilyPUdmg3%2FmAWUyMQByoh4ZBmmOkuUB8DT7QaAFsn5FciQ8cgDCIsZYHbV9ZdwIxWt6mJ3f3xSLiVoz0sAWWLWDbwq06USVuV69WFcplyaubtr5aBI9Uzs0dPngNRRMKTVrpv0IGSHI4aF%2F9JlTOOHImYr5DgplExElKQsvoMz35dAJ58vO0oKLrw7NaIgT%2BRd6IoU6cdEpoTYCf0x4l0RaBcHH4DMFk1pgkbK45MovTPd9%2FSk6ibKThRpNbnesBGDe%2FBOgewxnxooBX9yNBQTCd55%2BDDssJLPBjqkAWo6IdlI2s5Bmey8IQ81qsW3HZKT6u2WzUw0Mqu8kNVdmnbx8GiUAJpJYuO8YQKr%2BqhMhBwrel2dbGZxmddB3ARKwvjhYcSj3XsDs0G%2BAuQ%2FEERmn3DmWHNumS%2FQQTXvlzqk72FVkaYVSHug8x3VErMOA7IhCrC2bNEy66shlQGDPrUVAxZJy%2FKAS2qjTUffTaplTvJOjPI6WMVUJj2LEtmclwp9&X-Amz-Signature=1a4a88db0c7e36ff511266d6cfcdb1c1562a620fb469dafa133e065721066f5e&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-amz-checksum-mode=ENABLED&x-id=GetObject) --- ## 📇 Room Directory **Phonebooth (1 Person, ideal for virtual meetings)** - Herzogenhorn - Teufelsmühle - Roßkopf **Small Office (2-3 People, all with whiteboards)** - Spießhorn (cozy chairs, great for a 1:1 or interview) - Brend - Seebuck - Blauen **Medium Office/Conference Room (4-6 People, all with whiteboards)** - Belchen (seats 4) - Kandel (Monitor, seats 6) - Schauinsland (Monitor, seats 6) **Large Conference Room (10+ People)** - Feldberg (Whiteboard + Large Monitor, seats 14) **Chill Space** - Kaiserstuhl (need a moment to unwind or a cat nap, catch a breath here or try out the daybed) ## <meeting-notes readOnlyViewMeetingNoteUrl="https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5802293bac5f0d7870409">
	**FLUX 2.1 Release Planning Call** <mention-date start="2026-03-31"/>
	<summary>
		### Action Items
		- [ ] Maxim to test GPT-5.4 mini latency and create PR to existing branch [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d58021b7e8fc861a0f6116]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to coordinate with engineering on merging the updated prompt upsampling PR [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to talk to Matt about Amazon/Alexa pricing agreement [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to finalize feature set and pricing by end of week [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- [ ] Owais to write one-pager for 2.1 launch and update release calendar [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580feb87aedc3f228be84]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to update launch calendar page with consolidated information [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580d08ddbe1f793661cf9]
		- [ ] Alex to run human evaluation on GPT models with Maxim [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803384d0f1c74ae237ac]
		- [ ] Team to decide on Max scoring improvements (vision generation loop vs replacing Pro with Flex) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		### FLUX 2.1 Launch Timeline
		- **This week**: Send Pro endpoint to Elena Marina for evaluation, finalize feature set and pricing [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Next week**: Polish and ensure everything is ready [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Target launch**: April 14th (approximately 2 weeks out) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- Timeline may shift depending on Elena Marina evaluation results [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		### What's Launching with FLUX 2.1
		Releasing upgraded versions of Pro, Flex, and Max models simultaneously with: [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Improved prompt upsampling**: More realistic images, better character reference and text editing [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- **Auto aspect ratio inference**: From prompt content (e.g., "16:9" or "landscape") [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Visual grounding**: Web search for named entities in prompts [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Transparent background**: Background removal capability [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Better quality and latency** compared to current models [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- API parameter alignment with Google and OpenAI standards [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		### Technical Decisions & Discussion
		- **GPT model choice**: Need to test GPT-5.4 mini vs current 5.1 for latency before sending to Elena Marina [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- Partnership allows for re-evaluation if needed, relatively low cost concern [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- **Endpoint design**: New endpoints for each model (not drop-in replacement), users opt-in by choice [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580be812de011d15d6489][^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d58047ae07ef18d2841be1]
		- **Upsampling latency**: OpenAI upsampling takes \~5 seconds (majority of request time in best case), compared to 1.85s generation [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		- **Max scoring**: Considering improved scoring with custom prompts per generation and tournament-style comparison [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		### Pricing Complexity Concerns
		- Team pushing to simplify pricing model rather than adding complexity [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803b84c5c8ba2f4ae35d]
		- Grounding can be expensive (\~1.5 cents for 3 images) and should have separate pricing toggle [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Transparent background also incurs GPU costs that need margin calculation [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Proposal: Average out costs into simplified per-megapixel pricing rather than exposing all feature complexity [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Stefan emphasized avoiding more pricing variables and keeping it simple for customers [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		### Amazon/Alexa Partnership
		- Alexa wants access to new prompt upsampling, originally planned to launch tomorrow but delayed due to backend issues [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Likely don't need grounding for Alexa use cases (more world knowledge focused) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Decision needed on custom endpoint vs standard 2.1 endpoint with parameters [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Pricing needs to be locked in; need to clarify existing agreement with Alexa team [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Team leaning toward single endpoint with parameters rather than managing two separate endpoints [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		### GTM & Marketing Perspective
		- Owais noted this feels like a substantial launch, not just a small release [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580fb9b08f5c8d109bf16]
		- Multiple compelling use cases to showcase [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580fb9b08f5c8d109bf16]
		- Core value: Makes models easier to use, less reliant on expert prompting [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5806b99a5e8558da1c90f]
		- Quality of life improvements (auto aspect ratio, grounding) reduce user effort while improving results [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5806b99a5e8558da1c90f]
		- USP for customers: Higher realism, more smart features via prompting, better product consistency [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803b84c5c8ba2f4ae35d]

<content>
<meeting-notes readOnlyViewMeetingNoteUrl="https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5802293bac5f0d7870409">
	**FLUX 2.1 Release Planning Call** <mention-date start="2026-03-31"/>
	<summary>
		### Action Items
		- [ ] Maxim to test GPT-5.4 mini latency and create PR to existing branch [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d58021b7e8fc861a0f6116]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to coordinate with engineering on merging the updated prompt upsampling PR [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to talk to Matt about Amazon/Alexa pricing agreement [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to finalize feature set and pricing by end of week [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- [ ] Owais to write one-pager for 2.1 launch and update release calendar [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580feb87aedc3f228be84]
		- [ ] <mention-user url="user://276d872b-594c-81a6-b5dd-0002e0a9bb1c"/> to update launch calendar page with consolidated information [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580d08ddbe1f793661cf9]
		- [ ] Alex to run human evaluation on GPT models with Maxim [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803384d0f1c74ae237ac]
		- [ ] Team to decide on Max scoring improvements (vision generation loop vs replacing Pro with Flex) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		### FLUX 2.1 Launch Timeline
		- **This week**: Send Pro endpoint to Elena Marina for evaluation, finalize feature set and pricing [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Next week**: Polish and ensure everything is ready [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Target launch**: April 14th (approximately 2 weeks out) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- Timeline may shift depending on Elena Marina evaluation results [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		### What's Launching with FLUX 2.1
		Releasing upgraded versions of Pro, Flex, and Max models simultaneously with: [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Improved prompt upsampling**: More realistic images, better character reference and text editing [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- **Auto aspect ratio inference**: From prompt content (e.g., "16:9" or "landscape") [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Visual grounding**: Web search for named entities in prompts [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Transparent background**: Background removal capability [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- **Better quality and latency** compared to current models [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		- API parameter alignment with Google and OpenAI standards [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5800d8aded9bd033f40e3]
		### Technical Decisions & Discussion
		- **GPT model choice**: Need to test GPT-5.4 mini vs current 5.1 for latency before sending to Elena Marina [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- Partnership allows for re-evaluation if needed, relatively low cost concern [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580859018c5bfde19b457]
		- **Endpoint design**: New endpoints for each model (not drop-in replacement), users opt-in by choice [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580be812de011d15d6489][^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d58047ae07ef18d2841be1]
		- **Upsampling latency**: OpenAI upsampling takes \~5 seconds (majority of request time in best case), compared to 1.85s generation [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		- **Max scoring**: Considering improved scoring with custom prompts per generation and tournament-style comparison [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5801f9e01dbb08758de17]
		### Pricing Complexity Concerns
		- Team pushing to simplify pricing model rather than adding complexity [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803b84c5c8ba2f4ae35d]
		- Grounding can be expensive (\~1.5 cents for 3 images) and should have separate pricing toggle [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Transparent background also incurs GPU costs that need margin calculation [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Proposal: Average out costs into simplified per-megapixel pricing rather than exposing all feature complexity [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5808bbf37de2bc474d8ef]
		- Stefan emphasized avoiding more pricing variables and keeping it simple for customers [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		### Amazon/Alexa Partnership
		- Alexa wants access to new prompt upsampling, originally planned to launch tomorrow but delayed due to backend issues [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Likely don't need grounding for Alexa use cases (more world knowledge focused) [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Decision needed on custom endpoint vs standard 2.1 endpoint with parameters [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Pricing needs to be locked in; need to clarify existing agreement with Alexa team [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		- Team leaning toward single endpoint with parameters rather than managing two separate endpoints [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580cdade9de57e0a426b3]
		### GTM & Marketing Perspective
		- Owais noted this feels like a substantial launch, not just a small release [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580fb9b08f5c8d109bf16]
		- Multiple compelling use cases to showcase [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d580fb9b08f5c8d109bf16]
		- Core value: Makes models easier to use, less reliant on expert prompting [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5806b99a5e8558da1c90f]
		- Quality of life improvements (auto aspect ratio, grounding) reduce user effort while improving results [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5806b99a5e8558da1c90f]
		- USP for customers: Higher realism, more smart features via prompting, better product consistency [^https://www.notion.so/334c370222d580858330c6bdc698e225#334c370222d5803b84c5c8ba2f4ae35d]
	</summary>
	<notes>
		<empty-block/>
	</notes>

</meeting-notes>

<content>
<callout icon="🚫" color="gray_bg">
	The current program is on pause - Stay tuned for the updated tool for our coffee chat
</callout>
The coffee chat is a 30mins meeting each week with a randomly selected team mate that you will find automatically in your calendar in the weeks where you’re not off. 
Here’s a quick summary on how it works/why we have it:
- coffee chats are meant to be 30mins chats to mix up members of different teams on a regular basis as we grow - just to get to know each other.
- Chat about whatever you want (doesn't have to be work-related)
- based on your cal availability you will find a meeting slot with another BFL member in your cal in each week
- If the slot doesn't work (can be based on large timezone differences and packed calendars) simply check in with the team member you will meet and reschedule to a date that works for both
- if there's an uneven number of employees available in a week, one person has no meeting for that week. But feel free to simply reach out to someone else if you still want to participate and should be that person.
Happy ☕ -chatting!
<empty-block/>
</content>
</page>
