310c3702-22d5-8168-a474-de275623eeb9.title: Reseller Strategy — March 2026
310c3702-22d5-8168-a474-de275623eeb9.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/310c370222d58168a474de275623eeb9 as of 2026-03-30T09:41:24.192Z: {"title":"Reseller Strategy — March 2026"} # Updated Reseller Strategy — March 2026 ## TL;DR {toggle="true"} BFL's reseller channel peaked at \$1.20M monthly in August 2025 and has declined 54.7% since. The decline is concentrated in fal and replicate, both of whom are significantly short of their minimum commitments and operating under discount structures that were set against FLUX.1 economics, include future models automatically, and contain no promotional obligations. The current program is not working for BFL commercially or strategically. The good news: the overall channel is not broken. Runware is growing fast at 30% discount for \$2M commit. OpenRouter is ramping. **What this document proposes:** A two-tier reseller program (Preferred and Standard) built on four principles: 1. Discounts are earned through performance and promotional obligations, not just commits 2. The channel extends BFL's reach but cannot compete with direct 3. Co-marketing and FLUX attribution are conditions of access 4. Future models require fresh negotiation Preferred tier is capped at three partners, requires a \$2M minimum commit or 80% of prior year actual spend, whichever is higher, carries a 30% discount ceiling (model-specific, subject to margin analysis), and comes with meaningful BFL support including named partner manager, bi-weekly syncs, SLAs, and Day-0 model access. Standard tier is open to other resellers with no commit and minimal discount. Fal, replicate, and runware map to Preferred. Everyone else is Standard. ⚠️ **Decisions required this week:** - **Issue fal termination notice this week.** BFL has a 60-day termination for convenience right on the fal agreement that can be exercised at any time. Issuing notice now starts the 60-day clock and creates a clean forcing function for renegotiation. It does not commit BFL to exiting the relationship. It preserves both strategic options and signals to fal that the current terms are not being renewed passively. The longer BFL waits, the more runway fal has to delay the conversation. - **Replicate notice this week.** Amendment No. 2 expires May 31, 2026. The 90-day notice window to prevent auto-renewal is open now. Same play as fal. Issue notice alongside fal this week to start the renegotiation process on both relationships simultaneously. **The honest constraint:** The new program creates the right conditions for a strong reseller channel. It does not replace model velocity. When FLUX.3 ships and is clearly SOTA, partner behavior largely corrects itself. Until then, the program's objective is to hold ground, reset economics, and position BFL to activate the channel aggressively at FLUX.3 launch. --- ## State of the Resellers {toggle="true"} The reseller channel peaked at **\$1.20M in August 2025** and has declined **54.7%** to a \$546K monthly run rate as of February 2026. The decline is concentrated in fal and replicate. The remaining seven resellers are growing, flat, or negligible. The channel has two structural problems: over-reliance on two partners who were over-discounted at peak, and no scaled resellers emerging fast enough to replace lost volume.
Partner Peak Monthly Feb 2026 6-mo Avg ARR Decline from Peak Discount Status
fal \$736K (Sep '25) \$281K \$3.91M -62% 50% At-risk
replicate \$444K (Aug '25) \$186K \$2.48M -58% 40% At-risk
runware \$17K (Jun '25) \$47K \$365K +372% growth 10% Growing
together \$24K (Jul '25) \$13K \$163K -45% 10% At-risk
openrouter \$11K (Mar '26) \$11K \$106K Still ramping 5% Growing
fireworks \$7K (Sep '25) \$5K \$65K -25% 5% Flat
prodia \$43K (May '25) \$2K \$25K -95% 5% Inactive
deepinfra \$2K (Jan '25) \$1K \$9K -48% 10% Inactive
datacrunch \$147 (Oct '25) \$36 \$382 -76% 5% Inactive
**fal.** Down 62% from peak, running at \$3.91M ARR against a 50% discount. The decline reflects customers on fal's platform choosing competing models over FLUX, not customers leaving fal. Fal is retaining its developer base. FLUX is losing share within it. Against a \$6.5M annual commit, fal is approximately \$1.85M short. The economics must be reset at renewal as fal is using their discount margin to undercut BFL direct on enterprise deals. **replicate.** Same dynamic at lower scale. Down 58%, 40% discount, similar model concentration. Against a \$5M annual commit, replicate is approximately \$2.3M short. Renewal conversation is overdue. **runware****.** Started May 2025, now the channel's only clear growth story. Quarterly revenue: \$18K in Q2 2025, \$55K in Q3, \$79K in Q4, \$160K in Q1 2026. Growth despite no new major model releases from FLUX. New contract being negotiated at 30% discount for \$2M commit. **together.** Declining slowly for 18 months. No strategic differentiation. Renew at standard tier, no concessions. **openrouter.** Live since November 2025, already at \$106K ARR and still ramping. Only reseller distributing flux-2-klein-4b at any volume. Worth proactive outreach. **fireworks, deepinfra, prodia, datacrunch.** Combined ARR under \$100K. Maintain at standard tier. No dedicated resources. --- ## Direct vs. Reseller: Differentiated Value {toggle="true"} The reseller program exists to extend BFL's reach into developer communities where BFL does not have direct presence. It is not a substitute for direct enterprise relationships. The two channels serve different customers and must be structured to avoid competition. **Going direct:** - **Best available pricing.** Enterprise customers access pricing and custom endpoint rates that resellers cannot match or pass through. - **Custom model endpoints.** Fine-tunes, LoRAs, and task-specific variants are available exclusively through direct engagements with our FDE team. Resellers receive standard SKUs only. - **Dedicated technical support.** Access to BFL's FDE team for integration, evals, and optimization. - **SLA guarantees.** Enterprise SLAs are available direct only. - **Day-0 model access.** New models available on launch day. Preferred resellers follow after an exclusivity window. Standard resellers receive access on the public release date. - **Direct relationship with BFL.** Roadmap input, early access programs, and co-development opportunities are not available through resellers. **Going through a reseller:** - **Unified platform access.** Single API, billing relationship, and integration layer across hundreds of models. - **Existing integrations and community.** Faster onboarding for developers already on these platforms. - **Model comparison and switching.** Developers can benchmark FLUX against competing models in the same environment. **The ceiling resellers cannot cross.** Resellers may not offer customers custom endpoints, exclusive model variants, or pricing below agreed upon price floors regardless of tier or discount level. Custom endpoints are a direct-only asset. This must be addressed in all future and renewed agreements. --- ## The Problems {toggle="true"} ### **Problem 1: Resellers Have No Incentive to Prioritize FLUX, except at launch. ** {toggle="true"} Fal, Replicate, and most resellers in this program are inference marketplaces offering 1,000+ models in a single UI. Their platform surfaces whatever their customers choose, and customers pick the highest quality model available. This is not a relationship problem. It is their business model. Our resellers promoted FLUX.2 at launch. Customers chose competing models because at higher quality with more hype around the same time. Promotion did not move volume because the FLUX.2 was not clearly best-in-class at that moment. Resellers make it easy for customers switch models within days of a competitor launch. The deeper risk is that fal and replicate will increasingly orient around Google and OpenAI launches, which generate outsized press coverage and bring new developers onto their platforms. A reseller has every commercial reason to prioritize those moments over ours. Discounts do not change this. Fal is significantly short of their \$6.5M minimum commitment and performance continues to drop. The 50% discount changed neither end-customer choice nor partner behavior. **What the program can and cannot control.** Contractual obligations can create a floor. But they are a secondhand solution. The primary lever is model quality. When FLUX.3 ships and is clearly SOTA, we believe we will see our performance improve. Until then, the program's realistic objective is to hold ground and set us up for a successful FLUX.3 launch. **What the new program must include:** - **Limited exclusivity windows.** Preferred partners receive time-limited exclusive access to new models before other resellers. Being first on a new model release is commercially meaningful. Non-compliant partners receive access on the standard public release date. - **Premium model access as an earned benefit.** Access to premium models is a benefit of preferred partner status, not a baseline entitlement. Partners falling short on promotional obligations revert to standard model access until compliance is restored. ### Problem 2: Our Discount and Contract Structure Is Being Used Against Us {toggle="true"} At 40-50% discount, resellers have enough margin to offer customers 30-40% off BFL list price and still make margin. Resellers can undercut BFL direct on price, winning enterprise deals BFL was actively pursuing. BFL retains the revenue at 50% discount however, with no customer relationship, no visibility, and no ability to grow the account. FLUX.2 and newer models carry higher infrastructure costs. At current discount levels, some model variants (e.g. Max) are negative margin for BFL. The discount structure was set against FLUX.1 economics and never renegotiated when model cost profiles changed. Future models were included automatically in existing agreements, which is how partners ended up with 40-50% discounts on FLUX.2 despite its higher infrastructure cost. Neither major contract contains a promotional obligation, launch activation requirement, or customer data sharing clause. The agreements were structured as pure financial arrangements with no behavioral expectations. The commit-for-discount structure created liabilities on both sides. Fal is \$1.85M short of their \$6.5M commit. Replicate is \$2.3M short of their \$5M commit. That gap is leverage, but it cuts both ways. BFL can use it as a forcing function to restructure the relationship. Partners can call the bluff and walk away. **What needs to change:** - **Cap the discount resellers can pass to customers.** Resellers may not offer BFL model access below an agreed upon discount on list price. - **Discount levels must reflect model cost economics.** A flat discount across all models is not viable. FLUX.2 and future models require lower discount ceilings than FLUX.1. This must be model-specific in every new and renewed agreement. - **New models require fresh negotiation.** No existing discount tier or commit automatically extends to new model releases. FLUX.3 and beyond are negotiated separately. Preferred partners get first access to those conversations. - **Obligations built in from the start.** Every new and renewed agreement follows the Runware template. Promotional obligations, launch activation, and customer data sharing are conditions of the program, not goodwill expectations. - **Minimum commits must be enforced.** Commits should be reasonable and enforced as they create financial obligation and ensure partners have skin in the game. A reseller with a Google commit and no BFL commit will direct volume toward Google. - **Commit gap negotiation options:** 1. **Enforce and collect.** Pursue the shortfall as a cash liability. Not recommended as partners may exert their leverage and not pay. 2. **Waiver for restructure.** Waive the shortfall in exchange for signing a new agreement under revised terms. 3. **Rollover plus new commit.** Shortfall rolls into the new agreement as a carry-forward minimum, plus a fresh annual commit to access preferred tier. Recommended opening position as it’s the strongest outcome if the partner accepts it. ### Problem 3: We Have No Visibility Into Who Is Using FLUX or Why {toggle="true"} BFL does not know who the end customers are, what they are building, or what volume they are generating through the reseller channel. When a customer churns off FLUX via a reseller, we have no early warning signal and no path to recovery. Hundreds of millions of outputs flow through the reseller channel containing significant signal about what customers actually build with FLUX. We have access to none of it. **What the new program must require as conditions of preferred status:** - **Named account transparency.** Partners must identify end customers by name and use case. BFL uses this for account intelligence and product development only, with explicit contractual restrictions on approaching those customers directly without partner involvement. - **End-customer launch communication.** When BFL launches a new model, preferred partners must notify their active customer base within 5 business days. If a partner fails to execute, BFL retains the right to reach those customers directly. Silence is not an option. - **Aggregated usage data.** Quarterly reporting on volume by model, use case category, and customer feedback. Enough signal for BFL to understand what is being built and where demand is moving before it shows up as a competitive shift. ### Problem 4: Partner Relationships Are Fragmented and Reactive {toggle="true"} Reseller relationships at BFL have been managed across multiple people including founders and several members of the partnerships team. There is no single owner, no consistent engagement cadence, and no structured view of partner health. Partners experience BFL as disorganized. Strategic conversations happen sporadically rather than on a cadence that would make them useful. This has a direct commercial cost. Partners who feel neglected default to passive resale. In a market where resellers choose which models to feature and which to let atrophy, relationship quality is a competitive variable. Preferred partners are typically positioning themselves as enterprise solutions to their own customers. Without SLAs from BFL, they cannot credibly make that promise, and any reliability issues at the BFL layer directly damage their standing with enterprise accounts and thus our standing with the partner. **What the new program must do:** - Centralize partner ownership under a single function with clear accountability per partner. Build a structured engagement model that gives BFL consistent signal on partner health, model adoption, and competitive positioning. - Extend SLA commitments to preferred partners as a condition of the tier, enabling them to make credible enterprise promises to their own customers. --- ## New Program Structure {toggle="true"} ### Guiding Principles - **Program benefits must be earned.** Access to preferred pricing requires a minimum commit, demonstrated performance, and active promotional obligations. Tiers are revisited at renewal. - **The channel exists to extend BFL's reach, not compete with it.** Resellers access standard model SKUs. Custom endpoints, fine-tunes, and exclusive model variants are direct-only assets. No reseller regardless of tier can offer a customer something that BFL direct cannot match or exceed. - **Co-marketing is a condition of program access.** FLUX attribution, launch activation, and brand visibility in partner products are obligations tied to tier status. Partners benefit from BFL's model quality and brand. BFL requires visible credit in return. - **Future model releases require fresh negotiation.** No existing tier or commit automatically extends to new model classes. FLUX.3 and beyond are negotiated separately. Preferred partners receive first access to those conversations. --- ### Tier Structure Commit determines tier access from day one. Trailing spend determines tier retention at renewal. Partners who miss their commit by more than 20% step down to Standard at renewal. To prevent aspirational commits from recreating the fal and replicate failure mode, commits must be credible against trailing performance. A partner cannot access Preferred tier if their trailing six-month ARR is below 80% of the tier floor.
Preferred Standard
**Minimum Commit** \$2M or 80% of prior year spend, whichever is higher No commit required
**Partner Cap** Capped at 3 partners Open
**Reseller Discount** Up to 30%. Model specific. 5-10%
Max pass-through to customers Max discount 20% Max discount 10%
**Model Access** Full standard SKU set. Day-0 access on new launches Core models. Premium models are for Preferred Partners
**Custom Endpoints** None None
**SLA** Yes, terms defined per agreement No
**Sync Cadence** Bi-weekly Async (Slack/email)
**QBR** Quarterly Bi-Annual
**Dedicated Contact** Named Partner Manager (both sides) Partner Team
**Roadmap Access** Early access + NDA briefing Public launch comms only
**Co-marketing** Required (see below) Required (Limited to blog, social)
Partners Included fal, Replicate, Runware Everyone else
--- ### Promotional Obligations (Preferred) Promotional obligations are conditions of tier status, not best-efforts language. Partners who fail to meet them are reviewed for tier demotion at renewal. The following apply to all Preferred partners: **Day-0 launch obligations (every major model release as designated by BFL):** - Blog post featuring the new model published on launch day - Social media promotion across partner channels on launch day - Custom video content demonstrating the new model on launch day - Email promotion to existing customer base within 5 business days of launch **Ongoing obligations:** - FLUX model visible in partner product UI wherever model selection is available. - Participation in joint events and hackathons. - Quarterly usage reporting: volume by model, use case category, and customer demographics. - Named accounts for any end customer exceeding \$200K annual spend through the reseller. - Featured or recommended placement for new FLUX models for the first 30 days following a major launch. --- ### Model Access and Exclusivity Standard SKU access is available to all tiers. Preferred partners receive Day-0 access on new model launches. Standard partners receive access on the public release date. Custom endpoints, fine-tunes, and LoRAs are direct-only. No reseller tier receives access to custom model variants regardless of tier or commit size. This is the primary mechanism that ensures BFL direct always has something to offer that no reseller can replicate. --- ### Minimum Commit Structure The floor for each renewal period is the higher of: - The tier minimum (\$2M for Preferred), or - 80% of actual spend in the prior contract year. This floating floor means the minimum stays anchored to demonstrated performance at every renewal. A growing partner's floor rises automatically. A declining partner cannot lock in Preferred status at a floor they have already structurally moved past. For new partners with no prior year history, the \$2M baseline applies. The baseline is calculated against trailing twelve months of actual spend, not the prior contract year, to prevent gaming through contract timing. --- ## Why Partner with BFL {toggle="true"} The reseller program is designed to be a genuine commercial advantage for partners who are growing with FLUX, not a compliance framework for those who are not. Preferred partners get: - **First-mover advantage on new launches.** New model releases drive immediate spikes in developer interest. Preferred partners get access before the market. Being first is a meaningful commercial moment. Standard partners wait. - **Better economics.** Preferred partners access the deepest discounts BFL offers to resellers, structured against model cost economics so margins are sustainable on both sides. - **Roadmap visibility.** Preferred partners receive NDA briefings on upcoming models ahead of public announcement. - **SLA guarantees.** Preferred partners receive SLA commitments from BFL, enabling them to make credible enterprise promises to their own customers. - **Co-marketing and brand lift.** Joint announcements, case studies, events, and hackathons. Being a named FLUX preferred partner is a differentiating signal in a market with hundreds of competing models. - **A direct line into BFL.** Named partner manager, regular sync cadence, and a seat at the table for product feedback. Roadmap input from preferred partners is taken seriously. - **FLUX.3 access.** FLUX.3 is targeting SOTA across image, video, and audio. Preferred partners get Day-0 access, allowing them to participate in the launch moment and the developer buzz that follows. Non-preferred partners wait. --- # Reseller Strategy — Feb 2026 **Date:** Feb 23, 2026 \| **Author:** Seb \| **Status:** Needs review by team and then decision by Andi + Robin --- # Summary The reseller channel is declining. fal and Replicate are both down 68% from peak, both tracking well short of their commits. We have two contracts needing immediate action and a strategic decision about the program going forward. Core hypothesis: reseller discounts don't drive demand — users pick models based on quality and hype, not reseller margin structures. If true, the discounts we're giving are pure margin compression with no upside. --- # Contracts — Action Required **fal** — 50% discount, \$6.5M commit, API reselling only. Auto-renews May 1. - Shortfall: \~\$1.85M. Notice deadline missed Jan 30. - ⚠️ Legal: shortfall clause references "Amendment Term" — likely drafting error, enforceability unclear? - Cleaner path: §5.2.1 allows 60-day termination at any time. BFL can send notice now and exit before May 1 auto-renewal without invoking the shortfall. Shortfall still useful as a waiver carrot in negotiations. - **Action:** Decide on overall strategy first. With the 60-day notice period in hand, timing is manageable. **Replicate** — 40% discount, \$5.1M commit, Aug '25–Jul '26. *(Acquired by Cloudflare, Nov '25.)* - Shortfall: \~\$2.13M. Notice deadline: **May 2 — 68 days away.** - Same play as fal. Same 60-day termination right exists. - Peak (\$444K) was their very first month. Has declined every month since. **Runware** — 30% discount, \$2M commit, Jan 17 2026 – Jan 2027. Growing (\$23K → \$34K/mo). No future models by default. - 30% is out of step with the new structure, but that's useful. With fal and Replicate moving to \~10%/5% (tbd! see below), keeping Runware at 30% makes them the best-margined reseller in the market — a deliberate bet on making them a stronger player. A better-margined Runware can invest more in GTM and win more customers: more competition, less concentration risk for BFL. Move to normal program at Jan 2027 renewal. **All others** — 5% flat, no commit, no future models. --- # Revenue Snapshot
Peak Feb '26 Δ
fal \$705K (Sep '25) \$226K 🔴 −68%
Replicate \$444K (Aug '25, first month) \$141K 🔴 −68%
Runware \$23K \$34K 🟢 growing
--- # Strategic Options **Hypothesis: resellers can't move the market.** fal and Replicate offer FLUX alongside Seedream, NanoBanana, and others in the same UI. Users follow quality and hype — the market decides, not the reseller. The commit failures are the proof: if resellers could drive volume, they'd have hit their numbers. The truth is probably somewhere in the middle, but steep discounts clearly don't drive volume. They're a margin tax on volume BFL would have captured anyway. Moving fal/Replicate from 50%/40% to \~10% recovers \~\$1.8M/year with likely minimal volume impact. Going forward: minimal discounts, real value extracted through the obligations package. **Option A — Squeeze and Replace:** 5% flat for all resellers. No preferred tier. Use shortfall/60-day notice to exit or hard-restructure fal and Replicate. Force traffic back to direct. Works well if FLUX.3 is clearly SOTA. High risk if not — resellers already offer NanoBanana, Seedream, and others alongside FLUX. They don't need to swap, they just deprioritize us. BFL loses distribution without direct volume to compensate. **Option B — Restructure and Grow Beyond** *(preferred):* Use shortfall as leverage for a reset to new terms (lower discount, attribution, embargo). Don't push so hard they walk. Let the reseller position erode organically as MSFT Foundry, Bedrock, and co-sell channels scale. More resilient if FLUX.3 isn't clearly SOTA. Risk: fal/Replicate use the runway to deepen customer lock-in. Known tension: fal gives their own customers apparently up to \~30% discount, meaning at 50% from BFL they're keeping \~20pts of margin. If BFL moves to \~10%, fal either absorbs a massive margin hit or has to reprice their customers upward — they will use this as pushback. We need to understand the scale of this before the first conversation. **Both options depend heavily on FLUX.3 being clearly SOTA.** Embargo windows and preferred status have no teeth without it. --- # Preferred Program (Option B implementation)
Preferred Non-Preferred
Model access Day 0 4-week embargo
Discount \~10% (TBD) \~5% (TBD)
Attribution + co-marketing Required None
Status Revocable N/A
**Commit thresholds vs. co-marketing:** open question worth deliberating. Commits didn't protect BFL's revenue anyway (see current shortfalls), so their value as a protection mechanism is questionable. The alternative: waive commit requirements entirely in exchange for a stronger obligation package — co-marketing, attribution, full transparency into reseller accounts and usage, and a structured lead funnel back to BFL. This shifts the relationship from a financial guarantee (which resellers failed to honour) to ongoing behavioural obligations (which are harder to ignore and more valuable long-term). It also opens preferred status to smaller resellers like Prodia — more competition, less concentration risk. Worth deciding explicitly rather than defaulting to commits out of habit. **Program levers — what preferred status unlocks (and can restrict):** Beyond discounts and embargo windows, preferred status is a meaningful control point. These are levers we can apply now or over time: - **Pro/Max model access for preferred only:** Non-preferred resellers get dev only. Pro/Max exclusively for preferred partners and BFL direct. Pro is where BFL captures most value and brand attribution matters most. For FLUX.3+, this should be a non-negotiable condition of preferred status. - **Dev hosting rights:** FLUX dev models are already non-commercial under the FLUX Dev License — commercial hosting requires a BFL agreement. We already have the legal right to restrict or revoke this. The question is whether to enforce it and eventually build BFL-hosted dev with a LoRA trainer, letting the community self-host open-weights and enterprise clients self-host under license. Requires BFL to build infrastructure genuinely competitive with fal's. If we don't, developers stay on fal or move to OS models (mostly Chinese). - **LoRA/fine-tuning:** If BFL builds its own fine-tuning offering, include a clause in new agreements giving BFL the right to restrict specific reseller capabilities at renewal — without naming LoRA explicitly, which would tip the roadmap. The clause preserves the leverage quietly. - **Apache / truly open models — the open-source tension:** Models like Schnell and Klein 4B are Apache 2.0 — anyone can host them commercially, no agreement required, no lever available. Shifting future open releases to a more restrictive license (Commons Clause, SSPL, BSL) would allow community/self-hosting but prohibit commercial reselling. But it's a visible move away from BFL's open-source identity, which is core to community goodwill. The risk: it hands the "truly open" position to OS models (mostly Chinese) which would fill the vacuum immediately. Needs a deliberate leadership discussion. All levers only work if BFL's direct product is genuinely competitive — and if the marketing engine behind it is too. fal is strong at developer marketing: tutorials, community, integrations, visibility. BFL needs a comparable or better marketing motion to make direct a real alternative, not just a fallback. > 💬 **New input — Slack thread, Feb 18–25, 2026:** Internal discussion flagged an opportunity to require end-customers accessing FLUX via resellers to share contact info with BFL (similar to Anthropic's approach via GCP). Key opportunity: direct marketing to active end-users — cases exist where reseller customers stayed on old models simply because they didn't know new ones had launched. A related structural option: require BFL-issued API keys for all end-customers, even on reseller platforms, for direct usage visibility. Risks: relationship damage if BFL targets customers learned this way, and the ask may implicitly open the door to co-sell expectations. **Suggested next step: include end-customer data sharing and/or BFL-issued API keys as a term in the preferred program obligations package.** --- # Decisions Needed 1. **A or B?** 2. **C****ommit vs. obligations package:** Drop commits in favour of co-marketing, attribution, account transparency, and lead funnel? See Preferred Program section for full framing. 3. **Final discount levels** (Preferred vs. Non-Preferred). 4. **FLUX.3 confidence** — biggest variable in the risk profile of everything above.

The discount structure was set against FLUX.1 economics and never renegotiated when model cost profiles changed. Future models were included automatically in existing agreements, which is how partners ended up with 40-50% discounts on FLUX.2 despite its higher infrastructure cost. Neither major contract contains a promotional obligation, launch activation requirement, or customer data sharing clause. The agreements were structured as pure financial arrangements with no behavioral expectations. The commit-for-discount structure created liabilities on both sides. Fal is \$1.85M short of their \$6.5M commit. Replicate is \$2.3M short of their \$5M commit. That gap is leverage, but it cuts both ways. BFL can use it as a forcing function to restructure the relationship. Partners can call the bluff and walk away. **What needs to change:** - **Cap the discount resellers can pass to customers.** Resellers may not offer BFL model access below an agreed upon discount on list price. - **Discount levels must reflect model cost economics.** A flat discount across all models is not viable. FLUX.2 and future models require lower discount ceilings than FLUX.1. This must be model-specific in every new and renewed agreement. - **New models require fresh negotiation.** No existing discount tier or commit automatically extends to new model releases. FLUX.3 and beyond are negotiated separately. Preferred partners get first access to those conversations. - **Obligations built in from the start.** Every new and renewed agreement follows the Runware template. Promotional obligations, launch activation, and customer data sharing are conditions of the program, not goodwill expectations. - **Minimum commits must be enforced.** Commits should be reasonable and enforced as they create financial obligation and ensure partners have skin in the game. A reseller with a Google commit and no BFL commit will direct volume toward Google. - **Commit gap negotiation options:** 1. **Enforce and collect.** Pursue the shortfall as a cash liability. Not recommended as partners may exert their leverage and not pay. 2. **Waiver for restructure.** Waive the shortfall in exchange for signing a new agreement under revised terms. 3. **Rollover plus new commit.** Shortfall rolls into the new agreement as a carry-forward minimum, plus a fresh annual commit to access preferred tier. Recommended opening position as it’s the strongest outcome if the partner accepts it. ### Problem 3: We Have No Visibility Into Who Is Using FLUX or Why {toggle="true"} BFL does not know who the end customers are, what they are building, or what volume they are generating through the reseller channel. When a customer churns off FLUX via a reseller, we have no early warning signal and no path to recovery. Hundreds of millions of outputs flow through the reseller channel containing significant signal about what customers actually build with FLUX. We have access to none of it. **What the new program must require as conditions of preferred status:** - **Named account transparency.** Partners must identify end customers by name and use case. BFL uses this for account intelligence and product development only, with explicit contractual restrictions on approaching those customers directly without partner involvement. - **End-customer launch communication.** When BFL launches a new model, preferred partners must notify their active customer base within 5 business days. If a partner fails to execute, BFL retains the right to reach those customers directly. Silence is not an option. - **Aggregated usage data.** Quarterly reporting on volume by model, use case category, and customer feedback. Enough signal for BFL to understand what is being built and where demand is moving before it shows up as a competitive shift. ### Problem 4: Partner Relationships Are Fragmented and Reactive {toggle="true"} Reseller relationships at BFL have been managed across multiple people including founders and several members of the partnerships team. There is no single owner, no consistent engagement cadence, and no structured view of partner health. Partners experience BFL as disorganized. Strategic conversations happen sporadically rather than on a cadence that would make them useful. This has a direct commercial cost. Partners who feel neglected default to passive resale. In a market where resellers choose which models to feature and which to let atrophy, relationship quality is a competitive variable. Preferred partners are typically positioning themselves as enterprise solutions to their own customers. Without SLAs from BFL, they cannot credibly make that promise, and any reliability issues at the BFL layer directly damage their standing with enterprise accounts and thus our standing with the partner. **What the new program must do:** - Centralize partner ownership under a single function with clear accountability per partner. Build a structured engagement model that gives BFL consistent signal on partner health, model adoption, and competitive positioning. - Extend SLA commitments to preferred partners as a condition of the tier, enabling them to make credible enterprise promises to their own customers. --- ## New Program Structure {toggle="true"} ### Guiding Principles - **Program benefits must be earned.** Access to preferred pricing requires a minimum commit, demonstrated performance, and active promotional obligations. Tiers are revisited at renewal. - **The channel exists to extend BFL's reach, not compete with it.** Resellers access standard model SKUs. Custom endpoints, fine-tunes, and exclusive model variants are direct-only assets. No reseller regardless of tier can offer a customer something that BFL direct cannot match or exceed. - **Co-marketing is a condition of program access.** FLUX attribution, launch activation, and brand visibility in partner products are obligations tied to tier status. Partners benefit from BFL's model quality and brand. BFL requires visible credit in return. - **Future model releases require fresh negotiation.** No existing tier or commit automatically extends to new model classes. FLUX.3 and beyond are negotiated separately. Preferred partners receive first access to those conversations. --- ### Tier Structure Commit determines tier access from day one. Trailing spend determines tier retention at renewal. Partners who miss their commit by more than 20% step down to Standard at renewal. To prevent aspirational commits from recreating the fal and replicate failure mode, commits must be credible against trailing performance. A partner cannot access Preferred tier if their trailing six-month ARR is below 80% of the tier floor.
Preferred Standard
**Minimum Commit** \$2M or 80% of prior year spend, whichever is higher No commit required
**Partner Cap** Capped at 3 partners Open
**Reseller Discount** Up to 30%. Model specific. 5-10%
Max pass-through to customers Max discount 20% Max discount 10%
**Model Access** Full standard SKU set. Day-0 access on new launches Core models. Premium models are for Preferred Partners
**Custom Endpoints** None None
**SLA** Yes, terms defined per agreement No
**Sync Cadence** Bi-weekly Async (Slack/email)
**QBR** Quarterly Bi-Annual
**Dedicated Contact** Named Partner Manager (both sides) Partner Team
**Roadmap Access** Early access + NDA briefing Public launch comms only
**Co-marketing** Required (see below) Required (Limited to blog, social)
Partners Included fal, Replicate, Runware Everyone else
--- ### Promotional Obligations (Preferred) Promotional obligations are conditions of tier status, not best-efforts language. Partners who fail to meet them are reviewed for tier demotion at renewal. The following apply to all Preferred partners: **Day-0 launch obligations (every major model release as designated by BFL):** - Blog post featuring the new model published on launch day - Social media promotion across partner channels on launch day - Custom video content demonstrating the new model on launch day - Email promotion to existing customer base within 5 business days of launch **Ongoing obligations:** - FLUX model visible in partner product UI wherever model selection is available. - Participation in joint events and hackathons. - Quarterly usage reporting: volume by model, use case category, and customer demographics. - Named accounts for any end customer exceeding \$200K annual spend through the reseller. - Featured or recommended placement for new FLUX models for the first 30 days following a major launch. --- ### Model Access and Exclusivity Standard SKU access is available to all tiers. Preferred partners receive Day-0 access on new model launches. Standard partners receive access on the public release date. Custom endpoints, fine-tunes, and LoRAs are direct-only. No reseller tier receives access to custom model variants regardless of tier or commit size. This is the primary mechanism that ensures BFL direct always has something to offer that no reseller can replicate. --- ### Minimum Commit Structure The floor for each renewal period is the higher of: - The tier minimum (\$2M for Preferred), or - 80% of actual spend in the prior contract year. This floating floor means the minimum stays anchored to demonstrated performance at every renewal. A growing partner's floor rises automatically. A declining partner cannot lock in Preferred status at a floor they have already structurally moved past. For new partners with no prior year history, the \$2M baseline applies. The baseline is calculated against trailing twelve months of actual spend, not the prior contract year, to prevent gaming through contract timing. --- ## Why Partner with BFL {toggle="true"} The reseller program is designed to be a genuine commercial advantage for partners who are growing with FLUX, not a compliance framework for those who are not. Preferred partners get: - **First-mover advantage on new launches.** New model releases drive immediate spikes in developer interest. Preferred partners get access before the market. Being first is a meaningful commercial moment. Standard partners wait. - **Better economics.** Preferred partners access the deepest discounts BFL offers to resellers, structured against model cost economics so margins are sustainable on both sides. - **Roadmap visibility.** Preferred partners receive NDA briefings on upcoming models ahead of public announcement. - **SLA guarantees.** Preferred partners receive SLA commitments from BFL, enabling them to make credible enterprise promises to their own customers. - **Co-marketing and brand lift.** Joint announcements, case studies, events, and hackathons. Being a named FLUX preferred partner is a differentiating signal in a market with hundreds of competing models. - **A direct line into BFL.** Named partner manager, regular sync cadence, and a seat at the table for product feedback. Roadmap input from preferred partners is taken seriously. - **FLUX.3 access.** FLUX.3 is targeting SOTA across image, video, and audio. Preferred partners get Day-0 access, allowing them to participate in the launch moment and the developer buzz that follows. Non-preferred partners wait. --- # Reseller Strategy — Feb 2026 **Date:** Feb 23, 2026 \| **Author:** Seb \| **Status:** Needs review by team and then decision by Andi + Robin --- # Summary The reseller channel is declining. fal and Replicate are both down 68% from peak, both tracking well short of their commits. We have two contracts needing immediate action and a strategic decision about the program going forward. Core hypothesis: reseller discounts don't drive demand — users pick models based on quality and hype, not reseller margin structures. If true, the discounts we're giving are pure margin compression with no upside. --- # Contracts — Action Required **fal** — 50% discount, \$6.5M commit, API reselling only. Auto-renews May 1. - Shortfall: \~\$1.85M. Notice deadline missed Jan 30. - ⚠️ Legal: shortfall clause references "Amendment Term" — likely drafting error, enforceability unclear? - Cleaner path: §5.2.1 allows 60-day termination at any time. BFL can send notice now and exit before May 1 auto-renewal without invoking the shortfall. Shortfall still useful as a waiver carrot in negotiations. - **Action:** Decide on overall strategy first. With the 60-day notice period in hand, timing is manageable. **Replicate** — 40% discount, \$5.1M commit, Aug '25–Jul '26. *(Acquired by Cloudflare, Nov '25.)* - Shortfall: \~\$2.13M. Notice deadline: **May 2 — 68 days away.** - Same play as fal. Same 60-day termination right exists. - Peak (\$444K) was their very first month. Has declined every month since. **Runware** — 30% discount, \$2M commit, Jan 17 2026 – Jan 2027. Growing (\$23K → \$34K/mo). No future models by default. - 30% is out of step with the new structure, but that's useful. With fal and Replicate moving to \~10%/5% (tbd! see below), keeping Runware at 30% makes them the best-margined reseller in the market — a deliberate bet on making them a stronger player. A better-margined Runware can invest more in GTM and win more customers: more competition, less concentration risk for BFL. Move to normal program at Jan 2027 renewal. **All others** — 5% flat, no commit, no future models. --- # Revenue Snapshot
Peak Feb '26 Δ
fal \$705K (Sep '25) \$226K 🔴 −68%
Replicate \$444K (Aug '25, first month) \$141K 🔴 −68%
Runware \$23K \$34K 🟢 growing
--- # Strategic Options **Hypothesis: resellers can't move the market.** fal and Replicate offer FLUX alongside Seedream, NanoBanana, and others in the same UI. Users follow quality and hype — the market decides, not the reseller. The commit failures are the proof: if resellers could drive volume, they'd have hit their numbers. The truth is probably somewhere in the middle, but steep discounts clearly don't drive volume. They're a margin tax on volume BFL would have captured anyway. Moving fal/Replicate from 50%/40% to \~10% recovers \~\$1.8M/year with likely minimal volume impact. Going forward: minimal discounts, real value extracted through the obligations package. **Option A — Squeeze and Replace:** 5% flat for all resellers. No preferred tier. Use shortfall/60-day notice to exit or hard-restructure fal and Replicate. Force traffic back to direct. Works well if FLUX.3 is clearly SOTA. High risk if not — resellers already offer NanoBanana, Seedream, and others alongside FLUX. They don't need to swap, they just deprioritize us. BFL loses distribution without direct volume to compensate. **Option B — Restructure and Grow Beyond** *(preferred):* Use shortfall as leverage for a reset to new terms (lower discount, attribution, embargo). Don't push so hard they walk. Let the reseller position erode organically as MSFT Foundry, Bedrock, and co-sell channels scale. More resilient if FLUX.3 isn't clearly SOTA. Risk: fal/Replicate use the runway to deepen customer lock-in. Known tension: fal gives their own customers apparently up to \~30% discount, meaning at 50% from BFL they're keeping \~20pts of margin. If BFL moves to \~10%, fal either absorbs a massive margin hit or has to reprice their customers upward — they will use this as pushback. We need to understand the scale of this before the first conversation. **Both options depend heavily on FLUX.3 being clearly SOTA.** Embargo windows and preferred status have no teeth without it. --- # Preferred Program (Option B implementation)
Preferred Non-Preferred
Model access Day 0 4-week embargo
Discount \~10% (TBD) \~5% (TBD)
Attribution + co-marketing Required None
Status Revocable N/A
**Commit thresholds vs. co-marketing:** open question worth deliberating. Commits didn't protect BFL's revenue anyway (see current shortfalls), so their value as a protection mechanism is questionable. The alternative: waive commit requirements entirely in exchange for a stronger obligation package — co-marketing, attribution, full transparency into reseller accounts and usage, and a structured lead funnel back to BFL. This shifts the relationship from a financial guarantee (which resellers failed to honour) to ongoing behavioural obligations (which are harder to ignore and more valuable long-term). It also opens preferred status to smaller resellers like Prodia — more competition, less concentration risk. Worth deciding explicitly rather than defaulting to commits out of habit. **Program levers — what preferred status unlocks (and can restrict):** Beyond discounts and embargo windows, preferred status is a meaningful control point. These are levers we can apply now or over time: - **Pro/Max model access for preferred only:** Non-preferred resellers get dev only. Pro/Max exclusively for preferred partners and BFL direct. Pro is where BFL captures most value and brand attribution matters most. For FLUX.3+, this should be a non-negotiable condition of preferred status. - **Dev hosting rights:** FLUX dev models are already non-commercial under the FLUX Dev License — commercial hosting requires a BFL agreement. We already have the legal right to restrict or revoke this. The question is whether to enforce it and eventually build BFL-hosted dev with a LoRA trainer, letting the community self-host open-weights and enterprise clients self-host under license. Requires BFL to build infrastructure genuinely competitive with fal's. If we don't, developers stay on fal or move to OS models (mostly Chinese). - **LoRA/fine-tuning:** If BFL builds its own fine-tuning offering, include a clause in new agreements giving BFL the right to restrict specific reseller capabilities at renewal — without naming LoRA explicitly, which would tip the roadmap. The clause preserves the leverage quietly. - **Apache / truly open models — the open-source tension:** Models like Schnell and Klein 4B are Apache 2.0 — anyone can host them commercially, no agreement required, no lever available. Shifting future open releases to a more restrictive license (Commons Clause, SSPL, BSL) would allow community/self-hosting but prohibit commercial reselling. But it's a visible move away from BFL's open-source identity, which is core to community goodwill. The risk: it hands the "truly open" position to OS models (mostly Chinese) which would fill the vacuum immediately. Needs a deliberate leadership discussion. All levers only work if BFL's direct product is genuinely competitive — and if the marketing engine behind it is too. fal is strong at developer marketing: tutorials, community, integrations, visibility. BFL needs a comparable or better marketing motion to make direct a real alternative, not just a fallback. > 💬 **New input — Slack thread, Feb 18–25, 2026:** Internal discussion flagged an opportunity to require end-customers accessing FLUX via resellers to share contact info with BFL (similar to Anthropic's approach via GCP). Key opportunity: direct marketing to active end-users — cases exist where reseller customers stayed on old models simply because they didn't know new ones had launched. A related structural option: require BFL-issued API keys for all end-customers, even on reseller platforms, for direct usage visibility. Risks: relationship damage if BFL targets customers learned this way, and the ask may implicitly open the door to co-sell expectations. **Suggested next step: include end-customer data sharing and/or BFL-issued API keys as a term in the preferred program obligations package.** --- # Decisions Needed 1. **A or B?** 2. **C****ommit vs. obligations package:** Drop commits in favour of co-marketing, attribution, account transparency, and lead funnel? See Preferred Program section for full framing. 3. **Final discount levels** (Preferred vs. Non-Preferred). 4. **FLUX.3 confidence** — biggest variable in the risk profile of everything above.

2a3c3702-22d5-8073-8f14-e2abd7d4f5cc.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/2a3c370222d580738f14e2abd7d4f5cc as of 2025-11-06T18:21:41.813Z:

{"title":"**Proposal: Recruitment ops hire**"}
</properties>
<content>
**Tl;dr**
We need a Recruitment Coordinator now to prevent recruiting bottlenecks from limiting our growth velocity.
**Current state **
Right now, recruiters are handling
- Sourcing and screening candidates
- Coordinating 10+ interview loops weekly
- Managing candidate communications and experience
I also am
- Building our hiring processes 
- Partnering with hiring managers on role strategy
Additionally, Carolyne is currently scheduling onsite interviews on top of her office management responsibilities, splitting her focus between candidate coordination and her core operational work.
**The risk:** 
As hiring accelerates, coordinator-level work will increasingly crowd out strategic priorities. Interview scheduling delays, dropped candidate communications, and reactive rather than proactive recruiting will directly impact our ability to close critical hires and damage our employer brand in a competitive market.
**Scope for the role:**
- Scheduling all interviews, including onsites
- Handle candidates reimbursements and travel arrangements (domestic and international)
- Manage clear, timely, and professional communication with candidates and hiring managers
- Maintaining ATS data hygiene
- Defining and tracking key recruitment metrics and KPIs + Generating regular and ad-hoc reports and dashboards
- Sending + managing NDAs
- Onboarding handoffs
- Documenting, and improving the end-to-end recruitment process 
- Process optimisation - Identifying bottlenecks and improving efficiency in our hiring funnel
- Assess and recommend tools for faster more efficient hiring
- Coordinate migration to new ATS when we’re ready + Possibly lean into recruiting stuff
This frees me to focus on what actually moves the needle: pipeline building, closing hard-to-fill roles, talent strategy, and competitive positioning.
**Benefits**
- Speed to hire
- Candidate experience
- Data and insights
- Hiring manager satisfaction
</content>
</page>

Where are we spending disproportionate time troubleshooting?** We often prioritize the high-value, strategic deals or partnerships, but this ignores other critical legal work like compliance, privacy, and product counseling that needs to get done. ## 2. **Which critical projects have insufficient attention?** - **Privacy:** We have contractual obligations with investors to become compliance with relevant privacy laws by May 2025. The result would be both contractual violations as well as slow downs in our product releases, such as Playground. - **IP: **We need to formalize our IP program such as trademark applications, etc. We currently are not addressing these issues given the focus on commercial deals. - **Regulatory Compliance: **We should be starting our work to comply with relevant regulations that are being put into place, such as the EU AI Act or certain US state regulations. - Content moderation / AI “Safety” / “Security” build out - AI Product counseling ## **3. What tasks are being done by people too senior for them?** - Small commercial contracts that are volume-based and can be scaled with creating dedicated playbooks. - Line-item updates to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policies. ## 4. **What skills do we lack for upcoming priorities?** We have the requisite skills either in-house or through outside counsel, but we lack bandwidth. Hires will be about scaling. ## **Hiring Needs** - **Immediate:** Commercial Counsel to tackle and scale commercial agreements. - **Next 3-6 months: **Product and compliance counsel to tackle privacy and AI regulations. # Commercial Counsel (Senior) **Seniority:** 7-12 years of experience **Location: ** - UK, US Pacific, Germany **Process:** - 3 interviews. - Case Study - Onsite ## Job Description [Black Forest Labs](https://blackforestlabs.ai/) is a cutting-edge startup pioneering generative image and video models. Our team, which invented Stable Diffusion, Stable Video Diffusion, and [FLUX.1](https://blackforestlabs.ai/announcing-black-forest-labs/), is currently looking for a strong candidate to join us in developing large-scale data pipelines for training frontier models.  As a member of the Legal team, you will be our first commercial-focused Legal team member. You will be focused on negotiating and closing our commercial deals and partnership agreements, and you will be working closely with our sales, business development, finance, and technical teams. This is a unique opportunity to engage directly with the forefront of the legal, commercial, and AI fields. ### **Role: ** In this role, you will: - Be the go-to counsel and partner for several teams focused on commercial transactions and strategic partnerships. - Identify and address commercial, product, regulatory, privacy, and other legal risks and mitigations, in connection with commercial transactions. - Develop strategies for handling legal issues in creative ways and build processes for scaling flexible solutions that address risk. - Become an expert in AI commercial legal matters. ### **Ideal Experiences: ** - Have 7+ years of experience with a mix of in-house and technology-focused law firm commercial roles. - Commercially minded and understand the letter of the law and can approach problems in a practical, principled approach. - Experience scaling legal support for commercial teams. - Build cross-functional relationships and communication styles that resonate with teams to balance risk-taking with responsible development. - Have a strong sense of ownership, are inquisitive and enthusiastic about technology, enjoy being continually challenged, and can demonstrate sound judgment in ambiguous situations and articulate the reasoning for your choices. - Have a Juris Doctorate or equivalent and license or qualification to practice in the US, UK, or Germany. And also educate business side on legal issues. - How do you take back leverage when you’re a small company with a large company at the other side? - Closing Deals - Strategy for closing deals? - Toughest deal to close. - If you have 10 minutes to review an agreement, what is your approach? - Good answer ### **Stuart Taylor** {toggle="true"} Found the role on the career page. 30ac3702-22d5-815f-8325-d59a36f8c96a.text:

</properties>
<content>
<callout icon="💡" color="gray_bg">
	## Executive Summary
	Three hires addressing three distinct gaps, sequenced by urgency. First priority: Senior AE in the US immediately — Sam is already at capacity covering the full US book, and there is no one else hunting the US enterprise pipeline. Second priority: Senior AE in EU/Freiburg to absorb Anthony's accounts as he transitions into the interim Head of GTM role, and a portion of Seb's accounts so Seb can take on hunting again — without this hire the team cannot operate, making it the highest-risk gap. New enterprise revenue has been slow, and unlocking Seb to hunt is strategically important for the company. Third priority: Mid-Level AE in EU/Freiburg to convert inbound leads and \$3.3M in lost mid-market deals across both EU and US. The EU data shows the most immediate mid-market opportunity but this role covers both geos at first.
</callout>
# Overview
This document outlines the sales hiring plan through mid-2026. Three hires — 1 in Q1, 2 in Q2 — each addressing a distinct, data-backed gap.
**Core principle for H1:** The EU and US markets currently require fundamentally different sales motions. EU has strong inbound demand that needs to be converted — the leads and pipeline are there, we just haven't had the people to work them. US requires more hunting and enterprise pipeline development — the market is there but awareness and inbound volume lag behind. As we continue building out the revenue engine and marketing ramps up, these motions should converge over time. But for now, we're hiring for the reality on the ground in each geo.
# Why These Hires, Why Now
This plan follows a conversation between Seb, Dave, and Andi where we pressure-tested where sales hires should sit geographically. Dave's view — that long-term the split should skew more US-heavy — is correct and the data supports it. The US lead gap (16% of all-time leads vs. EU's 34%) likely reflects a brand awareness and demand gen gap rather than a lack of market. We're aligned on that. The nuance is timing: right now, EU has 1,991 unconverted leads and \$3.3M in lost mid-level deals sitting on the table with nobody working them. The US opportunity is real but requires a more outbound-heavy motion with a senior hire until the marketing engine catches up. The plan below hires for both geos simultaneously, with each role running the motion that fits the market today.
The geo analysis across 5,894 leads, pipeline, lost deals, API revenue, and licensing customers paints a clear picture.
On the EU side, we have a conversion problem, not a demand problem. EU accounts for 34% of all leads (1,991) and that share has been accelerating — recent months show EU climbing to 40% of new leads. DACH alone contributes 530+ leads. Not all of these are premium leads — the volume includes a long tail of smaller inquiries — but even accounting for that, the EU lead pool is significantly larger than any other geo and undertouched. There's \$3.3M in lost mid-level deals across 19 accounts that were never properly worked, and EU mid-market API revenue is nearly zero despite 16 direct licensing customers. That's not a lack of market — it's a lack of coverage. The gap between EU lead volume and EU closed revenue is the single clearest hiring signal we have.
On the US side, the picture is different. Leads are steady at \~16% but the enterprise pipeline is enormous — Gamma (\$5.5M), the studio deals Sam is working, and a hunting list of 30+ prospects (Anthropic, Perplexity, Airbnb, [Booking.com](http://Booking.com), Expedia, Notion, Target, Etsy, Marriott, Spotify, etc.) — though it needs to be determined based on the go-to-market motion whether these are sales accounts or partnerships accounts. The mega-deals (Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple) are mainly partnerships-led right now, but as these progress they'll likely need dedicated senior sales support on deal closing and commercial structuring. All 5 current Sr AE accounts are EU-based, which means we're structurally underweight in the US at the enterprise level. Meanwhile Sam has been focused on big studio deals — once those convert, he'll be fully occupied managing them. This isn't a performance issue; it's a capacity and prioritization question driven by how we allocated resources.
Licensing customers are actually balanced across geos (US 17, EU 16, APAC 9), which reinforces that both markets have real commercial traction — they just need different motions to scale.
# Q1: Senior AE — US-based (ASAP)
**Motion: Hunter — Gamma, AI natives, US enterprises**
We need more US presence. Gamma (\$5.5M) needs to transition to this role. The US hunting list is massive and untouched at the enterprise level. Sam is at capacity with studio deals that will keep him occupied once they convert.
Profile: enterprise hunter, comfortable opening doors with AI-native companies and large US enterprises. Strong new-business orientation.
# Q2: Senior AE — EU / Freiburg HQ + Mid-Level AE — EU / Freiburg HQ
These two hires run in parallel — they address different segments but both solve critical EU coverage gaps.
## Senior AE — EU / Freiburg HQ
**Motion: Hybrid — account absorption + active hunting**
This hire unlocks capacity for both Seb and Anthony and solves the EU Sr AE coverage gap.
**What they absorb:**
Anthony's current sales accounts transfer to this person as he moves into the interim Head of GTM role. A portion of Seb's accounts transfer too — freeing Seb to focus on hunting and org-building rather than farming an existing book. This person becomes the EU account owner for a core set of existing customers while also actively developing new pipeline.
**Why hybrid matters:**
A pure farmer would leave a hunting gap in EU. A pure hunter couldn't absorb the account complexity we're handing over. The right profile is someone who's genuinely comfortable doing both — managing and expanding existing relationships while also opening new doors in the EU market. This is a harder profile to find but it's the right one for where we are.
Profile: enterprise hybrid — relationship-driven enough to own and expand complex accounts, commercially hungry enough to hunt new logos. Technical buyer fluency essential. DACH/EU market familiarity strongly preferred. Freiburg-based for HQ proximity.
## Mid-Level AE — EU / Freiburg HQ
**Motion: Inbound conversion — we have demand here and need this person ASAP!**
Inbound-led, data-driven motion. 1,991 leads to convert, \$3.3M in lost mid-level deals to re-engage. Can stretch to cover Korea/Japan mornings (3 Korean license customers already: D2/Naver, Verda, SNOW).
The gap between EU lead volume (34%) and EU closed revenue is exactly what this role fixes. We need to kick off the search in Q1 so the person can start as early in Q2 as possible.
Profile: data-driven inbound converter, farmer-leaning. DACH market knowledge is a plus.
# Next Steps
Align with overall company hiring goals for Q2.
</content>
</page>

29ac3702-22d5-8095-bbaf-e4f28ae9c63d.title: Parental Policy
29ac3702-22d5-8095-bbaf-e4f28ae9c63d.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/29ac370222d58095bbafe4f28ae9c63d as of 2026-02-13T14:51:18.340Z: {"title":"Parental Policy"} At Black Forest Labs we believe that strong parental policies are essential to being a workplace where talented people can thrive. We want to support all parents in balancing the demands of work and family, because that support is critical for long-term wellbeing, performance, and retention. At the same time, we recognise that enhanced maternity leave plays a unique role. In practice, it is most often women who require longer leave following childbirth, and it is women who frequently weigh maternity benefits when deciding where to build their careers. If we want to be a company where women choose to work and stay then we need to provide a package that demonstrates real support at this important stage of life. We operate in a highly competitive, high-performance market and enhanced parental benefits are a way to stand out. They are not just “nice to have” or an afterthought, but a differentiator that signals our ambition to be innovative and people-first. We want to strike the right balance which means generous enough to make a difference but sustainable for us as a growing company. We want BFL to be a place where people feel supported in their careers and in their lives. That means offering enhanced leave that shows we understand the realities of parenthood for both parents and especially the importance of making women feel confident that they can both grow their families and their careers here. As is common with benefits, statutory allowances vary greatly across countries. With this plan our aim is to combine the statutory with a company policy to ensure a level of harmonisation. This policy is intended to sit alongside the statutory benefits available in your country and act as a top-up where applicable. It is not a legal document, so your employment contract will always take precedence. In countries where statutory benefits are more generous than those outlined here, the statutory benefits will apply. ## Policies
**Maternity/Birthing Parent Leave & Benefits** - You are entitled to 16 weeks of fully paid birthing parent/maternity leave (Enhanced Maternity Pay) and 8 further weeks at 50% pay. This is from the start of maternity leave. - If statutory maternity leave is more generous than the company’s enhanced leave, your entitlement will default to the statutory scheme in your particular country. - You will continue to receive statutory maternity protections, including the continuation of your benefits and accrual of annual leave during this period - If you have been with the company for less than 12 months by the time your baby is born, you are still eligible for the BFL enhanced maternity leave, but your pay may be prorated based on your length of service. - Our maternity leave policy applies equally in cases of adoption, so you’ll receive the same support and benefits
**Paternity/****Non-Birthing Parent Leave** - You are entitled to 4 weeks of paid leave immediately following the birth of your child - You also have an additional 4 weeks of paid leave that you can take in one block at any time during the first 12 months after birth - If statutory leave is more generous than the company’s enhanced leave, your entitlement will default to the statutory scheme. The more generous version will prevail. - Certain countries such as Germany have more generous longer term parental leave allowances that stretch over 3 years which you of course have the right to if you are based in Germany. - You will need to agree the timing of the additional 4 weeks leave with your manager in advance. If you do not use it within 12 months, the entitlement will expire. - If you have been with the company for less than 12 months at the time of the baby’s birth, you are entitled to the 4 weeks at birth only. - Our paternity/non-birthing leave policy applies equally in cases of adoption, so you’ll receive the same support and benefits
**Parental Support** Support for parents before birth, during parental leave and after returning to work are very different depending on the country you are in. As with our overall benefits approach we want to balance local statutory support with our commitment to equity, ensuring all team members have access to meaningful support, regardless of geography.
**Baby bonus**
We will pay all parents a baby bonus, which will be paid the month before your baby is due (and if your baby arrives early, it will be included in the next available payroll). This money is for you to spend however you see fit. To receive the baby bonus as a non-birthing parent, your partner must become pregnant after you’ve started employment with BFL. If you are the birthing parent, you’ll be eligible regardless of when your pregnancy begins. > Due to different taxes this amount will be different in different regions/countries. Directional amounts are below but speak to the People team to confirm. Similarly if your country isn’t listed speak to us. - EUR - €11,500 (currently Germany, EU countries) - US - \$10,000 - UK - £11,500 - Canada - CAD\$10,000 - Israel - ILS15,000
**Childcare support** Childcare arrangements and statutory support vary significantly from country to country. Some countries have very strong statutory childcare systems whereas some have very limited. We’ve shaped our approach to reflect that. - #BFL will contribute 30% of your monthly childcare cost, up to a maximum cap per month. This benefit is based on your actual childcare expenses. Only the eligible 30% can be reimbursed; higher amounts cannot be expensed. - The cap is different per country given the different cost levels. Please see below for directional amounts. - Please note that childcare support is taxable in most countries. - The support is for up to your child is 18 months old. - To benefit you need to be a full time employee. - Our childcare support is for when you have returned to work not whilst you are on parental leave. > **Childcare cap
**We’ve shaped the cap to reflect the varying support for childcare in different countries. Some countries have very strong statutory childcare systems whereas some have very limited.
🇩🇪 Germany - BFL will contribute 30% of your monthly childcare cost up to €200 per month
🇺🇸 US - BFL will contribute 30% of your monthly childcare cost up to \$900 per month
🇬🇧 UK - BFL will contribute 30% of your monthly childcare cost up to £700 per month
🇨🇦 Canada - BFL will contribute 30% of your monthly childcare cost up to CAD500 per month
🌍 All other countries - BFL will contribute 30% of your monthly childcare cost up to €300 per month
**Pregnancy Loss (miscarriage or stillbirth) **
**Maternity/Birthing parent** - We understand that the loss of a baby at any stage of pregnancy is deeply painful, and we are committed to supporting you with compassion and care. - Before 20 weeks of pregnancy: You will be entitled to up to 2 weeks of paid compassionate leave, with flexibility to take additional time as needed through sickness or other leave policies. - After 20 weeks of pregnancy (including stillbirth): You will be entitled to up to 5 weeks of paid compassionate leave, with flexibility to take additional time as needed. We hope this will ensure you have the time and space you need to grieve and recover. - We encourage you to take the time that feels right for you and to reach out to the HR team and/or your Lead so we can support you in whatever way is most helpful. All requests will be handled sensitively and confidentially. - Please note that in some countries, statutory leave for pregnancy loss may be more generous than outlined above. If you’re unsure, refer to your employment contract or reach out to the People team.
**Paternity/Non-Birthing Parent** - The loss of a baby is naturally also deeply painful for the father/non-birthing parent and we are committed to supporting you through that time. - Before 20 weeks of pregnancy: You will be entitled to one week of paid compassionate leave - After 20 weeks of pregnancy (including stillbirth): You will be entitled to up to 3 weeks of paid compassionate leave, with flexibility to take additional time as needed. We hope this will ensure you have the time and space you need to grieve and support your partner. - We encourage you to take the time that feels right for you and to reach out to the People team and/or your Lead so we can support you in whatever way is most helpful. All requests will be handled sensitively and confidentially.
## Processes
**Ahead of Maternity/Birthing parent leave** - We are happy to support you at any stage of your pregnancy so feel free to tell us when you are comfortable to do so. However there are country specific rules around this which need to be adhered to in order for us to be able to process your leave and so we ask that you adhere to those. You will find these on the separate government websites or we can help you confidentially as well. - We understand that it’s difficult to plan and that things can change quickly. However work with your Lead and HR and prep a handover as soon as possible so that if things happen quickly everyone is ready to go. This also includes making sure that documentation is updated and saved where colleagues can access it. - You can of course attend appointments for antenatal care and any other medical appointments. This is not different from our standard practice. As always, keep your manager informed of when you will need to be away. - Two months prior to expected birth, you will be under no obligation to travel or to go regularly to one of our offices. Please do what feels right for you.
**During Maternity/Birthing parent leave** - While on maternity/birthing parent leave, you will keep the same contractual benefits set out in your employment contract - You will continue to accrue your statutory holiday entitlement, including (where applicable) bank and/or public holidays - Your equity continues to vest during statutory parental leave. Extended or unpaid leave will be reviewed case by case. If you have questions, please speak to us in the People team. - If your holiday year ends during your maternity/birthing parent leave, please make sure you take your full year’s statutory entitlement before your leave begins - If you have a contractual performance/target-based bonus, the bonus may be prorated to reflect time actively worked during the relevant bonus period in line with local legal requirements. - You will remain bound by all your terms and conditions, including confidentiality, and are expected to continue following company policies and procedures - We will aim not to contact you unnecessarily during your maternity/birthing parent leave. However, we will keep you informed on company news and happenings and invite you to offsites and any other socials. There is of course no obligation for you to attend. - We will agree ahead of your maternity/birthing parent leave which method of comms is best for you.
**Coming back from Maternity/Birthing parent leave** - If you return to work before or at the end of your statutory leave (country specific), you return to the same job in which you were employed before and on the same terms. - We encourage you to talk to your manager about your return-to-work plans, including any flexible arrangements you may need. Please do this as early as you can, but no later than 8 weeks before your planned return date. - We appreciate that even if you’re coming back to work, your parental duties remain the same. Please chat to the People team, your manager and your team about how you would need to structure your day to allow for nursery pick up, bath and bedtime etc. There will be some flexibility needed from both sides but we want to make sure that you feel supported to do both responsibilities to the best of your ability.
** ** **Additional notes** - Your parental leave will work together with the statutory schemes in your country. It's designed to top up, not replace, what you’re already entitled to. - Please note that the duration of job-protected parental leave differs across countries. Where the statutory period of job protection is shorter than the enhanced leave provided by BFL, the BFL enhanced leave will apply (for example, 12 weeks of protected leave in the US versus a longer enhanced period at BFL). Where the statutory period is longer than the enhanced leave, the statutory period will prevail (for example, 12 months of protected leave in the UK). - The company will top up statutory leave so that you receive 100% of your salary during the enhanced period. This is from the start of the maternity leave. - All parental leave must be taken within 12 months of your child’s birth or arrival through adoption (unless the statutory time period is different). - Your benefits, such as health insurance, will continue as if you were actively working. > We will review the policy annually and reserve the right to make changes to this policy when necessary.
