343c3702-22d5-810d-8c59-ce8c35041700.title: Whistleblowing Policy
343c3702-22d5-810d-8c59-ce8c35041700.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/343c370222d5810d8c59ce8c35041700 as of 2026-04-15T13:40:51.326Z: {"title":"Whistleblowing Policy"} **Version:** 1.0 \| **Effective Date:** April 2026 \| **Owner:** Kaylee Davies, Head of People \| **Review Cycle:** Annual --- # 1. Purpose & Scope This policy sets out the company's commitment to creating an environment where employees, contractors, and workers feel safe raising genuine concerns about wrongdoing or unethical conduct. It applies to all individuals working for or with the company, regardless of the jurisdiction in which they are based. This policy is intended to comply with applicable whistleblowing legislation across all our operating jurisdictions. Where local law provides greater protections than this policy, local law takes precedence. --- # 2. What is a Whistleblower? A whistleblower is a person who discloses information about actual or suspected wrongdoing within or connected to the company. Whistleblowers play a critical role in upholding the legal and ethical standards that underpin a healthy business. Raising a concern in good faith is always encouraged, even if the concern later turns out to be unsubstantiated. Whistleblowers are entitled to legal protections under applicable local law, provided their disclosure is made in good faith and meets the relevant legal criteria in their jurisdiction. --- # 3. Applicable Legal Framework This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and workers regardless of the country in which they are based. Where local whistleblowing legislation provides rights or protections that go beyond this policy, those local laws take precedence and will be respected in full. Many jurisdictions in which we operate have enacted specific laws protecting individuals who report wrongdoing. While this policy does not enumerate every applicable statute - these vary by country and are subject to change - the company is committed to meeting or exceeding the minimum standards required by law in every jurisdiction where we employ people. If you are unsure of your rights under local law, you are encouraged to contact the People team or seek independent advice. The company will not penalise any employee for exercising rights granted to them under applicable local legislation. --- # 4. What Can Be Reported? This policy covers concerns about conduct that is, or that you reasonably believe to be: - Dishonest, fraudulent, or corrupt conduct, including bribery or financial misappropriation - Illegal, including theft, violence or threatened violence, drug use or dealing, or criminal damage to property - A breach of legal or regulatory obligations, including data protection, health and safety, or financial regulations - Unethical conduct, including any material breach of the Company's Code of Conduct or other internal policies - Grossly negligent conduct that endangers individuals, assets, or the company's reputation - Potentially damaging to the company, its employees, clients, or third parties - Misconduct or an improper state of affairs by a director, officer, or employee - A danger - or potential danger - to the public, to national security, or to financial systems - Harassment, discrimination, victimisation, or bullying - Unauthorised disclosure or misuse of confidential information, intellectual property, or trade secrets - A cover-up of any of the above - Solicitation to do any of the above --- # 5. What This Policy Does Not Cover This policy is not intended to replace or substitute other People processes. The following matters should be raised through alternative channels: - **Personal grievances** — disputes over pay, working conditions, or personal treatment → use the company's relevant procedure - **Performance concerns about a colleague** → speak to your line manager or People & Talent - **General feedback or suggestions** about company direction → raise through normal management channels If you are unsure whether your concern falls under this policy, please contact the People team for guidance. --- # 6. How to Make a Disclosure ## Internal Reporting Channels You are encouraged to use an internal reporting channel in the first instance. The following individuals are designated to receive whistleblowing disclosures:
Role Contact
Primary — Head of People & Talent Kaylee Davies
Secondary — General Counsel Adam Chen
If your concern relates to either of the above individuals, or if you do not feel comfortable raising it with them, you should use an external reporting channel (see below). ## Anonymous Reporting You may make a disclosure anonymously via the company's [anonymous reporting form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfziaHzsUt0hC0QRRUSCs7H3PXXsxU29IpYLMJMEywBr00xmQ/viewform?usp=preview). Anonymous reports are taken seriously and will be investigated where possible. However, anonymous reports may limit our ability to investigate fully, seek further information, or provide you with feedback. We therefore encourage you, where possible, to allow us to know your identity in confidence. ## External Reporting Channels In many jurisdictions, you have the right to report concerns directly to an external regulatory or governmental body. You do not need to exhaust internal channels first if you reasonably believe internal reporting would be ineffective or lead to retaliation. The relevant external body will depend on your country of employment and the nature of your concern. The People team can help identify the appropriate body, or you may seek independent advice. --- # 7. Confidentiality All disclosures will be treated with the highest possible level of confidentiality consistent with conducting a proper investigation. The identity of the person making a disclosure will not be shared without their prior consent, unless the company is legally required to do so. If it becomes necessary to reveal your identity in order to proceed with an investigation, we will discuss this with you first and explain the reasons. We will consider your views before making any decision to proceed. Third parties engaged to assist with an investigation - such as external legal counsel - will be subject to equivalent confidentiality obligations. --- # 8. Protection from Retaliation The company strictly prohibits any form of retaliation against any person who makes a disclosure in good faith under this policy. This includes: - Dismissal, redundancy, or any adverse change to terms of employment - Demotion, performance management, or disciplinary action taken in connection with a disclosure - Harassment, victimisation, or exclusion - Threats or other detrimental treatment Any employee found to have subjected a whistleblower to retaliation will face disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal. Retaliation may also give rise to legal liability under applicable employment law in all jurisdictions where we operate. --- # 9. Good Faith Reporting This policy applies to concerns raised honestly and in good faith, even if those concerns later prove to be unfounded. It does not protect individuals who knowingly make false or malicious allegations. Making a deliberately false allegation may itself constitute a disciplinary offence. --- # 10. Investigation Process Upon receipt of a disclosure, the company will: 1. Acknowledge receipt (where the reporter is not anonymous) within **5 business days** 2. Assess the disclosure and determine an appropriate course of action 3. Appoint an appropriately senior and independent individual to lead the investigation 4. Conduct a fair, thorough, and timely investigation 5. Provide the disclosing party with feedback on the outcome, to the extent permitted by confidentiality obligations and applicable law Timelines for feedback may be subject to minimum requirements under local law. The company will comply with any such requirements applicable in the reporter's jurisdiction. --- # 11. Record Keeping The company will maintain a confidential log of all disclosures made under this policy, in compliance with applicable data protection legislation including the GDPR and equivalent local laws. Records will be retained only for as long as necessary and in accordance with the company's data retention policy. --- # 12. Policy Review This policy will be reviewed annually by the People team, or sooner in response to significant changes in applicable law or company operations. Any material changes will be communicated to all employees. --- # 13. Questions & Further Guidance If you have any questions about this policy, or would like to discuss a potential concern in confidence before making a formal disclosure, please contact:
Role Contact
Head of People & Talent Kaylee Davies
General Counsel Adam Chen

This policy covers concerns about conduct that is, or that you reasonably believe to be: - Dishonest, fraudulent, or corrupt conduct, including bribery or financial misappropriation - Illegal, including theft, violence or threatened violence, drug use or dealing, or criminal damage to property - A breach of legal or regulatory obligations, including data protection, health and safety, or financial regulations - Unethical conduct, including any material breach of the Company's Code of Conduct or other internal policies - Grossly negligent conduct that endangers individuals, assets, or the company's reputation - Potentially damaging to the company, its employees, clients, or third parties - Misconduct or an improper state of affairs by a director, officer, or employee - A danger - or potential danger - to the public, to national security, or to financial systems - Harassment, discrimination, victimisation, or bullying - Unauthorised disclosure or misuse of confidential information, intellectual property, or trade secrets - A cover-up of any of the above - Solicitation to do any of the above --- # 5. What This Policy Does Not Cover This policy is not intended to replace or substitute other People processes. The following matters should be raised through alternative channels: - **Personal grievances** — disputes over pay, working conditions, or personal treatment → use the company's relevant procedure - **Performance concerns about a colleague** → speak to your line manager or People & Talent - **General feedback or suggestions** about company direction → raise through normal management channels If you are unsure whether your concern falls under this policy, please contact the People team for guidance. --- # 6. How to Make a Disclosure ## Internal Reporting Channels You are encouraged to use an internal reporting channel in the first instance. The following individuals are designated to receive whistleblowing disclosures:
Role Contact
Primary — Head of People & Talent Kaylee Davies
Secondary — General Counsel Adam Chen
If your concern relates to either of the above individuals, or if you do not feel comfortable raising it with them, you should use an external reporting channel (see below). ## Anonymous Reporting You may make a disclosure anonymously via the company's [anonymous reporting form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfziaHzsUt0hC0QRRUSCs7H3PXXsxU29IpYLMJMEywBr00xmQ/viewform?usp=preview). Anonymous reports are taken seriously and will be investigated where possible. However, anonymous reports may limit our ability to investigate fully, seek further information, or provide you with feedback. We therefore encourage you, where possible, to allow us to know your identity in confidence. ## External Reporting Channels In many jurisdictions, you have the right to report concerns directly to an external regulatory or governmental body. You do not need to exhaust internal channels first if you reasonably believe internal reporting would be ineffective or lead to retaliation. The relevant external body will depend on your country of employment and the nature of your concern. The People team can help identify the appropriate body, or you may seek independent advice. --- # 7. Confidentiality All disclosures will be treated with the highest possible level of confidentiality consistent with conducting a proper investigation. The identity of the person making a disclosure will not be shared without their prior consent, unless the company is legally required to do so. If it becomes necessary to reveal your identity in order to proceed with an investigation, we will discuss this with you first and explain the reasons. We will consider your views before making any decision to proceed. Third parties engaged to assist with an investigation - such as external legal counsel - will be subject to equivalent confidentiality obligations. --- # 8. Protection from Retaliation The company strictly prohibits any form of retaliation against any person who makes a disclosure in good faith under this policy. This includes: - Dismissal, redundancy, or any adverse change to terms of employment - Demotion, performance management, or disciplinary action taken in connection with a disclosure - Harassment, victimisation, or exclusion - Threats or other detrimental treatment Any employee found to have subjected a whistleblower to retaliation will face disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal. Retaliation may also give rise to legal liability under applicable employment law in all jurisdictions where we operate. --- # 9. Good Faith Reporting This policy applies to concerns raised honestly and in good faith, even if those concerns later prove to be unfounded. It does not protect individuals who knowingly make false or malicious allegations. Making a deliberately false allegation may itself constitute a disciplinary offence. --- # 10. Investigation Process Upon receipt of a disclosure, the company will: 1. Acknowledge receipt (where the reporter is not anonymous) within **5 business days** 2. Assess the disclosure and determine an appropriate course of action 3. Appoint an appropriately senior and independent individual to lead the investigation 4. Conduct a fair, thorough, and timely investigation 5. Provide the disclosing party with feedback on the outcome, to the extent permitted by confidentiality obligations and applicable law Timelines for feedback may be subject to minimum requirements under local law. The company will comply with any such requirements applicable in the reporter's jurisdiction. --- # 11. Record Keeping The company will maintain a confidential log of all disclosures made under this policy, in compliance with applicable data protection legislation including the GDPR and equivalent local laws. Records will be retained only for as long as necessary and in accordance with the company's data retention policy. --- # 12. Policy Review This policy will be reviewed annually by the People team, or sooner in response to significant changes in applicable law or company operations. Any material changes will be communicated to all employees. --- # 13. Questions & Further Guidance If you have any questions about this policy, or would like to discuss a potential concern in confidence before making a formal disclosure, please contact:
Role Contact
Head of People & Talent Kaylee Davies
General Counsel Adam Chen

It kicks in when the underlying policy limits are exhausted, helping protect against large claims or lawsuits. **Foreign Liability Policy** extends your coverage beyond U.S. borders. It typically includes: - **General Liability for International Operations**: Protects against third-party claims for bodily injury or property damage occurring outside the U.S. - **Foreign Voluntary Workers’ Compensation**: Provides coverage for employees injured while traveling abroad for work. - **Auto & Property Coverage**: Covers rented or owned vehicles and business equipment overseas. - **Kidnap & Ransom Protection** (if included): Offers assistance in case of security threats abroad.

22dc3702-22d5-80d7-893b-e01f78a7c080.title: BFL Internal Privacy Policy
22dc3702-22d5-80d7-893b-e01f78a7c080.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/22dc370222d580d7893be01f78a7c080 as of 2025-08-01T09:51:03.483Z: {"title":"BFL Internal Privacy Policy"} **BLUF:** This Internal Privacy Policy covers how BFL employees should handle all Personal Data, whether its the Personal Data of our employees, customers, and any other individuals. # **1. Overview** Maintaining the confidentiality, privacy and security of Personal Data (as defined below) is important to Black Forest Labs Inc. and its subsidiaries and affiliates (“**we**,” “**our**,” the “**Company**”) and essential to the fulfillment of our obligations under applicable laws. This Internal Privacy Policy (the “**Policy**”) establishes the Company’s internal policy for handling and safeguarding the Personal Data of employees, customers, and any other individuals whose Personal Data is in our possession or under our control. It identifies the principles that shape our approach to data privacy, assigns data protection responsibilities within the Company, and provides guidance on how to fulfill these responsibilities. # **2. Scope** This Policy applies to all employees, contractors, and other representatives (collectively, “**Personnel**”) of the Company and our affiliates. It covers access to and use of Personal Data in all Company systems, offices, locations, data centers and any other facility or database owned or administered by the Company. It may be supplemented by additional policies, procedures, guidelines, and standards. In particular, if local laws impose a higher standard or more specific requirements, the Company shall follow those higher standards or more specific requirements. # **3. Definitions** “**Personal Data**” means any data or information relating to an identified or identifiable individual, such as name, home address, email address, phone number, age, birth date, images and location. To the extent the Company handles Personal Data that is defined under an applicable law using a different term and/or definition, nothing in this Policy is intended to contradict the Company’s obligations under such law. “**Sensitive Personal Data**” means sensitive categories of Personal Data that often require heightened protection, such as government-issued identification numbers, racial or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, religious or philosophical beliefs, political opinions, and health and biometric data, as well as information about children or other vulnerable individuals. “**Process**” means any operation or set of operations performed on Personal Data, whether or not by automated means (e.g., collection, organization, storage, use, disclosure, destruction, etc.). # **4. Roles and Responsibilities** All Personnel play a critical role in ensuring that Personal Data is properly handled. Personnel are responsible for following this Policy and other Company policies related to privacy and data security at all times. The Legal Team is responsible for managing and maintaining all of the Company’s policies related to privacy and the protection of Personal Data, including this Policy. The Legal Team will coordinate with key stakeholders to develop procedures, guidelines, and standards as necessary for purposes of implementing the Policy, and will review and update the Policy at least annually. Other teams in the Company that may play a role in managing and implementing this Policy include teams tackling security, human resources, and finance. Any questions or concerns about this Policy should be directed to the Legal Team. You are responsible for contacting the Legal Team before you start any new project, partnership or any other initiative that involves new uses of Personal Data, and for working with the Legal Team to ensure compliance with applicable laws and this Policy. # **5. Commitment to Privacy Principles** The Fair Information Practice Principles (“**FIPPs**”) are a widely recognized set of privacy principles that are at the heart of many privacy laws around the globe. As defined by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, the FIPPs include: collection limitation, data quality, purpose specification, use limitation, security safeguards, openness, individual participation, and accountability. We are committed to upholding the FIPPs in connection with the collection and other Processing of Personal Data and complying with all applicable privacy laws and notices provided to individuals at or before the time of collection of any Personal Data. We expect Personnel to be aware of and to act at all times in furtherance of this commitment. # **6. Confidentiality and Disclosure** Personnel may only access Personal Data on a need-to-know basis, and such access must be restricted to the minimum access necessary for the performance of such Personnel’s responsibilities. The Legal Team is responsible for establishing and enforcing specific access controls based on the sensitivity of the Personal Data, and all Personnel must comply with such restrictions. Personnel may not disclose any Personal Data to a third party outside of the Company without first undertaking the appropriate review with the Legal Team to conduct due diligence on such third party and determine what steps should be taken to ensure the protection of such Personal Data, including whether specific contractual commitments or other safeguards are required. Such a review is required both for disclosures of Personal Data to third party service providers, as well as to any external parties that will use Personal Data for their own business purposes. The Legal Team is responsible for developing the review process and working with relevant groups within the Company in order to establish appropriate controls and procedures to trigger such a review. The Company may be required to disclose Personal Data to law enforcement, regulators, or other government authorities, including data protection authorities, upon receiving a valid request. When the Company receives a request from a government authority for Personal Data, the request must be promptly sent to the Legal Team. The Legal Team will review the request and coordinate and manage the response to the government authority. # **7. Use of Personal Data** Under applicable privacy laws and the Company’s contractual obligations, when the Company Processes the Personal Data of a customer / developer or their end-users (i.e., input or output), the Company generally cannot Process this Personal Data for purposes other than providing the Company’s services. To the extent there is any uncertainty as to whether Processing is for the purposes of providing the Company’s services, Personnel should contact the Legal Team for further guidance. When the Company is otherwise Processing Personal Data (e.g., in relation to Personnel or website visitors), the Company typically must provide individuals with a privacy notice at or before the time of collecting their Personal Data. Personnel may only use Personal Data for specific business purposes, consistent with any applicable privacy notice, privacy laws, and contractual obligations. Personnel are only permitted to Process Personal Data for the purpose for which it was collected, unless approval is obtained from the Legal Team to Process the Personal Data for secondary purpose. To ascertain whether Processing is compatible with the purposes for which the Personal Data was collected, Personnel must take into account the reasonable expectations of the relevant individual, the types of Personal Data Processed, and the impact of the intended further Processing on the relevant individual. To the extent there is any uncertainty as to whether Processing may be deemed a secondary purpose, Personnel should contact the Legal Team for further guidance. Unless the Legal Team approves otherwise (where permitted under applicable law), Sensitive Personal Data can only be collected and otherwise Processed after the Company has provided appropriate notice to the relevant individual and obtained explicit consent. Personnel must strictly limit the use of Sensitive Personal Data to the purposes for which it was collected and may not Process it for a secondary purpose without obtaining explicit consent from the relevant individual. Sensitive Personal Data must also be subject to appropriately enhanced policies, access controls, and security measures. To the extent Personal Data (including Sensitive Personal Data) will transfer from one country to another country, such cross-border transfer must comply with applicable privacy laws. The Company may be required to enter into specific contractual provisions or implement other data transfers mechanisms and safeguards to facilitate the international transfer of Personal Data, and the Legal Team must be consulted prior to making any such transfer. Any Processing of Personal Data (including Sensitive Personal Data) that poses a heightened risk to the rights and/or freedoms of individuals (including privacy rights)—taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the Processing—necessitates the completion of a data protection impact assessment, a process which shall be overseen by the Legal Team. # **8. Marketing** All Company marketing efforts must comply with applicable laws related to direct marketing, including any requirements to obtain consent from individuals prior to sending marketing communications and/or provide individuals with the opportunity to opt out of such marketing communications. If we receive an opt-out request, the Company must process opt-out requests without undue delay and at least within ten business days of receipt.Please contact the Legal Team for further information. # **9. Rights Requests** In some jurisdictions, individuals have certain rights with respect to their Personal Data under applicable privacy laws—for example, the rights to access, correct, and delete their information. The Company may be required by law to have in place procedures for receiving and responding to requests to exercise such rights (“**Rights Requests**”). Note that Rights Requests may go beyond the FIPP’s “Individual Participation” principle (see Section V above), and we are required to comply with all valid Rights Requests under applicable law. All Rights Requests received from consumers, customers, or other individuals outside of the Company must be immediately forwarded to the Legal Team. Rights Requests submitted by Personnel may be handled by the Human Resources Team where appropriate—for example, routine requests to access or correct Personal Data in the ordinary course of business. Any Rights Requests that the Human Resources Team is unable to fulfil or that go beyond routine requests must be submitted to the Legal Team. Prior to responding to any Rights Request, the Legal Team is responsible for completing any required verification procedures (depending on the type of request and the sensitivity of the Personal Data involved), assessing the Company’s legal obligations under applicable privacy laws, and considering whether any exceptions under such laws apply. The Company must respond to Rights Requests within the timeframe required under applicable privacy laws and must maintain internal records of the Rights Requests received and how the Company responded. # **10. Data security** The Company has implemented and maintains reasonable technical, physical, and organizational measures designed to protect Personal Data from accidental, unlawful or unauthorized access, use, loss, disclosure, alteration, destruction, or other Processing. For a description of such measures, contact the Legal Team. Personnel are responsible for reviewing such policies and understanding the role they play in maintaining the security of Personal Data. To better understand your role in protecting Personal Data, please contact the Legal Team. # **11. Security Incidents** The Company must notify data breaches to relevant authorities and/or impacted individuals as required by applicable law, and may otherwise voluntarily notify if the Company considers it appropriate to do so. The Infrastructure and Legal Teams are responsible for establishing appropriating data breach notification procedures. Any security incident, data breach, or other unauthorized, unlawful, or accidental access, use, loss, disclosure, alteration, destruction, or other Processing of Personal Data must be immediately reported to the Legal Team by emailing [legal@blackforestlabs.ai](mailto:legal@blackforestlabs.ai). Personnel who report suspected or known security events that may jeopardize the confidentiality, integrity, privacy or availability of Personal Data shall not be retaliated against, intimidated or otherwise prevented from making such a report.  For more information on security incidents and mandatory reporting, please reach out to the Legal Team. # **12. Training** All Personnel are required to complete relevant privacy and data security awareness training. The privacy and data security awareness training provided to Personnel during the onboarding process shall: - cover generally accepted privacy and data security practices aimed at reducing the risk of Personal Data being mishandled or unprotected; and - address Company policies, procedures, guidelines, and standards related to privacy and data security. All Personnel are required to retake security awareness training and re-acknowledge their understanding of the Company’s policies related to privacy and data security at least once every calendar year or when otherwise required by the Company. The Legal Team may provide both formal and informal additional privacy and data security awareness training on a periodic basis throughout the year. Any Personnel who violate any of the Company’s policies related to privacy or data security or undertakes an action that demonstrates a lack of privacy and data security awareness may be required to take additional privacy and data security awareness training. # **13. Consequences of violating Policy** Any violation of this Policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and prosecution. The Company reserves the right to notify appropriate law enforcement and/or governmental authorities of any unlawful activity and cooperate in any investigation of such activity. ### **Revision History**
**Date** **Event** **Approval**
11 July 2025 Initial approval and publication of Policy Adam Chen, Legal

It covers access to and use of Personal Data in all Company systems, offices, locations, data centers and any other facility or database owned or administered by the Company. It may be supplemented by additional policies, procedures, guidelines, and standards. In particular, if local laws impose a higher standard or more specific requirements, the Company shall follow those higher standards or more specific requirements. # **3. Definitions** “**Personal Data**” means any data or information relating to an identified or identifiable individual, such as name, home address, email address, phone number, age, birth date, images and location. To the extent the Company handles Personal Data that is defined under an applicable law using a different term and/or definition, nothing in this Policy is intended to contradict the Company’s obligations under such law. “**Sensitive Personal Data**” means sensitive categories of Personal Data that often require heightened protection, such as government-issued identification numbers, racial or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, religious or philosophical beliefs, political opinions, and health and biometric data, as well as information about children or other vulnerable individuals. “**Process**” means any operation or set of operations performed on Personal Data, whether or not by automated means (e.g., collection, organization, storage, use, disclosure, destruction, etc.). # **4. Roles and Responsibilities** All Personnel play a critical role in ensuring that Personal Data is properly handled. Personnel are responsible for following this Policy and other Company policies related to privacy and data security at all times. The Legal Team is responsible for managing and maintaining all of the Company’s policies related to privacy and the protection of Personal Data, including this Policy. The Legal Team will coordinate with key stakeholders to develop procedures, guidelines, and standards as necessary for purposes of implementing the Policy, and will review and update the Policy at least annually. Other teams in the Company that may play a role in managing and implementing this Policy include teams tackling security, human resources, and finance. Any questions or concerns about this Policy should be directed to the Legal Team. You are responsible for contacting the Legal Team before you start any new project, partnership or any other initiative that involves new uses of Personal Data, and for working with the Legal Team to ensure compliance with applicable laws and this Policy. # **5. Commitment to Privacy Principles** The Fair Information Practice Principles (“**FIPPs**”) are a widely recognized set of privacy principles that are at the heart of many privacy laws around the globe. As defined by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, the FIPPs include: collection limitation, data quality, purpose specification, use limitation, security safeguards, openness, individual participation, and accountability. We are committed to upholding the FIPPs in connection with the collection and other Processing of Personal Data and complying with all applicable privacy laws and notices provided to individuals at or before the time of collection of any Personal Data. We expect Personnel to be aware of and to act at all times in furtherance of this commitment. # **6. Confidentiality and Disclosure** Personnel may only access Personal Data on a need-to-know basis, and such access must be restricted to the minimum access necessary for the performance of such Personnel’s responsibilities. The Legal Team is responsible for establishing and enforcing specific access controls based on the sensitivity of the Personal Data, and all Personnel must comply with such restrictions. Personnel may not disclose any Personal Data to a third party outside of the Company without first undertaking the appropriate review with the Legal Team to conduct due diligence on such third party and determine what steps should be taken to ensure the protection of such Personal Data, including whether specific contractual commitments or other safeguards are required. Such a review is required both for disclosures of Personal Data to third party service providers, as well as to any external parties that will use Personal Data for their own business purposes. The Legal Team is responsible for developing the review process and working with relevant groups within the Company in order to establish appropriate controls and procedures to trigger such a review. The Company may be required to disclose Personal Data to law enforcement, regulators, or other government authorities, including data protection authorities, upon receiving a valid request. When the Company receives a request from a government authority for Personal Data, the request must be promptly sent to the Legal Team. The Legal Team will review the request and coordinate and manage the response to the government authority. # **7. Use of Personal Data** Under applicable privacy laws and the Company’s contractual obligations, when the Company Processes the Personal Data of a customer / developer or their end-users (i.e., input or output), the Company generally cannot Process this Personal Data for purposes other than providing the Company’s services. To the extent there is any uncertainty as to whether Processing is for the purposes of providing the Company’s services, Personnel should contact the Legal Team for further guidance. When the Company is otherwise Processing Personal Data (e.g., in relation to Personnel or website visitors), the Company typically must provide individuals with a privacy notice at or before the time of collecting their Personal Data. Personnel may only use Personal Data for specific business purposes, consistent with any applicable privacy notice, privacy laws, and contractual obligations. Personnel are only permitted to Process Personal Data for the purpose for which it was collected, unless approval is obtained from the Legal Team to Process the Personal Data for secondary purpose. To ascertain whether Processing is compatible with the purposes for which the Personal Data was collected, Personnel must take into account the reasonable expectations of the relevant individual, the types of Personal Data Processed, and the impact of the intended further Processing on the relevant individual. To the extent there is any uncertainty as to whether Processing may be deemed a secondary purpose, Personnel should contact the Legal Team for further guidance. Unless the Legal Team approves otherwise (where permitted under applicable law), Sensitive Personal Data can only be collected and otherwise Processed after the Company has provided appropriate notice to the relevant individual and obtained explicit consent. Personnel must strictly limit the use of Sensitive Personal Data to the purposes for which it was collected and may not Process it for a secondary purpose without obtaining explicit consent from the relevant individual. Sensitive Personal Data must also be subject to appropriately enhanced policies, access controls, and security measures. To the extent Personal Data (including Sensitive Personal Data) will transfer from one country to another country, such cross-border transfer must comply with applicable privacy laws. The Company may be required to enter into specific contractual provisions or implement other data transfers mechanisms and safeguards to facilitate the international transfer of Personal Data, and the Legal Team must be consulted prior to making any such transfer. Any Processing of Personal Data (including Sensitive Personal Data) that poses a heightened risk to the rights and/or freedoms of individuals (including privacy rights)—taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the Processing—necessitates the completion of a data protection impact assessment, a process which shall be overseen by the Legal Team. # **8. Marketing** All Company marketing efforts must comply with applicable laws related to direct marketing, including any requirements to obtain consent from individuals prior to sending marketing communications and/or provide individuals with the opportunity to opt out of such marketing communications. If we receive an opt-out request, the Company must process opt-out requests without undue delay and at least within ten business days of receipt.Please contact the Legal Team for further information. # **9. Rights Requests** In some jurisdictions, individuals have certain rights with respect to their Personal Data under applicable privacy laws—for example, the rights to access, correct, and delete their information. The Company may be required by law to have in place procedures for receiving and responding to requests to exercise such rights (“**Rights Requests**”). Note that Rights Requests may go beyond the FIPP’s “Individual Participation” principle (see Section V above), and we are required to comply with all valid Rights Requests under applicable law. All Rights Requests received from consumers, customers, or other individuals outside of the Company must be immediately forwarded to the Legal Team. Rights Requests submitted by Personnel may be handled by the Human Resources Team where appropriate—for example, routine requests to access or correct Personal Data in the ordinary course of business. Any Rights Requests that the Human Resources Team is unable to fulfil or that go beyond routine requests must be submitted to the Legal Team. Prior to responding to any Rights Request, the Legal Team is responsible for completing any required verification procedures (depending on the type of request and the sensitivity of the Personal Data involved), assessing the Company’s legal obligations under applicable privacy laws, and considering whether any exceptions under such laws apply. The Company must respond to Rights Requests within the timeframe required under applicable privacy laws and must maintain internal records of the Rights Requests received and how the Company responded. # **10. Data security** The Company has implemented and maintains reasonable technical, physical, and organizational measures designed to protect Personal Data from accidental, unlawful or unauthorized access, use, loss, disclosure, alteration, destruction, or other Processing. For a description of such measures, contact the Legal Team. Personnel are responsible for reviewing such policies and understanding the role they play in maintaining the security of Personal Data. To better understand your role in protecting Personal Data, please contact the Legal Team. # **11. Security Incidents** The Company must notify data breaches to relevant authorities and/or impacted individuals as required by applicable law, and may otherwise voluntarily notify if the Company considers it appropriate to do so. The Infrastructure and Legal Teams are responsible for establishing appropriating data breach notification procedures. Any security incident, data breach, or other unauthorized, unlawful, or accidental access, use, loss, disclosure, alteration, destruction, or other Processing of Personal Data must be immediately reported to the Legal Team by emailing [legal@blackforestlabs.ai](mailto:legal@blackforestlabs.ai). Personnel who report suspected or known security events that may jeopardize the confidentiality, integrity, privacy or availability of Personal Data shall not be retaliated against, intimidated or otherwise prevented from making such a report.  For more information on security incidents and mandatory reporting, please reach out to the Legal Team. # **12. Training** All Personnel are required to complete relevant privacy and data security awareness training. The privacy and data security awareness training provided to Personnel during the onboarding process shall: - cover generally accepted privacy and data security practices aimed at reducing the risk of Personal Data being mishandled or unprotected; and - address Company policies, procedures, guidelines, and standards related to privacy and data security. All Personnel are required to retake security awareness training and re-acknowledge their understanding of the Company’s policies related to privacy and data security at least once every calendar year or when otherwise required by the Company. The Legal Team may provide both formal and informal additional privacy and data security awareness training on a periodic basis throughout the year. Any Personnel who violate any of the Company’s policies related to privacy or data security or undertakes an action that demonstrates a lack of privacy and data security awareness may be required to take additional privacy and data security awareness training. # **13. Consequences of violating Policy** Any violation of this Policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment and prosecution. The Company reserves the right to notify appropriate law enforcement and/or governmental authorities of any unlawful activity and cooperate in any investigation of such activity. ### **Revision History**

# Guidelines
- Each class is split into 5 levels of severity, from 0 to 4, where 0 means that no harm content of that class exists whatsoever, and 4 being the maximum severity
- Severity classes often build upon each other, so the maximum severity level that applies should be used
	- For example, Sexual Severity Level 1 includes swimwear, while Level 2 includes bikini. “A woman wearing a bikini” fulfills both levels 1 and 2, so it should be labeled level 2
- While I have attempted to be comprehensive, the definitions are not exhaustive lists of all possible content. Content that isn’t clearly defined should be matched to the severity level that best matches, based on the general “vibe” of severity. Common sense is a legitimate way to handle this.
# Definitions
## Sexual
### Severity Level 0
- No sexual content whatsoever
### Severity Level 1
- Swimwear (that is less revealing than underwear), very tight clothing (e.g. latex bodysuits) 
- Kissing
- Slight fetish content (e.g. foot worship)
- Provocative poses or situations
- Text with sexual language and vocabulary
- Underwear not being worn (e.g. hanging bras)
### Severity Level 2
- People wearing only underwear, lingerie, bikinis, or equivalent revealing clothing
- A focus on prominent breasts, cleavage, butts, genital bulges
- Translucent or very revealing clothing
- Passionate kissing or licking
- Displays of general sexual intent
### Severity Level 3
- Nudity showing genitalia, or clothing so transparent that the subject is basically nude
- Cameltoes or penis outlines through clothes
- Genital fluids (urine, breast milk etc.)
- Sexually suggestive oral acts performed on objects (e.g. licking a popsicle held between someone else’s legs)
- Humping, masturbation, and other sexual acts performed while clothed
### Severity Level 4
- All sexual content more severe than level 3
- Sex, direct genital-contact masturbation, sex toy usage
	- Semen, even if described in a roundabout way as long as it is obvious (e.g. “a white gelatinous liquid spread across her breasts”)
- Extreme fetish acts (e.g. scat, piss play)
- Child sexualization, exploitation, abuse or grooming
## Hate
### Severity Level 0
- No hateful content whatsoever
### Severity Level 1
- Negative or hateful sentiment against individuals
- Derogatory depictions of individuals
- Middle fingers
### Severity Level 2
- Negative or hateful sentiments towards protected groups or religions
- Violence against protected groups or religions
- Depictions of slavery
- Moderately offensive derogatory terms and slurs
### Severity Level 3
- Very negative or hateful sentiments towards protected groups or religions
- Depictions of slavery with obvious racist motivation
- Very offensive derogatory terms and slurs
### Severity Level 4
- Nazi, KKK, Confederate, or other politically extreme imagery
- Overt racism, bigotry, discrimination or speech
- Extremely offensive slurs
## Violence
### Severity Level 0
- No violence whatsoever
### Severity Level 1
- Animated, cartoon, or clearly fictional violence or weaponry
- The presence of real weapons (not kitchen knives, chainsaws, or other tools) not being held or used by a human
- Knives being held
- Nonconsensual physical grabbing or restraints
- Minor fist fights
- People in imminent danger
- Depictions of war and battles without visible harm to humans (e.g. in the distance or the aftermath of)
- BDSM and other consensual violence
- Bones, skulls and skeletons
### Severity Level 2
- Real weaponry being brandished or used
- Animated corpses
- Small amounts of blood
- Intense physical fights with threat of major harm
- Depictions of war and battles with visible harm to humans
- Sexual assault
- Physical wounds
- Disturbing imagery
### Severity Level 3
- Real corpses
- Depictions of death or dying
- Moderate to large amounts of blood
- Hangings and nooses
- Grotesque and very disturbing imagery
- Cruel torture
### Severity Level 4
- Terrorists and terrorism
- Animal or child abuse
- Extreme gore and violence
## Self Harm
### Severity Level 0
- No self-harm whatsoever
### Severity Level 1
- Animated alcohol or injectables
- Slight or unlikely (yet possible) intent of self harm
### Severity Level 2
- Emaciated bodies or extreme weight loss, unless clearly involuntary (e.g. prison environments)
- Alcohol, smoking, marijuana
- Abstract or minor self harm
- Casual self harm encouragement
- Moderately likely intent of self harm
- Signs of past self harm
### Severity Level 3
- Gambling
- Non-medical pills and hard drugs
- Nooses
- Clear intent of self harm
- Bulimia
- Severe self harm encouragement
### Severity Level 4
- Major self harm resulting in life-threatening injury
- Suicide and hanging
- Illicit injectables

</content>

27ec3702-22d5-802e-acd7-d29555096d46.title: BFL Narrative
27ec3702-22d5-802e-acd7-d29555096d46.text:
Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://www.notion.so/27ec370222d5802eacd7d29555096d46 as of 2026-02-14T13:20:43.569Z: {"title":"BFL Narrative"} # 1. Our role in the world {toggle="true"} A clear definition of our role in the world, our vision and mission. Mainly for top-level communication when explaining the company. **Vision – What is our impact on the world**

Powering visual intelligence everywhere. **Mission – How we get there (new)


MAIN
**Deeply rooted in foundational research, we continually build state of the art technology **to redefine **the visual understanding of the world.
**Past - What we have done

**Building structure from chaos: Our team pioneered Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX.1 – milestones in the evolution of generative AI – making text to image generation accessible to everyone. **Present - What we are doing

**From imagination to reality:** **We are building powerful, controllable, and composable tools empowering millions of people fulfill their creative potential and enterprises to create, scale, and govern visual content. **Future - Where we are going

**From outputs to actions: Creating multimodal models as the foundational pillar of visual intelligence, across products, platforms, and realities. # 2. How we express it {toggle="true"} **First: **The descriptive expression of our positioning. Used primarily for outward-facing communication (e.g., website, decks).
 **About – A brief copy of who we are and what we do

Option 1:** We’re the leading frontier AI research lab, continuously building the most advanced technology that shapes** **the visual understanding of the world. Our most recent models power a wide range of products – turning imagination into reality with precision, speed, and creative control. Follow us into the new. **About Short - Company one-liner

**Black Forest Labs – The frontier AI research lab for visual intelligence. **About Long – A longer format copy of who we are and what we do (e.g. Website)
** **Vision** We exist to power visual intelligence everywhere. **
Mission** Rooted in foundational research, we continually build state-of-the-art technology that advances how the world is seen and understood. We’re a frontier AI research lab focused on shaping visual understanding – so powerful applications become possible, deployable, and genuinely useful.

Our latest models already power products across industries, turning imagination into reality with precision, speed, and creative control. **
The Journey

Our Past – Where we come from** Our team brought structure to chaos: pioneering **Latent Diffusion**, **Stable Diffusion**, and **FLUX.1**—milestones that made text-to-image generation accessible to millions and set a new standard. **
Our Present – What we’re doing now** From imagination to reality: we’re building powerful, controllable, composable tools. They help people fulfill their creative potential—and help enterprises **create, scale, and govern** visual outputs with confidence and consistency. **
Our Future – Where we’re headed** From outputs to actions: We are creating multimodal models that unify perception, generation, memory, and planning—becoming a foundational pillar of visual intelligence across products, platforms, and realities. Interactions will shift from human-led, AI-assisted to AI-led, human-assisted, with intent as the interface. **
Strong beliefs, weakly held – How we work ** We ship technology, not demos. We bias toward precision, speed, and control, treat governance as a feature, and design for usefulness today and compounding value tomorrow.

We believe foundational research becomes durable infrastructure, platform beats point tool, and small, exceptional teams move the frontier. Above all, we are bound not just by talent, but by relentless curiosity and a hunger for what’s next – because the next decade won’t be won by faster tools alone, but by foundational innovation and the teams that turn it into applied technology.

From our labs in Freiburg and San Francisco, we’re pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Never staying in the now.

**Follow us into the new.** **Second: **The creative translation of our positioning into feeling. It explains what it means to be a research lab, what drives us emotionally, and how we show up in the world—our voice, symbols, and rituals. It turns purpose into story and gives marketing, the website, and decks a coherent tone, so people don’t just understand us—they sense us.
**Brand Manifesto
** We don’t believe in done,
in final or finished. We believe
the only thing that matters
is what’s next. So we keep moving.
Keep making. Keep going. To leave behind what is
and imagine what if. Pulled forward by the new,
we are not here just to stay here. So if you are searching
for the finish line,
you won't find it here.
You won’t find us there. Because we are already off INTO THE NEW **Brand Message

INTO THE NEW.
** It’s a universal truth
Every great leap starts with a step into the unknown. It’s a mindset
We don’t cling to what is, we reach for what could be.
Exploration isn’t a phase. It’s our way forward. It’s a call to action
The next idea won’t come from the past. It waits in the new. **The Narrative’s Cosmos** Theme:
Imagination → Exploration → Transformation Speaks to:
Forward movement, curiosity, research mindset Function:
The invitation towards all to go beyond what's known and seen. A never ending leap toward what’s next. **Audience Talk Tracks** These are time-bound as the company evolves and advances its offering. For example, new products require tailored messages to communicate their advantages, and new technology calls for updated pitches to investors. Please treat them as valid, but limited in time.**

The Communication Approach
**Lead with inspiration. Convince with explanation.
### Customers {toggle="true"} **Who we are talking to:**
Enterprises and creators looking to create visual media with AI. **The goal:**
Own the category and further establish yourself as the recognized leader in generative media AI. **The approach:**
Put the product front and center, communicating features in ways that excite, inspire, and spark curiosity. **Headlines:** - Forget what is. Imagine what if. - Own every pixel. - Create the uncreated. - Don’t iterate the past. Create the future. - Model the new. - Play. Create. Manipulate. - There’s nothing you can’t change. - Grow a world. Out of your mind. - What hasn’t been can now be. - Unleash your Vorstellungskraft. - Reality is a spoon. Bend it. - Grow a world. Out of your mind. - Words change worlds. - How you say it is how you see it. - In the beginning was the word. - From imagination to image. - Nothing that you can’t rewrite. - Context is everything. Control it. - Think it. Type it. See it. ### Talent {toggle="true"} **Who we are talking to:** The current team and top talent open to new opportunities. **The goal:** Attract and retain a diverse group of highly ambitious and skilled people who share our drive and values. **The approach:** We stay true to our roots as researchers, carrying the same drive and curiosity into every part of the company, from product to sales. We welcome those who share this mindset to help shape the future of generative AI with us. - Welcome to the forest. - Not here to stay. - There is no final version. - Searching for researchers. - Let’s push boundaries not just pixels. - Build the features of the future. - Change the world by creating new ones. - Wanted: Frontier Developers (M/W/D) - If you can think it, you can make it.
### PR & Public {toggle="true"} **Who we are talking to:**
Publications that shape industry narratives and public opinion. **The goal:**

**Keep the momentum by continuously demonstrating our ambition as the European category leader building the infrastructure for the next era of media creation.

**Nothing is permanent** We know there’s nothing that can’t be changed for the better and embrace the consistent evolution of ideas. Change is not a challenge, but a constant.

**
**Optimistic** We speak with clarity and optimism, reflecting our belief in progress and a mindset that embraces possibility over permanence.
**Inspiring** We aim to spark curiosity and imagination, expressing ourselves in a way that invites exploration and encourages experimentation with the tools we create.
**Ambitious** We speak boldly, with the conviction of knowing who we are, and the drive to redefine what’s believed to be possible.

**From outputs to actions: Creating multimodal models as the foundational pillar of visual intelligence, across products, platforms, and realities. # 2. **Black Forest Labs – The frontier AI research lab for visual intelligence. **About Long – A longer format copy of who we are and what we do (e.g. Website)
** **Vision** We exist to power visual intelligence everywhere. **
Mission** Rooted in foundational research, we continually build state-of-the-art technology that advances how the world is seen and understood. We’re a frontier AI research lab focused on shaping visual understanding – so powerful applications become possible, deployable, and genuinely useful.

Our latest models already power products across industries, turning imagination into reality with precision, speed, and creative control. **
The Journey

Our Past – Where we come from** Our team brought structure to chaos: pioneering **Latent Diffusion**, **Stable Diffusion**, and **FLUX.1**—milestones that made text-to-image generation accessible to millions and set a new standard. **
Our Present – What we’re doing now** From imagination to reality: we’re building powerful, controllable, composable tools. They help people fulfill their creative potential—and help enterprises **create, scale, and govern** visual outputs with confidence and consistency. **
Our Future – Where we’re headed** From outputs to actions: We are creating multimodal models that unify perception, generation, memory, and planning—becoming a foundational pillar of visual intelligence across products, platforms, and realities. Interactions will shift from human-led, AI-assisted to AI-led, human-assisted, with intent as the interface. **
Strong beliefs, weakly held – How we work ** We ship technology, not demos. We bias toward precision, speed, and control, treat governance as a feature, and design for usefulness today and compounding value tomorrow.

We believe foundational research becomes durable infrastructure, platform beats point tool, and small, exceptional teams move the frontier. Above all, we are bound not just by talent, but by relentless curiosity and a hunger for what’s next – because the next decade won’t be won by faster tools alone, but by foundational innovation and the teams that turn it into applied technology.

From our labs in Freiburg and San Francisco, we’re pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Never staying in the now.

**Follow us into the new.** **Second: **The creative translation of our positioning into feeling. It explains what it means to be a research lab, what drives us emotionally, and how we show up in the world—our voice, symbols, and rituals. in final or finished. We believe
the only thing that matters
is what’s next. So we keep moving.
Keep making. Keep going. To leave behind what is
and imagine what if. Pulled forward by the new,
we are not here just to stay here. So if you are searching
for the finish line,
you won't find it here.
You won’t find us there. Because we are already off INTO THE NEW **Brand Message

INTO THE NEW.
** It’s a universal truth
Every great leap starts with a step into the unknown. It’s a mindset
We don’t cling to what is, we reach for what could be.
Exploration isn’t a phase. It’s our way forward. It’s a call to action
The next idea won’t come from the past. It waits in the new. **The Narrative’s Cosmos** Theme:
Imagination → Exploration → Transformation Speaks to:
Forward movement, curiosity, research mindset Function:
The invitation towards all to go beyond what's known and seen. A never ending leap toward what’s next. **Audience Talk Tracks** These are time-bound as the company evolves and advances its offering. For example, new products require tailored messages to communicate their advantages, and new technology calls for updated pitches to investors. Please treat them as valid, but limited in time.**
